summary: World-Value-Action Model targets VLA agents by adding an implicit planning structure around three coupled components: a world model for predicting task-relevant dynamics, a value model for evaluating likely outcomes, and an action model for choosing robot actions from vision and language context. The title suggests the interesting part is folding planning into the VLA policy itself, rather than relying on an explicit planner bolted onto perception-language-action mapping.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for building embodied agents that ground perception and language into action.

title: Unlabeled Multi-Robot Motion Planning with Improved Separation Trade-offs
summary: Unlabeled multi-robot motion planning is studied for unit-disk robots moving through polygonal environments, where robots are interchangeable and only need to occupy the target set rather than a specific assigned goal. The work focuses on polynomial-time solvability under separation assumptions between starts and targets, aiming to improve the trade-offs needed to guarantee collision-free coordinated motion despite the problem’s general hardness.

extra.full_text: We study unlabeled multi-robot motion planning for unit-disk robots in a polygonal environment. Although the problem is hard in general, polynomial-time solutions exist under appropriate separation assumptions on start and target positions.

title: Multi-Robot Coordination for Planning under Context Uncertainty
summary: Real-world robot teams often have to plan when the right objective depends on context that is not fully known in advance, such as which goals or tradeoffs matter in the current situation. This arXiv work appears to focus on multi-robot coordination under that kind of context uncertainty, where robots must reason jointly about plans while accounting for ambiguity in the operating priorities.

extra.full_text: Real-world robots often operate in settings where objective priorities depend on the underlying context of operation.

title: Empathetic Motion Generation for Humanoid Educational Robots via Reasoning-Guided Vision--Language--Motion Diffusion Architecture
summary: RG-VLMD generates instruction-aware co-speech gestures for humanoid educational robots by tying together vision, language, motion diffusion, and an explicit reasoning module. The focus is on making robot gestures fit both the spoken content and classroom context, so the motions are not just synchronized with speech but shaped toward more empathetic educational interaction.

extra.full_text: This article suggests a reasoning-guided vision-language-motion diffusion framework (RG-VLMD) for generating instruction-aware co-speech gestures for humanoid robots in educational scenarios.

title: RoboForge: Physically Optimized Text-guided Whole-Body Locomotion for Humanoids
summary: RoboForge targets the gap between text-generated human motion and motions a humanoid can actually execute, optimizing whole-body locomotion under physical constraints rather than just producing plausible animation. The available description is sparse, but the interesting piece is the text-guided pipeline’s focus on making generated behaviors robot-realizable for humanoids, where balance, contacts, and actuation limits usually break direct motion transfer.

extra.full_text: While generative models have become effective at producing human-like motions from text, transferring these motions to humanoid robots for physical execution remains challenging.

title: 2D or 3D: Who Governs Salience in VLA Models? -- Tri-Stage Token Pruning Framework with Modality Salience Awareness
summary: Tri-Stage Token Pruning is a modality-aware efficiency method for multi-visual-modal VLA models that decide actions from both 2D images and 3D inputs. It targets the question of whether 2D or 3D tokens dominate salience at different stages, pruning tokens in stages rather than treating all visual tokens uniformly.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as the mainstream of embodied intelligence. Recent VLA models have expanded their input modalities from 2D-only to 2D+3D paradigms, forming multi-visual-modal VLA (MVLA) models.

title: Fuzzy Logic Theory-based Adaptive Reward Shaping for Robust Reinforcement Learning (FARS)
summary: FARS uses fuzzy logic to adaptively shape rewards during reinforcement learning, aiming to make exploration less brittle in high-dimensional, long-horizon tasks where sparse or fixed rewards can stall learning. The mechanism is interesting because it adjusts reward guidance rather than relying on a static hand-designed signal, helping agents avoid local optima and learn more robust policies in realistic settings.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) often struggles in real-world tasks with high-dimensional state spaces and long horizons, where sparse or fixed rewards severely slow down exploration and cause agents to get trapped in local optima.

title: Long-Term Memory for VLA-based Agents in Open-World Task Execution
summary: Vision-Language-Action agents are extended with long-term memory so they can carry experience across open-world task execution instead of treating each lab automation episode in isolation. The focus is on complex chemical laboratory settings, where persistent memory is meant to address two practical limits of current VLA systems: weak long-horizon reasoning and the inability to accumulate reusable procedural experience over time.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated significant potential for embodied decision-making; however, their application in complex chemical laboratory automation remains restricted by limited long-horizon reasoning and the absence of persistent experience accumulation.

title: SLowRL: Safe Low-Rank Adaptation Reinforcement Learning for Locomotion
summary: SLowRL targets the risky last mile of sim-to-real locomotion by fine-tuning a deployed policy through safe low-rank adaptation rather than full, unconstrained hardware training. It is designed to reduce mechanical risk and sample inefficiency when adapting legged robot controllers on real hardware, focusing updates into a constrained low-rank space so the robot can improve while staying closer to the original simulated policy.

extra.full_text: Sim-to-real transfer of locomotion policies often leads to performance degradation due to the inevitable sim-to-real gap. Naively fine-tuning these policies directly on hardware is problematic, as it poses risks of mechanical failure and suffers from high sample inefficiency.

title: ForceVLA2: Unleashing Hybrid Force-Position Control with Force Awareness for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: ForceVLA2 targets contact-rich robot manipulation by moving beyond pure position control to hybrid force-position control with explicit force awareness. From the provided text, the core idea is to let an embodied AI system sense and regulate interaction forces during manipulation, aiming to improve stability, precision, and robustness in real-world contact-heavy tasks.

extra.full_text: Embodied intelligence for contact-rich manipulation has predominantly relied on position control, while explicit awareness and regulation of interaction forces remain under-explored, limiting stability, precision, and robustness in real-world tasks.

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Universal Horizon Models
summary: Universal Horizon Models target offline model-based RL’s compounding-error problem by learning a dynamics model that can predict over arbitrary horizons instead of repeatedly rolling out one-step predictions on its own generated states. The setup is meant to support value learning on imagined on-policy trajectories while reducing the drift that usually makes long synthetic rollouts unreliable.

extra.full_text: Model-based reinforcement learning (RL) offers a compelling approach to offline RL by enabling value learning on imagined on-policy trajectories. However, it often suffers from compounding errors due to repeated model inference on self-generated states.

title: Tactile Modality Fusion for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: TacFiLM is a lightweight fusion method for adding visual-tactile signals to vision-language-action robot policies. It targets a gap in current VLA models, which are semantically grounded and generalize well but still mostly perceive the world through vision alone, by giving the policy a way to condition its actions on touch as well as images and language.

extra.full_text: We propose TacFiLM, a lightweight modality-fusion approach that integrates visual-tactile signals into vision-language-action (VLA) models. While recent advances in VLA models have introduced robot policies that are both generalizable and semantically grounded, these models mainly rely on vision-based perception.

title: WestWorld: A Knowledge-Encoded Scalable Trajectory World Model for Diverse Robotic Systems
summary: WestWorld is a trajectory world model meant to learn and predict dynamics across many different robotic systems while explicitly encoding physical-structure knowledge. It targets a scaling problem in prior trajectory models: handling a large variety of system dynamics without treating each robot as an unstructured black box.

extra.full_text: Trajectory world models play a crucial role in robotic dynamics learning, planning, and control. While recent works have explored trajectory world models for diverse robotic systems, they struggle to scale to a large number of distinct system dynamics and overlook domain knowledge of physical structures.

title: HazardArena: Evaluating Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: HazardArena evaluates whether vision-language-action models can align their physical actions with semantic safety constraints, rather than just complete manipulation tasks. It targets the gap between a model’s inherited visual-linguistic knowledge and its learned action policy, testing whether robots recognize and avoid hazardous behavior implied by the scene or instruction.

extra.comment: Submitted to conference; 12 pages, 8 figures, including supplementary material
extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich world knowledge from vision-language backbones and acquire executable skills via action demonstrations. However, existing evaluations largely focus on action execution success, leaving action policies loosely coupled with visual-linguistic semantics.

title: ACT: Automated CPS Testing for Open-Source Robotic Platforms
summary: ACT targets the testing gap in open-source cyber-physical robotics software, where independently developed modules can interact in ways that leave serious platform-level errors hidden. It automates CPS testing for open-source robotic platforms, aiming to expose failures that ordinary module-level or contributor-driven testing may miss.

extra.full_text: Open-source software for cyber-physical systems (CPS) often lacks robust testing involving robotic platforms, resulting in critical errors that remain undetected. This is especially challenging when multiple modules of CPS software are developed by various open-source contributors.

title: PhyGile: Physics-Prefix Guided Motion Generation for Agile General Humanoid Motion Tracking
summary: PhyGile targets agile humanoid motion tracking by steering motion generation with a physics-prefix signal, rather than relying only on human motion priors learned from capture data. The motivation is that text-to-motion models trained on human datasets often encode biomechanics, contacts, mass distribution, and actuation assumptions that do not transfer cleanly to real humanoid robots.

extra.full_text: Humanoid robots are expected to execute agile and expressive whole-body motions in real-world settings. Existing text-to-motion generation models are predominantly trained on captured human motion datasets, whose priors assume human biomechanics, actuation, mass distribution, and contact strategies.

title: HumDex: Humanoid Dexterous Manipulation Made Easy
summary: HumDex tackles humanoid whole-body dexterous manipulation by focusing on the data bottleneck: collecting high-quality demonstrations efficiently. From the provided description, it appears aimed at making demonstration acquisition easier for humanoids that must coordinate body motion and hand-level manipulation, but the excerpt does not give enough detail to state the specific mechanism or results.

extra.full_text: This paper investigates humanoid whole-body dexterous manipulation, where the efficient collection of high-quality demonstration data remains a central bottleneck.

title: $Ψ_0$: An Open Foundation Model Towards Universal Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Ψ_0 (Psi-Zero) is presented as an open foundation model for humanoid loco-manipulation, targeting tasks that require a humanoid to coordinate whole-body movement with object interaction. The available text does not provide details on its architecture, training data, benchmarks, or results, so the concrete takeaway is that it aims to serve as a general-purpose base model for challenging humanoid control settings.

extra.full_text: We introduce $Ψ_0$ (Psi-Zero), an open foundation model to address challenging humanoid loco-manipulation tasks.

title: SPARK: Skeleton-Parameter Aligned Retargeting on Humanoid Robots with Kinodynamic Trajectory Optimization
summary: SPARK retargets human motion to humanoid robots by aligning skeleton parameters and then using kinodynamic trajectory optimization to make the resulting motion feasible under the robot’s kinematic and dynamic constraints. It is aimed at turning raw human demonstrations into usable priors for humanoid control policies, addressing the common failure mode where visually plausible motion cannot actually be executed by the target robot.

extra.full_text: Human motion provides rich priors for training general-purpose humanoid control policies, but raw demonstrations are often incompatible with a robot's kinematics and dynamics, limiting their direct use.

title: GRACE: A Unified 2D Multi-Robot Path Planning Simulator & Benchmark for Grid, Roadmap, And Continuous Environments
summary: GRACE is a simulator and benchmark for comparing multi-robot path planning methods across grid maps, roadmaps, and continuous 2D environments under a shared interface. It targets the gap between MAPF and MRMP evaluation by making modeling choices explicit and reproducible, so researchers can study how algorithms behave when the same planning problem is represented in different ways.

extra.comment: ICRA 2026, code will be released soon
extra.full_text: Advancing Multi-Agent Pathfinding (MAPF) and Multi-Robot Motion Planning (MRMP) requires platforms that enable transparent, reproducible comparisons across modeling choices.

title: Cybo-Waiter: A Physical Agentic Framework for Humanoid Whole-Body Locomotion-Manipulation
summary: Cybo-Waiter targets humanoid robots that must carry out open-ended natural-language service requests in real human spaces, where they have to coordinate locomotion, manipulation, and decision-making over long horizons despite incomplete observations. It frames the robot as a physical agentic system for whole-body locomotion-manipulation, aiming to connect language-level intent with reliable embodied execution rather than treating navigation and object interaction as separate problems.

extra.full_text: Robots are increasingly expected to execute open ended natural language requests in human environments, which demands reliable long horizon execution under partial observability.

title: Edge-Assisted Multi-Robot Visual-Inertial SLAM with Efficient Communication
summary: Edge-assisted multi-robot visual-inertial SLAM splits the mapping problem across robots, edge nodes, and the cloud so teams can keep real-time local estimates while still building a globally consistent map. The emphasis is on reducing the communication and compute burden on individual robots, using cloud/edge resources to handle the heavier global optimization and storage that onboard hardware struggles with.

extra.full_text: The integration of cloud computing and edge computing is an effective way to achieve global consistent and real-time multi-robot Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). Cloud computing effectively solves the problem of limited computing, communication and storage capacity of terminal equipment.

title: Kinodynamic Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Locomotion via Multi-Contact Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization
summary: KinoDynamic Motion Retargeting frames humanoid locomotion retargeting as a multi-contact, whole-body trajectory optimization problem rather than a simple pose or gait transfer step. The interesting part is that the retargeting explicitly accounts for kinodynamic feasibility and contact interactions across the full body, aiming to produce humanoid motions that are physically consistent for locomotion.

extra.full_text: We present the KinoDynamic Motion Retargeting (KDMR) framework, a novel approach for humanoid locomotion that models the retargeting process as a multi-contact, whole-body trajectory optimization problem.

title: SCDP: Learning Humanoid Locomotion from Partial Observations via Mixed-Observation Distillation
summary: SCDP targets deployable humanoid locomotion policies that do not depend on privileged full-body state estimates at test time. It uses mixed-observation distillation to learn from offline data while bridging the gap between rich training observations and the partial, noisier observations available on real robots.

extra.full_text: Distilling humanoid locomotion control from offline datasets into deployable policies remains a challenge, as existing methods rely on privileged full-body states that require complex and often unreliable state estimation.

title: On the Cost of Evolving Task Specialization in Multi-Robot Systems
summary: Evolutionary optimization is used to study how task specialization emerges in multi-robot systems, where splitting roles can simplify individual robot behaviors and improve group efficiency. The focus is on the tradeoff: earlier work showed that specialization can evolve, but this paper asks what costs are incurred when a robot collective becomes specialized rather than remaining more general-purpose.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication in the proceeding of ANTS 2026 - 15th International Conference on Swarm Intelligence
extra.full_text: Task specialization can lead to simpler robot behaviors and higher efficiency in multi-robot systems. Previous works have shown the emergence of task specialization during evolutionary optimization, focusing on feasibility rather than costs.

title: Reset-Free Reinforcement Learning for Real-World Agile Driving: An Empirical Study
summary: A reset-free RL setup is tested on a physical 1/10-scale car learning agile driving directly on a slippery indoor track, with training running continuously instead of relying on people to reposition the vehicle after failures. The interesting part is the real-world emphasis: it treats resets as a core bottleneck for robotic driving experiments and studies whether an agent can keep collecting useful experience under messy, failure-prone conditions.

extra.full_text: This paper presents an empirical study of reset-free reinforcement learning (RL) for real-world agile driving, in which a physical 1/10-scale vehicle learns continuously on a slippery indoor track without manual resets.

title: FAME: Force-Adaptive RL for Expanding the Manipulation Envelope of a Full-Scale Humanoid
summary: FAME uses force-adaptive reinforcement learning to help a full-scale humanoid stay balanced while applying or resisting external forces through its hands during bimanual manipulation. The idea targets a practical bottleneck in humanoid manipulation: hand interaction forces travel through the whole body, so balance control directly limits how far, hard, and reliably the robot can manipulate objects.

extra.full_text: Maintaining balance under external hand forces is critical for humanoid bimanual manipulation, where interaction forces propagate through the kinematic chain and constrain the feasible manipulation envelope.

title: DeReCo: Decoupling Representation and Coordination Learning for Object-Adaptive Decentralized Multi-Robot Cooperative Transport
summary: DeReCo targets decentralized multi-robot cooperative transport, where robots must move objects whose shapes and physical properties vary enough to break policies tuned to a single object type. It frames the problem around separating object representation learning from coordination learning, aiming to let teams adapt their transport behavior to new objects without relying on centralized control.

extra.full_text: Generalizing decentralized multi-robot cooperative transport across objects with diverse shapes and physical properties remains a fundamental challenge.

title: VORL-EXPLORE: A Hybrid Learning Planning Approach to Multi-Robot Exploration in Dynamic Environments
summary: VORL-EXPLORE targets multi-robot exploration in dense, changing environments by combining learned decision-making with planning, rather than treating frontier assignment and local navigation as separate brittle steps. From the provided description, its focus is making hierarchical exploration more robust when robots must coordinate while also reacting to dynamic obstacles or scene changes.

extra.full_text: Hierarchical multi-robot exploration commonly decouples frontier allocation from local navigation, which can make the system brittle in dense and dynamic environments.

title: GeoLoco: Leveraging 3D Geometric Priors from Visual Foundation Model for Robust RGB-Only Humanoid Locomotion
summary: GeoLoco targets humanoid locomotion from RGB alone, aiming to replace the usual dependence on active depth sensors by drawing 3D geometric priors from a visual foundation model. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available, but the work is framed around making camera-only perceptive walking more robust by injecting geometry that RGB policies typically lack.

extra.full_text: The prevailing paradigm of perceptive humanoid locomotion relies heavily on active depth sensors.

title: HybridMimic: Hybrid RL-Centroidal Control for Humanoid Motion Mimicking
summary: HybridMimic uses motion mimicking to help humanoid reinforcement-learning policies acquire complex behaviors by following human motion patterns. The title suggests a hybrid controller that combines learned RL behavior with centroidal control, aiming to keep the expressiveness of imitation while grounding the motion in whole-body dynamics.

extra.full_text: Motion mimicking, i.e., encouraging the control policy to mimic human motion, facilitates the learning of complex tasks via reinforcement learning (RL) for humanoid robots.

title: Moving Through Clutter: Scaling Data Collection and Benchmarking for 3D Scene-Aware Humanoid Locomotion via Virtual Reality
summary: Humanoid locomotion has become capable of flashy dynamic skills, but this arXiv work targets the harder problem of moving through cluttered 3D scenes rather than open, flat spaces. It focuses on scaling data collection and benchmarking for scene-aware humanoid navigation using virtual reality, suggesting a pipeline where humans can help generate realistic traversal behavior and evaluate robots in obstacle-rich environments.

extra.full_text: Recent advances in humanoid locomotion have enabled dynamic behaviors such as dancing, martial arts, and parkour, yet these capabilities are predominantly demonstrated in open, flat, and obstacle-free settings.

title: Multi-Robot Trajectory Planning via Constrained Bayesian Optimization and Local Cost Map Learning with STL-Based Conflict Resolution
summary: Multi-robot motion planning is formulated around Signal Temporal Logic specifications and kinodynamic constraints, using constrained Bayesian optimization to search for trajectories more efficiently than heavy sampling-based planners. The approach pairs local cost map learning with STL-based conflict resolution, aiming to make coordinated robot plans more scalable and adaptable when exact methods become computationally impractical.

extra.full_text: We address multi-robot motion planning under Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications with kinodynamic constraints. Exact approaches face scalability bottlenecks and limited adaptability, while conventional sampling-based methods require excessive samples to construct optimal trajectories.

title: ROSER: Few-Shot Robotic Sequence Retrieval for Scalable Robot Learning
summary: ROSER targets the mismatch between abundant long robot interaction logs and the scarce labeled, segmented demonstrations needed for training. It frames robot learning data curation as few-shot sequence retrieval, using a small number of task examples to find relevant segments in large continuous datasets so they can be reused for scalable downstream learning.

extra.full_text: A critical bottleneck in robot learning is the scarcity of task-labeled, segmented training data, despite the abundance of large-scale robotic datasets recorded as long, continuous interaction logs.

title: Tendon Force Modeling for Sim2Real Transfer of Reinforcement Learning Policies for Tendon-Driven Robots
summary: Tendon-driven robots can keep actuators off the moving structure and preserve compliance, but their nonlinear force transmission makes learned controllers hard to move from simulation to hardware. The paper focuses on modeling tendon forces for reinforcement-learning sim-to-real transfer, aiming to make simulated policies account for the actuation behavior that usually breaks deployment on complex tendon systems.

extra.full_text: Robots which make use of soft or compliant inter- actions often leverage tendon-driven actuation which enables actuators to be placed more flexibly, and compliance to be maintained. However, controlling complex tendon systems is challenging.

title: RoboLight: A Dataset with Linearly Composable Illumination for Robotic Manipulation
summary: RoboLight is a real-world robotic manipulation dataset of synchronized episodes captured while lighting conditions are systematically varied. Its focus on linearly composable illumination is meant to support analysis and training of manipulation policies that can separate task behavior from lighting changes, a practical gap in robot learning data collected under more fixed visual conditions.

extra.full_text: In this paper, we introduce RoboLight, the first real-world robotic manipulation dataset capturing synchronized episodes under systematically varied lighting conditions.

title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty
summary: ArthroCut is an autonomous policy-learning framework for knee arthroplasty robots that moves beyond preplanned assistive cutting toward context-aware action generation during bone resection. It targets the real-time decision-making gap in surgical robotics, aiming to let the robot adapt its cutting policy to operative context rather than simply execute surgeon-specified motions.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
extra.full_text: Despite rapid commercialization of surgical robots, their autonomy and real-time decision-making remain limited in practice. To address this gap, we propose ArthroCut, an autonomous policy learning framework that upgrades knee arthroplasty robots from assistive execution to context-aware action generation.

title: X-Loco: Towards Generalist Humanoid Locomotion Control via Synergetic Policy Distillation
summary: X-Loco targets the problem of putting upright walking, fall recovery, and whole-body coordination into a single humanoid locomotion controller instead of training separate policies for each skill. It uses synergetic policy distillation to merge controllers with different dynamics and objectives into a more generalist policy, aiming to preserve specialized skill performance while enabling smoother switching across challenging locomotion situations.

extra.full_text: While recent advances have demonstrated strong performance in individual humanoid skills such as upright locomotion, fall recovery and whole-body coordination, learning a single policy that masters all these skills remains challenging due to the diverse dynamics and conflicting control objectives involved.

title: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Control under Time-Varying Dynamics
summary: Model-based reinforcement learning is applied to control problems where the system dynamics change over time, such as from wear, drift, or shifting operating conditions. The framing targets a common gap in learning-based controllers, which often assume stationary dynamics even though many real robots and engineered systems gradually or abruptly move away from the model they were trained on.

extra.comment: 15 pages, 5 figues, 2 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
extra.full_text: Learning-based control methods typically assume stationary system dynamics, an assumption often violated in real-world systems due to drift, wear, or changing operating conditions. We study reinforcement learning for control under time-varying dynamics.

title: Boosting Vision-Language-Action Finetuning with Feasible Action Neighborhood Prior
summary: Vision-language-action finetuning is reframed around the idea that a robot state usually has a feasible action neighborhood rather than one uniquely correct next move. FAN uses that local set of near-equivalent actions as a prior during training, so policies are encouraged to treat small action variations that make indistinguishable task progress as valid instead of overfitting to a single demonstration action.

extra.full_text: In real-world robotic manipulation, states typically admit a neighborhood of near-equivalent actions. That is, for each state, there exist a feasible action neighborhood (FAN) rather than a single correct action, within which motions yield indistinguishable progress.

title: SOLE-R1: Video-Language Reasoning as the Sole Reward for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
summary: SOLE-R1 uses a vision-language model’s video-level reasoning as the only reward signal for on-robot reinforcement learning, replacing hand-engineered rewards or task-specific success detectors with language-conditioned assessment of rollout videos. The interesting bet is that a VLM can judge whether the robot is making progress from visual evidence alone, turning broad video-language understanding into a practical supervision source for physical robot policy learning.

extra.full_text: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities across diverse tasks, motivating efforts to leverage these models to supervise robot learning.

title: Sim-to-Real Fruit Detection Using Synthetic Data: Quantitative Evaluation and Embedded Deployment with Isaac Sim
summary: Synthetic fruit imagery from Isaac Sim is used to train object detectors for sim-to-real transfer when real training data is scarce, with evaluation focused on how well the synthetic-data models carry over to real fruit detection. The study also follows the pipeline through embedded deployment, so the result is not just a dataset-generation exercise but a quantitative look at detection performance under practical compute constraints.

extra.full_text: This study investigates the effectiveness of synthetic data for sim-to-real transfer in object detection under constrained data conditions and embedded deployment requirements.

title: Learning Human-Intention Priors from Large-Scale Human Demonstrations for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Human videos are treated as a source of manipulation priors, but the challenge is separating intent from scene perception, human motion, and embodiment-specific action. The paper focuses on learning human-intention priors from large-scale demonstrations so a robot can use the underlying goal structure of human manipulation rather than trying to directly imitate human movements.

extra.full_text: Human videos contain rich manipulation priors, but using them for robot learning remains difficult because raw observations entangle scene understanding, human motion, and embodiment-specific action.

title: QDTraj: Exploration of Diverse Trajectory Primitives for Articulated Objects Robotic Manipulation
summary: QDTraj targets robotic manipulation of articulated household objects by exploring diverse trajectory primitives rather than relying on a single motion pattern. The emphasis is on giving domestic robots a richer set of candidate motions for open-ended environments, where doors, drawers, lids, and other articulated objects can require different interaction trajectories depending on geometry and context.

extra.full_text: Thanks to the latest advances in learning and robotics, domestic robots are beginning to enter homes, aiming to execute household chores autonomously. However, robots still struggle to perform autonomous manipulation tasks in open-ended environments.

title: Knowledge-Guided Manipulation Using Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning
summary: KG-M3PO is a model-based reinforcement learning approach for partially observable robotic manipulation that ties together perception, symbolic knowledge graphs, and policy learning in a massively multi-task setting. The interesting piece is the explicit use of structured task knowledge to guide manipulation policies across many tasks, rather than treating perception and control as a purely end-to-end learning problem.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures. Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2026)
extra.full_text: This paper introduces Knowledge Graph based Massively Multi-task Model-based Policy Optimization (KG-M3PO), a framework for multi-task robotic manipulation in partially observable settings that unifies Perception, Knowledge, and Policy.

title: dWorldEval: Scalable Robotic Policy Evaluation via Discrete Diffusion World Model
summary: dWorldEval targets the bottleneck of evaluating robot policies at large scale by using a discrete diffusion world model as a proxy environment, rather than running every policy across thousands of real or simulated task settings. The idea is to make broad policy evaluation feasible across many environments and tasks, turning what is normally an expensive robotics benchmarking problem into a scalable model-based evaluation pipeline.

extra.full_text: Evaluating robotics policies across thousands of environments and thousands of tasks is infeasible with existing approaches. This motivates the need for a new methodology for scalable robotics policy evaluation.

title: ROSCell: A ROS2-Based Framework for Automated Formation and Orchestration of Multi-Robot Systems
summary: ROSCell is a ROS2-based framework aimed at manufacturing cells where heterogeneous robots and devices need to be assembled, coordinated, and reconfigured quickly for high-mix, low-volume production. It focuses on automating the formation and orchestration of multi-robot systems in flexible matrix production settings, where the practical challenge is keeping interconnected equipment adaptable as tasks change.

extra.full_text: Modern manufacturing under High-Mix-Low-Volume requirements increasingly relies on flexible and adaptive matrix production systems, which depend on interconnected heterogeneous devices and rapid task reconfiguration.

title: Task-Driven Co-Design of Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems
summary: Task-Driven Co-Design of Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems tackles the coupled problem of choosing robot designs, fleet makeup, and plans together rather than optimizing each layer separately. It frames heterogeneous multi-robot design around the downstream task, so the interesting part is the cross-domain reasoning: morphology, composition, and execution are treated as interdependent decisions in one design loop.

extra.full_text: Designing multi-agent robotic systems requires reasoning across tightly coupled decisions spanning heterogeneous domains, including robot design, fleet composition, and planning.

title: CaP-X: A Framework for Benchmarking and Improving Coding Agents for Robot Manipulation
summary: CaP-X studies whether Code-as-Policy can function as an autonomous controller for robot manipulation rather than just a complement to data-heavy VLA systems. It frames coding agents as policy generators for embodied tasks, aiming to benchmark their manipulation performance and improve how they turn perception and task goals into executable robot-control code.

extra.full_text: "Code-as-Policy" considers how executable code can complement data-intensive Vision-Language-Action (VLA) methods, yet their effectiveness as autonomous controllers for embodied manipulation remains underexplored.

title: ExpertGen: Scalable Sim-to-Real Expert Policy Learning from Imperfect Behavior Priors
summary: ExpertGen targets the data bottleneck in robot behavior cloning by learning expert policies in simulation from imperfect behavior priors, rather than relying on large amounts of expensive real-world teleoperation data. The interesting angle is the sim-to-real scaling strategy: it uses weaker prior behaviors as a starting point, then aims to turn them into higher-quality expert policies that can support more robust and generalizable robot learning.

extra.full_text: Learning generalizable and robust behavior cloning policies requires large volumes of high-quality robotics data. While human demonstrations (e.g., through teleoperation) serve as the standard source for expert behaviors, acquiring such data at scale in the real world is prohibitively expensive.

title: An Open Source Computer Vision and Machine Learning Framework for Affordable Life Science Robotic Automation
summary: An open-source robotics stack combines computer vision with machine-learning-based inverse kinematics to make life-science lab automation cheaper and more accessible. It targets concrete benchtop tasks such as colony picking and liquid handling, suggesting a route to repurpose affordable robotic hardware for workflows that usually require more specialized automation systems.

extra.full_text: We present an open-source robotic framework that integrates computer vision and machine learning based inverse kinematics to enable low-cost laboratory automation tasks such as colony picking and liquid handling.

title: Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action models are treated here as systems whose internal features may play very different roles in turning images and language into robot actions. The paper uses a mechanistic analysis to probe which representations actually drive action generation, aiming to separate behaviorally important features from ones that are present but less causally relevant.

extra.comment: Accepted to Multimodal Intelligence Workshop @ ICLR
extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models combine perception, language, and motor control in a single architecture, yet how they translate multimodal inputs into actions remains poorly understood.

title: From Inference Efficiency to Embodied Efficiency: Revisiting Efficiency Metrics for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action models are usually judged by inference-side metrics, but this paper argues that embodied agents need efficiency measures tied to real interaction costs across perception, language conditioning, and motor execution. It reframes evaluation around “embodied efficiency,” asking how well a VLA system converts computation into successful action in the physical world rather than just how cheaply it runs a forward pass.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently enabled embodied agents to perform increasingly complex tasks by jointly reasoning over visual, linguistic, and motor modalities.

title: Introducing M: A Modular, Modifiable Social Robot
summary: M is an open-source, low-cost social robot platform meant to make social robotics studies easier to reproduce, customize, and run outside the lab. Its emphasis is on reducing the practical friction around building and modifying robot hardware, giving researchers a more accessible platform for deployments in real-world social settings.

extra.full_text: We present M, an open-source, low-cost social robot platform designed to reduce platform friction that slows social robotics research by making robots easier to reproduce, modify, and deploy in real-world settings.

title: Web-Gewu: A Browser-Based Interactive Playground for Robot Reinforcement Learning
summary: Web-Gewu is a browser-based interactive playground for robot reinforcement learning aimed at lowering the compute and setup burden in robotics education. From the provided text, it focuses on making embodied-intelligence experiments easier to access without heavy local configuration, but no specific algorithms, tasks, or results are given.

extra.full_text: With the rapid development of embodied intelligence, robotics education faces a dual challenge: high computational barriers and cumbersome environment configuration.

title: Offload or Overload: A Platform Measurement Study of Mobile Robotic Manipulation Workloads
summary: Mobile robotic manipulation workloads are examined through a platform-level measurement study focused on the compute pressure created by foundation-model-based robot perception, planning, and control. The title frames the central tradeoff as whether these workloads should be offloaded from the robot or kept onboard, highlighting how physical AI gains can turn into system overload when deployed on mobile robotic platforms.

extra.full_text: Mobile robotic manipulation--the ability of robots to navigate spaces and interact with objects--is a core capability of physical AI. Foundation models have led to breakthroughs in their performance, but at a significant computational cost.

title: Action Draft and Verify: A Self-Verifying Framework for Vision-Language-Action Model
summary: Action Draft and Verify targets the speed-accuracy tradeoff in vision-language-action models by pairing fast diffusion-based action chunk generation with a self-verification step that checks whether proposed actions align with the visual-language context. The setup is interesting because it treats low-level continuous control not just as generation, but as draft-and-check inference, aiming to keep the efficiency of diffusion action experts while reducing unreliable actions in embodied tasks.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently demonstrated strong performance across embodied tasks. Modern VLAs commonly employ diffusion action experts to efficiently generate high-precision continuous action chunks, while auto-regressive generation can be slower and less accurate at low-level control.

title: ShapeGen: Robotic Data Generation for Category-Level Manipulation
summary: ShapeGen addresses category-level robotic manipulation under large within-category shape variation by generating training data across diverse object geometries. From the provided text, the central focus is on making manipulation policies more robust to everyday objects whose shapes differ substantially even within the same semantic class.

extra.full_text: Manipulation policies deployed in uncontrolled real-world scenarios are faced with great in-category geometric diversity of everyday objects.

title: Beyond Collision Avoidance: Multi-Robot Yielding and Spatial Affordance in Emergency Evacuations
summary: Mobile service robots in crowded evacuations need to do more than avoid collisions: they must yield in ways that preserve usable space for pedestrians in tight, high-stress settings. This arXiv work frames emergency evacuation as a multi-robot problem involving yielding behavior and spatial affordance, focusing on passively safe navigation when robots share confined routes with people.

extra.full_text: As mobile service robots increasingly coexist with pedestrians, ensuring passively safe behaviour during confined emergency evacuations is critical.

title: Before the Body Moves: Learning Anticipatory Joint Intent for Language-Conditioned Humanoid Control
summary: Language-conditioned humanoid control is framed around anticipatory joint intent: a representation that lets the controller act immediately while encoding where the body should be heading through upcoming transitions. The idea targets the mismatch between natural-language commands and streaming whole-body execution, so the robot is not just reacting to a command frame by frame but preparing its joints before visible motion changes occur.

extra.full_text: Natural language is an intuitive interface for humanoid robots, yet streaming whole-body control requires control representations that are executable now and anticipatory of future physical transitions.

title: RoboEvolve: Co-Evolving Planner-Simulator for Robotic Manipulation with Limited Data
summary: RoboEvolve targets the data bottleneck in robotic manipulation by co-evolving a planner and simulator so task-relevant behavior can be learned with limited physical interaction data. The interesting angle is the closed-loop relationship between planning and simulation: instead of treating the simulator as fixed, the system adapts both sides to make scarce task-aligned data go further.

extra.full_text: The scalability of robotic manipulation is fundamentally bottlenecked by the scarcity of task-aligned physical interaction data.

title: Your Vision-Language-Action Model Already Has Attention Heads For Path Deviation Detection
summary: VLA navigation models appear to contain internal attention heads that can signal when the robot is drifting from the instructed path, without adding a separate deviation detector. The result suggests that path-deviation awareness may already be encoded in the model’s vision-language-action representations, making it possible to monitor navigation failures by probing attention rather than retraining or bolting on extra supervision.

extra.comment: Keywords: Vision-Language Action (VLA), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Navigation Path Recovery, Robot Operating System (ROS)
extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong potential for predicting semantic actions in navigation tasks, demonstrating the ability to reason over complex linguistic instructions and visual contexts.

title: SafeManip: A Property-Driven Benchmark for Temporal Safety Evaluation in Robotic Manipulation
summary: SafeManip evaluates robotic manipulation safety through temporal properties rather than just end-state success, targeting failures where the order of events matters. It focuses on cases like contaminating a surface before contact or dropping an object too early, making safety violations explicit even when the overall task appears completed.

extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation is typically evaluated by task success, but successful completion does not guarantee safe execution. Many safety failures are temporal: a robot may touch a clean surface after contamination or release an object before it is fully inside an enclosure.

title: From Reaction to Anticipation: Proactive Failure Recovery through Agentic Task Graph for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Agentic Task Graph aims to make robotic manipulation recover from failures proactively rather than waiting for execution to break down. From the limited abstract text provided, the work targets dynamic, unstructured settings where manipulation plans are likely to fail and recovery needs to be built into the task structure itself rather than treated as an afterthought.

extra.full_text: Although robotic manipulation has made significant progress, reliable execution remains challenging because task failures are inevitable in dynamic and unstructured environments.

title: Mapping Embodied Affective Touch Strategies on a Humanoid Robot
summary: Affective touch for humanoid robots is framed as an embodied design problem, where the same emotional intent can change meaning depending on where the robot touches, what its body can physically do, and how much agency or social role people attribute to it. The work maps touch strategies across these constraints, giving HRI researchers a way to reason about robot touch as situated behavior rather than a generic emotional signal.

extra.full_text: Affective touch in human-robot interaction is shaped not only by emotional intent, but also by robot embodiment, including touch location, physical constraints, and perceived agency or social role.

title: Constraint-Aware Diffusion Priors for High-Fidelity and Versatile Quadruped Locomotion
summary: Constraint-Aware Diffusion Priors targets the scaling problem in quadruped locomotion when reinforcement and imitation learning are trained on large, heterogeneous motion datasets. It uses diffusion-based priors shaped by constraints so a robot can preserve high-fidelity, biomimetic movement while remaining versatile across locomotion behaviors, addressing a bottleneck that appears when conventional RL-plus-imitation pipelines absorb many motion sources.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning combined with imitation learning has significantly advanced biomimetic quadrupedal locomotion. However, scaling these frameworks to massive, multi-source datasets exposes fundamental bottlenecks.

title: Learning to Assist: Physics-Grounded Human-Human Control via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Learning to Assist targets humanoid robots for service and caregiving by framing assistance as a physics-grounded human-human control problem trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available beyond the goal of learning assistive humanoid behavior for daily-support scenarios.

extra.full_text: Humanoid robotics has strong potential to transform daily service and caregiving applications.

title: Towards Terrain-Aware Safe Locomotion for Quadrupedal Robots Using Proprioceptive Sensing
summary: Terrain-aware safe locomotion for quadrupeds is framed around using proprioceptive sensing to estimate uneven ground conditions and feed that information into safety-critical control. The paper targets the practical failure mode where robots must move without reliable external perception, focusing on how internal body and joint signals can support safer, more reliable walking over real-world terrain.

extra.full_text: Achieving safe quadrupedal locomotion in real-world environments has attracted much attention in recent years. When walking over uneven terrain, achieving reliable estimation and realising safety-critical control based on the obtained information is still an open question.

title: ProcVLM: Learning Procedure-Grounded Progress Rewards for Robotic Manipulation
summary: ProcVLM targets the feedback bottleneck in long-horizon robotic manipulation by learning progress rewards grounded in a task’s procedural stages rather than relying only on sparse success signals. It uses vision-language understanding to assess how far an execution has advanced through the intended procedure, giving robots denser training signals for tasks where intermediate progress matters.

extra.full_text: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires dense feedback that reflects how a task advances through its procedural stages, not merely whether the final outcome is successful.

title: Pri4R: Learning World Dynamics for Vision-Language-Action Models with Privileged 4D Representation
summary: Pri4R targets a common weakness in vision-language-action models: they can understand instructions and scenes semantically but often miss how the physical world changes over time in response to robot actions. It learns world dynamics through a privileged 4D representation, aiming to give VLAs a more grounded spatiotemporal model of interaction rather than relying only on visual-language correlations.

extra.full_text: Humans learn not only how their bodies move, but also how the surrounding world responds to their actions. In contrast, while recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit impressive semantic understanding, they often fail to capture the spatiotemporal dynamics governing physical interaction.

title: Active Embodiment Identification with Reinforcement Learning for Legged Robots
summary: Active Embodiment Identification trains a legged robot to deliberately take actions that reveal properties of its own body while also predicting those embodiment parameters explicitly. The interesting part is the coupling of reinforcement-learned probing behavior with embodiment estimation, so the robot is not just passively adapting from whatever motion data happens to occur but actively choosing informative interactions.

extra.full_text: We present an active embodiment identification method for legged robots that jointly learns information-seeking behavior and explicit embodiment prediction.

title: LaWM: Least Action World Models for Long-Horizon Physical Consistency from Visual Observations
summary: LaWM studies predictive world models for embodied AI that learn from visual observations while enforcing long-horizon physical consistency through a least-action principle. The interesting idea is to bias visual prediction toward trajectories that remain physically plausible over time, aiming to make learned models more useful for model-based reinforcement learning and robotic planning where small prediction errors can compound.

extra.full_text: Learning predictive world models from visual observations is a core problem in embodied AI, with applications to model-based reinforcement learning and robotic planning.

title: Multi-Robot Coordination in V2X Environments
summary: A V2X communication framework lets multiple social robots coordinate without a central controller while moving through dense urban traffic. The setup focuses on sharing local robot and traffic context so each robot can cooperate with nearby agents in real time, which is useful for navigation scenarios where pedestrians, vehicles, and other robots all affect one another.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication at the IEEE Intelligent Transportation Systems Conference (ITSC), 2026
extra.full_text: This paper presents a Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication framework that enables decentralized cooperation among social robots operating in complex urban traffic environments.

title: Perceptive Variable-Timing Footstep Planning for Humanoid Locomotion on Disconnected Footholds
summary: The paper tackles humanoid walking when safe footholds are separated into stepping-stone-like regions because obstacles, clutter, or slippery terrain make parts of the ground unusable. It focuses on perceptive footstep planning with variable timing, so the robot can reason not just about where to step on disconnected admissible footholds, but also when to take those steps during locomotion.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, 3 algorithms. Supplemental video at: https://youtu.be/5EeuBnSb66s
extra.full_text: Many real-world walking scenarios contain obstacles and unsafe ground patches (e.g., slippery or cluttered areas), leaving a disconnected set of admissible footholds that can be modeled as stepping-stone-like regions.

title: VOFA: Visual Object Goal Pushing with Force-Adaptive Control for Humanoids
summary: VOFA targets humanoid robots pushing large objects to specified goals using only onboard egocentric vision, a setting relevant to warehouse-style material handling. Its focus is force-adaptive control: coupling visual object-goal reasoning with pushing behavior that can adjust contact forces as the humanoid moves the object toward the target.

extra.full_text: The ability to push large objects in a goal-directed manner using onboard egocentric perception is an essential skill for humanoid robots to perform complex tasks such as material handling in warehouses.

title: Learning From Failures: Efficient Reinforcement Learning Control with Episodic Memory
summary: Early robot RL can waste many episodes on crashes, falls, and other premature terminations, so this paper focuses on turning those failures into reusable training signal through episodic memory. From the provided abstract fragment, the approach targets more efficient control learning in difficult exploration settings with contact-rich dynamics, but the specific memory mechanism, tasks, and quantitative results are not given.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success in robot learning. However, under challenging exploration and contact-rich dynamics, early-stage training is frequently dominated by premature terminations such as collisions and falls.

title: RoboAlign-R1: Distilled Multimodal Reward Alignment for Robot Video World Models
summary: RoboAlign-R1 trains robot video world models with rewards distilled from a multimodal reasoning model, targeting instruction following, manipulation success, and physical plausibility rather than just pixel reconstruction or perceptual similarity. The interesting shift is to make generated robot futures more useful for decision making by aligning the video model’s objective with whether the imagined rollout actually satisfies the task and obeys realistic manipulation dynamics.

extra.full_text: Existing robot video world models are typically trained with low-level objectives such as reconstruction and perceptual similarity, which are poorly aligned with the capabilities that matter most for robot decision making, including instruction following, manipulation success, and physical plausibility.

title: HarvestFlex: Strawberry Harvesting via Vision-Language-Action Policy Adaptation in the Wild
summary: HarvestFlex studies how vision-language-action policies can be adapted for real greenhouse tabletop strawberry harvesting, where the robot has to handle long action sequences, cluttered plants, occlusions, and shiny fruit surfaces. It focuses on transferring VLA behavior from more general settings into an in-the-wild agricultural manipulation task, making strawberry picking a concrete test case for whether these policies can cope with messy, visually difficult environments.

extra.full_text: This work presents the first study on transferring vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real greenhouse tabletop strawberry harvesting, a long-horizon, unstructured task challenged by occlusion and specular reflections.

title: Observing and Controlling Features in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action models are examined through the lens of feature observation and control, extending interpretability ideas from LLMs into embodied models with multimodal inputs and hybrid transformer-diffusion action heads. The interesting angle is that VLAs are harder to inspect than text-only models because perception and action are coupled, so being able to identify and steer internal features could make robot behavior more understandable and controllable.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) have shown remarkable progress towards embodied intelligence. While their architecture partially resembles that of Large Language Models (LLMs), VLAs exhibit higher complexity due to their multi-modal inputs/outputs and often hybrid nature of transformer and diffusion heads.

title: Enhancing RL Generalizability in Robotics through SHAP Analysis of Algorithms and Hyperparameters
summary: Reinforcement learning performance in robotics is examined through SHAP-based attribution over algorithm choices and hyperparameter settings, targeting the practical problem that policies often degrade when moved across environments. The study frames generalizability as something that can be diagnosed by identifying which configuration factors most strongly drive performance variation, giving researchers a more interpretable way to tune RL systems for deployment rather than relying on opaque sweeps.

extra.full_text: Despite significant advances in Reinforcement Learning (RL), model performance remains highly sensitive to algorithm and hyperparameter configurations, while generalization gaps across environments complicate real-world deployment.

title: Critic in the Loop: A Tri-System VLA Framework for Robust Long-Horizon Manipulation
summary: Critic in the Loop targets long-horizon visual manipulation by splitting responsibility across three systems: slower VLM-style semantic planning, faster reactive control, and a critic that monitors execution and catches failures as they unfold. The interesting angle is the explicit attempt to keep high-level reasoning in play without putting VLM latency on the real-time control path, using critique as a feedback mechanism for more robust manipulation over extended tasks.

extra.full_text: Balancing high-level semantic reasoning with low-level reactive control remains a core challenge in visual robotic manipulation. While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at cognitive planning, their inference latency precludes real-time execution.

title: Act, Think or Abstain: Complexity-Aware Adaptive Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Act, Think or Abstain targets the latency cost of adding reasoning to vision-language-action models by making inference complexity adaptive rather than fixed. From the title and abstract fragment, it appears to route robot decisions among direct action, extra deliberation, or abstention depending on task difficulty, aiming to preserve the benefits of reasoning while avoiding unnecessary computation on easier cases.

extra.full_text: Current research on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models predominantly focuses on enhancing generalization through established reasoning techniques. While effective, these improvements invariably increase computational complexity and inference latency.

title: Reinforcement Learning Trained Observer Control for Bearings-Only Tracking
summary: A deep reinforcement learning policy is used to choose observer maneuvers for autonomous bearings-only tracking, where the agent only sees angle measurements to a moving target rather than range. The tracking problem is cast as a belief MDP, with the belief state supplied by the posterior of a cubature Kalman filter, so the controller learns to act on uncertainty-aware target estimates instead of raw observations.

extra.full_text: This paper develops a deep reinforcement learning based observer control policy for autonomous bearings-only tracking of a moving target. The observer manoeuvre problem is formulated as a belief Markov decision process, where the belief state is represented by the posterior of a cubature Kalman filter (CKF).

title: AoI-Aware Multi-Robot Sensing and Transport on Connected Graphs
summary: AoI-Aware Multi-Robot Sensing and Transport on Connected Graphs studies teams of mobile robots that both collect measurements from distributed processes and relay them back to a base over a graph. The setup treats age of information from the moment sensing begins, so the objective accounts for stochastic parallel sensing times as well as hop-by-hop transport delays, making the scheduling problem closer to real monitoring pipelines than models that only age data after collection.

extra.full_text: A team of mobile robots monitors spatially distributed processes and delivers measurements to a base, where AoI is measured from sensing start, capturing both stochastic parallel sensing delays and hop-based propagation.

title: Learning Locomotion on Complex Terrain for Quadrupedal Robots with Foot Position Maps and Stability Rewards
summary: Uses foot position maps and stability-oriented rewards to train quadruped locomotion policies for complex terrain. The available text only establishes the problem area, so the concrete mechanism is the combination of terrain-aware foot placement representation with reward shaping aimed at keeping motion stable across difficult ground.

extra.full_text: Quadrupedal locomotion over complex terrain has been a long-standing research topic in robotics.

title: Distributed Algorithm with Emergent Area Partitioning and Base Station's Situation Awareness for Multi-Robot Patrolling
summary: Multiple robots coordinate patrols through a distributed algorithm that lets area partitions emerge from local behavior rather than being centrally assigned. The system also feeds situation-awareness information back to a base station, aiming to improve both surveillance efficiency and the operator’s ability to understand and respond to events.

extra.full_text: Patrolling with multiple robots offers efficient surveillance to detect and manage undesired situations. This necessitates improved patrol efficiency and operator situation awareness at base stations.

title: Decompose and Recompose: Reasoning New Skills from Existing Abilities for Cross-Task Robotic Manipulation

title: UAM: A Dual-Stream Perspective on Forgetting in VLA Training
summary: UAM argues that the usual VLA fine-tuning pipeline pays an “embodiment tax,” degrading the pretrained VLM’s multimodal knowledge because one encoder is forced to serve both semantic understanding and control. It adds a parallel Dorsal Expert initialized from a pretrained generative model and trained to predict visual dynamics, letting the full model train end-to-end on action data without freezing, gradient stops, or VL replay. The result preserves over 95% of the VLM’s multimodal capability while improving manipulation success on out-of-distribution tests with unseen objects, new object-target compositions, and instruction variation.

extra.full_text: Vision--language--action (VLA) models are typically built by fine-tuning a pretrained vision--language model (VLM) on action data. However, we show that this standard recipe systematically erodes the VLM's multimodal competence, a side effect we call the embodiment tax. But do VLAs have to forget? Inspired by the two-stream organization of biological vision, we trace this degradation to a structural bottleneck: current VLAs ask a single encoder to support both language-grounded semantics and control-relevant visual features, whereas biological vision separates recognition and visuomotor control into distinct pathways. Building on this view, we propose the Unified Action Model (UAM), which adds a parallel Dorsal Expert, an analog of the brain's dorsal pathway. To make the Dorsal Expert an effective second pathway and reduce the control-learning burden on the VLM, we initialize it from a pretrained generative model and train it with a mid-level reasoning objective that predicts visual dynamics. This design allows us to train the whole VLA end-to-end on action data alone: with no parameter freezing, no gradient stopping, and no auxiliary VL co-training, UAM retains over $95\%$ of the underlying VLM's multimodal capability and at the same time achieves the highest average success rate among baselines on a variety of manipulation tasks that probe out-of-distribution generalization, including unseen objects, novel object--target compositions, and instruction variation. Together, these results suggest that semantic preservation in VLAs can emerge from architectural separation itself, rather than being enforced by frozen weights or auxiliary data replay, and that this preserved semantic capability can naturally transfer from VLMs to semantic generalization in actions.

summary: Addresses force-aware control for humanoid robots with multi-fingered hands, focusing on how contact forces should be distributed across fingers during manipulation.
