extra.comment: This work has been accepted for publication in ICRA 2026
extra.full_text: In this paper, we address force-aware control and force distribution in robotic platforms with multi-fingered hands.

title: Entropy-Regularized Adjoint Matching for Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Entropy-Regularized Adjoint Matching targets offline RL with expressive generative policies, using flow-matching-style policy models to represent complex, multi-modal behavior from fixed datasets. The idea is to bring richer policy distributions into offline RL while regularizing the learned behavior with entropy, so the agent can model diverse action choices without relying on online exploration.

extra.full_text: Integrating expressive generative policies, such as flow-matching models, into offline reinforcement learning (RL) allows agents to capture complex, multi-modal behaviors.

title: Beyond Linear Attention: Softmax Transformers Implement In-Context Reinforcement Learning
summary: Softmax transformers are analyzed as in-context reinforcement learners, showing how they can adapt to new tasks from context alone without updating weights. The framing pushes beyond linear-attention accounts of in-context learning and argues that standard softmax attention can implement the mechanisms needed for reinforcement-learning-style adaptation.

extra.full_text: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) studies agents that, after pretraining, adapt to new tasks by conditioning on additional context without parameter updates.

title: BioProVLA-Agent: An Affordable, Protocol-Driven, Vision-Enhanced VLA-Enabled Embodied Multi-Agent System with Closed-Loop-Capable Reasoning for Biological Laboratory Manipulation
summary: BioProVLA-Agent targets wet-lab automation by combining protocol-driven execution with vision-enhanced VLA embodied agents and closed-loop reasoning for biological manipulation tasks. From the provided text, the concrete emphasis is on making lab robots more reliable and affordable in environments where repetitive procedures, reproducibility, and messy real-world execution constraints matter.

extra.full_text: Biological laboratory automation can reduce repetitive manual work and improve reproducibility, but reliable embodied execution in wet-lab environments remains challenging.

title: Experience Sharing in Mutual Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Language Models
summary: Mutual Reinforcement Learning runs RL post-training on multiple heterogeneous LLM policies at the same time, letting them exchange typed experience while preserving separate parameters, objectives, and tokenizers. The interesting part is that sharing experience is decoupled from forcing the models into a common architecture or training goal, so different language models can potentially learn from one another without being merged into a single policy.

extra.full_text: We introduce Mutual Reinforcement Learning, a framework for concurrent RL post-training in which heterogeneous LLM policies exchange typed experience while keeping separate parameters, objectives, and tokenizers.

title: Improved Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Smooth Kernels
summary: Improved Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Smooth Kernels targets continuous state-action RL without relying on the low-rank MDP assumptions that dominate much of the sample-efficiency theory. It reframes model-based RL around smooth kernel structure, aiming to preserve theoretical guarantees while allowing a less restrictive class of transition dynamics than classical low-rank formulations.

extra.full_text: For continuous state-action space scenarios, classical reinforcement learning (RL) theory predominantly focuses on low-rank Markov decision processes (MDPs), which provide sample-efficient guarantees at the expense of restrictive structural assumptions.

title: Anatomical Landmark-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Gastric Navigation
summary: Anatomical Landmark-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning targets autonomous navigation for wireless capsule endoscopy by using stomach landmarks to guide movement rather than relying on anatomy-specific policies that may not transfer well. The motivation is to improve mucosal coverage across variable patient anatomies, addressing a core limitation of current WCE navigation methods: they can miss diagnostically important regions because coverage is incomplete.

extra.full_text: Wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) enables painless visualization of the gastrointestinal tract, but its diagnostic potential is limited by incomplete mucosal coverage and poor transferability of existing navigation methods across patient anatomies.

title: Stabilized neural Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solvers: Error analysis and applications in model-based reinforcement learning
summary: Physics-informed neural solvers are used to approximate continuous-time Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations for optimal feedback control, targeting model-based reinforcement learning settings where the dynamics are known or learned. The work focuses on stabilizing these neural HJB solvers and analyzing their error, with applications aimed at making feedback synthesis more reliable in continuous control problems.

extra.full_text: Physics-informed neural solvers offer a promising route to model-based reinforcement learning in continuous time, where optimal feedback synthesis is governed by Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equations.

title: Convergence and Emergence of In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Chain of Thought
summary: In-context reinforcement learning lets an RL agent adapt to a new task at inference time by conditioning on examples or trajectories, without changing its weights. This paper studies how that ability emerges and converges when the agent also generates chain-of-thought reasoning, motivated by evidence that CoT can strengthen task adaptation from context alone.

extra.full_text: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) refers to the ability of RL agents to adapt to new tasks at inference time without parameter updates by conditioning on additional context. Recent empirical studies further demonstrate that Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation can amplify this ICRL capability.

title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning via a Poisson-Moreau Drift
summary: Analyzes almost-sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning when updates are driven by Markovian noise rather than independent samples. The title suggests the argument is built around a Poisson-Moreau drift mechanism, giving a way to translate stability structure into pathwise rate guarantees for these stochastic iterative algorithms.

extra.full_text: Establishing almost sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning under Markovian noise is a fundamental theoretical challenge.

title: Towards Differentially Private Reinforcement Learning with General Function Approximation
summary: Differentially private online reinforcement learning is extended beyond tabular and linear cases to settings with general function approximation. The paper provides theoretical guarantees for this broader regime, targeting RL agents that can learn with richer model classes while still protecting the privacy of interaction data.

extra.full_text: We present the first theoretical guarantees for differentially private online reinforcement learning (RL) with general function approximation, extending beyond prior work restricted to tabular and linear settings.

title: Multi-Objective Constraint Inference using Inverse reinforcement learning
summary: Multi-Objective Constraint Inference applies inverse reinforcement learning to infer safety and operational constraints from expert demonstrations in settings where an agent must balance multiple objectives. The idea is aimed at making reinforcement-learning agents respect implicit boundaries learned from expert behavior rather than relying only on hand-specified rules.

extra.full_text: Constraint inference is widely considered essential to align reinforcement learning agents with safety boundaries and operational guidelines by observing expert demonstrations.

title: Path-Coupled Bellman Flows for Distributional Reinforcement Learning
summary: Path-Coupled Bellman Flows targets distributional reinforcement learning by learning return distributions with flows that are coupled along Bellman backup paths, avoiding projection artifacts from finite-support or quantile methods. The formulation is designed to fix boundary mismatch at the flow source and reduce the variance that arises when bootstrapping uses independent noise for current and successor returns.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)
extra.full_text: Distributional reinforcement learning (DRL) models the full return distribution, but existing finite-support or quantile-based methods rely on projections, while recent flow-based approaches can suffer from \emph{boundary mismatch} at the flow source or from \emph{high-variance} bootstrapping when current and successor noises are independent.

title: Coordination Matters: Evaluation of Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Cooperative MARL evaluation often collapses team behavior into aggregate scores like return, success rate, or completion time, which can hide whether agents are actually coordinating well. This work focuses on coordination itself as an evaluation target, arguing that cooperative agents should be judged not just by outcomes but by the interaction patterns and dependencies that produce them.

extra.full_text: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) benchmarks commonly emphasize aggregate outcomes such as return, success rate, or completion time.

title: Learning to Cut: Reinforcement Learning for Benders Decomposition
summary: Benders decomposition is treated as a sequential decision problem in which a reinforcement learning agent learns which cuts to add as the master problem expands. The aim is to speed up two-stage stochastic programming under uncertainty by avoiding the slow convergence that comes from accumulating too many weak or unnecessary cuts.

extra.full_text: Benders decomposition (BD) is a widely used solution approach for solving two-stage stochastic programs arising in real-world decision-making under uncertainty. However, it often suffers from slow convergence as the master problem grows with an increasing number of cuts.

title: Operator-Guided Invariance Learning for Continuous Reinforcement Learning
summary: Operator-Guided Invariance Learning targets continuous-time, continuous-state/action reinforcement learning by using operator-specified value-preserving structure to make learning less sensitive to nuisance variation and distribution shift. The idea is to bake known invariances into the learning process so policies and value estimates can generalize more reliably while reducing the data burden and brittleness typical of continuous RL.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) with continuous time and state/action spaces is often data-intensive and brittle under nuisance variability and shift, motivating methods that exploit value-preserving structures to stabilize and improve learning.

title: DAISS: Phase-Aware Imitation Learning for Dual-Arm Robotic Ultrasound-Guided Interventions
summary: DAISS applies phase-aware imitation learning to dual-arm robotic ultrasound-guided interventions, targeting the coordination problem of manipulating an ultrasound probe and an interventional tool together. From the available text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified beyond using imitation learning to automate complex robotic manipulation in this setting.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning has shown strong potential for automating complex robotic manipulation.

title: LaST-R1: Reinforcing Robotic Manipulation via Adaptive Physical Latent Reasoning
summary: LaST-R1 targets robotic foundation models that need to reason over cluttered visual scenes before acting, framing manipulation as adaptive physical latent reasoning rather than direct perception-to-action mapping. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available, so the safe takeaway is that it focuses on making robot manipulation more robust in dynamic environments where visual complexity demands scene-level reasoning.

extra.full_text: Robotic foundation models require reasoning over complex visual scenes to execute adaptive actions in dynamic environments.

title: Toward Visually Realistic Simulation: A Benchmark for Evaluating Robot Manipulation in Simulation
summary: Robot manipulation policies are evaluated in simulation, but many benchmarks still look too synthetic to predict real-world behavior well. This benchmark targets that gap by focusing on visually realistic simulation as a testbed, making it easier to study how much appearance fidelity affects manipulation performance and sim-to-real reliability.

extra.full_text: Reliable simulation evaluation of robot manipulation policies serves as a high-fidelity proxy for real-world performance. Although existing benchmarks cover a wide range of task categories, they lack visual realism, creating a large domain gap between simulation and reality.

title: AdaGamma: State-Dependent Discounting for Temporal Adaptation in Reinforcement Learning
summary: AdaGamma replaces the usual fixed reinforcement-learning discount factor with a state-dependent one, so an agent can adapt its effective planning horizon and bootstrapping strength as it moves through different parts of an environment. From the provided text, the core idea is temporal adaptation: instead of treating all states as if they warrant the same lookahead, the method lets discounting vary with state to better match local decision dynamics.

extra.full_text: The discount factor in reinforcement learning controls both the effective planning horizon and the strength of bootstrapping, yet most deep RL methods use a single fixed value across all states.

title: Causal Reinforcement Learning for Complex Card Games: A Magic The Gathering Benchmark
summary: Causal RL is framed around a Magic: The Gathering benchmark, targeting a setting with long sequential decisions, hidden information, large masked action spaces, and explicit causal structure. The benchmark is meant to stress causal reasoning in a game environment that is substantially more complex than typical RL testbeds, making it useful for studying how agents handle interventions and decision dependencies under partial observability.

extra.full_text: Causal reinforcement learning (RL) lacks benchmarks for complex systems that combine sequential decision making, hidden information, large masked action spaces, and explicit causal structure.

title: Schedule-and-Calibrate: Utility-Guided Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning for Code LLMs
summary: Schedule-and-Calibrate targets the cost of training separate code-LLM RL specialists by using multi-task reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. It frames the problem around deciding how to schedule training across coding tasks and calibrate the unified model so it can preserve task-specific utility without multiplying deployment and training overhead.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards has proven effective at post-training LLMs for coding, yet deploying separate task-specific specialists incurs costs that scale with the number of tasks, motivating a unified multi-task RL (MTRL) approach.

title: BehaviorGuard: Online Backdoor Defense for Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: BehaviorGuard targets online backdoor defense in deep reinforcement learning, where poisoned policies can be triggered into unsafe behavior during deployment. Instead of depending on reward anomalies to reconstruct triggers and then finetune the model, it appears to focus on detecting or guarding against backdoored behavior as the agent acts, which is interesting for settings where attack signatures are not known in advance.

extra.full_text: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Current defenses typically rely on reward anomalies to reverse-engineer triggers and model finetuning to remove backdoors.

title: Robotic Grasping and Placement Controlled by EEG-Based Hybrid Visual and Motor Imagery
summary: EEG signals from visual and motor imagery are combined with robotic control so a user can drive grasping and placement through inferred intent rather than manual commands. The interesting piece is the hybrid VI/MI interface: it separates object- or scene-directed visual intention from motor-imagery control and uses that in real time to guide a robot through pick-and-place behavior.

extra.full_text: We present a framework that integrates EEG-based visual and motor imagery (VI/MI) with robotic control to enable real-time, intention-driven grasping and placement.

title: Transformers Provably Implement In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Policy Improvement
summary: The study analyzes whether transformers can perform in-context reinforcement learning by reading trajectory data and adapting their behavior without any weight updates. It focuses on a provable mechanism for policy improvement inside the transformer, showing how the model can infer a learning procedure from past trajectories and use it to choose better actions during context.

extra.full_text: We investigate the ability of transformers to perform in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL), where a model must infer and execute learning algorithms from trajectory data without parameter updates.

title: Unified Framework of Distributional Regret in Multi-Armed Bandits and Reinforcement Learning
summary: A unified treatment connects regret distributions across stochastic multi-armed bandits and episodic reinforcement learning, looking beyond expected regret to how regret varies as a random quantity. The work appears to formalize distributional regret in both settings under one framework, giving researchers a way to reason about tail behavior and risk-sensitive performance rather than only average-case learning efficiency.

extra.comment: Accepted at the Conference of Learning Theory (COLT) 2026
extra.full_text: We study the distribution of regret in stochastic multi-armed bandits and episodic reinforcement learning through a unified framework.

title: Adaptive Q-Chunking for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
summary: Adaptive Q-Chunking targets offline-to-online RL methods that execute actions in chunks, replacing a single fixed chunk length with a state-dependent choice. The idea is to keep the benefits of chunking, such as avoiding multi-step off-policy bias and producing more temporally coherent exploration, while letting the agent adapt how far it commits depending on the situation.

extra.full_text: Offline-to-online reinforcement learning with action chunking eliminates multi-step off-policy bias and enables temporally coherent exploration, but all existing methods use a fixed chunk size across every state.

title: Adaptive Policy Selection and Fine-Tuning under Interaction Budgets for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
summary: Policies are trained offline from previously collected data, then moved into a constrained online fine-tuning phase where interaction budget becomes the central resource. The work focuses on choosing which offline policy to deploy and adapt under that budget, aiming to make offline-to-online reinforcement learning more efficient when real robot or environment interactions are limited.

extra.full_text: In offline-to-online reinforcement learning (O2O-RL), policies are first safely trained offline using previously collected datasets and then further fine-tuned for tasks via limited online interactions.

title: Graph-SND: Sparse Aggregation for Behavioral Diversity in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Graph-SND targets the quadratic cost of System Neural Diversity in multi-agent reinforcement learning, where behavioral heterogeneity is computed by averaging pairwise distances across all agent pairs. It uses sparse aggregation to approximate or replace the full pairwise calculation, aiming to preserve the diversity signal while making SND practical for larger teams.

extra.full_text: System Neural Diversity (SND) measures behavioral heterogeneity in multi-agent reinforcement learning by averaging pairwise distances over all $\binom{n}{2}$ agent pairs, making each call quadratic in team size.

title: RLDX-1 Technical Report
summary: RLDX-1 targets a gap in Vision-Language-Action robot policies: although VLAs inherit broad scene understanding and language following from pretrained VLMs, they still fall short on real-world tasks that need motion awareness, long-term memory, and physical sensing. The technical report appears to frame RLDX-1 as an effort to expand robotic policies beyond language-conditioned perception into richer functional capabilities needed for complex embodied behavior.

extra.full_text: While Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown remarkable progress toward human-like generalist robotic policies through the versatile intelligence (i.e. broad scene understanding and language-conditioned generalization) inherited from pre-trained Vision-Language Models, they still struggle with complex real-world tasks requiring broader functional capabilities (e.g. motion awareness, long-term memory, and physical sensing).

title: A Harmonic Mean Formulation of Average Reward Reinforcement Learning in SMDPs
summary: A harmonic-mean formulation is used to analyze average-reward reinforcement learning for continuing semi-Markov decision processes, where actions can have variable holding times rather than uniform time steps. The framing targets undiscounted infinite-horizon settings and connects average reward optimization to SMDP structure, but the provided text does not give algorithmic details, experiments, or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Recent research has revived and amplified interest in algorithms for undiscounted average reward reinforcement learning in infinite-horizon, non-episodic (continuing) tasks. Semi-Markov decision processes (SMDPs) are of particular interest.

title: Test-Time Training for Visual Foresight Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Visual Foresight VLA models use predicted future visual states to guide robot actions, but this design can break under out-of-distribution visual or task shifts. The paper studies test-time training as a way to adapt VF-VLA models during deployment, aiming to make visual foresight more reliable when the robot encounters conditions that differ from its training data.

extra.full_text: Visual Foresight VLA (VF-VLA) has become a prominent architectural choice in the recent VLA due to its impressive performance. Nevertheless, the inherent design of VF-VLA makes it particularly vulnerable to out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts.

title: Data-dependent Exploration for Online Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
summary: Online RLHF is framed as an exploration problem where an LLM must decide what new preference feedback to collect while it is still being optimized. The work focuses on data-dependent exploration, using the feedback already observed to guide future sampling more efficiently than fixed or uncertainty-agnostic strategies.

extra.full_text: Online reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as a promising paradigm for aligning large language models (LLMs) by continuously collecting new preference feedback during training.

title: PlayWorld: Learning Robot World Models from Autonomous Play
summary: PlayWorld studies action-conditioned video models as robot world models, using data from autonomous play to learn a simulator-like predictor of how robot actions change future observations. The interesting angle is that the model is meant to improve directly from self-collected interaction data, pointing toward robot simulators that become more useful as the robot explores rather than relying only on hand-built physics or curated demonstrations.

extra.full_text: Action-conditioned video models offer a promising path to building general-purpose robot simulators that can improve directly from data.

title: Beyond Penalization: Diffusion-based Out-of-Distribution Detection and Selective Regularization in Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Offline RL often overvalues actions outside the dataset, and this work reframes the problem around explicitly detecting those out-of-distribution actions with a diffusion-based model rather than broadly penalizing anything unfamiliar. The resulting selective regularization aims to suppress genuinely risky extrapolation while preserving useful actions near or just beyond the behavior policy’s support, addressing a common failure mode of conservative offline RL methods.

extra.full_text: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) faces a critical challenge of overestimating the value of out-of-distribution (OOD) actions. Existing methods mitigate this issue by penalizing unseen samples, yet they fail to accurately identify OOD actions and may suppress beneficial exploration beyond the behavioral support.

title: Quantile Geometry Regularization for Distributional Reinforcement Learning
summary: Quantile Geometry Regularization targets a failure mode in quantile-based distributional RL where bootstrapped target quantiles can warp or collapse the learned return distribution. It regularizes the geometry of the quantile estimates during sampled quantile regression, aiming to keep the distributional representation well shaped rather than letting the targets drive degenerate estimates.

extra.full_text: Quantile-based distributional reinforcement learning methods learn return distributions through sampled quantile regression, but their bootstrapped target quantiles may induce distorted or degenerate distribution estimates.

title: OmniUMI: Towards Physically Grounded Robot Learning via Human-Aligned Multimodal Interaction
summary: OmniUMI extends UMI-style robot learning beyond RGB and trajectories by bringing physical interaction signals into the demonstration interface. The aim is more physically grounded imitation from human-aligned multimodal data, giving policies access to cues about contact and interaction that visuomotor-only setups largely miss.

extra.full_text: UMI-style interfaces enable scalable robot learning, but existing systems remain largely visuomotor, relying primarily on RGB observations and trajectory while providing only limited access to physical interaction signals.

title: Quantum Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning via Variational Quantum Circuits
summary: Quantum Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning via Variational Quantum Circuits applies variational quantum circuits to hierarchical reinforcement learning, using quantum function approximators within a temporally abstract decision-making setup. From the provided text, the concrete aim is efficiency and efficacy gains in reinforcement learning by combining HRL’s structured subtask-style control with the representational machinery of quantum circuits.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning is one of the most challenging learning paradigms where efficacy and efficiency gains are extremely valuable. Hierarchical reinforcement learning is a variant that leverages temporal abstraction to structure decision-making.

title: VA-FastNavi-MARL: Real-Time Robot Control with Multimedia-Driven Meta-Reinforcement Learning
summary: VA-FastNavi-MARL aligns asynchronous audio and visual commands into a shared latent representation so a robot controller can respond to heterogeneous multimedia instructions in real time. The interesting part is the combination of multimedia fusion with meta-reinforcement learning, aimed at making navigation/control policies adapt quickly as human commands arrive through different modalities.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME 2026)
extra.full_text: Interpreting dynamic, heterogeneous multimedia commands with real-time responsiveness is critical for Human-Robot Interaction. We present VA-FastNavi-MARL, a framework that aligns asynchronous audio-visual inputs into a unified latent representation.

title: Discovering Reinforcement Learning Interfaces with Large Language Models
summary: Large language models are used to help discover the observation and reward interfaces that reinforcement learning agents need for new environments, reducing the hand-engineering normally required before training can begin. The interesting part is the shift from using LLMs merely as planners or code generators to having them search over the task interface itself, making RL setup more automatic when the right state and reward specification is not obvious.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning systems rely on environment interfaces that specify observations and reward functions, yet constructing these interfaces for new tasks often requires substantial manual effort.

title: Decoupled Guidance Diffusion for Adaptive Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Decoupled Guidance Diffusion targets offline safe RL settings where a deployed policy must adjust to changing cost budgets, either between episodes or mid-episode. It frames policy generation with a diffusion model whose guidance for reward optimization and safety constraint satisfaction is separated, aiming to adapt behavior to the current safety budget without retraining.

extra.full_text: Offline safe reinforcement learning often requires policies to adapt at deployment time to safety budgets that vary across episodes or change within a single episode.

title: Build on Priors: Vision--Language--Guided Neuro-Symbolic Imitation Learning for Data-Efficient Real-World Robot Manipulation
summary: Build on Priors tackles data-efficient learning for real-world, long-horizon robot manipulation by combining vision-language guidance with neuro-symbolic imitation learning. From the available text, the core aim is to let robots acquire complex manipulation behaviors from only a handful of demonstrations, using prior structure rather than relying on large-scale trial data.

extra.full_text: Enabling robots to learn long-horizon manipulation tasks from a handful of demonstrations remains a central challenge in robotics.

title: Beyond Specialization: Robust Reinforcement Learning Navigation via Procedural Map Generators
summary: DRL navigation policies are trained with procedurally generated maps to reduce overfitting to hand-designed environment layouts. The idea is to use automated map diversity as a robustness mechanism, so policies learn navigation behavior that transfers beyond the structural patterns of their training worlds.

extra.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
extra.full_text: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) navigation policies often overfit to the structure of their training environments, as environmental diversity is typically constrained by the manual effort required to design diverse scenarios.

title: Visualizing Critic Match Loss Landscapes for Interpretation of Online Reinforcement Learning Control Algorithms
summary: Visualizes the critic match loss landscape for online reinforcement learning controllers, using the shape of that landscape as an interpretability tool for understanding why performance can degrade when system dynamics shift. The arXiv snippet frames the problem around RL’s dependence on empirical tuning rather than guaranteed robustness, so the concrete value is diagnostic: helping users inspect how the critic’s objective behaves under changing dynamics instead of treating controller performance as a black box.

extra.comment: Published in Acta Astronautica, Vol. 246, pp. 909-920, 2026. DOI:10.1016/j.actaastro.2026.04.045
extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning has proven its power on various occasions. However, its performance is not always guaranteed when system dynamics change. Instead, it largely relies on users' empirical experience.

title: Binary Rewards and Reinforcement Learning: Fundamental Challenges
summary: RLVR with binary verifiable rewards can raise a model’s single-sample reasoning accuracy while making its sampled outputs less diverse, so asking the model multiple times may cover fewer correct solution paths than before training. The paper frames this diversity collapse as a fundamental challenge of binary-reward reinforcement learning, where optimizing for pass/fail outcomes can concentrate probability mass on narrow behaviors even when broader coverage is what downstream reasoning use cases need.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a standard approach for improving reasoning in language models, yet models trained with RLVR often suffer from diversity collapse: while single-sample accuracy improves, multi-sample coverage degrades, sometimes falling below the base model.

title: ShapeGrasp: Simultaneous Visuo-Haptic Shape Completion and Grasping for Improved Robot Manipulation
summary: ShapeGrasp models grasping unfamiliar objects as a loop between vision, touch, and proprioception: it starts from a visual shape estimate, then refines object completion as the robot makes contact and adjusts its grasp. The interesting part is the simultaneous treatment of visuo-haptic shape completion and grasp planning, aiming to make manipulation more robust when the initial visual geometry is incomplete or uncertain.

extra.full_text: Humans grasp unfamiliar objects by combining an initial visual estimate with tactile and proprioceptive feedback during interaction. We present ShapeGrasp, a robotic implementation of this approach.

title: A Meta Reinforcement Learning Approach to Goals-Based Wealth Management
summary: MetaRL pre-trains a meta reinforcement learning policy across thousands of goals-based wealth management problems, borrowing the zero-shot adaptation idea from meta-learning and foundation-model pretraining. The aim is to let the learned policy transfer directly to new client goal configurations or market/planning settings without solving each wealth-management RL problem from scratch.

extra.full_text: Applying concepts related to zero-shot meta-learning and pre-training of foundation models, we develop a meta reinforcement learning approach (denoted MetaRL) that is pre-trained on thousands of goals-based wealth management (GBWM) problems.

title: Diffusion Policy through Conditional Proximal Policy Optimization
summary: Diffusion Policy through Conditional Proximal Policy Optimization appears to connect diffusion-policy style action generation with PPO-style reinforcement learning, targeting decision-making settings such as robotics where policies must produce structured continuous actions. From the provided text alone, the concrete mechanism, benchmarks, and results are not available, so the safest reading is that it explores a reinforcement-learning formulation for training conditional diffusion policies rather than just imitating data.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) has been extensively employed in a wide range of decision-making problems, such as games and robotics.

title: T$^2$PO: Uncertainty-Guided Exploration Control for Stable Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: T$^2$PO is an uncertainty-guided exploration control method for multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning, aimed at keeping reasoning LLMs stable as they interact over several steps. From the title and abstract snippet, it appears to focus on using uncertainty to regulate exploration during RL training, addressing a practical failure mode in interactive tasks where multi-turn learning can become unstable.

extra.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables. Accepted to ICML 2026 as a Spotlight Paper
extra.full_text: Recent progress in multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) has significantly improved reasoning LLMs' performances on complex interactive tasks.

title: Combining Trained Models in Reinforcement Learning
summary: Combining Trained Models in Reinforcement Learning addresses DRL’s sample inefficiency and poor transfer by focusing on how already-trained reinforcement learning models can be reused together rather than training a new agent from scratch. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, so the paper can only be summarized as an approach aimed at improving transfer and reducing sample cost by combining existing trained models.

extra.full_text: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has delivered strong results in domains such as Atari and Go, but it still suffers from high sample cost and weak transfer beyond the training setting.

title: Coopetition-Gym v1: A Formally Grounded Platform for Mixed-Motive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning under Strategic Coopetition
summary: Coopetition-Gym v1 is a benchmark platform for mixed-motive multi-agent reinforcement learning, aimed at settings where agents must navigate both cooperation and competition. It is framed around strategic coopetition, giving researchers a more formal testbed for studying policies in environments where incentives are not purely shared or purely adversarial.

title: Enhancing Multi-Robot Exploration Using Probabilistic Frontier Prioritization with Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixtures
summary: Probabilistic Frontier Prioritization uses Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixtures to help multiple robots decide which exploration frontiers are worth pursuing when communication is limited. The approach targets coordination in settings like search and rescue or environmental monitoring, where robots need to divide coverage intelligently without constant centralized updates.

extra.full_text: Multi-agent autonomous exploration is essential for applications such as environmental monitoring, search and rescue, and industrial-scale surveillance. However, effective coordination under communication constraints remains a significant challenge.

title: Quality-Aware Exploration Budget Allocation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Quality-Aware Exploration Budget Allocation targets the exploration bottleneck in cooperative MARL, where useful joint behaviors are hard to stumble on because the state-action space grows combinatorially across agents. It allocates exploration effort based on the quality of discovered coordination patterns, aiming to spend more budget on promising regions of joint strategy space rather than treating exploration uniformly.

extra.full_text: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) requires agents to discover joint strategies in a combinatorially large state-action space, yet effective coordination configurations are exceedingly rare.

title: Rhythm: Learning Interactive Whole-Body Control for Dual Humanoids
summary: Rhythm targets interactive whole-body control for pairs of humanoid robots, aiming to let dual-humanoid systems coordinate physically in shared environments rather than acting as isolated agents. From the available description, the emphasis is on learning control policies for collaborative, full-body interaction, but no specific training setup, benchmark, or quantitative result is provided.

extra.full_text: Realizing interactive whole-body control for multi-humanoid systems is critical for unlocking complex collaborative capabilities in shared environments.

title: IMR-LLM: Industrial Multi-Robot Task Planning and Program Generation using Large Language Models
summary: IMR-LLM applies large language models to industrial multi-robot coordination, aiming to turn manufacturing task descriptions into robot task plans and executable programs. The emphasis is on moving beyond simple household or single-manipulator settings toward collaborative production scenarios where several robots must divide and sequence complex work.

extra.full_text: In modern industrial production, multiple robots often collaborate to complete complex manufacturing tasks. Large language models (LLMs), with their strong reasoning capabilities, have shown potential in coordinating robots for simple household and manipulation tasks.

title: 3-D Relative Localization for Multi-Robot Systems with Angle and Self-Displacement Measurements
summary: 3-D Relative Localization for Multi-Robot Systems with Angle and Self-Displacement Measurements studies how a team of robots can estimate their relative positions using only local inter-robot angle observations and each robot’s own displacement measurements. The focus is on making relative localization work under measurement noise, where reconstructing consistent 3D geometry from limited local sensing is especially difficult.

extra.full_text: Realizing relative localization by leveraging inter-robot local measurements is a challenging problem, especially in the presence of measurement noise.

title: Rethinking Camera Choice: An Empirical Study on Fisheye Camera Properties in Robotic Manipulation
summary: An empirical study examines how fisheye camera properties affect policy learning in robotic manipulation, focusing on the tradeoff introduced by their very wide field of view. Rather than treating fisheye sensing as a straightforward upgrade over conventional cameras, it frames camera choice as a downstream learning problem where distortion, coverage, and visual context can change manipulation performance.

extra.full_text: The adoption of fisheye cameras in robotic manipulation, driven by their exceptionally wide Field of View (FoV), is rapidly outpacing a systematic understanding of their downstream effects on policy learning.

title: BAT: Balancing Agility and Stability via Online Policy Switching for Long-Horizon Whole-Body Humanoid Control
summary: BAT targets long-horizon whole-body humanoid control by switching online between policies that favor agility and policies that favor stability. The idea is to avoid forcing one controller to cover fast, precise, and robust behavior all at once, instead adapting the control mode over time as the task demands change.

extra.full_text: Despite recent advances in control, reinforcement learning, and imitation learning, developing a unified framework that can achieve agile, precise, and robust whole-body behaviors, particularly in long-horizon tasks, remains challenging.

title: Learning Humanoid Navigation from Human Data
summary: EgoNav trains a humanoid navigation system entirely from 5 hours of human walking data, using egocentric experience rather than robot demonstrations or finetuning. The result is a policy intended to transfer directly to a humanoid robot and traverse diverse, previously unseen environments, making the interesting point that useful humanoid navigation behavior can be learned from a small amount of human data alone.

extra.full_text: We present EgoNav, a system that enables a humanoid robot to traverse diverse, unseen environments by learning entirely from 5 hours of human walking data, with no robot data or finetuning.

title: Long-Reach Robotic Manipulation for Assembly and Outfitting of Lunar Structures
summary: Lunar construction robots will need to move and route cables over large structures while still doing precise manipulation at contact points, which makes long-reach assembly and outfitting a central autonomy problem. The work focuses on robotic manipulation methods for transporting, positioning, and finely handling electrical cabling in lunar surface infrastructure, where build-site robots may need to operate with limited or no direct human control.

extra.comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, to appear in the proceedings of iSpaRo 2025
extra.full_text: Future infrastructure construction on the lunar surface will require semi- or fully-autonomous operation from robots deployed at the build site. In particular, tasks such as electrical outfitting necessitate transport, routing, and fine manipulation of cables across large structures.

title: Which Reconstruction Model Should a Robot Use? Routing Image-to-3D Models for Cost-Aware Robotic Manipulation
summary: Robotic manipulation systems often do not need the same 3D reconstruction fidelity for every downstream action: a dexterous grasp may require detailed surfaces, while motion planning can work with a rougher mesh. This paper frames image-to-3D model choice as a routing problem, selecting reconstruction models by task needs and cost so robots avoid spending compute on unnecessarily high-fidelity geometry.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 7 tables, 3 figures. Supplementary material included. Project page: https://scout-model-routing.github.io
extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation tasks require 3D mesh reconstructions of varying quality: dexterous manipulation demands fine-grained surface detail, while collision-free planning tolerates coarser representations.

title: Robotic Dexterous Manipulation via Anisotropic Friction Modulation using Passive Rollers
summary: A robotic fingertip uses passive rollers that can be selectively braked or pivoted to change the friction and constraint directions at the contact point. By mechanically modulating anisotropic friction rather than relying only on force control, the design gives a hand more direct ways to regulate slip, rolling, and contact constraints during dexterous manipulation.

extra.comment: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics & Automation
extra.full_text: Controlling friction at the fingertip is fundamental to dexterous manipulation, yet remains difficult to realize in robotic hands. We present the design and analysis of a robotic fingertip equipped with passive rollers that can be selectively braked or pivoted to modulate contact friction and constraint directions.

title: ABot-PhysWorld: Interactive World Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation with Physics Alignment
summary: ABot-PhysWorld targets the gap between visually plausible robot videos and physically valid manipulation by aligning an interactive world foundation model with physics constraints. It is aimed at preventing common video-world-model failures like object penetration and anti-gravity motion, making the generated rollouts more useful for embodied simulation and planning.

extra.full_text: Video-based world models offer a powerful paradigm for embodied simulation and planning, yet state-of-the-art models often generate physically implausible manipulations - such as object penetration and anti-gravity motion - due to training on generic visual data and likelihood-based objectives that ignore physical laws.

title: Chasing Autonomy: Dynamic Retargeting and Control Guided RL for Performant and Controllable Humanoid Running
summary: Dynamic retargeting and control-guided reinforcement learning are used to train humanoid running controllers that are both fast and steerable. The focus is on closing the gap between dynamic, human-like running performance and practical controllability, rather than producing a policy that only works for a fixed gait or direction.

extra.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
extra.full_text: Humanoid robots have the promise of locomoting like humans, including fast and dynamic running.

title: MolmoB0T: Large-Scale Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation
summary: MolmoB0T argues that large-scale simulation can be enough for robot manipulation without real-world data collection or task-specific fine-tuning. It targets zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, challenging the usual assumption that physical data is necessary to bridge the gap between simulated training and deployment on real robots.

extra.full_text: A prevailing view in robot learning is that simulation alone is not enough; effective sim-to-real transfer is widely believed to require at least some real-world data collection or task-specific fine-tuning to bridge the gap between simulated and physical environments. We challenge that assumption.

title: Chameleon: Episodic Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
summary: Chameleon targets long-horizon robotic manipulation settings where the current camera view is not enough, because occlusions or earlier state changes can make identical observations require different actions. It frames the problem around episodic memory: using interaction history to disambiguate perceptually aliased states so a manipulation policy can choose actions based on what has happened, not just what it sees now.

extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation often requires memory: occlusion and state changes can make decision-time observations perceptually aliased, making action selection non-Markovian at the observation level because the same observation may arise from different interaction histories.

title: Decentralized End-to-End Multi-AAV Pursuit Using Predictive Spatio-Temporal Observation via Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Decentralized End-to-End Multi-AAV Pursuit targets aerial swarms chasing targets through clutter when each agent has only partial, noisy observations rather than clean ground-truth state. It frames pursuit as a deep reinforcement learning problem built around predictive spatio-temporal observation, so agents can coordinate from perception-level cues and anticipate target motion instead of relying on hand-crafted geometric abstractions.

extra.full_text: Decentralized cooperative pursuit in cluttered environments is challenging for autonomous aerial swarms, especially under partial and noisy perception. Existing methods often rely on abstracted geometric features or privileged ground-truth states, and therefore sidestep perceptual uncertainty in real-world settings.

title: EVA: Aligning Video World Models with Executable Robot Actions via Inverse Dynamics Rewards
summary: EVA treats a video generative model as a robot world model, but aligns its imagined rollouts with actions the robot can actually execute by scoring generated videos through an inverse dynamics model. The idea is to use inverse-dynamics rewards to push future-frame generation toward trajectories that are not just visually plausible, but recoverable as concrete robot commands for the downstream controller.

extra.full_text: Video generative models are increasingly used as world models for robotics, where a model generates a future visual rollout conditioned on the current observation and task instruction, and an inverse dynamics model (IDM) converts the generated frames into executable robot actions.

title: A Bayesian Reasoning Framework for Robotic Systems in Autonomous Casualty Triage
summary: Autonomous casualty-triage robots are framed as Bayesian decision-makers that must reason under uncertainty when sensor observations are noisy, missing, or ambiguous. The approach is aimed at mass-casualty settings where robots need to combine imperfect perceptual evidence into defensible triage decisions rather than treating raw detections as reliable facts.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
extra.full_text: Autonomous robots deployed in mass casualty incidents (MCI) face the challenge of making critical decisions based on incomplete and noisy perceptual data.

title: CorridorVLA: Explicit Spatial Constraints for Generative Action Heads via Sparse Anchors
summary: CorridorVLA adds explicit spatial structure to VLA action generation by using sparse anchors as constraints, rather than relying only on latent multimodal features to guide continuous control. The idea is to give the generative action head a more concrete notion of where actions should pass or remain feasible in space, which is especially relevant for robot policies operating in constrained environments such as corridors or narrow passages.

extra.full_text: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models often use intermediate representations to connect multimodal inputs with continuous control, yet spatial guidance is often injected implicitly through latent features.

title: Learning Safe-Stoppability Monitors for Humanoid Robots
summary: Emergency stop (E-stop) mechanisms are the de facto standard for robot safety.

title: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy of Reinforcement Learning-Model Predictive Control Integration for Linear Systems
summary: A systematic review organizes how reinforcement learning has been combined with model predictive control for linear systems, focusing on constrained decision-making and adaptive control. It frames RL-MPC integration as a taxonomy rather than a single algorithm, helping distinguish where learning enters the MPC loop and how these hybrids handle constraints, model uncertainty, or performance improvement.

extra.full_text: The integration of Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for constrained decision-making and adaptive control.

title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
summary: Cortex 2.0 targets long-horizon industrial manipulation by grounding robot world models in real deployment rather than relying only on reactive Vision-Language-Action behavior. From the provided excerpt, the interesting shift is toward execution that can stay reliable across robot embodiments, task sequences, and changing object distributions, though the text does not give enough detail to name the exact mechanism or results.

extra.full_text: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive.

title: Evolvable Embodied Agent for Robotic Manipulation via Long Short-Term Reflection and Optimization
summary: Evolvable Embodied Agent targets robotic manipulation by letting a robot adapt through environmental feedback rather than relying only on heavy pretraining or fixed task policies. Its long- and short-term reflection plus optimization loop is meant to improve cross-task generalization while keeping the adaptation process more interpretable than typical end-to-end methods.

extra.comment: This work has been accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN 2026)
extra.full_text: Achieving general-purpose robotics requires empowering robots to adapt and evolve based on their environment and feedback. Traditional methods face limitations such as extensive training requirements, difficulties in cross-task generalization, and lack of interpretability.

title: DiT4DiT: Jointly Modeling Video Dynamics and Actions for Generalizable Robot Control
summary: DiT4DiT targets a weakness in current vision-language-action robot models: they often inherit static image-text representations and then try to learn physical dynamics from much smaller robot action datasets. It frames robot control around jointly modeling video dynamics and actions, aiming to give the policy a more explicit handle on how scenes evolve under actions so it can generalize better beyond the demonstrations it was trained on.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot learning, but their representations are still largely inherited from static image-text pretraining, leaving physical dynamics to be learned from comparatively limited action data.

title: Cortical Policy: A Dual-Stream View Transformer for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Cortical Policy is a view-transformer policy for robotic manipulation that tries to fix the static, view-specific representations common in multi-view action prediction. It uses a dual-stream design to improve 3D spatial reasoning while adapting visual features dynamically across views, aiming to make manipulation policies less brittle when interpreting multi-camera observations.

extra.comment: Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026. 10 pages, 4 figures. Appendix included
extra.full_text: View transformers process multi-view observations to predict actions and have shown impressive performance in robotic manipulation. Existing methods typically extract static visual representations in a view-specific manner, leading to inadequate 3D spatial reasoning ability and a lack of dynamic adaptation.

title: StageCraft: Execution Aware Mitigation of Distractor and Obstruction Failures in VLA Models
summary: StageCraft targets failure modes in vision-language-action robot policies where distractor objects or physical obstructions derail execution. From the title and abstract fragment, it appears to make mitigation execution-aware, using what is happening during the robot’s rollout rather than relying only on broad pretraining over language, images, and demonstrations.

extra.full_text: Large scale pre-training on text and image data along with diverse robot demonstrations has helped Vision Language Action models (VLAs) to generalize to novel tasks, objects and scenes.

title: Efficient and Reliable Teleoperation through Real-to-Sim-to-Real Shared Autonomy
summary: Real-to-Sim-to-Real Shared Autonomy targets the bottleneck in fine-grained, contact-rich teleoperation, where even skilled operators struggle with slow and unreliable manipulation. The idea is to use a shared-autonomy loop grounded in real-to-sim-to-real transfer so the robot can take on parts of the contact-sensitive control burden while still letting the human guide the task.

extra.full_text: Fine-grained, contact-rich teleoperation remains slow, error-prone, and unreliable in real-world manipulation tasks, even for experienced operators.

title: Articulated-Body Dynamics Network: Dynamics-Grounded Prior for Robot Learning
summary: Articulated-Body Dynamics Network builds a policy prior around the physical structure of articulated robots, using link connectivity as an inductive bias rather than treating the robot as an unstructured control problem. The aim is to improve reinforcement-learning efficiency by grounding the network architecture in articulated-body dynamics, so learned policies can better exploit the kinematic and dynamic relationships between connected links.

extra.full_text: Recent work in reinforcement learning has shown that incorporating structural priors for articulated robots, such as link connectivity, into policy networks improves learning efficiency.

title: Speculative Policy Orchestration: A Latency-Resilient Framework for Cloud-Robotic Manipulation
summary: Speculative Policy Orchestration targets the latency problem in cloud-robotic manipulation by keeping execution from stalling when remote planning or reasoning is delayed. It appears to orchestrate speculative control policies so the robot can continue high-frequency manipulation despite network jitter, aiming to avoid command starvation and unsafe physical behavior.

extra.full_text: Cloud robotics enables robots to offload high-dimensional motion planning and reasoning to remote servers. However, for continuous manipulation tasks requiring high-frequency control, network latency and jitter can severely destabilize the system, causing command starvation and unsafe physical execution.

title: XRZero-G0: Pushing the Frontier of Dexterous Robotic Manipulation with Interfaces, Quality and Ratios
summary: XRZero-G0 focuses on the data bottleneck behind dexterous robot manipulation foundation models: getting high-quality demonstrations that are tightly aligned with robot actions. It appears to emphasize better operator interfaces, demonstration quality, and data-ratio choices as levers for scaling manipulation performance, but the provided text does not include enough detail to name the exact system design, benchmarks, or results.

extra.full_text: The acquisition of high-quality, action-aligned demonstration data remains a fundamental bottleneck in scaling foundation models for dexterous robot manipulation.

title: Agile Interception of a Flying Target using Competitive Reinforcement Learning
summary: Agile drone interception is cast as a two-player reinforcement learning problem, with one PPO-trained policy controlling a net-carrying interceptor and another controlling the evasive target. The setup is interesting because the target is not a scripted trajectory but a competing learned agent, so the interceptor has to develop pursuit behavior against an adaptive, agile opponent rather than overfitting to fixed maneuvers.

extra.full_text: This article presents a solution to intercept an agile drone by another agile drone carrying a catching net. We formulate the interception as a Competitive Reinforcement Learning problem, where the interceptor and the target drone are controlled by separate policies trained with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO).

title: Imperfect World Models are Exploitable
summary: Imperfect world models can mis-rank policies in a way that makes planning actively exploitable: the model says one policy is better while the real environment would prefer another. The paper formalizes this failure mode as an analogue of reward hacking, proves that exploitation is essentially unavoidable over large policy sets, and shows a sharper negative result than in finite reward hacking: the usual conditions that can guarantee unhackability do not have an equivalent protection against model exploitation. It then weakens the notion of exploitation to derive a safe planning horizon, clarifying when world-model planning can be trusted before model error becomes strategically dangerous.

extra.full_text: We propose a novel definition of model exploitation in reinforcement learning. Informally, a world model is exploitable if it implies that one policy should be strictly preferred over another while the environment's true transition model implies the reverse. We analogize our definition with a prior characterization of reward hacking but show that the associated proof of inevitability does not transfer to exploitation. To overcome this obstruction, we develop a general theory of reward hacking and model exploitation that proves that exploitation is essentially unavoidable on large policy sets and yields the corresponding claim for hacking as a special case. Unfortunately, we also find that the conditions that guarantee unhackability in finite policy sets have no counterpart that precludes exploitation. Consequently, we introduce a relaxed notion of exploitation and derive a safe horizon within which it can be avoided. Taken together, our results establish a formal bridge between reward hacking and model exploitation and elucidate the limits of safe planning in world models.

title: KiRAS: Keyframe Guided Self-Imitation for Robust and Adaptive Skill Learning in Quadruped Robots
summary: KiRAS trains a single quadruped control policy to learn multiple skills from skill-specific demonstrations, using keyframes to guide self-imitation and make learning more robust. From the available abstract text, the core idea is to combine reinforcement learning and imitation learning so the robot can adaptively reproduce diverse locomotion or behavior skills within one policy rather than training separate controllers.

extra.comment: Received by 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
extra.full_text: With advances in reinforcement learning and imitation learning, quadruped robots can acquire diverse skills within a single policy by imitating multiple skill-specific datasets.

title: Confusion-Aware In-Context-Learning for Vision-Language Models in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Confusion-Aware In-Context-Learning targets a common failure mode in VLM-based robot manipulation: objects that look or sound similar enough to trigger brittle, unpredictable choices. The method appears to make the in-context examples or prompting process explicitly aware of likely confusions, aiming to improve robustness when a robot must distinguish among confusable objects.

extra.comment: Accepted by the 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD 2026)
extra.full_text: Vision-language models (VLMs) have significantly improved the generalization capabilities of robotic manipulation. However, VLM-based systems often suffer from a lack of robustness, leading to unpredictable errors, particularly in scenarios involving confusable objects.

title: Chain of Uncertain Rewards with Large Language Models for Reinforcement Learning
summary: Chain of Uncertain Rewards uses large language models to help construct reward functions for reinforcement learning, targeting the tedious and often inconsistent process of hand-designing rewards. From the available text, the core idea is to bring LLM reasoning into reward design so RL agents can receive more effective training signals, but no concrete mechanism, benchmark, or result is provided.

extra.full_text: Designing effective reward functions is a cornerstone of reinforcement learning (RL), yet it remains a challenging and labor-intensive process due to the inefficiencies and inconsistencies inherent in traditional methods.

title: A Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Action Tokenizer for In-Context Imitation Learning in Robotics
summary: A hierarchical spatiotemporal action tokenizer is used to turn robot action trajectories into discrete tokens for in-context imitation learning. Its mechanism is two-stage vector quantization, suggesting a coarse-to-fine representation of actions that can preserve temporal and spatial structure while making demonstrations easier for a sequence model to condition on.

extra.full_text: We present a novel hierarchical spatiotemporal action tokenizer for in-context imitation learning. We first propose a hierarchical approach, which consists of two successive levels of vector quantization.

title: Diffusion Policy for Coordinated Control of a Nonholonomic Mobile Base and Dual Arms in Door Opening and Passing
summary: Diffusion Policy is used to coordinate a nonholonomic mobile base with two robot arms for the full sequence of opening and passing through a heavy, self-closing pull door. The setup targets the kind of bimanual, whole-body behavior humans use naturally: turning the handle, widening and holding the gap, switching arms when needed, and moving the base through while maintaining clearance.

extra.full_text: Opening heavy, self closing doors, especially those that require pulling remains a long standing challenge in robotics. Humans naturally employ both arms in a dexterous manner, rotating the handle, widening the gap, holding the door, switching arms when needed, and moving through while maintaining clearance.

title: EARL: Towards a Unified Analysis-Guided Reinforcement Learning Framework for Egocentric Interaction Reasoning and Pixel Grounding
summary: EARL targets egocentric interaction understanding for assistive robots and embodied agents, combining analysis-guided reinforcement learning with multimodal language models to improve both high-level reasoning about human-environment interactions and fine-grained pixel grounding. The provided text frames it as a unified framework for cases where current MLLMs can talk about first-person scenes but still fail to localize and reason accurately enough for reliable embodied interaction.

extra.comment: Accepted at ICML 2026. Project page: https://github.com/yuggiehk/EARL
extra.full_text: Understanding human--environment interactions from egocentric vision is essential for assistive robotics and embodied intelligent agents, yet existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs) still struggle with accurate interaction reasoning and fine-grained pixel grounding.

title: ToMPC: Task-oriented Model Predictive Control via ADMM for Safe Robotic Manipulation
summary: ToMPC formulates safe robotic manipulation as a task-oriented model predictive control problem, using ADMM to coordinate collision-free motion with contact-rich robot-environment interaction. The goal is to let a robot operate efficiently in open workspaces where it must both avoid obstacles and intentionally interact with surrounding objects or surfaces, rather than treating motion planning and interaction control as separate problems.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 10 figures, accepted by IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RAL)
extra.full_text: This paper proposes a task-oriented model predictive control (ToMPC) framework for safe and efficient robotic manipulation in open workspaces. The framework unifies collision-free motion and robot-environment interaction to address diverse scenarios.

title: WM-DAgger: Enabling Efficient Data Aggregation for Imitation Learning with World Models
summary: WM-DAgger targets the compounding-error problem in robotic imitation learning, where small mistakes push a policy into out-of-distribution states that were never covered by demonstrations. It uses world models to make data aggregation more efficient, aiming to expose and correct those failure-prone states without relying only on costly real-world rollouts.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning is a powerful paradigm for training robotic policies, yet its performance is limited by compounding errors: minor policy inaccuracies could drive robots into unseen out-of-distribution (OOD) states in the training set, where the policy could generate even bigger errors, leading to eventual failures.

title: 3D-Anchored Lookahead Planning for Persistent Robotic Scene Memory via World-Model-Based MCTS
summary: 3D-ALP is a planning engine for robotic manipulation that uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to reason ahead while grounding rollouts in a 3D-consistent world model. The interesting piece is the persistent scene memory: the planner can evaluate candidate actions against a spatially anchored model of the environment rather than relying only on immediate observations or short-horizon predictions.

extra.full_text: We present 3D-Anchored Lookahead Planning (3D-ALP), a System 2 reasoning engine for robotic manipulation that combines Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with a 3D-consistent world model as the rollout oracle.

title: Diffusion Reinforcement Learning Based Online 3D Bin Packing Spatial Strategy Optimization
summary: Diffusion Reinforcement Learning Based Online 3D Bin Packing Spatial Strategy Optimization applies diffusion-based reinforcement learning to online 3D bin packing, targeting the sample-efficiency problems that make standard DRL hard to use in logistics, warehousing, and intelligent manufacturing settings. The approach optimizes spatial placement strategies as items arrive, aiming to make learned packing policies more practical for dynamic packing scenarios where decisions must be made sequentially.

extra.comment: 8 pages, double-column. Jie Han and Tong Li contributed equally to this work. Qingyang Xu is the corresponding author
extra.full_text: The online 3D bin packing problem is important in logistics, warehousing and intelligent manufacturing, with solutions shifting to deep reinforcement learning (DRL) which faces challenges like low sample efficiency.

title: The Unified Autonomy Stack: Toward a Blueprint for Generalizable Robot Autonomy
summary: The Unified Autonomy Stack is an open-source, system-level autonomy stack designed to run resiliently across both aerial and ground robots with different morphologies. From the available abstract text, its value is mainly as a proposed blueprint for generalizable robot autonomy rather than a single task-specific planner or controller.

extra.full_text: We introduce and open-source the Unified Autonomy Stack, a system-level solution that enables resilient autonomy across diverse aerial and ground robot morphologies.

title: SI-Diff: A Framework for Learning Search and High-Precision Insertion with a Force-Domain Diffusion Policy
summary: SI-Diff tackles contact-rich robotic assembly by learning both the search phase and the final high-precision insertion under pose uncertainty, with the policy operating in the force domain rather than only from geometric or visual cues. It is aimed at tasks like peg-in-hole insertion where tiny clearances and misalignment make open-loop motion brittle, using a diffusion-policy formulation to produce compliant, contact-aware behavior.

extra.full_text: Contact-rich assembly is fundamental in robotics but poses significant challenges due to uncertainties in relative poses, such as misalignments and small clearances in peg-in-hole tasks.

title: Route Fragmentation Based on Resource-centric Prioritisation for Efficient Multi-Robot Path Planning in Agricultural Environments
summary: Route Fragmentation Based on Resource-centric Prioritisation targets multi-robot path planning in farms, where many robots repeatedly encounter tight, spatially dense bottlenecks such as crop rows, gates, or narrow passages. It frames planning around fragmented route segments and prioritizes shared navigation resources so robots can coordinate more efficiently through those constrained areas during long-horizon agricultural operations.

extra.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
extra.full_text: Agricultural environments present high proportions of spatially dense navigation bottlenecks for long-term navigation and operational planning of agricultural mobile robots.

title: Language-Grounded Decoupled Action Representation for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Language-Grounded Decoupled Action Representation targets the mismatch between vision-language reasoning and the continuous control signals needed for robotic manipulation. It frames the problem as separating high-level, language-grounded action understanding from low-level execution, giving the robot an intermediate action representation that can connect semantic task intent to motor control more cleanly.

extra.full_text: The heterogeneity between high-level vision-language understanding and low-level action control remains a fundamental challenge in robotic manipulation.

title: CoRAL: Contact-Rich Adaptive LLM-based Control for Robotic Manipulation
summary: CoRAL targets the gap between LLM/VLM semantic reasoning and the low-level physical adaptation needed for contact-rich manipulation. It uses language-model guidance as part of an adaptive control loop, aiming to let robots adjust during tasks where force, contact, and changing interaction dynamics matter rather than relying only on high-level plans.

extra.comment: 22 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables. Accepted to Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2026. Updated to camera-ready version with appendix and text/formatting revisions
extra.full_text: While Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities in high-level reasoning and semantic understanding, applying them directly to contact-rich manipulation remains a challenge due to their lack of explicit physical grounding and inability to perform adaptive control.

title: PVI: Plug-in Visual Injection for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: PVI targets VLA systems built from a pretrained vision-language model plus a flow-matching action expert, adding a plug-in visual injection mechanism for language-conditioned manipulation. From the provided text, the concrete result is simply that this sits within a now-strong VLA paradigm; no benchmark, dataset, or performance numbers are given.

extra.full_text: VLA architectures that pair a pretrained VLM with a flow-matching action expert have emerged as a strong paradigm for language-conditioned manipulation.

title: Decentralized Cooperative Localization for Multi-Robot Systems with Asynchronous Sensor Fusion
summary: Decentralized cooperative localization is applied to teams of nonholonomic mobile robots working without GPS and with limited communication, using asynchronous sensor fusion so robots can share localization information without relying on a central estimator or synchronized updates. The setup is aimed at making multi-robot localization more robust in realistic field conditions where measurements, messages, and robot motion updates arrive at different times.

extra.comment: Presented at the 13th RSI International Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics (ICRoM 2025)
extra.full_text: Decentralized cooperative localization (DCL) is a promising approach for nonholonomic mobile robots operating in GPS-denied environments with limited communication infrastructure.

title: Learning Visuomotor Policy for Multi-Robot Laser Tag Game
summary: Multi-robot laser tag is framed as a practical visuomotor control problem where robots must act under limited observability without depending on explicit depth maps or inter-robot communication. The paper studies learning a policy directly for this shooting-game-style setting, targeting the failure modes of classic modular pipelines in dynamic multi-robot interactions.

extra.full_text: In this paper, we study multi robot laser tag, a simplified yet practical shooting-game-style task. Classic modular approaches on these tasks face challenges such as limited observability and reliance on depth mapping and inter robot communication.

title: Device-Conditioned Neural Architecture Search for Efficient Robotic Manipulation
summary: Device-Conditioned Neural Architecture Search targets the mismatch between increasingly heavy visuomotor policies and the very different compute limits of real robot hardware. From the provided text, the work appears to search for manipulation policy architectures conditioned on deployment-device constraints, aiming to make robotic manipulation models more efficient on heterogeneous platforms.

extra.full_text: The growing complexity of visuomotor policies poses significant challenges for deployment with heterogeneous robotic hardware constraints.

title: RADAR: Closed-Loop Robotic Data Generation via Semantic Planning and Autonomous Causal Environment Reset
summary: RADAR targets the data bottleneck in robot learning by closing the loop around physical interaction collection: it uses semantic planning to generate useful robot behaviors and autonomously resets the environment through causal reasoning instead of relying on humans to stage each trial. The interesting piece is the reset mechanism, which treats recovery as part of the data-generation process, making large-scale interaction collection more scalable for settings where manual intervention would otherwise dominate cost and throughput.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
extra.full_text: The acquisition of large-scale physical interaction data, a critical prerequisite for modern robot learning, is severely bottlenecked by the prohibitive cost and scalability limits of human-in-the-loop collection paradigms.

title: Hyperbolic Multiview Pretraining for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Hyperbolic Multiview Pretraining for Robotic Manipulation argues that 3D-aware robot vision pretraining can benefit from moving embeddings out of flat Euclidean space and into hyperbolic geometry, where hierarchical and structural relationships among multiview observations may be represented more naturally. extra.full_text: While Isaac Lab provides massive parallel UAV simulation, OmniSafe and safe-control-gym provide constrained-RL benchmarks, and CBFKit provides control-barrier-function synthesis tooling, no existing framework unifies these capabilities for end-to-end safety-constrained training.

title: A Loss Landscape Visualization Framework for Interpreting Reinforcement Learning: An ADHDP Case Study
