summary: Reinforcement learning for control is examined through loss landscape visualization, using adaptive dynamic heuristic dynamic programming (ADHDP) as the case study. The work extends the authors’ earlier critic match loss landscape method to make critic training behavior more interpretable, giving researchers a way to inspect how the learned value approximation evolves rather than treating the controller as a black box.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning algorithms have been widely used in dynamic and control systems. However, interpreting their internal learning behavior remains a challenge. In the authors' previous work, a critic match loss landscape visualization method was proposed to study critic training.

title: Adapting Critic Match Loss Landscape Visualization to Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
summary: Extends critic match loss landscape visualization from online RL to off-policy reinforcement learning, using it to inspect the optimization geometry of critic learning under replay-based training. The result is a diagnostic view of how off-policy critics behave during optimization, aimed at making failure modes and learning dynamics more visible than scalar losses alone.

extra.full_text: This work extends an established critic match loss landscape visualization method from online to off-policy reinforcement learning (RL), aiming to reveal the optimization geometry behind critic learning.

title: Energy-Efficient Quadruped Locomotion with Compliant Feet
summary: Quadruped robots typically use rigid feet for simpler control and stable contact, but this paper explores compliant feet as a way to absorb impacts and recycle elastic energy during locomotion. The interesting mechanism is shifting some of the work normally handled by active control and motors into passive foot compliance, with the goal of reducing energy use while preserving effective gait stability.

extra.comment: 29 pages, 7 figures, supplemental videos link is mentioned in the paper
extra.full_text: Quadruped robots are often designed with rigid feet to simplify control and maintain stable contact during locomotion. While this approach is straightforward, it limits the ability of the legs to absorb impact forces and reuse stored elastic energy, leading to higher energy expenditure during locomotion.

title: LineMaster Pro: A Low-Cost Intelligent Line Following Robot with PID Control and Ultrasonic Obstacle Avoidance for Educational Robotics
summary: LineMaster Pro is an educational line-following robot designed to be much cheaper than typical $150-300 commercial kits while adding practical obstacle detection. It combines PID-based line tracking with ultrasonic obstacle avoidance, making it a more complete classroom platform for teaching control and sensing in mobile robotics.
authors: A. S. M. Ahsanul Sarkar Akib

extra.full_text: Line following robots are fundamental platforms in robotics education, yet commercially available solutions remain prohibitively expensive ($150-300$) while lacking integrated obstacle detection capabilities essential for real-world applications.

title: ScoRe-Flow: Complete Distributional Control via Score-Based Reinforcement Learning for Flow Matching
summary: ScoRe-Flow targets robotic policies built with Flow Matching by adding score-based reinforcement learning to control the full action distribution rather than only fitting demonstrations or optimizing sampled actions. From the provided text, the concrete claim is that FM policies already give fast, expressive action generation for embodied AI, and ScoRe-Flow appears to use that backbone to make distributional control more complete and trainable under RL.

extra.full_text: Flow Matching (FM) policies have emerged as an efficient backbone for robotic control, offering fast and expressive action generation that underpins recent large-scale embodied AI systems.

title: LIDEA: Human-to-Robot Imitation Learning via Implicit Feature Distillation and Explicit Geometry Alignment
summary: LIDEA targets the embodiment gap in learning robot manipulation from human videos by combining implicit feature distillation with explicit geometry alignment between human hands and robot arms. The setup is aimed at turning abundant human interaction footage into usable robot demonstrations, addressing the data bottleneck that limits scaling imitation learning beyond carefully collected robot trajectories.

extra.full_text: Scaling up robot learning is hindered by the scarcity of robotic demonstrations, whereas human videos offer a vast, untapped source of interaction data. However, bridging the embodiment gap between human hands and robot arms remains a critical challenge.

title: SmoothTurn: Learning to Turn Smoothly for Agile Navigation with Quadrupedal Robots
summary: SmoothTurn targets high-speed quadruped navigation where sharp direction changes can destabilize the robot, focusing on learning turning behaviors that stay smooth while preserving agility. It frames smooth turning as a locomotion capability for urgent real-world settings like rescue or inspection, where a quadruped must keep running fast while redirecting its path rather than slowing down for careful maneuvers.

extra.full_text: Quadrupedal robots show great potential for valuable real-world applications such as fire rescue and industrial inspection. Such applications often require urgency and the ability to navigate agilely, which in turn demands the capability to change directions smoothly while running in high speed.

title: NavOL: Navigation Policy with Online Imitation Learning
summary: NavOL targets robust robot navigation by replacing purely offline imitation with online imitation learning, so the policy can correct the distribution shift and compounding rollout errors that usually appear after deployment. The setup is positioned as an alternative to reinforcement learning for navigation, avoiding hand-designed rewards while aiming for more efficient policy learning.

extra.full_text: Learning robust navigation policies remains a core challenge in robotics. Offline imitation learning suffers from distribution shift and compounding errors at rollout, while reinforcement learning requires reward engineering and learns inefficiently.

title: Autonomous Integration and Improvement of Robotic Assembly using Skill Graph Representations
summary: Autonomous Integration and Improvement of Robotic Assembly using Skill Graph Representations targets the manual bottleneck in deploying robotic assembly systems by representing assembly know-how as skill graphs that can be integrated, adapted, and refined over time. The available text only states the motivation, so the safest summary is that it aims to let robots bring new assembly tasks and changing environments into an existing system with less hand engineering while improving execution performance through structured skill reuse.

extra.full_text: Robotic assembly systems traditionally require substantial manual engineering effort to integrate new tasks, adapt to new environments, and improve performance over time.

title: RAPID: Redundancy-Aware and Compatibility-Optimal Edge-Cloud Partitioned Inference for Diverse VLA Models
summary: RAPID targets the inference bottleneck in Vision-Language-Action models by splitting computation between an edge robot and the cloud, aiming to preserve real-time behavior without forcing all processing onto limited onboard hardware. Its focus is on making that partition redundancy-aware and compatibility-optimal across diverse VLA architectures, so the edge-cloud split can reduce repeated computation while still fitting the model’s structure.

extra.full_text: Vision Language Action (VLA) models are mainstream in embodied intelligence but face high inference costs. Edge-Cloud Collaborative (ECC) inference offers an effective fix by easing edge-device computing pressure to meet real-time needs.

title: MAVEN: A Meta-Reinforcement Learning Framework for Varying-Dynamics Expertise in Agile Quadrotor Maneuvers
summary: MAVEN targets agile quadrotor control under changing dynamics, where standard RL policies tend to break when the vehicle or environment shifts away from training conditions. It uses a meta-reinforcement learning setup to build varying-dynamics expertise, aiming for policies that can adapt online rather than memorizing one fixed dynamics regime.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for achieving online agile navigation with quadrotors. Despite this success, policies trained via standard RL typically fail to generalize across significant dynamic variations, exhibiting a critical lack of adaptability.

title: Few-Shot Adaptation to Non-Stationary Environments via Latent Trend Embedding for Robotics
summary: Few-Shot Adaptation to Non-Stationary Environments via Latent Trend Embedding targets concept shift in robotics, where a controller’s input-output mapping changes because of hidden environmental factors. From the provided abstract fragment, it appears to model those unobserved changes through a latent trend embedding so a robot can adapt with only a few examples as conditions drift.

extra.full_text: Robotic systems operating in real-world environments often suffer from concept shift, where the input-output relationship changes due to latent environmental factors that are not directly observable.

title: Hierarchical Task Model Predictive Control for Sequential Mobile Manipulation Tasks
summary: Hierarchical Task Model Predictive Control targets sequential mobile manipulation, where a robot has to coordinate base motion, arm actions, and task ordering over multiple steps. It appears to connect language-derived task plans with a model-predictive control hierarchy, aiming to make high-level instructions executable by a mobile manipulator in everyday, multi-stage settings.

extra.comment: 8 pages, Published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters ( Volume: 9, Issue: 2, February 2024)
extra.full_text: Mobile manipulators are envisioned to serve more complex roles in people's everyday lives. With recent breakthroughs in large language models, task planners have become better at translating human verbal instructions into a sequence of tasks.

title: AHD Agent: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Automatic Heuristic Design
summary: AHD Agent uses agentic reinforcement learning to automate the design of heuristics for NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, building on recent LLM-based automatic heuristic design systems that can generate and refine candidate algorithms. The interesting shift is treating heuristic discovery as an interactive learning process rather than a one-shot prompting pipeline, so the agent can search more deliberately for high-performing heuristic code.

extra.full_text: Automatic heuristic design (AHD) has emerged as a promising paradigm for solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). Recent works show that large language models (LLMs), when integrated into well-designed frameworks (i.e., LLM-AHD), can autonomously discover high-performing heuristics.

title: Embodied Human Simulation for Quantitative Design and Analysis of Interactive Robotics
summary: Embodied Human Simulation targets the evaluation bottleneck in physical human-robot interaction by modeling how human biomechanics and motor responses shape interactive dynamics. It is aimed at making robot hardware and controllers easier to analyze quantitatively before or alongside physical testing, especially for systems like wearables and collaborative humanoids where mechanical design and control are tightly coupled.

extra.full_text: Physical interactive robotics, ranging from wearable devices to collaborative humanoid robots, require close coordination between mechanical design and control. However, evaluating interactive dynamics is challenging due to complex human biomechanics and motor responses.

title: Quality over Quantity: Demonstration Curation via Influence Functions for Data-Centric Robot Learning
summary: Influence functions are used to identify which teleoperated demonstrations most help or hurt downstream robot policy learning, reframing dataset construction as a curation problem rather than simply scaling collection. The approach targets a common bottleneck in imitation learning: large demonstration corpora can contain low-quality or misleading trajectories, so selecting higher-value examples can improve training efficiency and policy performance without needing more data.

extra.full_text: Learning from demonstrations has emerged as a promising paradigm for end-to-end robot control, particularly when scaled to diverse and large datasets. However, the quality of demonstration data, often collected through human teleoperation, remains a critical bottleneck for effective data-driven robot learning.

title: Evaluation of an Actuated Spine in Agile Quadruped Locomotion
summary: An actuated spine is explored as a way to make quadruped robots more animal-like in fast, agile locomotion, where spinal motion can contribute to stability, speed, and gait efficiency. The work evaluates how adding this extra body degree of freedom affects dynamic quadruped movement, framing the spine as a practical mechanism for extending robot agility rather than just a biomimetic detail.

extra.full_text: The spine plays a crucial role in the dynamic locomotion of quadrupedal animals, improving the stability, speed, and efficiency of their gait, especially for fast-paced and highly agile movements. Therefore, the spine is also a promising and natural way to extend the capabilities of quadruped robots.

title: An Open-Source Robotics Research Platform for Autonomous Laparoscopic Surgery
summary: An open-source robotics platform is introduced for studying autonomous laparoscopic surgery, with an emphasis on the precision, safety, and kinematic constraints that make minimally invasive procedures hard to automate. From the provided text, the work appears to focus less on a single surgical policy result and more on giving researchers a reliable hardware/software basis for developing and evaluating autonomy in robot-assisted surgery.

extra.full_text: Autonomous robot-assisted surgery demands reliable, high-precision platforms that strictly adhere to the safety and kinematic constraints of minimally invasive procedures.

title: A Recipe for Stable Offline Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Stable offline multi-agent reinforcement learning is framed as a recipe for moving MARL away from expensive on-policy self-play and toward training from fixed datasets, analogous to the shift already seen in single-agent offline RL. The interesting part is the focus on stability: it targets the distribution shift and nonstationarity problems that make offline learning especially brittle when multiple agents’ policies interact.

extra.full_text: Despite remarkable achievements in single-agent offline reinforcement learning (RL), multi-agent RL (MARL) has struggled to adopt this paradigm, largely persisting with on-policy training and self-play from scratch.

title: TRIAGE: Type-Routed Interventions via Aleatoric-Epistemic Gated Estimation in Robotic Manipulation and Adaptive Perception -- Don't Treat All Uncertainty the Same
summary: TRIAGE separates uncertainty in robotic manipulation into aleatoric uncertainty from noisy or corrupted observations and epistemic uncertainty from model mismatch, then routes each type to different interventions instead of using one catch-all uncertainty score. The idea is that a robot should adapt its perception pipeline when the sensor stream is unreliable, but seek model correction or safer control when its learned dynamics no longer explain the world.

extra.full_text: Most uncertainty-aware robotic systems collapse prediction uncertainty into a single scalar score and use it to trigger uniform corrective responses. This aggregation obscures whether uncertainty arises from corrupted observations or from mismatch between the learned model and the true system dynamics.

title: Dynamic Properties and Motion Reproducibility of a Compact Pneumatically Actuated Humanoid Upper Body for Data-Driven Control
summary: A compact humanoid upper body is built around pneumatic actuation to support high-DOF, anthropomorphic physical interaction, then characterized for its dynamic behavior and repeatability under motion commands. The focus is on understanding how nonlinear pneumatic actuators affect reproducible movement, providing the measurements needed for data-driven control rather than relying on precise analytic actuator models.

extra.comment: 25 pages, 21 figures. Submitted to Advanced Robotics
extra.full_text: Pneumatically-actuated anthropomorphic robots with high degrees of freedom (DOF) offer significant potential for physical human-robot interaction. However, precise control of pneumatic actuators is challenging due to their inherent nonlinearities.

title: Relating Reinforcement Learning to Dynamic Programming-Based Planning
summary: Relates reinforcement learning and optimal planning through their shared dynamic-programming roots in sequential decision making and optimal control. The available description is high-level, so the clearest takeaway is that it frames RL and dynamic programming-based planning as closely connected methods rather than separate toolkits.

extra.full_text: This paper bridges some of the gap between optimal planning and reinforcement learning (RL), both of which share roots in dynamic programming applied to sequential decision making or optimal control.

title: Referring-Aware Visuomotor Policy Learning for Closed-Loop Manipulation
summary: Referring-Aware Visuomotor Policy Learning targets closed-loop manipulation policies that need to recover when execution drifts from the demonstrated trajectory or the scene changes enough to require rerouting. From the available description, the emphasis is on making a policy trained only from original expert demonstrations more robust to out-of-distribution errors during rollout, rather than relying on additional corrective data or replanning supervision.

extra.full_text: This paper addresses a fundamental problem of visuomotor policy learning for robotic manipulation: how to enhance robustness in out-of-distribution execution errors or dynamically re-routing trajectories, where the model relies solely on the original expert demonstrations for training.

title: Encoding Predictability and Legibility for Style-Conditioned Diffusion Policy
summary: Encoding Predictability and Legibility for Style-Conditioned Diffusion Policy targets the tradeoff in human-robot collaboration between fast, efficient motion and movements that humans can readily interpret. It frames predictability and legibility as style conditions for a diffusion policy, aiming to generate robot trajectories whose expressive qualities can be controlled without simply sacrificing task efficiency.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 18th International Conference on Social Robotics (ICSR 2026)
extra.full_text: Striking a balance between efficiency and transparent motion is a core challenge in human-robot collaboration, as highly expressive movements often incur unnecessary time and energy costs.

title: Modular Reinforcement Learning For Cooperative Swarms
summary: Modular reinforcement learning is applied to cooperative robot swarms where each resource-limited robot observes and coordinates with only a small local neighborhood rather than the full collective. The setup targets the credit-assignment problem in decentralized swarms: individual robots learn local interaction policies despite not directly knowing how their actions affect global utility.

extra.full_text: A cooperative robot swarm is a collective of computationally-limited robots that share a common goal. Each robot can only interact with a small subset of its peers, without knowing how this affects the collective utility.

title: Robots Need Some Education: On the complexity of learning in evolutionary robotics
summary: Evolutionary robotics and robot learning both automate robot optimization, but they differ in whether they target morphology, controllers, or learned behavior, and in the time scale over which adaptation happens. The piece frames “education” as a complexity issue: robots may need structured learning processes rather than direct optimization alone, especially when evolution-like search and within-lifetime learning interact.

extra.full_text: Evolutionary Robotics and Robot Learning are two fields in robotics that aim to automatically optimize robot designs. The key difference between them lies in what is being optimized and the time scale involved.

title: SuperSuit: An Isomorphic Bimodal Interface for Scalable Mobile Manipulation
summary: SuperSuit targets the data-collection bottleneck for wheeled mobile manipulators by using an isomorphic bimodal interface, aiming to make long-horizon demonstrations easier to acquire for systems where navigation and arm control are tightly coupled. The available description only states the motivation, so the concrete mechanism, evaluation setup, and results are not specified here.

extra.full_text: High-quality, long-horizon demonstrations are essential for embodied AI, yet acquiring such data for tightly coupled wheeled mobile manipulators remains a fundamental bottleneck.

title: Robotic Affection -- Opportunities of AI-based haptic interactions to improve social robotic touch through a multi-deep-learning approach
summary: Robotic Affection targets the gap between haptic sensing for manipulation and haptic behavior for social touch, where gestures like handshakes or comforting strokes need to convey affect rather than just control contact forces. It frames AI-based haptic interaction as a multi-deep-learning problem for improving how social robots perceive, generate, and adapt touch in human-robot interaction.

extra.comment: AI for Haptics and Haptics for AI: Challenges and Opportunities Workshop at the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 26), April 13 - 17 2026, Barcelona, Spain
extra.full_text: Despite the advancement in robotic grasping and dexterity through haptic information, affective social touch, such as handshaking or reassuring stroking, remains a major challenge in Human-Robot-Interaction.

title: SPIRIT: Perceptive Shared Autonomy for Robust Robotic Manipulation under Deep Learning Uncertainty
summary: SPIRIT targets robotic manipulation settings where learned perception can be brittle or hard to trust, using perceptive shared autonomy to keep a human in the loop when deep learning uncertainty matters. From the provided abstract fragment, the work is positioned around making manipulation more reliable in safety-critical deployments by combining robot autonomy with uncertainty-aware human assistance, rather than relying on opaque perception alone.

extra.full_text: Deep learning (DL) has enabled impressive advances in robotic perception, yet its limited robustness and lack of interpretability hinder reliable deployment in safety critical applications.

title: VinePT-Map: Pole-Trunk Semantic Mapping for Resilient Autonomous Robotics in Vineyards
summary: VinePT-Map targets the long-term mapping problem for vineyard robots by focusing on stable semantic structure: poles and trunks rather than visually changeable canopy appearance. The idea is to make autonomous navigation and localization more resilient to perceptual aliasing, seasonal growth, and other field changes that often break agricultural robot deployments.

extra.full_text: Reliable long-term deployment of autonomous robots in agricultural environments remains challenging due to perceptual aliasing, seasonal variability, and the dynamic nature of crop canopies.

title: From Prompt to Physical Actuation: Holistic Threat Modeling of LLM-Enabled Robotic Systems
summary: Large language models in robotic planning create a direct path from malicious prompts, corrupted sensor/context inputs, or unsafe generated plans to real-world actuation. The paper frames that full prompt-to-motion pipeline as a security problem, emphasizing how failures that might look like ordinary LLM misuse can become physical safety risks once model outputs drive autonomous robots.

extra.comment: Submitted to 23rd Annual International Conference on Privacy, Security, and Trust (PST2026)
extra.full_text: As large language models are integrated into autonomous robotic systems for task planning and control, compromised inputs or unsafe model outputs can propagate through the planning pipeline to physical-world consequences.

title: Swimming Under Constraints: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Framework for Quadrupedal Bio-Inspired Propulsion
summary: Safe reinforcement learning is used to train quadruped-inspired swimming gaits that remain stable despite destabilizing lift fluctuations and full 6-DoF fluid coupling. The setup targets bio-inspired aquatic robots where high-thrust propulsion can easily trade off against control safety, framing swimming as a constrained policy-learning problem rather than just maximizing speed or thrust.

extra.full_text: Bio-inspired aquatic propulsion offers high thrust and maneuverability but is prone to destabilizing forces such as lift fluctuations, which are further amplified by six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) fluid coupling.

title: Behavior-Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Receding-Horizon Credit Assignment for High-Performance Control
summary: Behavior-Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Receding-Horizon Credit Assignment targets high-performance robot control while keeping learned policies aligned with expert behavior. From the provided abstract fragment, the focus is on combining behavior constraints with a receding-horizon credit assignment scheme, but there are not enough details here to state the algorithmic specifics, benchmarks, or empirical results.

extra.full_text: Learning high-performance control policies that remain consistent with expert behavior is a fundamental challenge in robotics.

title: Characterization and Correlation of Robotic Snake Scale Friction and Locomotion Speed
summary: Snake robots can exploit frictional anisotropy in their scales to move across varied terrain, but the relationship between scale friction and locomotion speed is often hard to quantify directly. This study characterizes the friction behavior of robotic snake scales and correlates those measurements with resulting locomotion speed, clarifying how scale-surface interactions translate into faster or slower gait performance.

extra.comment: Accepted for 9th IEEE-RAS International Conference on Soft Robotics (RoboSoft 2026), 8 pages, 7 figures
extra.full_text: Snake robots are inspired by the ability of biological snakes to move over rock, grass, leaves, soil, up trees, along pavement and more. Their ability to move in multiple distinct environments is due to their legless locomotion strategy, which combines distinct gaits with a skin that exhibits frictional anisotropy.

title: Chain of World: World Model Thinking in Latent Motion
summary: Chain of World targets a weakness in VLA models by shifting world-model prediction into latent motion dynamics instead of spending capacity reconstructing visually redundant future frames. It frames embodied reasoning around the temporal and causal structure of how the scene is expected to change, which is interesting because it tries to make prediction useful for action rather than treating video generation as the objective.

extra.comment: Accepted by CVPR2026. Project page: https://fx-hit.github.io/cowvla-io/
extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are a promising path toward embodied intelligence, yet they often overlook the predictive and temporal-causal structure underlying visual dynamics. World-model VLAs address this by predicting future frames, but waste capacity reconstructing redundant backgrounds.

title: Rethinking Policy Diversity in Ensemble Policy Gradient in Large-Scale Reinforcement Learning
summary: Ensemble policy gradient is revisited as a way to make large-scale reinforcement learning explore better when running tens of thousands of parallel environments. Instead of relying on a single policy’s limited sampling behavior, the approach uses multiple policies to collect more diverse experience, targeting the exploration bottleneck that appears at very high environment counts.

extra.full_text: Scaling reinforcement learning to tens of thousands of parallel environments requires overcoming the limited exploration capacity of a single policy. Ensemble-based policy gradient methods, which employ multiple policies to collect diverse samples, have recently been proposed to promote exploration.

title: Learning Thermal-Aware Locomotion Policies for an Electrically-Actuated Quadruped Robot
summary: Electrically actuated quadrupeds can overheat during sustained, high-torque locomotion, so this study trains locomotion policies that account for motor thermal buildup rather than optimizing motion alone. The aim is to keep the robot mobile on complex terrain while reducing the risk of triggering motor overheat protection, which is a practical bottleneck for long-duration deployment.

extra.full_text: Electrically-actuated quadrupedal robots possess high mobility on complex terrains, but their motors tend to accumulate heat under high-torque cyclic loads, potentially triggering overheat protection and limiting long-duration tasks.

title: MotuBrain: An Advanced World Action Model for Robot Control
summary: MotuBrain is a robot control model that tries to close the gap between semantically strong Vision-Language-Action systems and the fine-grained dynamics needed for precise manipulation. It jointly models video and action with a UniDiffuser-style formulation and a three-stream Mixture-of-Transformers architecture, aiming to learn both what is happening in the scene and how robot actions change it.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generalize semantically well but often lack fine-grained modeling of world dynamics. We present MotuBrain, a unified World Action Model that jointly models video and action under a UniDiffuser formulation with a three-stream Mixture-of-Transformers architecture.

title: A Physical Imitation Learning Pipeline for Energy-Efficient Quadruped Locomotion Assisted by Parallel Elastic Joint
summary: Animals’ ability to offload part of locomotion control onto passive body mechanics motivates a quadruped learning pipeline that incorporates a parallel elastic joint to reduce active control effort. The work frames energy-efficient robot locomotion as an embodied physical intelligence problem, using physical imitation learning to exploit intrinsic body dynamics rather than relying solely on high-bandwidth motor commands.

extra.full_text: Due to brain-body co-evolution, animals' intrinsic body dynamics play a crucial role in energy-efficient locomotion, which shares control effort between active muscles and passive body dynamics -- a principle known as Embodied Physical Intelligence.

title: Multi-Camera View Scaling for Data-Efficient Robot Imitation Learning
summary: Multi-Camera View Scaling targets the data bottleneck in robot imitation learning by using multiple camera viewpoints to expand the visual diversity available from expert demonstrations. The work is aimed at helping manipulation policies generalize across environment variation without requiring costly new demonstrations for every setting.

extra.full_text: The generalization ability of imitation learning policies for robotic manipulation is fundamentally constrained by the diversity of expert demonstrations, while collecting demonstrations across varied environments is costly and difficult in practice.

title: Thinking in Text and Images: Interleaved Vision--Language Reasoning Traces for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
summary: Long-horizon manipulation is framed as a reasoning problem that has to stay consistent in both language-level plans and visual-spatial constraints. The paper explores interleaved vision-language reasoning traces, where text and images are used together to support robot planning over extended manipulation sequences.

extra.full_text: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires plans that are both logically coherent and geometrically grounded.

title: A Model-based Visual Contact Localization and Force Sensing System for Compliant Robotic Grippers
summary: Model-based visual sensing is used to estimate both contact location and grasp force in compliant robotic grippers, aiming to add force awareness without embedding fragile or expensive sensors into the fingers. The interesting angle is the trade-off: it treats deformation seen by vision as a signal for contact and force, which could make soft grippers safer for delicate manipulation while keeping the hardware mechanically simple.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
extra.full_text: Grasp force estimation can help prevent robots from damaging delicate objects during manipulation and improve learning-based robotic control. Integrating force sensing into deformable grippers negotiates trade-offs in cost, complexity, mechanical robustness, and performance.

title: Do World Action Models Generalize Better than VLAs? A Robustness Study
summary: The study compares world action models, which predict how a robot’s environment will change under candidate actions, against vision-language-action models for real-world robot action planning robustness. From the provided text, the central question is whether explicitly modeling action-conditioned future dynamics yields better generalization than directly mapping perception and language to actions.

extra.full_text: Robot action planning in the real world is challenging as it requires not only understanding the current state of the environment but also predicting how it will evolve in response to actions.

title: Stochastic Entanglement of Deterministic Origami Tentacles For Universal Robotic Gripping
summary: Origami-inspired robotic grippers are used here as compact, mechanically flexible tentacles for universal grasping, with the aim of capturing randomly shaped objects in dynamic settings without multiplying actuators or control channels. The interesting mechanism is the pairing of deterministic origami tentacle structure with stochastic entanglement, letting the gripper exploit passive wrapping and contact interactions rather than relying on finely planned finger motions.

extra.full_text: Origami-inspired robotic grippers have shown promising potential for object manipulation tasks due to their compact volume and mechanical flexibility. However, robust capture of objects with random shapes in dynamic working environments often comes at the cost of additional actuation channels and control complexity.

title: Egocentric Tactile and Proximity Sensors as Observation Priors for Humanoid Collision Avoidance
summary: Egocentric tactile and proximity sensors are treated as observation priors for humanoid collision avoidance, focusing on how sensor coverage, modality, and range shape the robot’s ability to move safely without relying on external vision. The paper targets the practical design question of which body-distributed sensing properties actually support avoidant behavior, especially in occluded settings where camera-based perception is brittle.

extra.comment: This work was accepted at the 8th RoboTac Workshop at the International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
extra.full_text: Collision-free motion is often aided by tactile and proximity sensors distributed on the body of the robot due to their resistance to occlusion as opposed to external cameras. However, how to shape the sensor's properties, such as sensing coverage; type; and range, to enable avoidant behavior remains unclear.

title: Learning Smooth and Robust Space Robotic Manipulation of Dynamic Target via Inter-frame Correlation
summary: Learning Smooth and Robust Space Robotic Manipulation of Dynamic Target via Inter-frame Correlation addresses on-orbit servicing where a robot must manipulate a moving, non-cooperative target. From the available text, it appears to focus on using correlations between consecutive frames to make manipulation smoother and more robust under target dynamics, but the snippet does not provide enough detail on the model, experiments, or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: On-orbit servicing represents a critical frontier in future aerospace engineering, with the manipulation of dynamic non-cooperative targets serving as a key technology.

title: Can a Robot Walk the Robotic Dog: Triple-Zero Collaborative Navigation for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Triple Zero Path Planning (TZPP) coordinates heterogeneous robots for collaborative navigation without requiring training, prior environment knowledge, or simulation. The title’s “robot walking the robotic dog” framing suggests a leader–follower style setting where different robot embodiments navigate together, with the interesting claim being that coordination can be achieved directly rather than learned or precomputed.

extra.full_text: We present Triple Zero Path Planning (TZPP), a collaborative framework for heterogeneous multi-robot systems that requires zero training, zero prior knowledge, and zero simulation.

title: Generative Control as Optimization: Time Unconditional Flow Matching for Adaptive and Robust Robotic Control
summary: Time Unconditional Flow Matching reframes generative robot control as an optimization problem, targeting the fixed inference schedules that make diffusion- and flow-based imitation policies inefficient when different states require different amounts of computation. The method appears aimed at adaptive, robust control by letting generation effort vary with state complexity, but the provided text does not include benchmarks or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Diffusion models and flow matching have become a cornerstone of robotic imitation learning, yet they suffer from a structural inefficiency where inference is often bound to a fixed integration schedule that is agnostic to state complexity.

title: RobotPan: A 360$^\circ$ Surround-View Robotic Vision System for Embodied Perception
summary: RobotPan is a 360-degree surround-view vision system for robots, aimed at giving embodied agents continuous visual awareness during navigation and loco-manipulation. It is especially framed around settings where humans may need to monitor, guide, collect data from, or take over a robot, making wide-field perception part of the interface between autonomy and human control.

extra.full_text: Surround-view perception is increasingly important for robotic navigation and loco-manipulation, especially in human-in-the-loop settings such as teleoperation, data collection, and emergency takeover.

title: An Efficient Beam Search Algorithm for Active Perception in Mobile Robotics
summary: Active perception is framed as a planning problem for mobile robots that must choose both motion and sensing actions to gather the most useful observations for a mission. The paper centers on an efficient beam search algorithm, using a bounded set of promising candidate action sequences to keep perception-aware planning tractable while still exploring informative future views.

extra.comment: Accepted to The International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR). Project page: https://efficient-beam-search.github.io/
extra.full_text: Active perception is a fundamental problem in autonomous robotics in which the robot must decide where to move and what to sense in order to obtain the most informative observations for accomplishing its mission.

title: Modernising Reinforcement Learning-Based Navigation for Embodied Semantic Scene Graph Generation
summary: Modernising Reinforcement Learning-Based Navigation for Embodied Semantic Scene Graph Generation links RL-based embodied navigation with semantic scene graph construction, aiming to help agents build world models that capture objects, relations, and spatial context rather than geometry alone. The emphasis is on making these semantic models useful for objective-driven self-adaptation in uncertain, resource-constrained settings such as Organic Computing.

extra.full_text: Semantic world models enable embodied agents to reason about objects, relations, and spatial context beyond purely geometric representations. In Organic Computing, such models are a key enabler for objective-driven self-adaptation under uncertainty and resource constraints.

title: CROSS: A Mixture-of-Experts Reinforcement Learning Framework for Generalizable Large-Scale Traffic Signal Control
summary: CROSS uses a mixture-of-experts reinforcement learning setup for adaptive traffic signal control, aiming to make signal policies scale better across large urban road networks rather than overfitting to one intersection layout or traffic pattern. It targets autonomous smart-city traffic management by dynamically choosing signal phases to reduce congestion, with the interesting angle being the use of expert specialization to improve generalization in large-scale control.

extra.full_text: Recent advances in robotics, automation, and artificial intelligence have enabled urban traffic systems to operate with increasing autonomy towards future smart cities, powered in part by the development of adaptive traffic signal control (ATSC), which dynamically optimizes signal phases to mitigate congestion and optimize traffic.

title: VistaBot: View-Robust Robot Manipulation via Spatiotemporal-Aware View Synthesis
summary: VistaBot targets the brittleness of end-to-end manipulation policies trained from a fixed camera by using spatiotemporal-aware view synthesis to expose the robot to viewpoint variation. The idea is to make the visual input more robust to camera pose changes without requiring real multi-view training data, improving generalization when the camera shifts at test time.

extra.comment: This paper has been accepted to ICRA 2026
extra.full_text: Recently, end-to-end robotic manipulation models have gained significant attention for their generalizability and scalability. However, they often suffer from limited robustness to camera viewpoint changes when training with a fixed camera.

title: Kinematic Optimization of Phalanx Length Ratios in Robotic Hands Using Potential Dexterity
summary: The study uses potential dexterity as a task-agnostic way to evaluate how different phalanx length ratios affect robotic hand dexterity during design. Instead of testing against particular objects or manipulation scenarios, it frames finger-link proportions as a kinematic optimization problem, aiming to identify hand geometries that preserve dexterous motion capacity before task-specific design choices are fixed.

extra.comment: This manuscript has been submitted for possible publication
extra.full_text: In the design stage of robotic hands, it is not straightforward to quantitatively evaluate the effect of phalanx length ratios on dexterity without defining specific objects or manipulation tasks.

title: Drift-Based Policy Optimization: Native One-Step Policy Learning for Online Robot Control
summary: Drift-Based Policy Optimization targets the inference bottleneck in generative robot policies by learning a native one-step policy for online control instead of relying on iterative multi-step denoising. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified beyond replacing slow multimodal action generation with a faster policy-learning approach for robotic manipulation.

extra.full_text: Although multi-step generative policies achieve strong performance in robotic manipulation by modeling multimodal action distributions, they require multi-step iterative denoising at inference time.

title: GAPG: Geometry Aware Push-Grasping Synergy for Goal-Oriented Manipulation in Clutter
summary: GAPG tackles goal-oriented grasping in clutter by pairing grasp attempts with geometry-aware pushes that clear space around occluded or stacked targets. The idea is to use pushing not as a generic auxiliary skill but as part of a coordinated push-grasp policy aimed at making the specific target object graspable when a direct grasp would fail.

extra.full_text: Grasping target objects is a fundamental skill for robotic manipulation, but in cluttered environments with stacked or occluded objects, a single-step grasp is often insufficient. To address this, previous work has introduced pushing as an auxiliary action to create graspable space.

title: ARM: Advantage Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Manipulation
summary: ARM introduces advantage reward modeling for long-horizon robotic manipulation, targeting the credit-assignment problem that makes sparse-reward RL hard to train. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, so the summary can only say that the method uses reward modeling around advantages to provide more useful learning signal for extended manipulation tasks.

extra.full_text: Long-horizon robotic manipulation remains challenging for reinforcement learning (RL) because sparse rewards provide limited guidance for credit assignment.

title: Swim2Real: VLM-Guided System Identification for Sim-to-Real Transfer
summary: Swim2Real uses a vision-language model to tune a 16-parameter simulator for a robotic fish directly from swimming videos. The interesting part is the calibration loop: VLM feedback replaces hand-designed search stages, aiming to make sim-to-real transfer for soft aquatic robots less dependent on bespoke system-identification pipelines.

extra.full_text: We present Swim2Real, a pipeline that calibrates a 16-parameter robotic fish simulator from swimming videos using vision-language model (VLM) feedback, requiring no hand-designed search stages.

title: Locomotion of an Elastic Snake Robot via Natural Dynamics
summary: Elastic snake robots can move more efficiently by using their own compliance and passive dynamics rather than treating elasticity as something to suppress. The paper focuses on locomotion that deliberately exploits the robot’s nonlinear natural dynamics, extending earlier elastic snake-robot results that had only partially used those effects.

extra.full_text: Nature suggests that exploiting the elasticities and natural dynamics of robotic systems could increase their locomotion efficiency. Prior work on elastic snake robots supports this hypothesis, but has not fully exploited the nonlinear dynamic behavior of the systems.

title: FLASH: Fast Learning via GPU-Accelerated Simulation for High-Fidelity Deformable Manipulation in Minutes
summary: FLASH targets the simulation bottleneck in deformable-object manipulation by using GPU-accelerated high-fidelity simulation to make contact-rich robot learning fast enough to run in minutes. The setup is positioned as an Isaac Sim-style scaling story for deformable manipulation rather than rigid bodies, aiming to preserve detailed deformable dynamics while making policy learning practical at much shorter iteration times.

extra.full_text: Simulation frameworks such as Isaac Sim have enabled scalable robot learning for locomotion and rigid-body manipulation; however, contact-rich simulation remains a major bottleneck for deformable object manipulation.

title: AeroScene: Progressive Scene Synthesis for Aerial Robotics
summary: AeroScene targets the bottleneck of hand-built drone simulation environments by using progressive generative scene synthesis for aerial robotics. From the provided abstract fragment, it appears focused on scaling up realistic simulator world creation so drone systems can be trained or evaluated across richer, less manually curated environments.

extra.full_text: Generative models have shown substantial impact across multiple domains, their potential for scene synthesis remains underexplored in robotics. This gap is more evident in drone simulators, where simulation environments still rely heavily on manual efforts, which are time-consuming to create and difficult to scale.

title: VolumeDP: Modeling Volumetric Representation for Manipulation Policy Learning
summary: VolumeDP targets the 2D-to-3D mismatch in visual imitation learning by modeling manipulation observations as volumetric representations before predicting actions. Instead of forcing policies to infer 3D structure directly from flat images, it gives the policy an explicit spatial substrate for reasoning about object geometry and motion, with the goal of improving robustness in manipulation.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning is a prominent paradigm for robotic manipulation. However, existing visual imitation methods map 2D image observations directly to 3D action outputs, imposing a 2D-3D mismatch that hinders spatial reasoning and degrades robustness.

title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
summary: Pretrained vision-language-action models are evaluated under continual robot policy learning, where new skills are added over time without retraining from scratch or erasing earlier behaviors. The result is that these large pretrained policies appear much more resistant to catastrophic forgetting than expected, suggesting their broad visual-language-action representations may provide a stronger foundation for incremental robot skill acquisition.

extra.full_text: Continual learning is a long-standing challenge in robot policy learning, where a policy must acquire new skills over time without catastrophically forgetting previously learned ones.

title: HRDexDB: A Large-Scale Dataset of Dexterous Human and Robotic Hand Grasps
summary: HRDexDB is a large-scale multimodal dataset of high-fidelity dexterous grasping sequences spanning both human hands and multiple robotic hand embodiments. It is aimed at studying grasp behavior across biological and robotic morphologies, giving researchers a shared source of detailed sequences for learning, comparison, and transfer in dexterous manipulation.

extra.full_text: We present HRDexDB, a large-scale, multi-modal dataset of high-fidelity dexterous grasping sequences featuring both human and diverse robotic hands.

title: RoCo Challenge at AAAI 2026: Benchmarking Robotic Collaborative Manipulation for Assembly Towards Industrial Automation
summary: RoCo Challenge at AAAI 2026 is a benchmark effort for robotic collaborative manipulation in industrial assembly settings, aimed at testing embodied AI systems on coordinated, continuous action rather than isolated perception. From the provided text, the concrete technical details are sparse, but the framing suggests an evaluation suite focused on how robots work together on assembly tasks relevant to automation.

extra.full_text: Embodied Artificial Intelligence (EAI) is rapidly developing, gradually subverting previous autonomous systems' paradigms from isolated perception to integrated, continuous action.

title: Learning Structured Robot Policies from Vision-Language Models via Synthetic Neuro-Symbolic Supervision
summary: Vision-language models are used to generate synthetic neuro-symbolic supervision so robot policies can learn structured, interpretable behavior rather than opaque end-to-end visuomotor mappings. The approach aims to retain the flexibility of VLM-guided robot control while exposing intermediate policy structure that can be inspected and analyzed for real-world deployment.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have recently demonstrated strong capabilities in mapping multimodal observations to robot behaviors. However, most current approaches rely on end-to-end visuomotor policies that remain opaque and difficult to analyze, limiting their use in real-world robotic applications.

title: Failure Identification in Imitation Learning Via Statistical and Semantic Filtering
summary: Imitation-learned robot policies can fail when deployments drift outside their training distribution, so this work targets failure identification rather than policy learning itself. It frames real-world breakdowns such as hardware faults, defective parts, and unexpected human actions as rare out-of-distribution events, using statistical and semantic filtering to flag executions likely to go wrong.

extra.comment: 8 pages, Appendix coming soon, accepted at ICRA 2026
extra.full_text: Imitation learning (IL) policies in robotics deliver strong performance in controlled settings but remain brittle in real-world deployments: rare events such as hardware faults, defective parts, unexpected human actions, or any state that lies outside the training distribution can lead to failed executions.

title: Access Timing as Scaffolding: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to GenAI in Education
summary: Access Timing as Scaffolding frames GenAI use in education as a reinforcement learning problem: instead of giving students unrestricted access, the system learns when AI help should be available so it supports learning without encouraging dependence. The idea is to treat timing itself as the scaffold, using policy learning to balance assistance against metacognitive engagement and independent problem solving.

extra.full_text: In recent years, generative AI (GenAI) in educational settings has become ubiquitous in students' daily lives, despite its potential to induce over-reliance, metacognitive disengagement, and diminished learning when used unrestrictedly.

title: Reactive Robot-Centric Safety for Autonomous Navigation in Constrained and Dynamic Environments
summary: Addresses real-time safety for autonomous navigation in tight, changing environments using only onboard sensing. The focus is a reactive, robot-centered safety mechanism, suggesting a controller or safety layer that can respond online to nearby obstacles and dynamic constraints without relying on external infrastructure or prior global knowledge.

extra.full_text: In this work, we address the problem of ensuring real-time safety in autonomous robot navigation, in spatially constrained dynamic environments, by utilizing only onboard sensors.

title: Where to Perch in a Tree: Vision-Guidance for Tree-Grasping Drones
summary: The study builds a vision-guided pipeline for autonomous drones that need to choose where to grasp and perch on a tree. It analyzes tree imagery with segmentation, binary morphology, and machine-learning-style image processing to infer branch shape and structure, then uses that assessment to identify a suitable perch location for a tree-grasping drone.

extra.comment: Work in progress version accepted to the Recent Advances in Robotic Perception for Forestry
extra.full_text: This study demonstrates a method to locate an ideal perch location on a tree for vision-guided autonomous tree-perching drones. Various image processing algorithms, including those used for machine learning, image segmentation and binary image morphology, are implemented to assess the shape and structure of a tree.

title: Driving Intents Amplify Planning-Oriented Reinforcement Learning
summary: Driving Intents Amplify Planning-Oriented Reinforcement Learning addresses mode collapse in continuous-action driving policies trained from only one demonstrated trajectory per scene. It conditions planning-oriented reinforcement learning on explicit driving intents, letting the policy represent semantically different maneuvers instead of sampling only small variations around the demonstration.

extra.full_text: Continuous-action policies trained on a single demonstrated trajectory per scene suffer from mode collapse: samples cluster around the demonstrated maneuver and the policy cannot represent semantically distinct alternatives.

title: HECTOR: Human-centric Hierarchical Coordination and Supervision of Robotic Fleets under Continual Temporal Tasks
summary: HECTOR addresses the problem of supervising large robot fleets that must coordinate over ongoing temporal tasks without requiring an operator to micromanage each robot. It frames fleet control as human-centric hierarchical coordination, letting a supervisor guide or intervene at higher levels while the system manages task allocation and execution across robots under continual temporal constraints.

extra.full_text: Robotic fleets can be extremely efficient when working concurrently and collaboratively, e.g., for delivery, surveillance, search and rescue. However, it can be demanding or even impractical for an operator to directly control each robot.

title: Chrono-Gymnasium: An Open-Source, Gymnasium-Compatible Distributed Simulation Framework
summary: Chrono-Gymnasium wraps high-fidelity physics simulation in a Gymnasium-compatible, distributed framework so robotics and mechanical-systems experiments can use heavier simulators inside RL and optimization workflows. It is aimed at cases where sim-to-real fidelity matters but single-machine simulation throughput becomes the bottleneck, letting researchers scale data collection without giving up more detailed dynamics.

extra.full_text: High-fidelity physics simulation is essential for closing the sim-to-real gap in robotics and complex mechanical systems. However, the computational overhead of high-fidelity engines often limits their use in data-intensive tasks like Reinforcement Learning (RL) and global optimization.

title: CaMeRL: Collision-Aware and Memory-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning for UAV Navigation in Multi-Scale Obstacle Environments
summary: CaMeRL tackles UAV obstacle avoidance in environments where obstacles vary in physical scale, a factor that many depth-based navigation policies underemphasize compared with density or count. It augments reinforcement learning with collision-aware modeling and memory over depth observations, aiming to move beyond single-frame geometric cues so the UAV can better handle multi-scale obstacle layouts.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
extra.full_text: In obstacle avoidance navigation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), variations in obstacle scale have received strangely less attention than obstacle number or density. Existing methods typically extract purely geometric features from single-frame depth observations.

title: DRL-STAF: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for State-Aware Forecasting of Complex Multivariate Hidden Markov Processes
summary: DRL-STAF uses deep reinforcement learning to forecast complex multivariate hidden Markov processes where observations are nonlinear and nonstationary, latent regimes shift over time, and multiple sequences influence one another. The interesting angle is its state-aware framing: rather than treating forecasting as a purely supervised sequence problem, it models decisions around hidden-state dynamics and cross-sequence dependencies directly.

extra.full_text: Forecasting multivariate hidden Markov processes is challenging due to nonlinear and nonstationary observations, latent state transitions, and cross-sequence dependencies.

title: LEMON: Learning Executable Multi-Agent Orchestration via Counterfactual Reinforcement Learning
summary: LEMON trains LLM-based multi-agent systems to produce executable orchestration designs, jointly deciding agent roles, capacity allocation, and task dependencies rather than relying on hand-designed coordination patterns. It uses counterfactual reinforcement learning to evaluate how orchestration choices affect both answer quality and execution efficiency, targeting the core bottleneck that multi-agent performance often depends as much on workflow structure as on the underlying models.

extra.full_text: Large language models (LLMs) have become a strong foundation for multi-agent systems, but their effectiveness depends heavily on orchestration design. Across different tasks, role design, capacity assignment, and dependency construction jointly affect both solution quality and execution efficiency.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Semantic Rewards Enables Low-Resource Language Expansion without Alignment Tax
summary: Reinforcement learning with semantic rewards is used to expand LLM capability in low-resource languages while trying to avoid the usual tradeoff where target-language gains damage broader alignment or general skills. The approach frames language expansion around meaning-preserving feedback rather than only surface-form matching, aiming to improve performance in the new language without catastrophic forgetting.

extra.full_text: Extending large language models (LLMs) to low-resource languages often incurs an "alignment tax": improvements in the target language come at the cost of catastrophic forgetting in general capabilities.

title: Matrix-Space Reinforcement Learning for Reusing Local Transition Geometry
summary: Matrix-Space Reinforcement Learning targets compositional generalization by reusing the local transition structure found in earlier rollouts, rather than only transferring whole skills or learned predictive models. It treats prior experience as reusable geometry in transition space, aiming to identify which local dynamics remain relevant when the agent faces a new sequential decision-making task.

extra.full_text: Compositional generalization in sequential decision-making requires identifying which parts of prior rollouts remain useful for new tasks. Existing methods reuse skills or predictive models, but often overlook rich local transition geometry and dynamics.

title: Robotic Nanoparticle Synthesis via Solution-based Processes
summary: A screw geometry-based manipulation planner is used to automate solution-phase nanoparticle synthesis on a robot, with gold and magnetite nanoparticles as the demonstration cases. The interesting part is the translation of chemistry-lab liquid handling and vessel manipulation into geometric motion primitives, aiming to make wet-chemistry synthesis more repeatable and programmable.

extra.full_text: We present a screw geometry-based manipulation planning framework for the robotic automation of solution-based synthesis, exemplified through the preparation of gold and magnetite nanoparticles.

title: GenCircuit-RL: Reinforcement Learning from Hierarchical Verification for Genetic Circuit Design
summary: GenCircuit-RL applies reinforcement learning to genetic circuit design using hierarchical verification as the feedback signal, aiming to reduce the expert hand-tuning that still dominates synthetic biology workflows. From the available text, it appears focused on automating or guiding the search for circuit designs rather than just modeling them, with the interesting piece being the use of structured verification to make RL feedback more reliable for biological design constraints.

extra.full_text: Genetic circuit design remains a laborious, expert-driven process despite decades of progress in synthetic biology.

title: MetaAgent-X : Breaking the Ceiling of Automatic Multi-Agent Systems via End-to-End Reinforcement Learning
summary: MetaAgent-X targets automatic construction of multi-agent workflows, trying to move beyond hand-designed or fixed orchestration schemes. From the provided description, the central idea is to use end-to-end reinforcement learning to learn how agents should be instantiated and coordinated, but no benchmarks, mechanisms, or quantitative results are given here.

extra.full_text: Automatic multi-agent systems aim to instantiate agent workflows without relying on manually designed or fixed orchestration.

title: Diagnosing Training Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
summary: Modern LLM reinforcement learning pipelines often generate rollouts in one system and optimize the policy in another, assuming both compute identical token probabilities. This paper focuses on diagnosing when that training-inference match breaks, which matters because even small probability discrepancies can corrupt RL updates and make debugging large-scale training runs difficult.

extra.full_text: Modern LLM RL systems separate rollout generation from policy optimization. These two stages are expected to produce token probabilities that match exactly.

title: Learning Selective Merge Policies for Deadline-Constrained Coded Caching via Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Deep reinforcement learning is used to learn when a coded-caching server should selectively merge cached content into a single multicast message under deadline constraints. The idea is to exploit users’ cached side information to reduce peak network load while avoiding merges that would miss timing requirements, turning the merge decision into a learned policy rather than a fixed rule.

extra.full_text: With the coded caching, the server can use the information the users have cached to serve multiple users at a time by sending a single coded multi-casting message, i.e., the merged message, thereby relieving the peak network loads.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Calling Agents in Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)
summary: Reinforcement learning is applied to tool-calling agents that operate over FHIR electronic health records, treating the patient record as a directed graph of healthcare resources rather than a flat text store. The focus is on training agents to navigate and query interoperable clinical data through tools, which is interesting because FHIR’s graph structure makes retrieval and reasoning a systems problem as much as a language-model problem.

extra.full_text: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) is the dominant standard for interoperable exchange of healthcare data. In FHIR, electronic health records form a directed graph of resources.

title: Generative Floor Plan Design with LLMs via Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
summary: Uses LLMs trained with reinforcement learning and verifiable rewards to generate professional floor plans that satisfy hard spatial constraints such as room dimensions, target areas, and inter-room connectivity. The interesting part is the reward design: instead of relying only on subjective visual quality, it can automatically check whether generated layouts meet explicit architectural requirements while still aiming for functional and aesthetic plans.

extra.full_text: An AI system for professional floor plan design must precisely control room dimensions and areas while respecting the desired connectivity between rooms and maintaining functional and aesthetic quality.

title: R2R2: Robust Representation for Intensive Experience Reuse via Redundancy Reduction in Self-Predictive Learning
summary: R2R2 targets the overfitting that appears when off-policy reinforcement learning reuses scarce robot data very aggressively under high update-to-data ratios. It focuses on instability in self-predictive learned representations rather than only critic bias, using redundancy reduction to make intensive experience reuse more robust in data-scarce robotics settings.

extra.comment: Accepted at the Forty-Third International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026). This is the camera-ready version
extra.full_text: For reinforcement learning in data-scarce domains like real-world robotics, intensive data reuse enhances efficiency but induces overfitting. While prior works focus on critic bias, representation-level instability in Self-Predictive Learning (SPL) under high Update-to-Data (UTD) regimes remains underexplored.

title: CO-MAP: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to the Qubit Allocation Problem
summary: CO-MAP applies reinforcement learning to qubit allocation in quantum compilation, learning how to map logical qubits in an abstract circuit onto the physical qubits of a quantum device. The interesting angle is that it treats a core compiler bottleneck as a sequential decision problem, aiming to produce mappings that make real hardware execution more feasible despite limited qubit connectivity.

extra.full_text: A quantum compiler is a critical piece in the quantum computing pipeline since it allows an abstract quantum circuit to be run on a physical quantum computer. One extremely important subproblem in quantum compilation is the generation of a logical to physical qubit mapping.

title: AttenA+: Rectifying Action Inequality in Robotic Foundation Models
summary: AttenA+ targets a training mismatch in robotic foundation models: the usual objective treats every action in a trajectory as equally informative, even though some decisions matter much more for task success than others. The method appears to reweight or rectify this action-level inequality during optimization, aiming to make robot policies learn more from temporally important actions instead of smoothing them into a homogeneous loss.

extra.full_text: Existing robotic foundation models, while powerful, are predicated on an implicit assumption of temporal homogeneity: treating all actions as equally informative during optimization.

title: HLS-Seek: QoR-Aware Code Generation for High-Level Synthesis via Proxy Comparative Reward Reinforcement Learning
summary: HLS-Seek targets LLM-based high-level synthesis code generation where functional correctness is not enough, because pragma choices and code structure directly determine latency and FPGA resource use. It frames generation around QoR-aware optimization, using proxy comparative reward reinforcement learning to steer C/C++ HLS outputs toward better latency-resource tradeoffs rather than merely compiling correctly.

extra.full_text: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) compiles algorithmic C/C++ descriptions into hardware, with Quality of Results (QoR) -- latency and resource utilization -- critically governed by pragma configurations and code structure. Existing LLM-based HLS approaches train for functional correctness but ignore QoR entirely.

title: MARLIN: Multi-Agent Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable LLM Inference in Cloud Datacenters
summary: MARLIN targets the energy cost of cloud LLM inference, where serving requests can dominate lifecycle energy use, by framing datacenter scheduling as a multi-agent game-theoretic reinforcement learning problem. The system appears aimed at coordinating inference workloads across cloud resources to reduce energy consumption while preserving service quality, making sustainability a first-class objective in LLM serving rather than an after-the-fact accounting metric.

extra.full_text: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become increasingly prevalent in cloud-based platforms, propelled by the introduction of AI-based consumer and enterprise services. LLM inference requests in particular account for up to 90% of total LLM lifecycle energy use, dwarfing training energy costs.

title: Dyadic Partnership(DP): A Missing Link Towards Full Autonomy in Medical Robotics
summary: Dyadic Partnership (DP) argues that medical robots need a middle layer between pure tele-manipulation and full autonomy, where the surgeon and robot share control in a structured partnership. The idea is to move beyond robots that mainly extend human hands with better access, dexterity, tremor reduction, and imaging, toward systems whose intelligence actively participates in clinical tasks while keeping the human meaningfully in the loop.

extra.full_text: For the past decades medical robotic solutions were mostly based on the concept of tele-manipulation. While their design was extremely intelligent, allowing for better access, improved dexterity, reduced tremor, and improved imaging, their intelligence was limited.

title: GraspSense: Physically Grounded Grasp and Grip Planning for a Dexterous Robotic Hand via Language-Guided Perception and Force Maps
summary: GraspSense targets dexterous hand manipulation where the right grasp depends on how stiffness, friction, or fragility vary across an object, not just on geometry. It combines language-guided perception with force maps so the hand can plan both where to grasp and how hard to grip based on physically meaningful contact regions.

extra.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Minor non-semantic changes in the main scheme
extra.full_text: Dexterous robotic manipulation requires more than geometrically valid grasps: it demands physically grounded contact strategies that account for the spatially non-uniform mechanical properties of the object.

title: Events as Triggers for Behavioral Diversity in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Agents are trained to use events as triggers for switching behavior, so diversity emerges when task conditions change rather than being maintained uniformly throughout an episode. The idea targets multi-agent cooperation settings where agents need coordinated but differentiated roles, with the interesting emphasis on timing: not just learning diverse policies, but learning when behavioral diversity should appear.

extra.full_text: Effective multi-agent cooperation requires agents to adopt diverse behaviors as task conditions evolve-and to do so at the right moment.

title: ICRL: Learning to Internalize Self-Critique with Reinforcement Learning
summary: ICRL trains language-model agents to retain the benefit of self-critique after the critique is no longer provided, using reinforcement learning to turn external feedback into more reliable underlying behavior. The motivating failure mode is that an agent can correct itself when shown a critique but repeat the same mistake on the original query later, so the method targets that gap between prompted correction and internalized capability.

extra.full_text: Large language model-based agents make mistakes, yet critique can often guide the same model toward correct behavior. However, when critique is removed, the model may fail again on the same query, indicating that it has not internalized the critique's guidance into its underlying capability.

title: Multi-Dimensional Behavioral Evaluation of Agentic Stock Prediction Systems Using Large Language Model Judges with Closed-Loop Reinforcement Learning Feedback
summary: Agentic stock-prediction systems are evaluated beyond aggregate forecast error by using large language model judges to score multiple behavioral dimensions. The setup adds closed-loop reinforcement-learning feedback, so the evaluator is not just measuring point-forecast accuracy but shaping how the forecasting agent behaves during financial prediction.

extra.comment: 24 pages, 5 figures, 14 tables. Research Article submitted to Journal of Forecasting (Wiley)
extra.full_text: Forecast evaluation in finance has relied on aggregate accuracy metrics and predictive-accuracy tests built on point-forecast errors.

title: CoGE: Sim-to-Real Online Geometric Estimation for Monocular Colonoscopy
summary: CoGE targets monocular colonoscopy, where estimating depth and reconstructing the scene from a single camera can give surgeons 3D spatial awareness for navigation. It focuses on sim-to-real online geometric estimation, suggesting a method that adapts geometric cues learned or modeled in simulation to real colonoscopy video during use.

extra.full_text: Geometric estimation including depth estimation and scene reconstruction is a crucial technique for colonoscopy which can provide surgeons with 3D spatial perception and navigation.

title: Revisiting Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards from a Contrastive Perspective
summary: GRPO is recast as a discriminative objective: a weighted score difference between positive and negative samples, giving a contrastive view of why reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can improve LLM reasoning. That reformulation makes the mechanics of RLVR more explicit and suggests its gains can be understood through how the model separates rewarded from unrewarded outputs rather than only through the usual policy-optimization lens.

extra.full_text: RLVR has become a widely adopted paradigm for improving LLMs' reasoning capabilities, and GRPO is one of its most representative algorithms. In this paper, we first show that GRPO admits an equivalent discriminative reformulation as a weighted positive-negative score difference.

title: ChipMATE: Multi-Agent Training via Reinforcement Learning for Enhanced RTL Generation
summary: ChipMATE targets RTL generation in settings closer to real chip design flows, where vendors may not have golden testbenches available during generation and cannot send proprietary code to closed API models. It frames RTL coding as a trainable multi-agent reinforcement learning problem, aiming to let organizations fine-tune open, deployable agents on internal RTL corpora while respecting air-gapped security constraints.

extra.full_text: Existing API-based agentic systems for RTL code generation are fundamentally misaligned with industrial practice: they assume a golden testbench is available at generation time, rely on closed-source APIs incompatible with chip vendors' air-gapped security requirements, and cannot be trained on vendors' proprietary RTL codebases, leaving valuable internal data unused.

title: Training LLMs with Reinforcement Learning for Intent-Aware Personalized Question Answering
summary: The paper frames personalized question answering as a problem of inferring the user’s implicit intent, not just matching the literal query text. It trains LLMs with reinforcement learning to produce answers grounded in that inferred “why,” aiming to make responses better aligned with individual needs and context.

extra.full_text: Effective personalized question answering (PQA) in language models requires grounding responses in the user's underlying intent, where intent refers to the implicit ``why'' behind a query beyond its explicit wording.

title: COSMIC: Concurrent Optimization of Structure, Material, and Integrated Control for robotic systems
summary: COSMIC targets robot co-design by optimizing structure, material, and integrated control together rather than treating body design and controller design as separate stages. The motivating idea is closer to biological co-evolution: autonomy can improve when a robot’s morphology, physical properties, and control policy are searched jointly instead of patched together after the fact.

extra.full_text: Replicating and surpassing the autonomy of natural organisms remains a long-standing goal in robotics. Yet most robotic systems have their structure, materials, and control designed separately, in sharp contrast to the co-evolution in nature.

title: QAP-Router: Tackling Qubit Routing as Dynamic Quadratic Assignment with Reinforcement Learning
summary: QAP-Router frames qubit routing as a dynamic Quadratic Assignment Problem, using reinforcement learning to make routing decisions that account for how local swaps affect later compilation steps. The interesting angle is treating routing as a sequential global optimization problem rather than a series of greedy local fixes, targeting the NP-hard behavior that makes efficient quantum circuit mapping difficult.

extra.full_text: Qubit routing is a fundamental problem in quantum compilation, known to be NP-hard. Its dynamic nature makes local routing decisions propagate and compound over time, making global efficient solutions challenging.

title: PriorZero: Bridging Language Priors and World Models for Decision Making
summary: PriorZero aims to use the world knowledge embedded in large language models to improve reinforcement learning agents’ decision-making. From the available text, it appears to focus on connecting language-derived priors with learned world models, so an RL agent can use broad commonsense or task knowledge rather than relying only on trial-and-error experience.
