extra.full_text: Leveraging the rich world knowledge of Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents offers a promising path toward general intelligence.

title: Transferable Delay-Aware Reinforcement Learning via Implicit Causal Graph Modeling
summary: Transferable Delay-Aware Reinforcement Learning via Implicit Causal Graph Modeling tackles the problem that random delays blur which actions actually caused later state changes, making standard temporal credit assignment unreliable. It appears to model delayed action effects through an implicit causal graph so a policy can learn the underlying propagation structure and transfer more robustly across delay conditions.

extra.full_text: Random delays weaken the temporal correspondence between actions and subsequent state feedback, making it difficult for agents to identify the true propagation process of action effects.

title: Simulation Distillation: Pretraining World Models in Simulation for Rapid Real-World Adaptation
summary: Simulation Distillation pretrains robot world models in simulation so they can adapt quickly when exposed to small, imperfect batches of real interaction data. The target setting is long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation, where directly finetuning policies tends to be sample-inefficient and fragile, so the interesting move is to transfer structured predictive dynamics rather than relying on end-to-end policy updates alone.

extra.full_text: Robot learning requires adaptation methods that improve reliably from limited, mixed-quality interaction data. This is especially challenging in long-horizon, contact-rich tasks, where end-to-end policy finetuning remains inefficient and brittle.

title: High-lift Wing Separation Control via Bayesian Optimization and Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Wall-resolved LES is used to study active flow control on a 30P30N high-lift wing at Rec = 450,000 and 23 degrees angle of attack, targeting separation control under demanding high-lift conditions. The interesting angle is the pairing of Bayesian optimization with deep reinforcement learning to search control strategies, suggesting a route from expensive simulation-based flow physics toward automated actuator policies.

extra.full_text: This study investigates active flow control (AFC) of a 30P30N high-lift wing at a Reynolds number Re$_c$ = 450,000 and angle of attack $α$ = 23$^\circ$ using wallresolved large-eddy simulations (LES).

title: When Simulation Lies: A Sim-to-Real Benchmark and Domain-Randomized RL Recipe for Tool-Use Agents
summary: Tool-use language agents are tested under assumptions that often break in deployment: clean inputs, clear tool registries, and dependable APIs. This arXiv paper frames that gap as a sim-to-real problem for tool use, introducing a benchmark and a domain-randomized reinforcement learning recipe aimed at making agents more robust when simulated tool environments misrepresent real-world messiness.

extra.comment: Dataset, code, and benchmark leaderboard are available at https://github.com/WillChow66/robustbench-tc-release.git and https://huggingface.co/spaces/willchow66/robustbench-tc-leaderboard
extra.full_text: Tool-use language agents are evaluated on benchmarks that assume clean inputs, unambiguous tool registries, and reliable APIs.

title: Beyond Imitation: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning for Adaptive Diffusion Navigation Policies
summary: Diffusion navigation policies can already map raw visual observations directly to multi-modal robot trajectories, avoiding the usual localization, mapping, and planning stack while benefiting from large imitation datasets. This work pushes that setup beyond static imitation by fine-tuning the diffusion policy with reinforcement learning, aiming to make navigation behavior adapt better when deployment conditions or task demands differ from the demonstrations.

extra.full_text: Diffusion-based robot navigation policies trained on large-scale imitation learning datasets, can generate multi-modal trajectories directly from the robot's visual observations, bypassing the traditional localization-mapping-planning pipeline and achieving strong zero-shot generalization.

title: Active Sensing with Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Emitter Localization from RF Observations
summary: Meta-reinforcement learning is used to drive active sensing for localizing RF emitters that disrupt GNSS, targeting settings where indoor structure and multipath make passive localization unreliable. The approach learns how to choose sensing actions from RF observations so an agent can adapt its search strategy to new emitter configurations, framing interference localization as a sequential decision problem rather than a fixed estimation pipeline.

extra.full_text: Global navigation satellite system (GNSS) interference poses a serious threat to reliable positioning, especially in indoor and multipath-rich environments where source localization is highly challenging.

title: Skill1: Unified Evolution of Skill-Augmented Agents via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Skill1 trains language-model agents to manage a persistent skill library end to end, learning when to retrieve an existing skill, how to apply it during task execution, and how to distill new reusable skills from experience. The interesting part is that these normally separate steps are optimized together with reinforcement learning, so the agent’s repertoire can evolve as it encounters new tasks rather than remaining a static prompt bank.

extra.full_text: A persistent skill library allows language model agents to reuse successful strategies across tasks. Maintaining such a library requires three coupled capabilities. The agent selects a relevant skill, utilizes it during execution, and distills new skills from experience.

title: Adaptive TD-Lambda for Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Adaptive TD-Lambda targets cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning by tuning the TD(λ) trade-off between Monte Carlo returns and bootstrapped value estimates instead of treating λ as a fixed hyperparameter. The idea is to reduce bias and variance in value or critic learning for value-based and actor-critic MARL methods, but the provided text does not include the adaptation rule, experimental setup, or reported results.

extra.full_text: TD($λ$) in value-based MARL algorithms or the Temporal Difference critic learning in Actor-Critic-based (AC-based) algorithms synergistically integrate elements from Monte-Carlo simulation and Q function bootstrapping via dynamic programming, which effectively addresses the inherent bias-variance trade-off in value estimation.

title: Rainbow Deep Q-Learning with Kinematics-Aware Design for Cooperative Delta and 3-RRS Parallel Robot Insertion
summary: Rainbow Deep Q-learning is applied to cooperative peg-in-hole insertion with two parallel manipulators: a Delta robot and a 3-RRS arm. The interesting part is the kinematics-aware design, which folds the robots’ parallel mechanisms into the reinforcement-learning setup rather than treating control as a generic black-box policy-learning problem.

extra.full_text: This paper presents a kinematics-aware deep reinforcement learning framework based on Rainbow Deep Q-Networks (DQN) for cooperative peg-in-hole manipulation by a Delta parallel robot and a 3-RRS (Revolute--Revolute--Spherical) parallel manipulator.

title: Priority-Driven Control and Communication in Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Priority-driven control and communication uses reinforcement learning to learn event-triggered policies for decentralized multi-agent systems when accurate dynamics models are not available. The approach targets bandwidth-limited networked agents, deciding when communication is worth spending rather than relying on fixed or model-based triggering rules.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 23rd IFAC World Congress
extra.full_text: Event-triggered control provides a mechanism for avoiding excessive use of constrained communication bandwidth in networked multi-agent systems. However, most existing methods rely on accurate system models, which may be unavailable in practice.

title: Value-Decomposed Reinforcement Learning Framework for Taxiway Routing with Hierarchical Conflict-Aware Observations
summary: Taxiway routing is framed as a reinforcement-learning problem where aircraft movement decisions and surface conflict avoidance are handled together rather than as separate steps. The approach uses value decomposition with hierarchical conflict-aware observations, so individual routing choices can reflect both local taxiway context and broader interaction risks among aircraft on the airport surface.

extra.full_text: Taxiway routing and on-surface conflict avoidance are coupled safety-critical decision problems in airport surface operations.

title: Newton's Lantern: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Finetuning AC Power Flow Warm Start Models
summary: Newton's Lantern targets AC power flow solvers by finetuning neural warm-start models with reinforcement learning rather than relying only on supervised imitation. The point is to produce initial guesses that keep Newton-Raphson iteration counts low even on heavily loaded grid cases near voltage collapse, where supervised warm starts tend to fail to generalize.

extra.full_text: Neural warm starts can sharply reduce the number of Newton-Raphson iterations required to solve the AC power flow problem, but existing supervised approaches generalize poorly on heavily loaded instances near voltage collapse.

title: RoboMemArena: A Comprehensive and Challenging Robotic Memory Benchmark
summary: RoboMemArena is a benchmark for testing how well robotic systems use memory when tasks stretch over time and the robot cannot observe everything it needs at once. It focuses on long-horizon behavior where past observations and actions must be retained and reused, making it a targeted stress test for a capability that standard robot benchmarks often under-specify.

extra.full_text: Memory is a critical component of robotic intelligence, as robots must rely on past observations and actions to accomplish long-horizon tasks in partially observable environments.

title: Dynamic Skill Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Agentic reinforcement learning systems are starting to treat external skills as modular tools that can be acquired, reused, and retired rather than static add-ons baked into a model. Dynamic Skill Lifecycle Management appears to focus on managing that process over time, so an agent can keep its skill set aligned with changing tasks instead of relying only on parametric memory or a fixed tool library.

extra.comment: Implementation code is available at https://github.com/ejhshen/SLIM
extra.full_text: Large language model agents increasingly rely on external skills to solve complex tasks, where skills act as modular units that extend their capabilities beyond what parametric memory alone supports.

title: Equivariant Reinforcement Learning for Clifford Quantum Circuit Synthesis
summary: Equivariant reinforcement learning is used to synthesize Clifford quantum circuits for all-to-all connected devices, exploiting symmetries in the circuit synthesis problem rather than treating each qubit configuration independently. The available text does not give the learning setup, benchmarks, or quantitative results, so the concrete takeaway is that it frames Clifford circuit synthesis as an RL problem structured by equivariance to improve generalization or search efficiency.

extra.full_text: We consider the problem of synthesizing Clifford quantum circuits for devices with all-to-all qubit connectivity.

title: DeepRefine: Agent-Compiled Knowledge Refinement via Reinforcement Learning
summary: DeepRefine targets the problem of keeping agent-compiled knowledge bases useful for LLM agents on open-ended, knowledge-intensive tasks. It frames knowledge refinement as a reinforcement-learning process, so an agent can improve persistent external knowledge rather than merely retrieve or append to it, but the provided text does not include details on the training setup, benchmarks, or results.

extra.full_text: Agent-compiled knowledge bases provide persistent external knowledge for large language model (LLM) agents in open-ended, knowledge-intensive downstream tasks.

title: Neural Co-state Policies: Structuring Hidden States in Recurrent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Neural Co-state Policies targets reinforcement learning under partial observability by structuring the hidden state of recurrent policies rather than treating it as an opaque memory vector. From the title and abstract snippet, the idea is to give recurrent agents a more principled internal representation for tracking missing state information while acting from incomplete observations.

extra.full_text: A key capability of intelligent agents is operating under partial observability: reasoning and acting effectively despite missing or incomplete state observations.

title: HyperEyes: Dual-Grained Efficiency-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Parallel Multimodal Search Agents
summary: HyperEyes targets multimodal search queries that break into independent entity lookups, replacing the usual one-entity-at-a-time tool loop with a parallel agent that can issue multiple searches while avoiding redundant interaction rounds. Its dual-grained, efficiency-aware reinforcement learning setup appears designed to decide both how to decompose the query and how aggressively to parallelize retrieval, trading off answer quality against tool-call and latency costs.

extra.full_text: Existing multimodal search agents process target entities sequentially, issuing one tool call per entity and accumulating redundant interaction rounds whenever a query decomposes into independent sub-retrievals.

title: Balancing Efficiency and Fairness in Traffic Light Control through Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Deep reinforcement learning is used to adapt traffic light control to changing urban traffic conditions, targeting both network efficiency and fairness rather than optimizing only aggregate delay or throughput. From the provided text, the paper frames the problem as a response to the brittleness of fixed or traditional signal plans under dynamic congestion, but it does not give enough detail here to identify the specific DRL algorithm, evaluation setup, or quantitative results.

extra.comment: Paper accepted to the 2026 IFAC World Congress, held in Busan (KOR), August 23rd-28th, 2026
extra.full_text: Urban traffic congestion presents a significant challenge for modern cities, which impacts mobility and sustainability. Traditional traffic light control systems often fail to adapt to dynamic conditions, leading to inefficiencies.

title: Learning Tactile-Aware Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation Policies
summary: Quadrupedal loco-manipulation is framed around the missing contact information that vision and proprioception cannot reliably infer during evolving, contact-rich interactions. The work learns tactile-aware locomotion-manipulation policies, using touch as an additional feedback channel so a quadruped can better handle uncertain physical contact with its environment.

extra.full_text: Quadrupedal loco-manipulation is commonly built on visual perception and proprioception. Yet reliable contact-rich manipulation remains difficult: vision and proprioception alone cannot resolve uncertain, evolving interactions with the environment.

title: Skill-R1: Agent Skill Evolution via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Skill-R1 treats agent skills as the thing to optimize directly, using reinforcement learning to evolve reusable natural-language procedures rather than fine-tuning or repeatedly prompt-engineering the underlying LLM. That makes the approach potentially useful for improving planning, tool use, and action policies even when the task model is closed-source or expensive to adapt.

extra.full_text: Agentic large language models often rely on skills, reusable natural language procedures that guide planning, action, and tool use. In practice, skills are typically improved through prompt engineering or by aligning the task LLM itself, which is costly, model-specific, and often infeasible for closed-source models.

title: SKG-VLA: Scene Knowledge Graph Priors for Structured Scene Semantics and Multimodal Reasoning for Decision Making
summary: SKG-VLA appears to use scene knowledge graph priors to give a vision-language-action system more structured semantic understanding of a scene, so its decisions can draw on object relations and multimodal reasoning rather than only raw visual-language features. The provided text is sparse and oddly centered on complaint-handling evidence rather than robot experiments, so the safest read is that the work targets decision making over heterogeneous inputs and emphasizes structured representations for more interpretable reasoning.

extra.full_text: Decision making in large-scale complaint handling systems increasingly relies on heterogeneous evidence, including complaint narratives, screenshots, order metadata, historical interactions, and platform policies.

title: AssemLM: Spatial Reasoning Multimodal Large Language Models for Robotic Assembly
summary: AssemLM targets the spatial reasoning bottleneck in robotic assembly, where a model has to understand fine-grained part relationships and manipulation-relevant geometry rather than just recognize objects. From the provided text, the work appears to frame assembly as a multimodal large-language-model problem for embodied agents, but the excerpt does not include the specific architecture, dataset, benchmark, or results needed to summarize its mechanism or performance more concretely.

extra.full_text: Spatial reasoning is a fundamental capability for embodied intelligence, especially for fine-grained manipulation tasks such as robotic assembly.

title: Reinforcement Learning Measurement Model
summary: Reinforcement Learning Measurement Model addresses interactive assessments where each learner’s sequence of actions carries information that conventional item response theory tends to discard. It appears to recast measurement around sequential process data, using a reinforcement-learning-style model to connect behavior over time with assessment outcomes.

extra.full_text: Interactive assessments generate sequential process data that are not well handled by conventional item response models.

title: When (and How) to Trust the Expert: Diagnosing Query-Time Expert-Guided Reinforcement Learning
summary: Continuous-control RL often starts with a decent but imperfect controller, such as a tuned PID or hand-designed gait, and this study examines when it helps or hurts to query that controller as an expert during learning. It diagnoses expert-guided RL methods under a shared lens, especially with suboptimal experts, aiming to clarify which query-time mechanisms actually improve learning rather than assuming the expert is always trustworthy.

extra.full_text: Many continuous-control problems ship with a competent but suboptimal controller (a tuned PID, a hand-designed gait). A growing family of methods uses such controllers as queryable experts during RL, but each method has been proposed in isolation, on a different benchmark, without imperfect-expert testing.

title: TiPToP: A Modular Open-Vocabulary Planning System for Robotic Manipulation
summary: TiPToP connects pretrained vision foundation models to an existing task-and-motion planner so a robot can turn RGB images and natural-language instructions into multi-step manipulation plans. Its appeal is the modular open-vocabulary setup: perception can ground objects and scene information from raw images, while the TAMP layer handles the symbolic and geometric planning needed to execute longer-horizon manipulation tasks.

extra.full_text: We present TiPToP, an extensible modular system that combines pretrained vision foundation models with an existing Task and Motion Planner (TAMP) to solve multi-step manipulation tasks directly from input RGB images and natural-language instructions.

title: LEGO: Latent-space Exploration for Geometry-aware Optimization of Humanoid Kinematic Design
summary: LEGO targets humanoid kinematic design by moving morphology search into a latent space where geometry-aware optimization can explore plausible body configurations more systematically than hand-tuned intuition. From the provided text, the concrete result details are not available, but the framing suggests a method for searching humanoid structures and joint layouts through learned or structured latent representations rather than direct manual design.

extra.full_text: Designing robot morphologies and kinematics has traditionally relied on human intuition, with little systematic foundation.

title: Octopus Protocol: One-Shot Hardware Discovery and Control for AI Agents via Infrastructure-as-Prompts
summary: Octopus Protocol treats hardware bring-up as an in-context discovery problem: an AI agent probes a device once, infers its interfaces and controllable functions, and turns that “infrastructure” into prompts rather than relying on prewritten drivers, SDKs, or ROS primitives. The interesting shift is that the expensive, hardware-specific control layer is generated on demand for new devices, aiming to let agentic robotics systems adapt to unfamiliar hardware without the usual manual primitive-writing bottleneck.

extra.full_text: Recent agentic-robotics systems, from Code-asPolicies to modern vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models, presuppose that drivers, SDKs, or ROS-style primitives for the target hardware already exist. Writing those primitives is the dominant engineering cost of bringing up new hardware for agent control.

title: Automated Robotic Moisture Monitoring in Agricultural Fields
summary: A robotic kit is paired with in-field moisture sensor circuits to automate soil moisture monitoring across large agricultural plantations. The system targets the labor and time cost of manually checking distributed field conditions, using a low-cost robot-and-sensor setup to collect moisture information more efficiently.

extra.comment: 2018 International Seminar on Intelligent Technology and Its Applications (ISITIA)
extra.full_text: Monitoring moisture level of land in a large-scale plantation is tedious. The main objective of this project is to use a robotic kit in collaboration with the on-field moisture sensor circuits, thereby creating an efficient and economical moisture monitoring system.

title: APPLV: Adaptive Planner Parameter Learning from Vision-Language-Action Model
summary: APPLV targets mobile robot navigation in tight, constrained spaces by using a vision-language-action model to adapt the parameters of a classical planner instead of relying on fixed, hand-tuned settings. It sits between safety-oriented traditional navigation and end-to-end learning: the planner keeps structured control behavior, while learned perception and reasoning adjust it to the current environment.

extra.full_text: Autonomous navigation in highly constrained environments remains challenging for mobile robots. Classical navigation approaches offer safety assurances but require environment-specific parameter tuning; end-to-end learning bypasses parameter tuning but struggles with precise control in constrained spaces.

title: Hierarchical Prompting with Dual LLM Modules for Robotic Task and Motion Planning
summary: Hierarchical Prompting with Dual LLM Modules splits robotic task-and-motion planning into two language-driven layers, aiming to make service and assistance robots easier to direct through natural human instructions. From the available description, it appears to use separate LLM modules to structure high-level task reasoning and lower-level motion planning, but no benchmark, implementation details, or results are provided here.

extra.full_text: We present a hierarchical language-driven framework for robotic task and motion planning to improve natural, intuitive human-robot interaction in service and assistance scenarios.

title: OmniGuide: Universal Guidance Fields for Enhancing Generalist Robot Policies
summary: OmniGuide targets the gap between broad VLA robot policies and the harder manipulation cases where they struggle, such as cluttered scenes, precise placement, and tasks needing richer spatial or semantic reasoning. It does so by adding “universal guidance fields” that can steer a generalist policy toward better task execution without replacing the underlying policy, making the approach interesting as a modular way to upgrade existing VLA systems.

extra.full_text: Vision-language-action(VLA) models have shown great promise as generalist policies for a large range of relatively simple tasks. However, they demonstrate limited performance on more complex tasks, such as those requiring complex spatial or semantic understanding, manipulation in clutter, or precise manipulation.

title: Interpreting Reinforcement Learning Agents with Susceptibilities
summary: Susceptibilities are used here as an interpretability probe for reinforcement learning agents, measuring how posterior expectations of chosen observables shift when the training loss is perturbed. The idea is to expose which parts of an agent’s learned behavior or internal quantities are most sensitive to objective-level changes, giving a more mechanistic view than simply inspecting rewards or policies.

extra.full_text: Susceptibilities are a technique for neural network interpretability that studies the response of posterior expectation values of observables to perturbations of the loss.

title: Separation Assurance between Heterogeneous Fleets of Small Unmanned Aerial Systems via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Dense urban sUAS traffic is modeled as heterogeneous fleets, where each operator’s aircraft share the same configuration and policy but differ across fleets in sensing, communication, and equipage. The paper uses multi-agent reinforcement learning for tactical separation assurance, aiming to learn deconfliction behavior that can handle interactions among multiple independently operated fleets rather than assuming a single homogeneous aircraft population.

extra.full_text: In the envisioned future dense urban airspace, multiple companies will operate heterogeneous fleets of small unmanned aerial systems (sUASs), where each fleet includes several homogeneous aircraft with identical policies and configurations, e.g., equipage, sensing, and communication ranges, making tactical deconfliction highly complex for the aircraft.

title: CommandSwarm: Safety-Aware Natural Language-to-Behavior-Tree Generation for Robotic Swarms
summary: CommandSwarm targets natural-language control of robot swarms by translating operator instructions into executable behavior trees while checking for unsupported actions, malformed structures, and unsafe plans. The interesting part is the safety-aware generation layer: it treats language-to-policy translation as a constrained program synthesis problem for multi-robot behavior, rather than simply asking a model to emit swarm commands directly.

extra.full_text: Natural-language interfaces can make swarm robotics more accessible to non-expert operators, but they must translate ambiguous user intent into executable swarm behaviors without unsupported actions, malformed programs, or unsafe plans.

title: PhySPRING: Structure-Preserving Reduction of Physics-Informed Twins via GNN
summary: PhySPRING uses graph neural networks to reduce physics-informed digital twins while preserving the structure needed to predict object dynamics under interaction. It targets robotics settings where a compact twin must still support reliable real-to-sim-to-real reasoning, but the provided text does not include benchmark results or quantitative performance details.

extra.full_text: Physics-based digital twins aim to predict the dynamics of real-world objects under interaction, enabling real-to-sim-to-real applications in robotics.

title: ExpThink: Experience-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Chain-of-Thought Compression
summary: ExpThink targets the token and latency overhead of long chain-of-thought reasoning in large reasoning models by using experience-guided reinforcement learning to adaptively compress reasoning traces. Rather than applying a fixed shortening rule, it learns when and how much CoT can be compressed while preserving task performance, aiming to make extended reasoning cheaper at inference time.

extra.comment: 39 pages, 18 figures. Code and model checkpoints will be released upon publication
extra.full_text: Large reasoning models (LRMs) achieve strong performance via extended chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, yet suffer from excessive token consumption and high inference latency.

title: LiteGUI: Distilling Compact GUI Agents with Reinforcement Learning
summary: LiteGUI targets lightweight vision-language agents that can run on-device for cross-platform GUI automation. It focuses on improving compact agents despite limited model capacity, using reinforcement learning and distillation to make them more capable for automated interface interaction.

extra.full_text: Developing lightweight, on-device vision-language GUI agents is essential for efficient cross-platform automated interaction. However, current on-device agents are constrained by limited model capacity, and further performance improvements remain urgently needed.

title: RELO: Reinforcement Learning to Localize for Visual Object Tracking
summary: RELO recasts target localization in visual object tracking as a reinforcement learning problem, replacing handcrafted heatmap-style spatial priors with direct optimization toward tracking metrics like IoU and AUC. The appeal is that the localization policy is trained against the same kind of overlap-based objective used to judge trackers, rather than a surrogate signal that may not line up with final tracking performance.

extra.full_text: Conventional visual object trackers localize targets using handcrafted spatial priors, often in the form of heatmaps. Such priors provide only surrogate supervision and are poorly aligned with tracking optimization and evaluation metrics, such as intersection over union (IoU) and area under the success curve (AUC).

title: SparseRL-Sync: Lossless Weight Synchronization with ~100x Less Communication
summary: SparseRL-Sync targets distributed RL setups where policy weights must be pushed from trainer nodes to rollout workers often enough to avoid stale behavior. It compresses those synchronizations by sending sparse weight updates while preserving exact reconstruction, aiming for roughly 100x less communication without changing the resulting model weights.

extra.comment: Code will be released at https://github.com/scitix/helix
extra.full_text: In large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) systems with decoupled Trainer-Rollout execution, the Trainer must regularly synchronize policy weights to the Rollout side to limit policy staleness. When inter-node bandwidth is abundant, such synchronization is usually only a small fraction of end-to-end cost.

title: Preference-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Space-Time Efficient Online 3D Bin Packing
summary: Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning is applied to online 3D bin packing, where a robot must choose placements as items arrive while balancing spatial efficiency against time or execution cost. The available excerpt only establishes the warehouse automation setting and the paper’s focus, so the substantive claim is that packing behavior is conditioned on user or task preferences rather than optimized for a single fixed objective.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation 2026. Project Website: https://step-packing.github.io
extra.full_text: Robotic bin packing is widely deployed in warehouse automation, with current systems achieving robust performance through heuristic and learning-based strategies.

title: Revisiting Adam for Streaming Reinforcement Learning
summary: Revisiting Adam for Streaming Reinforcement Learning looks at how adaptive optimization behaves when an agent learns online from each interaction without storing or replaying experience. The paper focuses on Adam in the streaming RL setting, aiming to clarify when its update mechanics help or hurt compared with more conventional choices for continual, sample-by-sample learning.

extra.full_text: Learning from a sequence of interactions, as soon as observations are perceived and acted upon, without explicitly storing them, holds the promise of simpler, more efficient and adaptive algorithms.

title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction
summary: StraTA targets long-horizon LLM agents by moving beyond step-by-step reactive optimization toward strategic trajectory abstraction, so the agent can reason over higher-level patterns in its behavior rather than only local actions. The motivation is that better abstractions over trajectories should improve exploration and make credit assignment less brittle when rewards depend on decisions made far earlier in an interaction.

extra.full_text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as interactive agents, but optimizing them for long-horizon decision making remains difficult because current methods are largely purely reactive, which weakens both exploration and credit assignment over extended trajectories.

title: Cross-Modal Navigation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Cross-Modal Navigation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning tackles embodied navigation when sensory inputs are complementary but hard to align cleanly across modalities. Instead of training one large policy over all inputs, it frames the problem as a multi-agent reinforcement learning setup, letting modality-specific agents handle richer sensory streams while reducing the burden on a single monolithic representation.

extra.full_text: Robust embodied navigation relies on complementary sensory cues. However, high-quality and well-aligned multi-modal data is often difficult to obtain in practice. Training a monolithic model is also challenging as rich multi-modal inputs induce complex representations and substantially enlarge the policy space.

title: Sequential Design of Genetic Circuits Under Uncertainty With Reinforcement Learning
summary: Sequential reinforcement learning is used to choose genetic-circuit design experiments while accounting for both stochastic biomolecular reactions and shifts across lab or experimental conditions. The setup treats circuit optimization as an uncertain, step-by-step decision problem, aiming to make design choices that remain useful when the underlying biology and measurement context vary.

extra.full_text: The design of biological systems is hindered by uncertainty arising from both intrinsic stochasticity of biomolecular reactions and variability across laboratory or experimental conditions. In this work, we present a sequential framework to optimize genetic circuits under both forms of uncertainty.

title: Grounding Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models Through Explicit Language-Action Alignment
summary: Grounding Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models Through Explicit Language-Action Alignment focuses on making robot explanations and instructions line up with what the robot actually does in its environment. The idea is to add explicit alignment between language and low-level actions inside a hierarchical vision-language-action model, so the robot’s natural-language communication is grounded in both task structure and observed behavior rather than being a detached commentary.

extra.full_text: Achieving robot transparency is a critical step toward effective human-robot collaboration. To be transparent, a robot's natural language communication must be consistent with its actions and explicitly grounded in the task and environment.

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Rotation Profile Control in Tokamaks
summary: Offline reinforcement learning is used to learn tokamak plasma rotation-profile controllers from existing data, targeting a control problem that matters for stability, confinement, and transport but is hard to solve with hand-designed policies. The framing is interesting because it treats rotation control as a data-driven sequential decision problem, aiming to improve profiles without requiring risky online exploration in an operating fusion device.

extra.full_text: Tokamaks remain leading candidates for achieving practical fusion energy, yet many important control problems inside these devices are still difficult or unsolved. One such challenge is controlling the plasma rotation profile, which strongly influences stability, confinement, and transport.

title: RoboPlayground: Democratizing Robotic Evaluation through Structured Physical Domains
summary: RoboPlayground targets a bottleneck in robot manipulation evaluation: benchmarks are usually fixed, expert-authored sets of tasks with hard-coded instances, constraints, and success rules. It frames evaluation around structured physical domains, aiming to make it easier for broader users to define, vary, and extend manipulation tests rather than relying on a small set of static benchmark designs.

extra.comment: Yi Ru Wang and Carter Ung contributed equally
extra.full_text: Evaluation of robotic manipulation systems has largely relied on fixed benchmarks authored by a small number of experts, where task instances, constraints, and success criteria are predefined and difficult to extend.

title: GaussFly: Contrastive Reinforcement Learning for Visuomotor Policies in 3D Gaussian Fields
summary: GaussFly targets monocular visuomotor control for autonomous aerial vehicles, framing flight policy learning around contrastive reinforcement learning in 3D Gaussian fields. From the provided text, the concrete setup is a vision-only AAV policy learning problem where the interesting angle is using an explicit 3D Gaussian scene representation to support control from a single camera.

extra.full_text: Learning visuomotor policies for Autonomous Aerial Vehicles (AAVs) relying solely on monocular vision is an attractive yet highly challenging paradigm.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Compositional Generalization with Outcome-Level Optimization
summary: Reinforcement learning is used here to target compositional generalization at the outcome level, rather than training models mainly to imitate supervised target outputs. The setup is aimed at helping models correctly handle new combinations of familiar primitives, addressing a failure mode where standard fine-tuning can learn surface patterns without reliably composing known parts in unfamiliar ways.

extra.full_text: Compositional generalization refers to correctly interpret novel combinations of known primitives, which remains a major challenge. Existing approaches often rely on supervised fine-tuning, which encourages models to imitate target outputs.

title: Reward-Decomposed Reinforcement Learning for Immersive Video Role-Playing
summary: Reward-Decomposed Reinforcement Learning trains role-playing agents to optimize separate rewards for character style, scene atmosphere, and evolving tension, rather than treating dialogue quality as a single undifferentiated signal. It targets immersive video and VR role-playing settings where an agent needs to stay in character while also responding to the emotional pacing and ambience of the scene.

extra.full_text: Text-based role-playing models can imitate character styles, yet they often fail to reflect a scene's atmosphere and evolving tension, both essential for immersive applications such as Virtual Reality (VR) games and interactive narratives.

title: Maximizing Rollout Informativeness under a Fixed Budget: A Submodular View of Tree Search for Tool-Use Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Rollout Informativeness under a Fixed Budget (RIFB) measures how much useful, non-vanishing policy-gradient signal a fixed set of tool-use rollouts contributes to GRPO training. The paper frames rollout selection for tree-search-based tool-use agents through a submodular optimization lens, suggesting that the structure of informativeness can guide budgeted search toward rollouts that matter most for reinforcement learning.

extra.full_text: We formalize Rollout Informativeness under a Fixed Budget (RIFB) as the expected non-vanishing policy-gradient mass that a tool-use rollout set injects into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).

title: SkiP: When to Skip and When to Refine for Efficient Robot Manipulation
summary: SkiP makes imitation-learned robot policies faster by treating long, low-information free-space motion differently from contact-heavy moments like grasping, alignment, and insertion. Its action relabeling scheme trains the policy to jump directly to the next key segment during redundant stretches, then predict densely inside key segments identified automatically from motion complexity via Motion Spectrum Keying. Across 72 simulated manipulation tasks and three real-robot tasks, it cuts executed steps by 15-40% while preserving or improving success rates across several policy backbones.

extra.full_text: Previous imitation learning policies predict future actions at every control step, whether in smooth motion phases or precise, contact-rich operation phases. This uniform treatment is wasteful: most steps in a manipulation trajectory traverse free space and carry little task-relevant information, while a small fraction of \emph{key} steps around contacts, grasps, and alignment demand dense, high-resolution prediction. We propose a novel \emph{action relabeling} mechanism: at each timestep in a skip segment, we replace the behavior cloning target with the action at the entrance of the next key segment, enabling the policy to leap over redundant steps in a single decision. The resulting \textbf{Skip Policy (SkiP)} dynamically leaps over skip segments and intensively refines actions in key segments, within a single unified network requiring no learned skip planner or hierarchical structure. To automatically partition demonstrations into key and skip segments without manual annotation, we introduce \emph{Motion Spectrum Keying} (MSK), a fast, task-agnostic procedure that detects local motion complexity from action signals. Extensive experiments across 72 simulated manipulation tasks and three real-robot tasks show that SkiP reduces executed steps by $15$--$40\%$ while matching or improving success rates across various policy backbones. extra.full_text: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled effective perception and language models for robots, but their deployment remains computationally expensive, increasing latency and energy use.

title: A Benchmark of Dexterity for Anthropomorphic Robotic Hands
summary: A Benchmark of Dexterity for Anthropomorphic Robotic Hands targets the messy way “dexterity” is used across robotic-hand papers, where different hands are often judged by incompatible task sets and criteria. It frames dexterity as something that needs a shared benchmark for anthropomorphic hands, so researchers can compare designs more meaningfully instead of relying on loosely matched demonstrations or ad hoc evaluations.

extra.full_text: Dexterity is a central yet ambiguously defined concept in the design and evaluation of anthropomorphic robotic hands. In practice, the term is often used inconsistently, with different systems evaluated under disparate criteria, making meaningful comparisons across designs difficult.

title: A Soft Robotic Interface for Chick-Robot Affective Interactions
summary: An animal-centered soft robotic affective interface is designed for newly hatched chicks, targeting the core ARI requirement that the animal find the robot socially relevant, non-threatening, and potentially attractive. The work frames acceptance as the central design problem for welfare-oriented chick-robot interaction, using a soft body and affective interaction cues to make the robot better suited to early-life social engagement.

extra.full_text: The potential of Animal-Robot Interaction (ARI) in welfare applications depends on how much an animal perceives a robotic agent as socially relevant, non-threatening and potentially attractive (acceptance). Here, we present an animal-centered soft robotic affective interface for newly hatched chicks (Gallus gallus).

title: The Sustainability Gap in Robotics: A Large-Scale Survey of Sustainability Awareness in 50,000 Research Articles
summary: A large-scale survey examines how robotics papers talk about sustainability, using nearly 50,000 open-access arXiv cs.RO articles published from 2015 through early 2026. It treats sustainability as both a communication and motivation signal across the literature, giving researchers a broad view of how often environmental or societal concerns appear in robotics research and where the field’s stated priorities may lag behind sustainability needs.

extra.full_text: We present a large-scale survey of sustainability communication and motivation in robotics research. Our analysis covers nearly 50,000 open-access papers from arXiv's cs.RO category published between 2015 and early 2026.

title: REAP: Reinforcement-Learning End-to-End Autonomous Parking with Gaussian Splatting Simulator for Real2Sim2Real Transfer
summary: REAP targets the brittle edge cases in autonomous parking, especially mechanical and dead-end slots where conventional systems often fail. It uses reinforcement learning with an end-to-end policy trained through a Gaussian Splatting simulator, aiming for Real2Sim2Real transfer so behaviors learned in simulation can carry back to real parking scenarios.

extra.full_text: In recent years, autonomous parking has made significant advances, yet parking tasks still face challenges in extreme scenarios such as mechanical and dead-end parking slots, often resulting in failures.

title: CONTACT: CONtact-aware TACTile Learning for Robotic Disassembly
summary: CONTACT studies robotic disassembly as a tactile, contact-driven manipulation problem, where success depends on sensing force-mediated state changes rather than just aligning parts geometrically. The available description frames it around learning from tactile contact during disassembly, but does not provide enough detail to summarize the specific model, experiments, or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Robotic disassembly involves contact-rich interactions in which successful manipulation depends not only on geometric alignment but also on force-dependent state transitions.

title: Sustainable Transfer Learning for Adaptive Robot Skills
summary: Investigates whether reinforcement-learning policies for peg-in-hole insertion can be transferred across different robot platforms instead of relearning each skill from scratch. The emphasis is on sample efficiency and sustainability: reusing prior robot data to reduce training time while adapting manipulation skills to new hardware.

extra.full_text: Learning robot skills from scratch is often time-consuming, while reusing data promotes sustainability and improves sample efficiency. This study investigates policy transfer across different robotic platforms, focusing on peg-in-hole task using reinforcement learning (RL).

title: Search-based Robustness Testing of Laptop Refurbishing Robotic Software
summary: The Danish Technological Institute is examining search-based robustness testing for robotic software used in laptop refurbishing, a setting where industrial robots need to handle variable, real-world repair and reuse workflows. The available description only identifies the application area and institutional context, so the concrete testing algorithm, evaluation setup, and results are not specified here.

extra.full_text: The Danish Technological Institute (DTI) focuses on transferring advanced technologies (including robots) to the industry and the public sector.

title: RichMap: A Reachability Map Balancing Precision, Efficiency, and Flexibility for Rich Robot Manipulation Tasks
summary: RichMap is a reachability-map representation for robot manipulation that aims to keep high-precision reachability information usable without making planning too slow or rigid. It is designed for richer manipulation settings where a robot needs flexible choices over poses or task constraints, rather than a coarse binary notion of whether a point is reachable.

extra.full_text: This paper presents RichMap, a high-precision reachability map representation designed to balance efficiency and flexibility for versatile robot manipulation tasks.

title: RK-MPC: Residual Koopman Model Predictive Control for Quadruped Locomotion in Offroad Environments
summary: RK-MPC uses a residual Koopman model inside model predictive control to give quadruped locomotion a more accurate learned dynamics predictor without making the controller too slow for real-time use. It is aimed at offroad terrain, where model mismatch matters, and the interesting part is the balance between data-driven fidelity and the computational constraints of MPC on a legged robot.

extra.full_text: This paper presents Residual Koopman MPC (RK-MPC), a Koopman-based, data-driven model predictive control framework for quadruped locomotion that improves prediction fidelity while preserving real-time tractability.

title: TouchDrive: Electronics-Free Tactile Sensing Interface for Assistive Grasping
summary: TouchDrive explores assistive robotic grasping with a tactile interface that avoids electronic sensors and complex processing pipelines. The idea is to make grasp feedback simpler and more accessible, targeting adaptive manipulation of diverse objects without the hardware and software overhead common in conventional sensing-based systems.

extra.comment: Accepted at ICRA 2026 workshop on Visuo-Tactile Perception, Learning, Control for Manipulation: Embodied Tactile Intelligence in Predictive Perception, Learning & Control in Grasping & Manipulation, Emerging the Role of Embodiment and Visuo -Tactile - LLM Foundation Models (ICRA RoboTac 2026)
extra.full_text: Assistive robotic grasping plays an important role in enabling safe and adaptive manipulation of diverse objects. However, existing systems often rely on electronic sensing and multi-stage processing pipelines, increasing system complexity and reducing accessibility.

title: A Comparative Study of INDI and NDI with Nonlinear Disturbance Observer for Aerial Robotics
summary: A simulation study compares Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion against Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion augmented with a nonlinear disturbance observer for fully actuated aerial robots. The focus is robustness under disturbances, asking whether INDI’s incremental feedback structure or NDI+NDO’s explicit disturbance estimation gives better behavior in challenging flight conditions.

extra.full_text: This work presents a simulation-based comparative robustness analysis of Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI) and Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion augmented with a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDI+NDO) for fully actuated aerial robots.

title: Resource-Constrained Robotic Planning in the face of Mixed Uncertainty
summary: Addresses robot planning when both measurable noise and hard-to-model unknowns affect execution, while resources such as energy, time, or budget remain tightly bounded. The focus is on making plans that remain feasible under mixed uncertainty rather than treating all uncertainty as a single probabilistic model, which is useful for robots operating outside well-characterized lab conditions.

extra.full_text: Robots operate under significant uncertainty, from quantifiable noise to unquantifiable unknowns, and must account for strict operational constraints, such as limited resources.

title: RoTri-Diff: A Spatial Robot-Object Triadic Interaction-Guided Diffusion Model for Bimanual Manipulation
summary: RoTri-Diff is a diffusion model for bimanual manipulation that centers the spatial triadic relationship among the two robot arms and the manipulated object, targeting the continuous coordination needed when both hands must act together. From the provided text, the concrete takeaway is its framing of dual-arm control around robot-object interaction structure rather than treating the two arms as independent action streams.

extra.full_text: Bimanual manipulation is a fundamental robotic skill that requires continuous and precise coordination between two arms.

title: ReinVBC: A Model-based Reinforcement Learning Approach to Vehicle Braking Controller
summary: ReinVBC applies model-based reinforcement learning to automate calibration of a vehicle braking controller, targeting a production process that normally depends on extensive manual tuning. From the provided text, the focus is on reducing engineering labor and calibration time while preserving braking performance tied to vehicle safety and steerability.

extra.full_text: Braking system, the key module to ensure the safety and steer-ability of current vehicles, relies on extensive manual calibration during production. Reducing labor and time consumption while maintaining the Vehicle Braking Controller (VBC) performance greatly benefits the vehicle industry.

title: Towards Considerate Human-Robot Coexistence: A Dual-Space Framework of Robot Design and Human Perception in Healthcare
summary: Robotics is framed here as a healthcare coexistence problem, linking how robots are designed with how people perceive and respond to them in shared clinical spaces. The dual-space framework appears to connect robot capabilities, interaction style, and workflow integration with human expectations and comfort, aiming to make healthcare robots feel more considerate rather than merely functional.

extra.full_text: The rapid advancement of robotics, spanning expanded capabilities, more intuitive interaction, and more integration into real-world workflows, is reshaping what it means for humans and robots to coexist.

title: A Contrastive Fewshot RGBD Traversability Segmentation Framework for Indoor Robotic Navigation
summary: Contrastive Fewshot RGBD Traversability Segmentation targets indoor navigation by segmenting safe free space from RGB-D input, with emphasis on obstacles that pure RGB models can miss, such as thin chair legs. It frames traversability as a few-shot segmentation problem and uses contrastive learning to make the model more robust when only limited labeled examples are available.

extra.full_text: Indoor traversability segmentation aims to identify safe, navigable free space for autonomous agents, which is critical for robotic navigation. Pure vision-based models often fail to detect thin obstacles, such as chair legs, which can pose serious safety risks.

title: Adapting Neural Robot Dynamics on the Fly for Predictive Control
summary: Adapts neural dynamics models online so a predictive controller can keep using learned robot dynamics as real-world conditions shift, rather than relying on an oversimplified physics model or retraining a data-heavy model from scratch. The interesting angle is the on-the-fly update loop for autonomous mobile robots, aimed at making model predictive control more accurate under effects that are hard to capture analytically.

extra.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
extra.full_text: Accurate dynamics models are critical for the design of predictive controller for autonomous mobile robots. Physics-based models are often too simple to capture relevant real-world effects, while data-driven models are data-intensive and slow to train.

title: From Prompt to Physical Action: Structured Backdoor Attacks on LLM-Mediated Robotic Control Systems
summary: LLMs are being inserted into robot-control loops as translators from natural-language prompts to executable actions, which creates a new attack surface between user intent and physical behavior. The paper studies structured backdoor attacks in this setting, where malicious trigger patterns in prompts can cause an LLM-mediated robot controller to produce attacker-chosen physical actions while otherwise appearing to behave normally.

extra.full_text: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into robotic control pipelines enables natural language interfaces that translate user prompts into executable commands.

title: COMB: Common Open Modular robotic platform for Bees
summary: COMB is an open, modular robotic platform designed to work inside real honeybee colonies, where hardware has to fit tight hive geometries, survive propolis and other fouling, and operate under colony-specific environmental constraints. It is built to combine sensing with localized actuation while letting researchers swap or adapt modules without redesigning the whole system for each experiment.

extra.full_text: Experimental access to real honeybee colonies requires robotic systems capable of operating within limited spatial constraints, tolerating hive-specific fouling and environmental conditions, and supporting both sensing and localized actuation without frequent hardware redesign.

title: Semantic Risk-Aware Heuristic Planning for Robotic Navigation in Dynamic Environments: An LLM-Inspired Approach
summary: Semantic Risk-Aware Heuristic Planning brings LLM-style semantic reasoning into classical robot navigation by using higher-level scene understanding to guide path planning under dynamic risk. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, so the clearest takeaway is that it sits at the intersection of symbolic/semantic reasoning and traditional motion planning, aiming to make robots choose safer routes in changing environments.

extra.comment: 5 pages, 5 figures. Experimental study on semantic risk-aware heuristic planning for robotic navigation
extra.full_text: The integration of Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning principles into classical robot path planning represents a rapidly emerging research direction.

title: Do We Really Need Immediate Resets? Rethinking Collision Handling for Efficient Robot Navigation
summary: Robot navigation training is often made brittle and sample-inefficient by treating any collision as an immediate episode-ending failure, and this paper questions that default reset rule. It reframes collision handling as something that can be managed within an episode rather than by globally restarting the environment, aiming to make deep RL navigation learn more efficiently from recoverable mistakes.

extra.full_text: Should a single collision necessarily terminate an entire navigation episode? In most deep reinforcement learning (DRL) frameworks for robot navigation, this remains the standard practice: every collision immediately triggers a global environment reset and is penalized as a complete task failure.

title: RoboMME: Benchmarking and Understanding Memory for Robotic Generalist Policies
summary: RoboMME is an arXiv benchmark focused on memory in robotic generalist policies, especially for long-horizon manipulation where the robot must retain history rather than react only to the current observation. It targets cases like counting repeated actions and handling objects that become temporarily occluded, making it a probe for whether a policy can use past context in history-dependent manipulation.

extra.full_text: Memory is critical for long-horizon and history-dependent robotic manipulation. Such tasks often involve counting repeated actions or manipulating objects that become temporarily occluded.

title: Safety-Critical Centralized Nonlinear MPC for Cooperative Payload Transportation by Two Quadrupedal Robots
summary: A centralized nonlinear model predictive controller coordinates two quadrupedal robots carrying a shared payload, with safety-critical constraints built into the control loop. From the available description, the emphasis is on cooperative whole-system planning for payload transport rather than treating each robot independently.

extra.full_text: This paper presents a safety-critical centralized nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) framework for cooperative payload transportation by two quadrupedal robots.

title: Cognition to Control - Multi-Agent Learning for Human-Humanoid Collaborative Transport
summary: Cognition to Control studies how a humanoid can turn a human partner’s high-level intent into stable whole-body motion during collaborative transport. It frames the problem as multi-agent learning, emphasizing continuous adaptation to the human while maintaining contact stability, but the provided excerpt does not include task setup details, benchmarks, or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Effective human-robot collaboration (HRC) requires translating high-level intent into contact-stable whole-body motion while continuously adapting to a human partner.

title: Efficient Autonomous Navigation of a Quadruped Robot in Underground Mines on Edge Hardware
summary: A quadruped navigation system is designed for underground mines, where the robot has to move through narrow, uneven, dark, GPS-denied tunnels with little or no communication. The emphasis is on autonomous operation on edge hardware, making the setup relevant for mine inspection or exploration scenarios where relying on remote compute or infrastructure is impractical.

extra.full_text: Embodied navigation in underground mines faces significant challenges, including narrow passages, uneven terrain, near-total darkness, GPS-denied conditions, and limited communication infrastructure.

title: Failure Mechanisms and Risk Estimation for Legged Robot Locomotion on Granular Slopes
summary: Legged locomotion on sand dunes and other granular slopes is framed around the way low shear strength and gravity-biased yielding make footing fail asymmetrically. The paper appears to focus on identifying those failure mechanisms and estimating locomotion risk, giving legged robots a way to reason about when slope traversal is likely to become unstable rather than treating granular terrain as just another low-friction surface.

extra.full_text: Locomotion on granular slopes such as sand dunes remains a fundamental challenge for legged robots due to reduced shear strength and gravity-induced anisotropic yielding of granular media.

title: Tune to Learn: How Controller Gains Shape Robot Policy Learning
summary: Controller gains are treated not just as a stiffness or compliance setting, but as a factor that can change how effectively manipulation policies learn through a position-control interface. The paper studies how gain choices shape robot policy learning, challenging the usual practice of tuning them only for desired task behavior rather than for the learning dynamics they induce.

extra.comment: Equal contribution between first two authors; order determined by coin flip. Project website: https://younghyopark.me/tune-to-learn
extra.full_text: Position controllers have become the dominant interface for executing learned manipulation policies. Yet a critical design decision remains understudied: how should we choose controller gains for policy learning? The conventional wisdom is to select gains based on desired task compliance or stiffness.

title: Design, Modeling and Direction Control of a Wire-Driven Robotic Fish Based on a 2-DoF Crank-Slider Mechanism
summary: A wire-driven robotic fish is built around a 2-DoF crank-slider mechanism for Body-Caudal Fin locomotion, using motor-driven actuation to shape and control tail motion. The design is aimed at biomimetic swimming for applications such as environmental monitoring and biological surveys, with direction control handled through the mechanical coupling rather than treating propulsion and steering as separate add-ons.

extra.full_text: Robotic fish have attracted growing attention in recent years owing to their biomimetic design and potential applications in environmental monitoring and biological surveys. Among robotic fish employing the Body-Caudal Fin (BCF) locomotion pattern, motor-driven actuation is widely adopted.

title: Generative adversarial imitation learning for robot swarms: Learning from human demonstrations and trained policies
summary: Generative adversarial imitation learning is applied to robot swarms so agents can learn collective behavior from either human demonstrations or rollouts of already trained policies. The interesting angle is the comparison between these two demonstration sources in a swarm setting, where the learned policy has to reproduce coordinated group behavior rather than a single robot’s actions.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA 2026)
extra.full_text: In imitation learning, robots are supposed to learn from demonstrations of the desired behavior. Most of the work in imitation learning for swarm robotics provides the demonstrations as rollouts of an existing policy.

title: DriveDreamer-Policy: A Geometry-Grounded World-Action Model for Unified Generation and Planning
summary: DriveDreamer-Policy is a world-action model for autonomous driving that tries to unify instruction-conditioned action planning with temporally coherent scene generation. It grounds the model in 3D geometry so planned ego-actions and generated future driving scenes stay spatially consistent, positioning it as a bridge between VLA-style reasoning and world-model prediction.

extra.full_text: Recently, world-action models (WAM) have emerged to bridge vision-language-action (VLA) models and world models, unifying their reasoning and instruction-following capabilities and spatio-temporal world modeling.

title: Uni-Skill: Building Self-Evolving Skill Repository for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation
summary: Uni-Skill targets the brittleness of fixed robot skill libraries by letting a manipulation system build and update its own skill repository as it encounters new compositional tasks. The interesting part is the self-evolving loop: instead of requiring manual additions for every new capability, the system uses foundation-model-driven skill composition and repository growth to improve generalization across tasks.

extra.full_text: While skill-centric approaches leverage foundation models to enhance generalization in compositional tasks, they often rely on fixed skill libraries, limiting adaptability to new tasks without manual intervention.

title: Robust Autonomous Control of a Magnetic Millirobot in In Vitro Cardiac Flow
summary: Untethered magnetic millirobots are being developed for minimally invasive cardiac procedures, but pulsatile blood flow makes autonomous navigation difficult. This paper focuses on robust closed-loop control of a magnetic millirobot in an in vitro cardiac-flow setting, aiming to keep the robot controllable despite the rapid, periodic disturbances that resemble conditions inside the heart.

extra.full_text: Untethered magnetic millirobots offer significant potential for minimally invasive cardiac therapies; however, achieving reliable autonomous control in pulsatile cardiac flow remains challenging.

title: A ROS 2 Wrapper for Florence-2: Multi-Mode Local Vision-Language Inference for Robotic Systems
summary: A ROS 2 wrapper brings Florence-2 into robotic systems as a local vision-language inference component, packaging multi-mode perception behind middleware interfaces rather than treating the model as a standalone demo. It is aimed at making richer semantic vision easier to reproduce and deploy in robot stacks, where integration, latency, and software plumbing often matter as much as the underlying VLM’s raw capability.

extra.full_text: Foundation vision-language models are becoming increasingly relevant to robotics because they can provide richer semantic perception than narrow task-specific pipelines. However, their practical adoption in robot software stacks still depends on reproducible middleware integrations rather than on model quality alone.

title: From Transportation to Manipulation: Transforming Magnetic Levitation to Magnetic Robotics
summary: Magnetic levitation systems are framed here as a bridge from flexible in-machine transport toward magnetic robotics, using controlled levitated motion to move beyond material flow and into manipulation. The interesting angle is that the same MagLev properties that help high-mix, low-volume factories dynamically optimize throughput could also support more dexterous, reconfigurable robotic handling inside automated production systems.

extra.full_text: Magnetic Levitation (MagLev) systems fundamentally increase the flexibility of in-machine material flow in industrial automation. Therefore, these systems enable dynamic throughput optimization, which is especially beneficial for high-mix low-volume manufacturing.

title: Focal plane wavefront control with model-based reinforcement learning
summary: Focal plane wavefront control is framed as a way to improve high-contrast imaging for directly observing potentially habitable exoplanets with extremely large telescopes. From the provided text, the paper appears to connect model-based reinforcement learning to the control problem at the focal plane, but there is not enough detail here to say what algorithm it uses, how it is evaluated, or what result it achieves.

extra.full_text: The direct imaging of potentially habitable exoplanets is one prime science case for high-contrast imaging instruments on extremely large telescopes.

title: Ablation Study of Multimodal Perception, Language Grounding, and Control for Human-Robot Interaction in an Object Detection and Grasping Task
summary: A multimodal human-robot interaction system for object detection and grasping is dissected by ablating its language, perception, and control components: the LLM that extracts actions from user input, the visual grounding module that links language to objects, and the motion controller that executes grasps. The study is aimed at showing how each module affects end-to-end task performance, making the system less of a black box and clarifying where failures in language-grounded robotic grasping are likely to originate.

extra.full_text: This manuscript extends our previous multimodal human-robot interaction system by introducing a controlled ablation study of the three modules that most strongly influence end-to-end performance: the large language model used for action extraction, the perception system used for visual grounding, and the controller used for motion execution.

title: TacMamba: A Tactile History Compression Adapter Bridging Fast Reflexes and Slow VLA Reasoning
summary: TacMamba targets visually ambiguous manipulation settings where touch, not vision, gives the decisive signal, such as confirming whether a button actually clicked. It appears to use a tactile history compression adapter to bridge fast low-level tactile reflexes with slower vision-language-action reasoning, preserving useful touch context without forcing the VLA policy to process raw tactile streams directly.

extra.full_text: In visually ambiguous manipulation such as detecting button click tactile feedback is often the sole source of ground truth.

title: LiPS: Lightweight Panoptic Segmentation for Resource-Constrained Robotics
summary: LiPS targets panoptic segmentation for robots that cannot afford heavy perception models, combining semantic scene understanding with instance-level object reasoning in a lightweight form. The available abstract frames the problem clearly, but does not provide enough detail to say what architecture, compression mechanism, benchmarks, or quantitative results make the system effective.

extra.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICIP 2026. Under review
extra.full_text: Panoptic segmentation is a key enabler for robotic perception, as it unifies semantic understanding with object-level reasoning. However, the increasing complexity of state-of-the-art models makes them unsuitable for deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as mobile robots.

title: MSACT: Multistage Spatial Alignment for Stable Low-Latency Fine Manipulation
summary: MSACT targets fine-grained real-world manipulation where bimanual robots need fast control but visual pose estimates can drift when only a small number of demonstrations are available. It uses multistage spatial alignment to stabilize localization for low-latency control, aiming to make delicate manipulation more reliable under the data constraints typical of real robot setups.

extra.full_text: Real-world fine manipulation, particularly in bimanual manipulation, typically requires low-latency control and stable visual localization, while collecting large-scale data is costly and limited demonstrations may lead to localization drift.

title: Topology-Driven Anti-Entanglement Control for Soft Robots
summary: Soft robots operating in tightly constrained manufacturing spaces can easily wrap around obstacles or themselves, so this study frames anti-entanglement as a multi-agent reinforcement learning control problem. It focuses on topology-driven control, using the robot’s winding or entanglement structure as part of the feedback signal for coordinating soft-body motion in complex environments.

extra.full_text: In the field of precision manufacturing in complex constrained environments, the role of soft robots is increasingly prominent, and the realization of anti-winding control based on multi-intelligent body reinforcement learning has become a research hotspot.

title: ICAT: Incident-Case-Grounded Adaptive Testing for Physical-Risk Prediction in Embodied World Models
summary: ICAT tests video-generative embodied world models on physical-risk prediction using incident-case-grounded hazardous scenarios, targeting whether imagined rollouts preserve danger cues and severe outcomes. The reported finding is that these models often soften or omit the consequences of risky actions, which can make planners or policies trained on their simulations learn unsafe preferences.

extra.full_text: Video-generative world models are increasingly used as neural simulators for embodied planning and policy learning, yet their ability to predict physical risk and severe consequences is rarely evaluated.We find that these models often downplay or omit key danger cues and severe outcomes for hazardous actions, which can induce unsafe preferences during planning and training on imagined rollouts.

title: Passive iFIR filters for data-driven velocity control in robotics
summary: Passive iFIR filters are used as a data-driven velocity controller for nonlinear robotic manipulators, aiming to preserve passivity while keeping the design burden close to that of a conventional PID loop. In the reported result, the controller improves tracking performance over an optimized PID baseline without requiring substantially more complex tuning or modeling.

extra.full_text: We present a passive, data-driven velocity control method for nonlinear robotic manipulators that achieves better tracking performance than optimized PID with comparable design complexity.

title: Beyond Hard Constraints: Budget-Conditioned Reachability For Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Budget-conditioned reachability reframes safe offline reinforcement learning by moving beyond fixed hard constraints and letting policies reason over an explicit safety budget. From the limited abstract text, the work appears to target MDP-based sequential decision problems where offline agents must balance performance with reachability-based safety guarantees under different allowable risk levels.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 36th International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS 2026)
extra.full_text: Sequential decision making using Markov Decision Process underpins many realworld applications. Both model-based and model free methods have achieved strong results in these settings.

title: Detection of Adversarial Attacks in Robotic Perception
summary: Deep neural semantic segmentation can fail under adversarial perturbations in ways that matter directly for robot safety, since perception errors propagate into navigation and manipulation decisions. The work focuses on detecting such adversarial attacks in robotic perception pipelines, but the provided text does not specify the detection mechanism, datasets, or quantitative results.

extra.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Accepted and presented at STE 2025, Transilvania University of Brasov, Romania
extra.full_text: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) achieve strong performance in semantic segmentation for robotic perception but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks, threatening safety-critical applications.

title: GraSP-STL: A Graph-Based Framework for Zero-Shot Signal Temporal Logic Planning via Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
summary: GraSP-STL tackles offline zero-shot planning for robot behaviors specified in Signal Temporal Logic, aiming to satisfy temporal goals without retraining for each new specification. It frames the problem around graph-based planning combined with offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning, so the system can compose behavior toward STL objectives from previously collected experience.

extra.full_text: This paper studies offline, zero-shot planning under Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications.

title: IMPASTO: Integrating Model-Based Planning with Learned Dynamics Models for Robotic Oil Painting Reproduction
summary: IMPASTO tackles robotic oil painting by combining model-based stroke planning with learned dynamics models that predict how a soft brush, pigment, and canvas interaction will change the image. It is aimed at settings where faithful simulators and step-by-step human demonstrations are unavailable, so the interesting part is the closed loop between force-sensitive brush control, learned brushstroke effects, and multi-step planning for reproducing paintings.

extra.full_text: Robotic reproduction of oil paintings using soft brushes and pigments requires force-sensitive control of deformable tools, prediction of brushstroke effects, and multi-step stroke planning, often without human step-by-step demonstrations or faithful simulators.

title: Critic-Free Deep Reinforcement Learning for Maritime Coverage Path Planning on Irregular Hexagonal Grids
summary: Efficient maritime surveillance over large, irregular regions is cast as a coverage path planning problem on irregular hexagonal grids, targeting missions like search and rescue and environmental monitoring. The approach uses critic-free deep reinforcement learning to allocate sensing motion without relying on a value-function critic, aiming to make coverage planning more tractable in geometrically complex ocean areas.

extra.full_text: Maritime surveillance missions, such as search and rescue and environmental monitoring, rely on the efficient allocation of sensing assets over vast and geometrically complex areas.

title: Control Without Control: Defining Implicit Interaction Paradigms for Autonomous Assistive Robots
summary: Autonomous assistive robots are framed here around implicit interaction: ways a robot can infer when and how to help without requiring explicit commands from a disabled user. The paper appears to focus on defining these interaction paradigms for assistive settings, where reducing command burden and preserving user autonomy are central design constraints.
