extra.full_text: Assistive robotic systems have shown growing potential to improve the quality of life of those with disabilities.

title: DecompGrind: A Decomposition Framework for Robotic Grinding via Cutting-Surface Planning and Contact-Force Adaptation
summary: DecompGrind targets robotic grinding of workpieces whose geometry and material hardness change the local removal resistance during contact. It frames the process around decomposing the object into cutting surfaces for planning, then adapts contact force during execution so the robot can maintain effective material removal under varying local conditions.

extra.full_text: Robotic grinding is widely used for shaping workpieces in manufacturing, but it remains difficult to automate this process efficiently. In particular, efficiently grinding workpieces of different shapes and material hardness is challenging because removal resistance varies with local contact conditions.

title: Robot Planning and Situation Handling with Active Perception
summary: Robots can already generate plans for complex tasks, but this work focuses on what happens when execution runs into unexpected real-world changes such as jammed doors or objects fallen in the path. It frames active perception as part of planning and situation handling, so the robot can seek out the information it needs to interpret a disruption and adapt its behavior rather than simply fail when the original plan no longer fits.

extra.full_text: Current robots are capable of computing plans to accomplish complex tasks. However, real-world environments are inherently open and dynamic, and unforeseen situations frequently arise during plan execution, such as jamming doors and fallen objects on the floor.

title: MetaTune: Adjoint-based Meta-tuning via Robotic Differentiable Dynamics
summary: MetaTune targets the practical problem of tuning disturbance observer-based robot controllers, where controller gains and observer parameters interact in ways that make manual tuning difficult. It uses adjoint-based meta-tuning through robotic differentiable dynamics, suggesting a gradient-based way to optimize the coupled control-and-observer parameters for robustness under uncertainty.

extra.full_text: Disturbance observer-based control has shown promise in robustifying robotic systems against uncertainties. However, tuning such systems remains challenging due to the strong coupling between controller gains and observer parameters.

title: Partial Motion Imitation for Learning Cart Pushing with Legged Manipulators
summary: Partial Motion Imitation trains legged manipulators to push carts by imitating only the parts of motion that matter for the task, rather than trying to reproduce a full reference trajectory. The focus is practical loco-manipulation: coordinating legged locomotion and manipulation so a robot can transport or push objects in real environments, with cart pushing as the concrete test case.

extra.full_text: Loco-manipulation is a key capability for legged robots to perform practical mobile manipulation tasks, such as transporting and pushing objects, in real-world environments.

title: Massive Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning for Active SLAM
summary: Massive Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning for Active SLAM uses GPU-scale parallelization to train policies for choosing SLAM actions that reduce map and localization uncertainty. The interesting angle is applying deep RL to a traditionally computation-heavy planning problem by exploiting many parallel simulation rollouts, making Active SLAM training more scalable rather than relying only on hand-designed exploration heuristics.

extra.full_text: Recent advances in parallel computing and GPU acceleration have created new opportunities for computation-intensive learning problems such as Active SLAM -- where actions are selected to reduce uncertainty and improve joint mapping and localization.

title: Drive My Way: Preference Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model for Personalized Driving
summary: Drive My Way tackles personalized autonomous driving by aligning a vision-language-action model with individual driving preferences, treating behavior as a mix of stable habits and short-term intent. The setup is aimed at capturing differences in actions like acceleration, braking, merging, yielding, and overtaking across situations, so the driving policy can adapt to how a particular person tends to drive rather than enforcing a single generic style.

extra.comment: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2026); Project website: https://dmw-cvpr.github.io/
extra.full_text: Human driving behavior is inherently personal, which is shaped by long-term habits and influenced by short-term intentions. Individuals differ in how they accelerate, brake, merge, yield, and overtake across diverse situations.

title: arg-VU: Affordance Reasoning with Physics-Aware 3D Geometry for Visual Understanding in Robotic Surgery
summary: arg-VU targets affordance reasoning for robotic surgery, linking visual understanding to how tools can act on deformable, compliant tissue. It frames the problem around physics-aware 3D geometry, aiming to capture how surgical tool motion and tissue deformation are dynamically coupled rather than treating affordances as static visual labels.

extra.full_text: Affordance reasoning provides a principled link between perception and action, yet remains underexplored in surgical robotics, where tissues are highly deformable, compliant, and dynamically coupled with tool motion.

title: Towards Generalizable Robotic Data Flywheel: High-Dimensional Factorization and Composition
summary: Addresses the data bottleneck for generalist robot models by treating robotic data collection as a generalizable “data flywheel,” organized around high-dimensional factorization and composition. The emphasis is on systematically collecting and curating diverse robot experience so models can reuse factors of variation more efficiently, rather than relying on ever-larger but loosely structured datasets.

extra.full_text: The lack of sufficiently diverse data, coupled with limited data efficiency, remains a major bottleneck for generalist robotic models, yet systematic strategies for collecting and curating such data are not fully explored.

title: System Design for Maintaining Internal State Consistency in Long-Horizon Robotic Tabletop Games
summary: Long-horizon tabletop games are treated as a state-consistency problem, where perception and execution errors can corrupt the shared internal game state and then cascade through planning and control. The system design focuses on keeping that accumulated state aligned over time so a robot can continue interacting coherently despite small mistakes, a practical concern for games and other extended manipulation tasks where early errors otherwise derail later decisions.

extra.full_text: Long-horizon tabletop games pose a distinct systems challenge for robotics: small perceptual or execution errors can invalidate accumulated task state, propagate across decision-making modules, and ultimately derail interaction.

title: Integrating Deep RL and Bayesian Inference for ObjectNav in Mobile Robotics
summary: Mobile object search is framed as an ObjectNav problem under partial observability, combining deep reinforcement learning for navigation decisions with Bayesian inference to maintain beliefs under perceptual uncertainty. The approach targets the exploration-efficiency tradeoff in indoor robotics, using probabilistic updates to guide where the robot should search rather than relying on reactive navigation alone.

extra.comment: Accepted and to be published in the ICARSC 2026 26th IEEE International Conference on Autonomous Robot Systems and Competitions
extra.full_text: Autonomous object search is challenging for mobile robots operating in indoor environments due to partial observability, perceptual uncertainty, and the need to trade off exploration and navigation efficiency.

title: LATS: Large Language Model Assisted Teacher-Student Framework for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Traffic Signal Control
summary: LATS targets adaptive traffic signal control with a teacher-student setup for multi-agent reinforcement learning, where large language models assist the learning process rather than directly controlling intersections. From the available text, the concrete problem is real-time traffic-light adjustment to improve flow and reduce delays, but there are no details on the teacher mechanism, benchmarks, or reported gains to summarize further.

extra.full_text: Adaptive Traffic Signal Control (ATSC) aims to optimize traffic flow and minimize delays by adjusting traffic lights in real time.

title: VTAM: Video-Tactile-Action Models for Complex Physical Interaction Beyond VLAs
summary: VTAM extends video-action modeling for embodied AI by adding tactile input, aiming to predict actions for complex physical interactions where vision alone may miss contact-rich dynamics. From the provided text, it frames raw video streams as a way to learn implicit world dynamics and produce temporally consistent action predictions, positioning video-tactile-action models as an alternative to vision-language-action systems for manipulation.

extra.full_text: Video-Action Models (VAMs) have emerged as a promising framework for embodied intelligence, learning implicit world dynamics from raw video streams to produce temporally consistent action predictions.

title: Learning Multi-Agent Local Collision-Avoidance for Collaborative Carrying tasks with Coupled Quadrupedal Robots
summary: Multiple quadrupedal robots are trained to coordinate local collision avoidance while jointly carrying a coupled load, targeting settings like warehouses or construction sites where teams must move together through constrained space. The interesting part is the multi-agent framing: each robot has to avoid collisions without breaking the coupled carrying formation, so locomotion, coordination, and object transport are treated as one linked control problem.

extra.full_text: Robotic collaborative carrying could greatly benefit human activities like warehouse and construction site management. However, coordinating the simultaneous motion of multiple robots represents a significant challenge.

title: Fleet-Level Battery-Health-Aware Scheduling for Autonomous Mobile Robots
summary: Fleet-Level Battery-Health-Aware Scheduling for Autonomous Mobile Robots studies task allocation and charging as a fleet-level optimization problem rather than treating each robot’s battery in isolation. It targets the practical bottleneck of shared charging resources, where scheduling decisions have to balance mission throughput with battery degradation across multiple autonomous mobile robots.

extra.full_text: Autonomous mobile robot fleets must coordinate task allocation and charging under limited shared resources, yet most battery aware planning methods address only a single robot.

title: Cross-Modal Reinforcement Learning for Navigation with Degraded Depth Measurements
summary: Cross-modal reinforcement learning is used to make visual navigation more robust when depth sensing is unreliable, combining degraded depth measurements with complementary grayscale image information. The idea is to let the policy draw on grayscale cues when depth becomes noisy or incomplete, so navigation does not collapse under sensor degradation.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 24th European Control Conference (ECC) 2026
extra.full_text: This paper presents a cross-modal learning framework that exploits complementary information from depth and grayscale images for robust navigation.

title: Beyond Viewpoint Generalization: What Multi-View Demonstrations Offer and How to Synthesize Them for Robot Manipulation?
summary: Multi-view demonstrations are studied as more than a way to make robot policies robust to camera changes, with the authors measuring how they affect manipulation performance, scaling, and learned behavior. The paper asks whether extra views provide genuinely useful training signal for control, then examines how such demonstrations can be synthesized rather than collected from many physical viewpoints.

extra.full_text: Does multi-view demonstration truly improve robot manipulation, or merely enhance cross-view robustness? We present a systematic study quantifying the performance gains, scaling behavior, and underlying mechanisms of multi-view data for robot manipulation.

title: Partial Attention in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Safe Multi-Agent Control
summary: Partial attention is applied to deep reinforcement learning for safe multi-agent control, using attention to focus each agent’s policy on the most relevant parts of the shared sequential state rather than treating all inputs uniformly. The idea is to bring the relevance-filtering behavior that makes attention effective in generative AI into coordinated control settings where safety constraints matter, though the provided text does not include specific experiments or quantitative results.

extra.comment: This work has been accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 American Control Conference (ACC), New Orleans, Louisiana, USA
extra.full_text: Attention mechanisms excel at learning sequential patterns by discriminating data based on relevance and importance. This provides state-of-the-art performance in advanced generative artificial intelligence models. This paper applies this concept of an attention mechanism for multi-agent safe control.

title: Bimanual Robot Manipulation via Multi-Agent In-Context Learning
summary: Multi-agent in-context learning is used to coordinate bimanual robot manipulation with off-the-shelf, text-only LLMs, predicting actions without task-specific training. The interesting angle is that the two arms are treated as cooperating agents, letting language-model reasoning structure dual-arm control while preserving the generalization benefits of ICL.

extra.full_text: Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful reasoning engines for embodied control. In particular, In-Context Learning (ICL) enables off-the-shelf, text-only LLMs to predict robot actions without any task-specific training while preserving their generalization capabilities.

title: PRM-as-a-Judge: A Dense Evaluation Paradigm for Fine-Grained Robotic Auditing
summary: PRM-as-a-Judge reframes robot evaluation as dense process auditing rather than a binary pass/fail score, using a process reward model to judge fine-grained execution qualities along the way. The goal is to expose where a policy is making progress, wasting motion, becoming unstable, or failing gracefully, so evaluations capture behavior that ordinary success rates flatten away.

extra.full_text: Current robotic evaluation is still largely dominated by binary success rates, which collapse rich execution processes into a single outcome and obscure critical qualities such as progress, efficiency, and stability.

title: A Framework for Closed-Loop Robotic Assembly, Alignment and Self-Recovery of Precision Optical Systems
summary: Robotic closed-loop assembly is applied to precision free-space optical systems, a domain that still relies heavily on manual alignment despite broader automation gains in lab science. The framework targets assembly, alignment, and self-recovery, suggesting a system that can not only place optical components but also iteratively correct misalignment and recover from errors during operation.

extra.full_text: Robotic automation has transformed scientific workflows in domains such as chemistry and materials science, yet free-space optics, which is a high precision domain, remains largely manual.

title: Learning Hybrid-Control Policies for High-Precision In-Contact Manipulation Under Uncertainty
summary: Reinforcement learning is used to learn hybrid-control policies for high-precision manipulation while the robot is already in contact with its environment, a setting where uncertainty makes purely analytical controllers difficult to tune. Instead of directly predicting end-effector pose changes from state observations, the work focuses on policies that can handle the control structure needed for precise in-contact behavior under uncertainty.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning-based control policies have been frequently demonstrated to be more effective than analytical techniques for many manipulation tasks. Commonly, these methods learn neural control policies that predict end-effector pose changes directly from observed state information.

title: Achieving Interaction Fluidity in a Wizard-of-Oz Robotic System: A Prototype for Fluid Error-Correction
summary: A Wizard-of-Oz robotic speech system is used here as a prototype testbed for making error correction feel less disruptive during human-robot interaction. The focus is on “interaction fluidity”: letting a human recover from speech or interpretation errors in a way that keeps the exchange moving, rather than turning the robot interface into a slow sequence of breakdowns and repairs.

extra.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, Workshop on Errors, Mistakes, and Failures in Humans and Robots at 2026 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
extra.full_text: Achieving truly fluid interaction with robots with speech interfaces remains a hard problem, and the experience of current Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) remains laboured and frustrating.

title: XEmbodied: A Foundation Model with Enhanced Geometric and Physical Cues for Large-Scale Embodied Environments
summary: XEmbodied targets the annotation bottleneck behind large-scale Vision-Language-Action training by building a foundation model that emphasizes geometric and physical cues in embodied environments. From the available text, it is aimed at helping autonomous systems learn from complex scenes with higher-quality scalable supervision, rather than relying only on language-vision correlations.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models drive next-generation autonomous systems, but training them requires scalable, high-quality annotations from complex environments.

title: COFFAIL: A Dataset of Successful and Anomalous Robot Skill Executions in the Context of Coffee Preparation
summary: COFFAIL is a robot manipulation dataset centered on coffee preparation, with executions that include both successful runs and anomalous failures rather than only polished demonstrations. Its value is in giving researchers a more realistic corpus for studying skill execution, failure detection, and recovery across multiple manipulation skills in a concrete household task setting.

extra.comment: Presented as an extended abstract at the 2nd German Robotics Conference (GRC)
extra.full_text: In the context of robot learning for manipulation, curated datasets are an important resource for advancing the state of the art; however, available datasets typically only include successful executions or are focused on one particular type of skill.

title: ROI-Driven Foveated Attention for Unified Egocentric Representations in Vision-Language-Action Systems
summary: ROI-Driven Foveated Attention targets vision-language-action systems for embodied AI, using region-of-interest guidance to build unified egocentric representations from interaction data. From the available text, the emphasis is on making better use of limited and structured physical interaction data rather than treating egocentric perception uniformly across the whole frame.

extra.full_text: The development of embodied AI systems is increasingly constrained by the availability and structure of physical interaction data.

title: Rusty Flying Robots: Learning a Full Robotics Stack with Real-Time Operation on an STM32 Microcontroller in a 9 ECTS MS Course
summary: A master’s projects course teaches the full robotics pipeline through flying robots, covering dynamics, state estimation, controls, and planning rather than isolating those topics in separate assignments. Students implement the stack for real-time operation on an STM32 microcontroller, making the course as much about embedded constraints and deployable autonomy as about the standard robotics algorithms.

extra.comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Robotics in Education (RiE), 2026
extra.full_text: We describe a novel masters-level projects class that teaches robotics along the traditional robotics pipeline (dynamics, state estimation, controls, planning).

title: R2-Dreamer: Redundancy-Reduced World Models without Decoders or Augmentation
summary: R2-Dreamer targets image-based model-based RL by learning compact world-model representations without relying on pixel reconstruction, decoders, or data augmentation. Instead of spending capacity modeling irrelevant background regions, it aims to reduce representational redundancy so the learned dynamics focus more directly on task-relevant visual information.

extra.full_text: A central challenge in image-based Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) is to learn representations that distill essential information from irrelevant visual details. While promising, reconstruction-based methods often waste capacity on large task-irrelevant regions.

title: SG-CoT: An Ambiguity-Aware Robotic Planning Framework using Scene Graph Representations
summary: SG-CoT uses a scene graph as an explicit queryable representation for LLM-based robot planning, letting the planner iteratively inspect objects, relations, and scene structure when an instruction or environment is ambiguous. The two-stage loop is aimed at making ambiguity detection and clarification part of the planning process rather than relying on the language model to infer everything from raw context.

extra.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters for possible publication
extra.full_text: Ambiguity poses a major challenge to large language models (LLMs) used as robotic planners. In this letter, we present Scene Graph-Chain-of-Thought (SG-CoT), a two-stage framework where LLMs iteratively query a scene graph representation of the environment to detect and clarify ambiguities.

title: An Annotation-to-Detection Framework for Autonomous and Robust Vine Trunk Localization in the Field by Mobile Agricultural Robots
summary: An annotation-to-detection pipeline targets vine trunk localization for mobile agricultural robots operating in unstructured, previously unseen fields. It focuses on making trunk detection robust under the variability of real vineyards, where changing geometry, clutter, and field conditions make reliable localization difficult.

extra.full_text: The dynamic and heterogeneous nature of agricultural fields presents significant challenges for object detection and localization, particularly for autonomous mobile robots that are tasked with surveying previously unseen unstructured environments.

title: Can LLMs Prove Robotic Path Planning Optimality? A Benchmark for Research-Level Algorithm Verification
summary: Robotic path planning often depends on approximation algorithms because many formulations are NP-hard, so verifying optimality claims is a natural stress test for LLMs beyond routine coding or theorem recall. This benchmark targets research-level algorithm verification: whether LLMs can reason through proofs that a robotic path-planning method is optimal or has the promised approximation guarantee, rather than merely producing a plausible plan.

extra.full_text: Robotic path planning problems are often NP-hard, and practical solutions typically rely on approximation algorithms with provable performance guarantees for general cases.

title: Final Report for the Workshop on Robotics & AI in Medicine
summary: The CARE Workshop on Robotics and AI in Medicine brought together researchers, clinicians, industry participants, and federal stakeholders in Indianapolis on December 1, 2025 to define priorities for robotics and AI in healthcare. Its final report appears to synthesize that discussion into a national vision for advancing medical robotics and AI, emphasizing coordination across technical research, clinical needs, industry translation, and policy.

extra.full_text: The CARE Workshop on Robotics and AI in Medicine, held on December 1, 2025 in Indianapolis, convened leading researchers, clinicians, industry innovators, and federal stakeholders to shape a national vision for advancing robotics and artificial intelligence in healthcare.

title: Specification-Aware Distribution Shaping for Robotics Foundation Models
summary: Specification-Aware Distribution Shaping aims to make robotics foundation models respect formal, time-dependent task and safety requirements rather than relying only on learned language-conditioned behavior. It appears to shape the model’s action distribution during deployment around explicit specifications, targeting stronger safety and satisfaction guarantees for robots operating across diverse tasks and environments.

extra.full_text: Robotics foundation models have demonstrated strong capabilities in executing natural language instructions across diverse tasks and environments. However, they remain largely data-driven and lack formal guarantees on safety and satisfaction of time-dependent specifications during deployment.

title: Consistency-Driven Dual LSTM Models for Kinematic Control of a Wearable Soft Robotic Arm
summary: Consistency-driven dual LSTM models learn the forward and inverse kinematics of a pneumatically actuated soft robotic arm built into a wearable device. By training the two directions together under a consistency constraint, the approach targets the hard part of soft-arm control: mapping between actuator inputs and deformable arm motion accurately enough for kinematic control.

extra.full_text: In this paper, we introduce a consistency-driven dual LSTM framework for accurately learning both the forward and inverse kinematics of a pneumatically actuated soft robotic arm integrated into a wearable device.

title: Physics-informed offline reinforcement learning eliminates catastrophic fuel waste in maritime routing
summary: Physics-informed offline reinforcement learning is applied to maritime voyage routing, targeting the failure mode where learned policies can choose catastrophically fuel-inefficient routes. The framing suggests replacing heuristic routing with a constraint-aware offline RL approach that uses physical structure to reduce fuel waste, aimed at cutting emissions from a sector responsible for about 3% of global greenhouse gases.

extra.full_text: International shipping produces approximately 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet voyage routing remains dominated by heuristic methods.

title: DreamPlan: Efficient Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Planners via Video World Models
summary: DreamPlan targets robotic manipulation planning by reinforcement fine-tuning vision-language planners with help from video world models. It builds on the commonsense reasoning already present in large VLMs, using imagined visual rollouts to make planning more efficient for manipulation settings.

extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation requires sophisticated commonsense reasoning, a capability naturally possessed by large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs).

title: Iterated Invariant EKF for Quadruped Robot Odometry
summary: Iterated Invariant EKF for Quadruped Robot Odometry applies a Kalman-filter-based state estimator to quadruped odometry, targeting efficient real-time state estimation for legged robots. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available beyond the use of Kalman filtering, so the work can only be characterized as an odometry method built around computationally efficient EKF-style estimation.

extra.full_text: Kalman filter-based algorithms are fundamental for mobile robots, as they provide a computationally efficient solution to the challenging problem of state estimation.

title: Development of Low-Cost and Bidirectional Syringe Pumps for Soft Robotics Applications
summary: Low-cost bidirectional syringe pumps are developed to drive the inflation and deflation cycles needed by Silicone Voxel-Based Soft Robots, whose shape changes depend on controlled pneumatic actuation of individual voxels. The interesting piece is the focus on an inexpensive, reversible pumping mechanism tailored to soft-robotics experiments, making it easier to build and test Silibot behaviors without relying on bulkier or more expensive pneumatic hardware.

extra.full_text: Soft robotics leverages deformable materials to develop robots capable of navigating unstructured and dynamic environments. Silicone Voxel-Based Soft Robots (Silibots) are a type of pneumatically actuated soft robots that rely on the inflation and deflation of their voxels for shape-shifting behaviors.

title: DEX-Mouse: A Low-cost Portable and Universal Interface with Force Feedback for Data Collection of Dexterous Robotic Hands
summary: DEX-Mouse is a low-cost, portable teleoperation interface for collecting dexterous hand demonstrations with force feedback, aimed at making physically consistent data collection easier for robotic hands. It targets the bottleneck in data-driven dexterous manipulation: getting large amounts of high-quality human demonstration data through a universal interface rather than hand-specific or expensive capture setups.

extra.full_text: Data-driven dexterous hand manipulation requires large-scale, physically consistent demonstration data.

title: PhysMoDPO: Physically-Plausible Humanoid Motion with Preference Optimization
summary: PhysMoDPO targets text-conditioned humanoid motion generation by making diffusion-produced motions more physically plausible through preference optimization. From the provided abstract fragment, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, but the work sits in the line of large-scale motion-diffusion models and appears focused on aligning generated human motion with physical feasibility rather than only visual or text-matching quality.

extra.full_text: Recent progress in text-conditioned human motion generation has been largely driven by diffusion models trained on large-scale human motion data.

title: SuperGrasp: Single-View Object Grasping via Superquadric Similarity Matching, Evaluation, and Refinement
summary: SuperGrasp tackles single-view robotic grasping by matching partially observed object geometry to superquadric shape abstractions, then using that representation to generate, evaluate, and refine grasp candidates under missing 3D information. The interesting part is its attempt to make grasp feasibility more stable from incomplete observations by combining shape-level similarity with an explicit refinement loop, rather than relying only on raw single-view geometry.

extra.comment: Minor revisions to the manuscript content, author order, and experimental results
extra.full_text: Robotic grasping from single-view observations remains a critical challenge in manipulation. However, existing methods still struggle to generate reliable grasp candidates and stably evaluate grasp feasibility under incomplete geometric information.

title: GAP: Geometric Anchor Pre-training for Data-Efficient Visuomotor Learning of Manipulation Tasks
summary: GAP adds a lightweight action-free warm-up before imitation learning, training the spatial pooling adapter on simulated object masks so its keypoints stay on the object, cover its extent, and remain sharp over time while the vision foundation model stays frozen. Those geometric anchors give few-shot visuomotor policies a more stable coordinate interface under scarce demonstrations and scene shifts, outperforming stronger attention poolers and full fine-tuning on RoboMimic and ManiSkill, including 62% success on RoboMimic Can with 15 demos and 61% on ManiSkill StackCube with 30 demos.

extra.full_text: Learning visuomotor policies from scarce expert demonstrations remains a core challenge in robotic manipulation. A primary hurdle lies in distilling high-dimensional RGB representations into control-relevant geometry without overfitting. While using frozen pre-trained Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) improves data efficiency, it also shifts most task adaptation onto a small spatial pooling module, which can latch onto task-irrelevant shortcuts and lose geometric grounding when finetuned with few data samples. More broadly, pre-trained visual representations used for policy learning have been observed to struggle under even minor scene perturbations, highlighting the need for robustness-oriented inductive biases. We propose Geometric Anchor Pre-training (GAP), a simple, action-free warm-up stage that regularizes the spatial adapter before downstream imitation learning. GAP pre-trains the pooling layer on a lightweight simulated proxy task where object masks are available at no cost, encouraging the adapter to produce keypoints that lie on the object, cover its spatial extent, and remain sharp and repeatable over time. This yields stable geometric anchors that provide a reliable coordinate interface for few-shot policy learning, while keeping the VFM frozen. We evaluate GAP on RoboMimic and ManiSkill under severe data scarcity (15-50 demonstrations) and domain shift. A simple adapter regularized with GAP consistently outperforms stronger attention-based poolers and end-to-end fine-tuning, achieving 62% success on RoboMimic Can with 15 demonstrations (+16% over AFA), 63% on the long-horizon high-precision Tool Hang task with 50 demonstrations, and 61% on ManiSkill StackCube with 30 demonstrations (+11% over full fine-tuning). The proxy stage is lightweight and fully decoupled from downstream tasks, making it practical to reuse across environments and manipulation skills.

title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Sim-and-Real Co-Training in Generative Robot Policies
summary: Co-training is examined as a way to train generative robot policies by mixing a small amount of real robot data with much larger surrogate sources such as simulation or cross-embodiment data. The study focuses on the mechanism behind why sim-and-real training helps, aiming to explain how the real data anchors the policy while the surrogate data expands coverage rather than treating the recipe as a black-box scaling trick.

extra.full_text: Co-training, which combines limited in-domain real-world data with abundant surrogate data such as simulation or cross-embodiment robot data, is widely used for training generative robot policies.

title: From Folding Mechanics to Robotic Function: A Unified Modeling Framework for Compliant Origami
summary: Compliant origami is modeled as a single mechanics problem that spans ideal rigid folding, elastic deformation, and stability-driven shape transitions, rather than treating those regimes separately. The goal is to give robot designers a way to predict how lightweight folded structures will move, deform, and switch configurations when used as reconfigurable robotic components.

extra.full_text: Origami inspired architectures offer a powerful route toward lightweight, reconfigurable, and programmable robotic systems. Yet, a unified mechanics framework capable of seamlessly bridging rigid folding, elastic deformation, and stability driven transitions in compliant origami remains lacking.

title: Ego to World: Collaborative Spatial Reasoning in Embodied Systems via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Embodied agents with limited egocentric views learn to collaborate on spatial reasoning by sharing partial observations and optimizing their coordination through reinforcement learning. The setup targets the ego-to-world problem in multi-agent systems, where distributed viewpoints must be fused despite occlusion and ambiguity to recover a more reliable understanding of the environment.

extra.full_text: Understanding the world from distributed, partial viewpoints is a fundamental challenge for embodied multi-agent systems. Each agent perceives the environment through an ego-centric view that is often limited by occlusion and ambiguity.

title: Bots and Blocks: Presenting a project-based approach for robotics education
summary: Bots and Blocks presents a project-based robotics education effort aimed at helping students engage with robotics as a modern technology. From the provided abstract fragment, the emphasis is on using hands-on robotics projects to teach practical and socially relevant aspects of the field, though no specific platform, curriculum structure, evaluation, or learning outcomes are given.

extra.full_text: To prepare students for upcoming trends and challenges, it is important to teach them about the helpful and important aspects of modern technologies, such as robotics.

title: From Scanning Guidelines to Action: A Robotic Ultrasound Agent with LLM-Based Reasoning
summary: Robotic ultrasound is framed here as an agentic scanning problem: an LLM reasons from clinical scanning guidelines and the current acquisition context to decide how the robot should move next. The aim is to reduce dependence on an expert sonographer’s moment-to-moment judgment while preserving the adaptive decision-making needed to acquire reproducible ultrasound views.

extra.full_text: Robotic ultrasound offers advantages over free-hand scanning, including improved reproducibility and reduced operator dependency. In clinical practice, US acquisition relies heavily on the sonographer's experience and situational judgment.

title: M2HRI: An LLM-Driven Multimodal Multi-Agent Framework for Personalized Human-Robot Interaction
summary: M2HRI uses an LLM-driven multimodal multi-agent setup to coordinate multiple robots in personalized human-robot interaction, treating each robot as an individual with its own identity rather than as an interchangeable unit. The idea is to let robot individuality shape user perception while still enabling coordinated group behavior, targeting social settings like homes and hospitals where people may interact with several robots at once.

extra.full_text: Multi-robot systems hold significant promise for social environments such as homes and hospitals, yet existing multi-robot works treat robots as functionally identical, overlooking how robots individual identity shape user perception and how coordination shapes multi-robot behavior when such individuality is present.

title: Learning POMDP World Models from Observations with Language-Model Priors
summary: Learning POMDP World Models from Observations with Language-Model Priors studies how an agent can infer a usable internal model of a partially observable environment from observations, using language-model priors to guide that learning. The framing is aimed at settings like robots, navigation agents, and game-playing systems where effective action depends on reconstructing hidden state and dynamics rather than just reacting to the current observation.

extra.full_text: Whether navigating a building, operating a robot, or playing a game, an agent that acts effectively in an environment must first learn an internal model of how that environment works.

title: ComFree-Sim: A GPU-Parallelized Analytical Contact Physics Engine for Scalable Contact-Rich Robotics Simulation and Control
summary: ComFree-Sim targets the contact-resolution bottleneck in robotics simulation by replacing the usual complementarity or constrained-optimization solve for non-penetration and Coulomb friction with a GPU-parallelized analytical contact physics engine. The interesting part is the scalability angle: contact-rich scenes that normally become expensive as contact density rises can be simulated and used for control without the per-step iterative solves that dominate mainstream engines.

extra.full_text: Physics simulation for contact-rich robotics is often bottlenecked by contact resolution: mainstream engines enforce non-penetration and Coulomb friction via complementarity constraints or constrained optimization, requiring per-step iterative solves whose cost grows superlinearly with contact density.

title: TinySDP: Real Time Semidefinite Optimization for Certifiable and Agile Edge Robotics
summary: TinySDP targets the gap between semidefinite relaxations for geometric motion-planning constraints and the compute limits of embedded robot controllers. It is a real-time SDP solver designed for edge robotics, aiming to make certifiable optimization practical in agile control loops where conventional SDP solvers are too slow or heavy.

extra.comment: Accepted to Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2026. 11 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Project website: https://a2r-lab.org/TinySDP/
extra.full_text: Semidefinite programming (SDP) provides a principled framework for convex relaxations of nonconvex geometric constraints in motion planning, yet existing solvers are too computationally expensive for real-time control, particularly on resource-constrained embedded systems.

title: Vision-guided Autonomous Dual-arm Extraction Robot for Bell Pepper Harvesting
summary: A vision-guided dual-arm robot is aimed at automating bell pepper harvesting, a crop where picking can represent up to half of production costs. The system is interesting because it targets the practical mechanics of autonomous extraction rather than just detection, combining perception with coordinated two-arm manipulation for a labor-intensive greenhouse task.

extra.comment: 9 pages; first four authors have equal contribution
extra.full_text: Agricultural robotics has emerged as a critical solution to the labor shortages and rising costs associated with manual crop harvesting. Bell pepper harvesting, in particular, is a labor-intensive task, accounting for up to 50% of total production costs.

title: SID: Sliding into Distribution for Robust Few-Demonstration Manipulation
summary: SID targets robust few-demonstration manipulation by trying to make learned policies hold up when object poses, camera viewpoints, or disturbances shift away from the narrow demonstration setting. The core idea is to “slide” demonstrations into a broader distribution, giving the policy more useful variation from limited data rather than relying on many collected examples.

extra.full_text: Generalizing robotic manipulation across object poses, viewpoints, and dynamic disturbances is difficult, especially with only a few demonstrations.

title: CLASP: Closed-loop Asynchronous Spatial Perception for Open-vocabulary Desktop Object Grasping
summary: CLASP targets open-vocabulary desktop grasping by putting VLM-based object understanding inside a closed-loop, asynchronous spatial perception system rather than relying on a single open-loop plan. It is aimed at the practical failure modes of low-level manipulation: limited multimodal grasp demonstrations, weak geometric grounding that can make VLMs hallucinate spatial relations, and changes in the scene during execution.

extra.full_text: Robot grasping of desktop object is widely used in intelligent manufacturing, logistics, and agriculture.Although vision-language models (VLMs) show strong potential for robotic manipulation, their deployment in low-level grasping faces key challenges: scarce high-quality multimodal demonstrations, spatial hallucination caused by weak geometric grounding, and the fragility of open-loop execution in dynamic environments.

title: Path-conditioned Reinforcement Learning-based Local Planning for Long-Range Navigation
summary: Long-range navigation is framed as a hierarchical setup where a global planner produces a route, breaks it into waypoints, and a learned local planner follows them in sequence. The path-conditioned reinforcement learning component appears aimed at making local decisions that stay aligned with the longer global path, rather than treating each waypoint as an isolated target.

extra.full_text: Long-range navigation is commonly addressed through hierarchical pipelines in which a global planner generates a path, decomposed into waypoints, and followed sequentially by a local planner.

title: Benchmarking the Energy Cost of Assurance in Neuromorphic Edge Robotics
summary: Benchmarks the energy overhead of adding assurance mechanisms to neuromorphic edge robots, focusing on the tension between robustness and power limits in deployed embodied AI. The available abstract is very sparse, but the core question is concrete: how much energy trustworthy AI safeguards cost when they run on constrained robotic hardware rather than in the cloud.

extra.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Accepted and presented at the STEAR 2026 Workshop on Sustainable and Trustworthy Edge AI for Robotics, HiPEAC 2026, Krakow, Poland
extra.full_text: Deploying trustworthy artificial intelligence on edge robotics imposes a difficult trade-off between high-assurance robustness and energy sustainability.

title: Sumo: Dynamic and Generalizable Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
summary: Sumo is a sim-to-real system for legged robots that uses whole-body control to move and manipulate large, heavy objects dynamically rather than treating locomotion and manipulation as separate problems. The interesting part is its emphasis on generalizable loco-manipulation: training in simulation so a real robot can coordinate legs and body contacts to push, carry, or otherwise handle objects that would be difficult for a manipulator-only setup.

extra.full_text: This paper presents a sim-to-real approach that enables legged robots to dynamically manipulate large and heavy objects with whole-body dexterity.

title: End-to-End O-RAN Testbed for Edge-AI-Enabled 5G/6G Connected Industrial Robotics
summary: An end-to-end O-RAN testbed is presented for connected industrial robotics, tying edge-AI capabilities into 5G/6G-style cellular infrastructure. The available description frames it as a practical platform for studying how intelligent RAN control and edge computation can support low-latency, networked robotic systems in industrial settings.

extra.full_text: Connected robotics is one of the principal use cases driving the transition towards more intelligent and capable 6G mobile cellular networks.

title: Macro-Action Based Multi-Agent Instruction Following through Value Cancellation
summary: Macro-Action Based Multi-Agent Instruction Following through Value Cancellation tackles MARL settings where agents must obey interrupting natural-language instructions even when those commands conflict with their learned long-horizon goals. The method appears to operate at the macro-action level and uses value cancellation to suppress or offset objective-driven behavior that would interfere with instruction following, aiming to make multi-agent policies more responsive to external commands during execution.

extra.full_text: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in real-world use cases may need to adapt to external natural language instructions that interrupt ongoing behavior and conflict with long-horizon objectives.

title: Learning What Can Be Picked: Active Reachability Estimation for Efficient Robotic Fruit Harvesting
summary: Active reachability estimation is applied to robotic fruit harvesting, focusing on learning which fruits can actually be picked rather than treating all detected targets as equally reachable. The motivation is practical: high-value crop harvesting is labor-intensive and increasingly constrained by workforce shortages, so estimating pickability efficiently could help robots spend less time attempting unreachable or unharvestable fruit.

extra.full_text: Agriculture remains a cornerstone of global health and economic sustainability, yet labor-intensive tasks such as harvesting high-value crops continue to face growing workforce shortages.

title: X-Imitator: Spatial-Aware Imitation Learning via Bidirectional Action-Pose Interaction
summary: X-Imitator targets robotic manipulation policies where perception and action are too often handled as separate stages, making spatial reasoning a bottleneck. It frames imitation learning around bidirectional action-pose interaction, so the robot’s predicted actions and spatial pose understanding inform each other during policy learning rather than being fused only after the fact.

extra.full_text: Effectively handling the interplay between spatial perception and action generation remains a critical bottleneck in robotic manipulation.

title: Cooperative Robotics Reinforced by Collective Perception for Traffic Moderation
summary: Cooperative robots positioned near non-line-of-sight intersections use collective perception to detect approaching traffic and physically moderate vehicle movement, aiming to protect drivers who lack V2X equipment or may miss in-vehicle warnings. The interesting shift is from simply broadcasting alerts to having roadside robotic agents perceive hidden hazards together and intervene in the traffic scene itself.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)
extra.full_text: Collisions at non-line-of-sight (NLOS) intersections remain a major safety concern because drivers have limited visibility of approaching traffic. V2X based warnings can reduce these risks, yet many vehicles are not equipped with V2X and drivers may ignore in vehicle alerts.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Elliptical Cylinder Motion Control Tasks
summary: Reinforcement learning is applied to motion-control tasks for an elliptical cylinder, a limited-input dynamical system in the same broad family of underactuated control benchmarks as the inverted pendulum. The work appears to frame the cylinder’s motion as a difficult control problem where conventional solutions are nontrivial, using RL as a way to learn policies for managing the constrained actuation.

extra.full_text: The control of devices with limited input always bring attention to solve by research due to its difficulty and non-trival solution. For instance, the inverted pendulum is benchmarking problem in control theory and machine learning.

title: HeteroGenManip: Generalizable Manipulation For Heterogeneous Object Interactions
summary: HeteroGenManip targets robotic manipulation where the robot must handle interactions between different kinds of objects, rather than repeating skills within a single object category. The available description only states the problem framing, so the concrete mechanism, benchmark setup, and results are not specified here.

extra.full_text: Generalizable manipulation involving cross-type object interactions is a critical yet challenging capability in robotics.

title: Introducing Environmental Constraints to Grasping Strategies for Paper-Like Flexible Materials Using a Soft Gripper
summary: A soft gripper is used to manipulate paper-like flexible materials while explicitly accounting for environmental constraints that affect grasp choice. The approach focuses on adapting grasping strategies to the way thin, bendable objects interact with surrounding surfaces, which is central for moving from isolated pick-and-place demos toward more realistic industrial or service settings.

extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation of flexible objects is widely required in both industrial and service applications.

title: Learning Athletic Humanoid Tennis Skills from Imperfect Human Motion Data
summary: Learning athletic humanoid tennis skills from imperfect human motion data targets the problem of getting a simulated or robotic humanoid to perform fast, coordinated tennis motions from real athlete demonstrations that may be noisy or incomplete. The interesting part is the emphasis on high-dynamic rallies with a high-speed ball, where the system has to turn imperfect human motion into usable control policies for agile hitting behavior rather than just replaying clean motion clips.

extra.full_text: Human athletes demonstrate versatile and highly-dynamic tennis skills to successfully conduct competitive rallies with a high-speed tennis ball.

title: Forecast-aware Gaussian Splatting for Predictive 3D Representation in Language-Guided Pick-and-Place Manipulation
summary: Forecast-GS builds a predictive 3D scene representation for language-conditioned pick-and-place, using Gaussian splatting not just to model the current workspace but to forecast how the scene should evolve under manipulation. The interesting part is the coupling of language-guided action intent with a 3D representation that can anticipate post-action structure, which could make perception more useful for planning than a static reconstruction alone.

extra.full_text: We introduce Forecast-aware Gaussian Splatting (Forecast-GS), a predictive 3D representation framework for language-conditioned robotic manipulation.

title: XQCfD: Accelerating Fast Actor-Critic Algorithms with Prior Data and Prior Policies
summary: XQCfD adapts the sample-efficient XQC actor-critic for robotic manipulation settings where online exploration is costly, combining demonstration-augmented replay, pretrained policies, and stationary policy architectures that preserve a strong initial policy instead of quickly unlearning it. The stationary architecture gives higher-entropy predictions that support out-of-distribution policy improvement, and the method performs strongly on sparse-reward Adroit, Robomimic, and MimicGen tasks while using a low update-to-data ratio and avoiding ensemble networks.

extra.full_text: For reinforcement learning in the real world online exploration is expensive A common practice in robotic reinforcement learning is to incorporate additional data to improve sample efficiency Expert demonstration data is often crucial for solving hard exploration tasks with sparse rewards While prior data is used to augment experience and pretrain models we show that the design of existing algorithms fails to achieve the sample efficiency that is possible in this setting due to a failure to use pretrained policies effectively We propose XQCfD which extends the sample-efficient XQC actor-critic to learn from demonstrations using augmented replay buffers pretrained policies and stationary policy architectures designed to avoid rapidly unlearning the strong initial policy like prior works We show our stationary network architecture enables policy improvement out-of-distribution better than standard network architectures due to its higher entropy predictions XQCfD achieves state of the art performance across a range of complex manipulation tasks with sparse rewards from the popular Adroit Robomimic and MimicGen benchmarks -- notably with a low update-to-data ratio and no ensemble networks

title: Nano-U: Efficient Terrain Segmentation for Tiny Robot Navigation
summary: Nano-U targets terrain segmentation on tiny mobile robots, where conventional segmentation models are too large for microcontroller-class memory and compute budgets. It focuses on making outdoor terrain understanding practical for small platforms, trading the usual heavy vision stack for an efficient model suitable for onboard navigation in unstructured environments.

extra.full_text: Terrain segmentation is a fundamental capability for autonomous mobile robots operating in unstructured outdoor environments. However, state-of-the-art models are incompatible with the memory and compute constraints typical of microcontrollers, limiting scalable deployment in small robotics platforms.

title: A Generalized Theory of Load Distribution in Redundantly-actuated Robotic Systems
summary: Presents a generalized theory for how applied loads are shared through a rigid body when it is manipulated by redundantly actuated robotic systems made of multiple independent closed-loop kinematic chains. The interesting piece is that it treats load distribution as a system-level property of redundancy and closed-loop constraints, giving a more general way to reason about internal forces in multi-chain manipulation setups.

extra.comment: 20 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to The International Journal of Robotics Research
extra.full_text: This paper presents a generalized theory which describes how applied loads are distributed within rigid bodies handled by redundantly-actuated robotic systems composed of multiple independent closed-loop kinematic chains.

title: Deployment-Time Reliability of Learned Robot Policies
summary: Learned robot manipulation policies can look strong in controlled settings but fail at deployment when distribution shift, accumulated mistakes, and task-level dependencies interact. The work frames deployment-time reliability as the central obstacle for using these policies in real-world systems, focusing attention on how robustness breaks down after training rather than just on capability gains.

extra.comment: Stanford University PhD dissertation, 2026. 182 pages, 37 figures. Available from Stanford Digital Repository
extra.full_text: Recent advances in learning-based robot manipulation have produced policies with remarkable capabilities. Yet, reliability at deployment remains a fundamental barrier to real-world use, where distribution shift, compounding errors, and complex task dependencies collectively undermine system performance.

title: SafeMind: A Risk-Aware Differentiable Control Framework for Adaptive and Safe Quadruped Locomotion
summary: SafeMind targets the gap between agile learned quadruped locomotion and the lack of formal safety guarantees when the robot faces model uncertainty, noisy perception, and messy contact conditions. It frames locomotion control as a risk-aware differentiable control problem, aiming to adapt online while keeping safety constraints explicit rather than relying purely on policy behavior learned in simulation.

extra.full_text: Learning-based quadruped controllers achieve impressive agility but typically lack formal safety guarantees under model uncertainty, perception noise, and unstructured contact conditions.

title: ASTER: Attitude-aware Suspended-payload Quadrotor Traversal via Efficient Reinforcement Learning
summary: ASTER uses efficient reinforcement learning to control a quadrotor carrying a cable-suspended payload through agile traversal, explicitly accounting for the payload’s attitude rather than treating it as a simple trailing mass. The interesting challenge is the system’s non-smooth hybrid dynamics: cable tension changes and payload motion can make fast maneuvers brittle, so the method targets stable, attitude-aware flight in regimes where conventional smooth-model controllers struggle.

extra.full_text: Agile maneuvering of the quadrotor cable-suspended system is significantly hindered by its non-smooth hybrid dynamics.

title: ScanDP: Generalizable 3D Scanning with Diffusion Policy
summary: ScanDP applies diffusion policy to learning-based 3D scanning, aiming to choose scanning actions that efficiently capture target objects in 3D. From the provided text, the work is positioned around making object scanning more accurate and efficient, but the excerpt does not include enough detail to summarize its architecture, training setup, benchmarks, or results.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Project Page: https://treeitsuki.github.io/ScanDP/
extra.full_text: Learning-based 3D Scanning plays a crucial role in enabling efficient and accurate scanning of target objects.

title: Octopus-inspired Distributed Control for Soft Robotic Arms: A Graph Neural Network-Based Attention Policy with Environmental Interaction
summary: SoftGM controls segmented soft robotic arms with an octopus-like distributed policy, using a graph neural network with attention to coordinate arm segments during target reaching. Instead of assuming a full map of obstacle geometry, the arm discovers obstacles online through environmental interaction, making the approach aimed at contact-rich settings where global scene information is unavailable or unreliable.

extra.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables, submitted for IROS 2026
extra.full_text: This paper proposes SoftGM, an octopus-inspired distributed control architecture for segmented soft robotic arms that learn to reach targets in contact-rich environments using online obstacle discovery without relying on global obstacle geometry.

title: ActiveGlasses: Learning Manipulation with Active Vision from Ego-centric Human Demonstration
summary: ActiveGlasses studies how ego-centric human demonstrations with active vision could support robot manipulation learning, aimed at scaling real-world data collection for everyday robot deployment. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified beyond the focus on learning manipulation from human demonstrations captured through an active-vision glasses setup.

extra.full_text: Large-scale real-world robot data collection is a prerequisite for bringing robots into everyday deployment.

title: A low-cost mockup to simulate robotic laser cutting in nuclear decommissioning
summary: A low-cost experimental mockup is presented for simulating robotic laser cutting of containers during nuclear decommissioning. It is meant to reproduce the cutting process in a safer, cheaper test setting, giving researchers a practical platform for studying and validating robotic tooling before deployment in hazardous nuclear environments.

extra.comment: 7 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Under Review for TAROS 2026 (Towards Autonomous Robotic Systems)
extra.full_text: This paper introduces a low-cost experimental mockup to simulate the laser cutting process of containers in nuclear decommissioning.

title: SEA-Nav: Efficient Policy Learning for Safe and Agile Quadruped Navigation in Cluttered Environments
summary: SEA-Nav targets the hard problem of training quadrupeds to move safely and quickly through densely cluttered spaces. From the provided text, the concrete claim is that it focuses on making policy learning more efficient for agile navigation under obstacle-heavy conditions, but the excerpt does not include the mechanism, experiments, or results needed to say more without inventing details.

extra.full_text: Efficiently training quadruped robot navigation in densely cluttered environments remains a significant challenge.

title: Receptogenesis in a Vascularized Robotic Embodiment
summary: A vascularized robot is presented as an embodiment that can generate new hardware during operation, extending adaptability beyond software control or prebuilt morphologies. The central idea is receptogenesis: forming ex novo physical structures through an internal vascular system, giving the robot a route to modify its own body in response to changing needs.

extra.comment: Supplementary Files currently unavailable online. Please contact the First Author to request any Supplementary Files
extra.full_text: Equipping robotic systems with the capacity to generate $\textit{ex novo}$ hardware during operation extends control of physical adaptability.

title: Omni-scale Learning-based Sequential Decision Framework for Order Fulfillment of Tote-handling Robotic Systems
summary: Tote-handling robotic systems are framed as a sequential decision problem for modern intralogistics, where shrinking load units and mixed-order fulfillment make pallet-style planning less suitable. The proposed omni-scale learning-based framework appears aimed at coordinating decisions across different operational scales, from individual tote handling to broader fulfillment flow, so robots can manage small-batch warehouse movement more effectively.

extra.full_text: Driven by the rapid expansion of e-commerce and small-batch production, the size of the intralogistics load unit of finished goods, semi-finished goods and raw materials is steadily shrinking. Totes are gradually replacing pallets as the primary handling and storage container.

title: TRIP-Bag: A Portable Teleoperation System for Plug-and-Play Robotic Arms and Leaders
summary: TRIP-Bag is a portable teleoperation setup meant to make robotic-arm data collection easier to move between hardware platforms, pairing plug-and-play support for robot arms with compatible leader devices. The motivation is practical: learning-based manipulation needs large, diverse demonstrations, and a bag-scale teleop system lowers the friction of collecting them across different robots and sites.

extra.full_text: Large scale, diverse demonstration data for manipulation tasks remains a major challenge in learning-based robot policies.

title: Beyond Amplitude: Channel State Information Phase-Aware Deep Fusion for Robotic Activity Recognition
summary: Wi-Fi CSI is used here as a non-line-of-sight sensing signal for recognizing robotic arm activities, with the emphasis shifted from the usual amplitude-only features to phase-aware deep fusion. The interesting piece is that it treats CSI phase as a useful motion descriptor rather than noise or a preprocessing nuisance, aiming to improve recognition of robot activity from wireless channel changes.

extra.comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP), May 4--8, 2026, Barcelona, Spain
extra.full_text: Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) has emerged as a promising non-line-of-sight sensing modality for human and robotic activity recognition. However, prior work has predominantly relied on CSI amplitude while underutilizing phase information, particularly in robotic arm activity recognition.

title: Predictive Control with Indirect Adaptive Laws for Payload Transportation by Quadrupedal Robots
summary: Develops a hierarchical planning and control scheme for quadruped payload transport that couples model predictive control with an indirect adaptive law updated by gradient descent. The interesting piece is the online adaptation layer, which is meant to improve robustness when the payload changes or is uncertain while preserving the structure of MPC for whole-body motion planning.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
extra.full_text: This paper formally develops a novel hierarchical planning and control framework for robust payload transportation by quadrupedal robots, integrating a model predictive control (MPC) algorithm with a gradient-descent-based adaptive updating law.

title: How to utilize failure demo data?: Effective data selection for imitation learning using distribution differences in attention mechanism
summary: Uses failed robot demonstrations as a training signal for imitation learning by selecting data based on distribution differences in the policy’s attention mechanism, rather than simply discarding failures. The idea is to identify which failure examples contain useful behavioral contrast or recovery-relevant structure, making messy human-collected demonstration sets more valuable for learning robust robotic policies.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning for robotic tasks has relied primarily on policies trained only on successful demonstrations, although failures are unavoidable during human data collection.

title: Vector Field Augmented Differentiable Policy Learning for Vision-Based Drone Racing
summary: Vector Field Augmented Differentiable Policy Learning targets vision-based autonomous drone racing, where a drone has to fly fast through clutter while still avoiding obstacles reliably. The description points to a policy-learning approach augmented with vector fields, likely using them to shape agile trajectories and obstacle-aware control from visual input, but the provided text does not include experimental results or benchmark numbers.

extra.full_text: Autonomous drone racing in complex environments requires agile, high-speed flight while maintaining reliable obstacle avoidance.

title: Integrating Causal DAGs in Deep RL: Activating Minimal Markovian States with Multi-Order Exposure
summary: Integrating Causal DAGs in Deep RL studies how to recover Markovian state representations when an agent only sees raw variables that may not themselves define a proper state. It uses causal directed acyclic graphs and multi-order exposure to activate a minimal set of variables that preserves the Markov property, aiming to make online RL more reliable in settings where state design is ambiguous.

extra.full_text: Online reinforcement learning (RL) relies on the Markov property for guaranteed performance, but real-world applications often lack well-defined states given raw observed variables.

title: Toward Global Intent Inference for Human Motion by Inverse Reinforcement Learning
summary: The authors use inverse reinforcement learning to ask whether human reaching motions can be explained by one global cost function rather than separate criteria tuned to each person or posture. The interesting test is whether such a unified objective can both account for observed arm trajectories and generalize to predicting new reaching movements, which would make intent inference less dependent on individualized motion models.

extra.full_text: This paper investigates whether a single, unified cost function can explain and predict human reaching movements, in contrast with existing approaches that rely on subject- or posture-specific optimization criteria.

title: Learning-Guided Force-Feedback Model Predictive Control with Obstacle Avoidance for Robotic Deburring
summary: Learning-guided force-feedback MPC brings real-time contact forces into torque-controlled robotic deburring while still enforcing obstacle-avoidance constraints. The approach targets the gap between classical MPC formulations and contact-rich industrial finishing, where the controller must regulate tool interaction forces and avoid collisions at the same time.

extra.full_text: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is widely used for torque-controlled robots, but classical formulations often neglect real-time force feedback and struggle with contact-rich industrial tasks under collision constraints.

title: Automating Manual Tasks through Intuitive Robot Programming and Cognitive Robotics
summary: Natural language instructions and supportive gestures are combined into an end-user programming interface for robots, with LLMs translating spoken intent into executable robot programs and computer vision grounding the gestures. The idea is to let non-experts specify manual tasks through human-like interaction rather than code or teach pendants, tying cognitive robotics to a practical programming workflow.

extra.comment: This submission contains both an English translation and the original German version. The German version was originally published in the Proceedings of the 71st GfA Conference (2025)
extra.full_text: This paper presents a novel concept for intuitive end-user programming of robots, inspired by natural interaction between humans. Natural language and supportive gestures are translated into robot programs using large language models (LLMs) and computer vision (CV).

title: Milestone-Guided Policy Learning for Long-Horizon Language Agents
summary: Milestone-Guided Policy Learning targets the reinforcement-learning bottleneck in long-horizon language-agent tasks, where sparse delayed rewards make it hard to learn dozens of sequential decisions. From the provided text, the central idea is to guide policy learning with intermediate milestones so the agent gets structure across extended action sequences, but no specific benchmarks or results are given.

extra.full_text: While long-horizon agentic tasks require language agents to perform dozens of sequential decisions, training such agents with reinforcement learning remains challenging.

title: Optimal Transport for LLM Reward Modeling from Noisy Preference
summary: Optimal Transport for LLM Reward Modeling from Noisy Preference addresses the problem that RLHF reward models are trained on human preference data that can be corrupted or inconsistent. It frames reward modeling through optimal transport, aiming to make preference learning more robust when comparisons are noisy rather than treating all labels as clean signal.

extra.full_text: Reward models are fundamental to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), yet real-world datasets are inevitably corrupted by noisy preference.

title: Simulation-Driven Evolutionary Motion Parameterization for Contact-Rich Granular Scooping with a Soft Conical Robotic Hand
summary: Simulation-driven evolutionary motion parameterization is used to tune how a soft conical robotic hand performs contact-rich scooping in granular materials. The setup targets tool-based scooping where the robot must handle objects or media with changing size, shape, and material state, using simulation to search for motion parameters that make the soft hand more effective in these difficult interactions.

extra.full_text: Tool-based scooping is vital in robot-assisted tasks, enabling interaction with objects of varying sizes, shapes, and material states.

title: LITHE: Bridging Best-Effort Python and Real-Time C++ for Hot-Swapping Robotic Control Laws on Commodity Linux
summary: LITHE targets hierarchical robot control stacks where a Python “Brain” computes high-level decisions while a real-time C++ “Spine” runs the low-level controller. It focuses on hot-swapping robotic control laws on commodity Linux, bridging Python’s flexibility with C++ timing guarantees so researchers can iterate on controllers without giving up the real-time execution path.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots & Systems (IROS) 2026
extra.full_text: Modern robotic systems rely on hierarchical control, where a high-level "Brain" (Python) directs a lower-level "Spine" (C++ real-time controller).

title: Underwater Embodied Intelligence for Autonomous Robots: A Constraint-Coupled Perspective on Planning, Control, and Deployment
summary: Autonomous underwater robots are framed through a constraint-coupled view, where planning, control, and deployment are treated as tightly linked by underwater limits such as communication, sensing, energy, vehicle dynamics, and environmental uncertainty. The paper appears to synthesize how embodied AI methods can make subsea robots more reliable for monitoring, inspection, resource exploration, and long-horizon missions, with the interesting angle being the explicit coupling of autonomy algorithms to the physical and operational constraints of underwater work.

extra.comment: This article is currently under review
extra.full_text: Autonomous underwater robots are increasingly deployed for environmental monitoring, infrastructure inspection, subsea resource exploration, and long-horizon exploration.

title: A Position Statement on Endovascular Models and Effectiveness Metrics for Mechanical Thrombectomy Navigation, on behalf of the Stakeholder Taskforce for AI-assisted Robotic Thrombectomy (START)
summary: START lays out a consensus position on how to model endovascular anatomy and measure effectiveness for AI-assisted robotic navigation in mechanical thrombectomy. extra.comment: Published in Journal of the American Heart Association
extra.full_text: While we are making progress in overcoming infectious diseases and cancer; one of the major medical challenges of the mid-21st century will be the rising prevalence of stroke.

title: SwiftBot: A Decentralized Platform for LLM-Powered Federated Robotic Task Execution
summary: SwiftBot targets federated robot task execution, where natural-language commands have to be translated into coordinated actions across heterogeneous edge robots without relying on a central controller. It combines LLM-driven instruction handling with decentralized resource management, aiming to let distributed robots share task execution while accounting for uneven compute capacity at the edge.

extra.full_text: Federated robotic task execution systems require bridging natural language instructions to distributed robot control while efficiently managing computational resources across heterogeneous edge devices without centralized coordination.

title: SurgSync: Time-Synchronized Multi-Modal Data Collection Framework and Dataset for Surgical Robotics
summary: SurgSync targets the data bottleneck behind more autonomous surgical robots by providing a time-synchronized collection framework for multi-modal robotic surgery data. It is aimed at capturing aligned streams needed to study higher-level control beyond direct surgeon teleoperation, such as supervised or full autonomy, and packages that capability with a surgical robotics dataset.

extra.full_text: Most existing robotic surgery systems adopt a human-in-the-loop paradigm, often with the surgeon directly teleoperating the robotic system. Adding intelligence to these robots would enable higher-level control, such as supervised autonomy or even full autonomy.

title: Learning-Based Robust Control: Unifying Exploration and Distributional Robustness for Reliable Robotics via Free Energy
summary: Learning-based robust control is framed through free energy, tying together the need to explore while learning policies with distributional robustness at deployment. The aim is to give robotic controllers a computational model that can adapt from data without losing reliability guarantees when the field conditions differ from training.

extra.full_text: A key challenge towards reliable robotic control is devising computational models that can both learn policies and guarantee robustness when deployed in the field.

title: Learning from Imperfect Demonstrations via Temporal Behavior Tree-Guided Trajectory Repair
summary: Temporal Behavior Tree-Guided Trajectory Repair targets the messy-demonstration problem in robot learning by using a temporal behavior tree structure to identify and repair flawed parts of trajectories before they are used for policy learning. The idea is interesting because it treats imperfect demonstrations as recoverable training data rather than simply filtering them out or forcing imitation learning to absorb their noise.

extra.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
extra.full_text: Learning robot control policies from demonstrations is a powerful paradigm, yet real-world data is often suboptimal, noisy, or otherwise imperfect, posing significant challenges for imitation and reinforcement learning.

title: A Multi-Layer Sim-to-Real Framework for Gaze-Driven Assistive Neck Exoskeletons
summary: A multi-layer sim-to-real pipeline is used to develop a gaze-driven powered neck exoskeleton for people with dropped head syndrome, aiming to restore more natural head support and movement when neck muscles are too weak to do so reliably. The system links user gaze intent to assisted neck motion, with simulation-to-hardware transfer as the central mechanism for making the controller practical on a real wearable device.

extra.comment: IEEE International Conference on Robotics & Automation (ICRA), 2026. Equal Contribution from the first two authors
extra.full_text: Dropped head syndrome, caused by neck muscle weakness from neurological diseases, severely impairs an individual's ability to support and move their head, causing pain and making everyday tasks challenging. Our long-term goal is to develop an assistive powered neck exoskeleton that restores natural movement.

title: Unified Learning of Temporal Task Structure and Action Timing for Bimanual Robot Manipulation
summary: Unified Learning of Temporal Task Structure and Action Timing targets bimanual manipulation by learning both the ordering or overlap of subtasks and the precise timing and duration of each action.
