extra.full_text: Temporal task structure is fundamental for bimanual manipulation: a robot must not only know that one action precedes or overlaps another, but also when each action should occur and how long it should take.

title: Robotic Foundation Models for Industrial Control: A Comprehensive Survey and Readiness Assessment Framework
summary: Robotic foundation models are positioned as a route to more flexible industrial robot control, especially for systems that can follow instructions or learn from demonstrations rather than being hand-programmed for each task. The survey focuses on the gap between that promise and deployment reality, assessing where RFMs are actually ready for industrial control and what technical or operational barriers still limit their use.

extra.full_text: Robotic foundation models (RFMs) are emerging as a promising route towards flexible, instruction- and demonstration-driven robot control, however, a critical investigation of their industrial applicability is still lacking.

title: A Hazard-Informed Data Pipeline for Robotics Physical Safety
summary: The report lays out a Robotics Physical Safety Framework that starts by explicitly declaring the assets in a robotic system, then enumerates vulnerabilities and uses hazards to drive synthetic data generation. Its emphasis is on turning safety analysis into a structured data pipeline, so robotics teams can generate training or evaluation data around physically meaningful failure modes rather than generic edge cases.

extra.comment: 4th International Conference on Automation and Mechatronics Engineering (ICAME 2026)
extra.full_text: This report presents a structured Robotics Physical Safety Framework based on explicit asset declaration, systematic vulnerability enumeration, and hazard-driven synthetic data generation.

title: Environment-Aware Path Generation for Robotic Additive Manufacturing of Structures
summary: Robotic additive manufacturing is framed here as a construction process that should generate toolpaths in response to the surrounding environment, rather than relying entirely on precomputed offline slicing. The work targets structure-scale AM, where adapting the path during fabrication could make robotic printing more flexible when site conditions or geometry differ from an a priori plan.

title: Residual RL--MPC for Robust Microrobotic Cell Pushing Under Time-Varying Flow
summary: Residual RL-MPC is used to keep a magnetic rolling microrobot in pushing contact with a cell while following a waypoint-sampled path through time-varying Poiseuille flow. The setup targets the hard part of contact-rich micromanipulation: small flow disturbances can quickly break contact and create large lateral drift, so the learned residual augments model predictive control to improve robustness during planar cell pushing.

extra.full_text: Contact-rich micromanipulation in microfluidic flow is challenging because small disturbances can break pushing contact and induce large lateral drift. We study planar cell pushing with a magnetic rolling microrobot that tracks a waypoint-sampled reference curve under time-varying Poiseuille flow.

title: Planning in 8 Tokens: A Compact Discrete Tokenizer for Latent World Model
summary: Planning in 8 Tokens describes a compact discrete tokenizer for latent world models, aimed at representing environment dynamics in a very small token budget while still supporting planning or policy learning. From the provided abstract fragment, the work appears to focus on making action-conditioned simulation more efficient by compressing the latent dynamics into just eight tokens, but no concrete experiments or results are given here.

extra.full_text: World models provide a powerful framework for simulating environment dynamics conditioned on actions or instructions, enabling downstream tasks such as action planning or policy learning.

title: CT-Enabled Patient-Specific Simulation and Contact-Aware Robotic Planning for Cochlear Implantation
summary: CT-derived patient anatomy is used to simulate cochlear-implant electrode insertion with explicit contact-force prediction, giving a patient-specific model of when the electrode may press, lock, or buckle inside the cochlea. The planning component uses those contact estimates to choose robotic insertion motions that regulate force and reduce intracochlear trauma risk, targeting one of the practical failure points in robotic CI surgery.

extra.full_text: Robotic cochlear-implant (CI) insertion requires precise prediction and regulation of contact forces to minimize intracochlear trauma and prevent failure modes such as locking and buckling.

title: A Multi-View 3D Telepresence System for XR Robot Teleoperation
summary: A multi-view 3D telepresence system for XR robot teleoperation gives operators a richer spatial view of remote robots than conventional screen interfaces, targeting settings like remote maintenance, search and rescue, fleet operation, and robot-learning data collection. It focuses on making teleoperation more intuitive by improving 3D visualization and depth cues, which are often the weak point in standard camera-feed setups.

extra.full_text: Robot teleoperation is critical for applications such as remote maintenance, fleet robotics, search and rescue, and data collection for robot learning. Effective teleoperation requires intuitive 3D visualization with reliable depth cues, which conventional screen-based interfaces often fail to provide.

title: Towards Edge Intelligence via Autonomous Navigation: A Robot-Assisted Data Collection Approach
summary: Mobile robots are used as proactive data collectors for edge intelligence, navigating through complex environments to gather large-scale, high-quality data rather than relying on static or manually placed sensors. The work frames autonomous navigation as part of the data pipeline itself, making robot motion and sensing decisions central to improving what edge systems can learn from their surroundings.

extra.comment: 6 pages, 9 figures, submitted to IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC) 2026
extra.full_text: With the growing demand for large-scale and high-quality data in edge intelligence systems, mobile robots are increasingly deployed to collect data proactively, particularly in complex environments.

title: Human-Robot Copilot for Data-Efficient Imitation Learning
summary: Human-Robot Copilot tackles the data scarcity problem in imitation learning by helping a robot recover when a policy trained from few teleoperated demonstrations drifts into out-of-distribution states. It focuses on compounding errors and environmental stochasticity, framing the system as a copilot that can keep execution closer to demonstrated behavior when the learned policy alone would be brittle.

extra.full_text: Collecting human demonstrations via teleoperation is a common approach for teaching robots task-specific skills. However, when only a limited number of demonstrations are available, policies are prone to entering out-of-distribution (OOD) states due to compounding errors or environmental stochasticity.

title: Optimizing Neurorobot Policy under Limited Demonstration Data through Preference Regret
summary: Preference Regret targets robot reinforcement learning from demonstrations when expert trajectories are scarce or expensive to collect, reframing policy optimization around regret under limited preference information rather than assuming abundant demonstrations. The idea is aimed at making neurorobot policies learn more effectively from small demonstration sets, a practical constraint that standard RLfD setups often sidestep.

extra.full_text: Robot reinforcement learning from demonstrations (RLfD) assumes that expert data is abundant; this is usually unrealistic in the real world given data scarcity as well as high collection cost.

title: Python Bindings for a Large C++ Robotics Library: The Case of OMPL
summary: OMPL’s Python bindings expose a large, performance-oriented C++ motion-planning library to Python, letting robotics researchers prototype planners, run reproducible experiments, and connect OMPL more easily to simulation or learning stacks. The interesting part is the engineering bridge itself: keeping OMPL’s C++ performance and breadth while making it usable from the Python workflows that dominate rapid robotics experimentation.

extra.full_text: Python bindings are a critical bridge between high-performance C++ libraries and the flexibility of Python, enabling rapid prototyping, reproducible experiments, and integration with simulation and learning frameworks in robotics research.

title: HandelBot: Real-World Piano Playing via Fast Adaptation of Dexterous Robot Policies
summary: HandelBot tackles dexterous piano playing with a multi-fingered robot hand, framing it as a high-precision real-world manipulation problem where collecting enough good demonstrations is the bottleneck. From the provided abstract fragment, the work appears centered on fast adaptation of robot policies so a dexterous hand can transfer or tune its behavior efficiently for piano performance rather than relying on extensive task-specific data.

extra.full_text: Mastering dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands has been a grand challenge in robotics for decades. Despite its potential, the difficulty of collecting high-quality data remains a primary bottleneck for high-precision tasks.

title: ManipulationNet: An Infrastructure for Benchmarking Real-World Robot Manipulation with Physical Skill Challenges and Embodied Multimodal Reasoning
summary: ManipulationNet is a benchmarking infrastructure for real-world robot manipulation, built around physical skill challenges and embodied multimodal reasoning rather than passive perception alone. It frames dexterous manipulation as a core testbed for physical AI, focusing on how robots use perception, language, and action to alter objects and environments under unstructured real-world conditions.

extra.full_text: Dexterous manipulation enables robots to purposefully alter the physical world, transforming them from passive observers into active agents in unstructured environments. This capability is the cornerstone of physical artificial intelligence.

title: Modeling and Control of a Pneumatic Soft Robotic Catheter Using Neural Koopman Operators
summary: Neural Koopman operators are used to model and control a pneumatic soft robotic catheter for cardiac interventions, aiming to capture the catheter’s nonlinear soft-body dynamics in a form suitable for control. The work sits at the intersection of soft robotics and catheter automation, where better learned dynamics models could improve the precision and stability of robot-assisted navigation compared with manual catheter manipulation.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
extra.full_text: Catheter-based interventions are widely used for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac diseases. Recently, robotic catheters have attracted attention for their ability to improve precision and stability over conventional manual approaches.

title: A Novel Modular Cable-Driven Soft Robotic Arm with Multi-Segment Reconfigurability
summary: A modular soft robotic arm is built from stackable cable-driven segments, with each segment controlled independently so the arm can be reconfigured for different lengths, structures, and task requirements. The interesting part is the architecture: instead of a fixed soft arm, it treats the manipulator as a scalable multi-segment system whose morphology and control layout can be adapted to the application.

extra.full_text: This paper presents a novel, modular, cable-driven soft robotic arm featuring multi-segment reconfigurability. The proposed architecture enables a stackable system with independent segment control, allowing scalable adaptation to diverse structural and application requirements.

title: Architectural HRI: Towards a Robotic Paradigm Shift in Human-Building Interaction
summary: Architectural HRI frames buildings as robotic systems whose walls, facades, services, and spatial elements can sense, communicate, and physically reconfigure around occupants. The interesting shift is from human-building interaction as adaptive environmental control toward embodied actuation of architecture itself, bringing robotics concepts like control, interfaces, and coordinated motion into the design of lived space.

extra.full_text: Recent advances in sensing, communication, interfaces, control, and robotics are expanding Human-Building Interaction (HBI) beyond adaptive building services and facades toward the physical actuation of architectural space.

title: LLM-Foraging: Large Language Models for Decentralized Swarm Robot Foraging
summary: LLM-Foraging applies large language models to decentralized swarm robot foraging, targeting a weakness of methods like CPFA whose GA- or RL-tuned policies often overfit to one team size, arena, and resource layout. The idea is to use an LLM-driven mechanism to adapt foraging behavior more flexibly across deployment conditions, rather than relying on offline parameter optimization tied to a fixed scenario.

extra.full_text: Swarm foraging algorithms, such as the central-place foraging algorithm (CPFA), typically rely on offline parameter optimization using genetic algorithms (GA) or reinforcement learning, yielding policies tightly coupled to a specific combination of team size, arena size, and resource distribution.

title: Robust Tightly-Coupled Filter-Based Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimation and Graph-Based Evaluation for Autonomous Drone Racing
summary: Robust Tightly-Coupled Filter-Based Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimation targets the state-estimation bottleneck in autonomous drone racing, where high speed and aggressive maneuvers can degrade visual perception while compute budgets stay tight. It combines a filter-based monocular visual-inertial estimator with graph-based evaluation, aiming to keep pose estimates reliable enough for racing drones under fast, visually challenging flight conditions.

extra.full_text: Autonomous drone racing (ADR) demands state estimation that is simultaneously computationally efficient and resilient to the perceptual degradation experienced during extreme velocity and maneuvers.

title: Realistic Lip Motion Generation Based on 3D Dynamic Viseme and Coarticulation Modeling for Human-Robot Interaction
summary: Realistic Lip Motion Generation builds lip-sync for humanoid robots around 3D dynamic visemes, modeling mouth shapes as time-varying units rather than static phoneme-to-pose mappings. It also incorporates coarticulation, so neighboring sounds influence each other’s lip motion, aiming to make robot speech look more natural during human-robot interaction.

extra.full_text: Realistic lip synchronization is essential for the natural human-robot non-verbal interaction of humanoid robots. Motivated by this need, this paper presents a lip motion generation framework based on 3D dynamic viseme and coarticulation modeling.

title: OpenGo: An OpenClaw-Based Robotic Dog with Real-Time Skill Switching
summary: OpenGo is a robotic dog built on the OpenClaw platform that targets real-time switching among multiple embodied skills, rather than treating each behavior or scenario as a separate control problem. The paper frames skill acquisition, organization, and rapid selection as the central bottleneck for deploying a single robot agent in dynamic environments, with the system intended as an open platform for studying that kind of adaptive quadruped intelligence.

extra.full_text: Adaptation to complex tasks and multiple scenarios remains a significant challenge for a single robot agent. The ability to acquire organize, and switch between a wide range of skills in real time, particularly in dynamic environments, has become a fundamental requirement for embodied intelligence.

title: Online Safety Filter for Deformable Object Manipulation with Horizon Agnostic Neural Operators
summary: Online Safety Filter for Deformable Object Manipulation with Horizon Agnostic Neural Operators targets safety-critical manipulation of fluids, cloth, and soft objects, where learned policies often rely on reward shaping and can violate constraints at deployment. It frames safety as an online filtering problem and uses horizon-agnostic neural operators to enforce constraints over deformable-object dynamics without tying the filter to a fixed prediction horizon.

extra.full_text: Safety critical control of robotic manipulation tasks involving deformable media such as fluids, cloth, and soft objects remains challenging because existing learning based approaches encode safety indirectly through reward shaping, which provides no guarantee of constraint satisfaction at deployment.

title: An Integrated Soft Robotic System for Measuring Vital Signs in Search and Rescue Environments
summary: Soft robotic components are being integrated into search-and-rescue robots to support victim assessment after disasters, with a focus on measuring heart rate and contact pressure in environments where direct human access may be difficult or unsafe. The interesting gap it targets is practical triage in post-disaster scenarios: prior rescue robotics work has advanced victim assessment, but heart-rate sensing remains unresolved and pressure assessment appears largely unexplored.

extra.full_text: Robots are frequently utilized in search-and-rescue operations. In recent years, significant advancements have been made in the field of victim assessment. However, there are still open issues regarding heart rate measurement, and no studies have been found that assess pressure in post-disaster scenarios.

title: RoboGPU: Accelerating GPU Collision Detection for Robotics
summary: RoboGPU targets GPU-accelerated collision detection for robotics, a bottleneck in planning and simulation as autonomous systems move into domains like medical care, transportation, and home assistance. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available, so it can only be characterized as work on making robot collision checking faster on GPUs rather than evaluated in detail.

extra.full_text: Autonomous robots are increasingly prevalent in our society, emerging in medical care, transportation vehicles, and home assistance.

title: FATE: Closed-Loop Feasibility-Aware Task Generation with Active Repair for Physically Grounded Robotic Curricula
summary: FATE targets a common failure mode in LLM-generated robot curricula: tasks that sound valid but cannot actually be executed in simulation because the goals or objectives are physically misgrounded. It closes the loop by checking feasibility and actively repairing generated tasks, aiming to produce curricula whose language, objectives, and simulated physics stay aligned.

extra.full_text: Recent breakthroughs in generative simulation have harnessed Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate diverse robotic task curricula, yet these open-loop paradigms frequently produce linguistically coherent but physically infeasible goals, stemming from ungrounded task specifications or misaligned objective formulations.

title: Reconfiguration of supernumerary robotic limbs for human augmentation
summary: Wearable supernumerary robotic limbs are treated as reconfigurable augmentation devices that should adapt their form and behavior to both the human wearer and the surrounding task context. From the limited abstract text available, the focus is on personalized interaction and seamless environmental adaptation rather than a fixed extra-limb design, but no specific mechanism, evaluation, or quantitative result is provided.

extra.full_text: Wearable robots aim to seamlessly adapt to humans and their environment with personalized interactions.

title: Bridging Discrete Planning and Continuous Execution for Redundant Robot
summary: Voxel-grid reinforcement learning is used here as a practical planning interface for redundant manipulators, turning continuous robot motion into a discrete path-planning problem that is easier to reproduce and train. From the provided text, the work appears focused on connecting that discrete voxel-based planner to the continuous execution demands of a redundant robot, but no specific mechanism, experiments, or results are given.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IFAC World Congress 2026
extra.full_text: Voxel-grid reinforcement learning is widely adopted for path planning in redundant manipulators due to its simplicity and reproducibility.

title: LLM-Flax : Generalizable Robotic Task Planning via Neuro-Symbolic Approaches with Large Language Models
summary: LLM-Flax targets the heavy setup cost of neuro-symbolic robotic task planners, where experts normally have to hand-write domain rules and generate many solved training problems for a GNN-based object scorer. It uses large language models to help generalize the planning machinery to new domains, reducing the amount of manual symbolic engineering and supervised data needed when moving a robot planner beyond its original task setting.

extra.full_text: Deploying a neuro-symbolic task planner on a new domain today requires significant manual effort: a domain expert must author relaxation and complementary rules, and hundreds of training problems must be solved to supervise a Graph Neural Network (GNN) object scorer.

title: Alter-Art: Exploring Embodied Artistic Creation through a Robot Avatar
summary: Alter-Art explores a robot avatar as an embodied medium for artistic creation, positioning the machine less as an independent artist or co-creator and more as a physical extension that preserves a tighter link to the human artist. The interesting move is the focus on that in-between space: using robotics to reshape how artwork is made without severing authorship and intent from the person directing the creative act.

extra.full_text: As with every emerging technology, new tools in the hands of artists reshape the nature of artwork creation. Current frameworks for robotics in arts deploy the robot as an autonomous creator or a collaborator, thus leaving a certain gap between the human artist and the machine.

title: Flip Stunts on Bicycle Robots using Iterative Motion Imitation
summary: Iterative Motion Imitation trains bicycle robots to perform a front flip by starting from reference motions that are not directly feasible, then repeatedly using rollouts from earlier policies as improved imitation targets. The result is a reinforcement-learning pipeline that can bootstrap a highly dynamic stunt from imperfect demonstrations, showing how policy-generated trajectories can gradually become useful training references for underactuated robotic maneuvers.

extra.comment: 8 Pages, Accepted to the IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
extra.full_text: This work demonstrates a front-flip on bicycle robots via reinforcement learning, particularly by imitating reference motions that are infeasible and imperfect. To address this, we propose Iterative Motion Imitation(IMI), a method that iteratively imitates trajectories generated by prior policy rollouts.

title: Computational Design and Co-Robotic Fabrication for Material Reuse in Architecture
summary: Computational design and co-robotic fabrication are used to help architecture reuse materials instead of following the usual take-make-use-dispose construction cycle. From the limited text available, the project appears to connect circular design goals with robotic construction workflows, aiming to reduce waste and resource demand in building practice.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication in Proceedings of the 45th Annual Conference of the Association for Computer Aided Design in Architecture (ACADIA 2025)
extra.full_text: Climate change and resource depletion demand a shift from the dominant linear "take-make-use-dispose" paradigm of construction toward circular, low-waste practices.

title: Design of an In-Pipe Robot with Contact-Angle-Guided Kinematic Decoupling for Crosstalk-Suppressed Locomotion
summary: An in-pipe inspection robot is designed to handle both forward traction and fast rolling reorientation inside tight pipe networks with elbows and 3D fittings. Its contact-angle-guided kinematic decoupling is meant to suppress crosstalk between axial motion and roll posture correction, making locomotion more controllable in confined, curved pipeline geometries.

extra.full_text: In-pipe inspection robots must traverse confined pipeline networks with elbows and three-dimensional fittings, requiring both reliable axial traction and rapid rolling reorientation for posture correction.

title: ROSClaw: An OpenClaw ROS 2 Framework for Agentic Robot Control and Interaction
summary: ROSClaw is a ROS 2 framework that connects foundation-model agents to OpenClaw robots, aiming to make language-driven planning, perception, actuation, and interaction less tied to one-off robot-model integrations. From the provided abstract fragment, its emphasis is on giving researchers a reusable control and interaction layer for agentic robot experiments rather than rebuilding the stack around each model or platform.

extra.full_text: Foundation models can endow robots with open-ended reasoning, language understanding, and adaptive planning, yet connecting a model to a physical robot today requires bespoke integration that couples perception, actuation, and safety to a single model and platform.

title: RHINO-AR: An Augmented Reality Exhibit for Teaching Mobile Robotics Concepts in Museums
summary: RHINO-AR is an interactive augmented-reality museum exhibit that places the historical mobile robot RHINO back into its original Deutsches Museum Bonn setting. It extends the earlier RHINO-VR reconstruction by moving from a fully virtual recreation to an AR experience aimed at teaching mobile robotics concepts in the physical exhibition space.

extra.full_text: We present RHINO-AR, an interactive Augmented Reality (AR) museum exhibit that reintroduces the historical mobile robot RHINO into its original exhibition environment at the Deutsches Museum Bonn. The system builds on our previous work RHINO-VR, which reconstructed the robot and the environment in virtual reality.

title: A Minimum-Energy Control Approach for Redundant Mobile Manipulators in Physical Human-Robot Interaction Applications
summary: A minimum-energy control strategy is applied to redundant mobile manipulators during physical human-robot interaction, targeting systems that must coordinate a mobile base and arm while safely exchanging forces with people. The setup is motivated by human-assistive mobile manipulation, where redundancy can be used to perform contact-rich tasks that fixed-base manipulators cannot handle, while explicitly minimizing control effort.

extra.full_text: Research on mobile manipulation systems that physically interact with humans has expanded rapidly in recent years, opening the way to tasks which could not be performed using fixed-base manipulators.

title: Learning from the Best: Smoothness-Driven Metrics for Data Quality in Imitation Learning
summary: Behavioral cloning is reframed around demonstration quality, using smoothness-driven metrics to identify which trajectories are likely to support better imitation rather than weighting all data equally. The idea targets common real-world failure modes such as uneven operator skill, teleoperation artifacts, and procedural inconsistency, giving a policy learner a way to prefer cleaner, more reliable demonstrations before training.

extra.full_text: In behavioral cloning (BC), policy performance is fundamentally limited by demonstration data quality. Real-world datasets contain trajectories of varying quality due to operator skill differences, teleoperation artifacts, and procedural inconsistencies, yet standard BC treats all demonstrations equally.

title: QuadFM: Foundational Text-Driven Quadruped Motion Dataset for Generation and Control
summary: QuadFM is a text-driven quadruped motion dataset aimed at filling a gap between low-level locomotion data and richer behaviors described in language. It is positioned as a foundation resource for generating and controlling quadruped motions that include diverse gaits, emotionally expressive actions, and semantic prompts, with an eye toward more intuitive human-robot interaction.

extra.full_text: Despite significant advances in quadrupedal robotics, a critical gap persists in foundational motion resources that holistically integrate diverse locomotion, emotionally expressive behaviors, and rich language semantics-essential for agile, intuitive human-robot interaction.

title: Wiggle and Go! System Identification for Zero-Shot Dynamic Rope Manipulation
summary: Wiggle and Go uses learned simulation priors to identify rope dynamics and guide goal-conditioned dynamic manipulation without task-specific real-world tuning. The system targets fast, failure-sensitive rope throwing or placement tasks, where a poor action can cause long recovery delays, by using its simulation-informed model to choose accurate motions zero-shot.

extra.full_text: Many robotic tasks are unforgiving; a single mistake in a dynamic throw can lead to unacceptable delays or unrecoverable failure. To mitigate this, we present a novel approach that leverages learned simulation priors to inform goal-conditioned dynamic manipulation of ropes for efficient and accurate task execution.

title: FingerEye: Continuous and Unified Vision-Tactile Sensing for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: FingerEye targets the perception gap in dexterous manipulation by providing continuous, unified vision-tactile sensing across pre-contact, contact initiation, and post-contact phases. The idea is to give a robot feedback before and during touch so it can adjust grasping and manipulation actions as the interaction unfolds, rather than treating vision and tactile sensing as separate or phase-specific signals.

extra.full_text: Dexterous robotic manipulation requires comprehensive perception across all phases of interaction: pre-contact, contact initiation, and post-contact. Such continuous feedback allows a robot to adapt its actions throughout interaction.

title: EquiBim: Learning Symmetry-Equivariant Policy for Bimanual Manipulation
summary: EquiBim targets bimanual robot imitation learning by training policies that respect symmetry structure, so paired-arm behaviors can generalize across mirrored or coordinated configurations more naturally. From the available text, it is an arXiv paper about learning symmetry-equivariant policies for complex manipulation from demonstrations, with the interesting angle being the use of geometric symmetry as an inductive bias for two-handed robot control.

extra.full_text: Robotic imitation learning has achieved impressive success in learning complex manipulation behaviors from demonstrations.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Manipulation Understanding with Enriched Semantic Event Chains
summary: Neuro-Symbolic Manipulation Understanding with Enriched Semantic Event Chains targets robot manipulation reasoning by modeling how object relations change across an action sequence, so a system can recognize the current step and anticipate what should happen next. From the provided text, the work centers on enriched semantic event chains as a structured representation for temporal object-interaction dynamics in human environments, but no benchmark, dataset, or quantitative result is given.

extra.full_text: Robotic systems operating in human environments must reason about how object interactions evolve over time, which actions are currently being performed, and what manipulation step is likely to follow.

title: Visual-Tactile Peg-in-Hole Assembly Learning from Peg-out-of-Hole Disassembly
summary: Visual-Tactile Peg-in-Hole Assembly Learning from Peg-out-of-Hole Disassembly studies how to learn peg insertion from the reverse process: taking a peg out of a hole, which can provide structured experience without the same costly exploration burden as reinforcement learning from scratch. The setup targets peg-in-hole assembly using visual and tactile feedback, aiming to turn disassembly trajectories into useful guidance for the harder insertion policy.

extra.full_text: Peg-in-hole (PiH) assembly is a fundamental yet challenging robotic manipulation task. While reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise in tackling such tasks, it requires extensive exploration.

title: ETac: A Lightweight and Efficient Tactile Simulation Framework for Learning Dexterous Manipulation
summary: ETac targets the bottleneck in training tactile-aware dexterous manipulation policies: soft-body tactile simulation is useful but often too slow or expensive for large-scale learning. It presents a lightweight tactile simulation framework meant to preserve contact information needed by policies while reducing computational cost, making tactile sensing more practical in robot learning pipelines.

extra.full_text: Tactile sensors are increasingly integrated into dexterous robotic manipulators to enhance contact perception. However, learning manipulation policies that rely on tactile sensing remains challenging, primarily due to the trade-off between fidelity and computational cost of soft-body simulations.

title: Wrench-Aware Admittance Control for Unknown-Payload Manipulation
summary: Wrench-Aware Admittance Control addresses compliant manipulation when an unknown payload shifts the effective center of mass away from the tool center point, creating extra wrist forces and torques that can destabilize or bias the interaction. The method appears to adapt admittance control using the measured offset wrench at the robot wrist, so the robot can handle payload-induced dynamics rather than treating them as external disturbance or contact force.

extra.full_text: Unknown payloads can strongly affect compliant robotic manipulation, especially when the payload center of mass is not aligned with the tool center point. In this case, the payload generates an offset wrench at the robot wrist.

title: Quadruped Parkour Learning: Sparsely Gated Mixture of Experts with Visual Input
summary: Quadruped Parkour Learning tackles legged locomotion over difficult parkour-style terrain, especially discontinuities like elevated steps, using a sparsely gated mixture-of-experts policy with visual input. The interesting angle is the routing mechanism: instead of relying on one monolithic controller, the robot can selectively activate specialized experts from perception to handle different terrain demands.

extra.full_text: Robotic parkour provides a compelling benchmark for advancing locomotion over highly challenging terrain, including large discontinuities such as elevated steps.

title: Enhancing Vision-Based Policies with Omni-View and Cross-Modality Knowledge Distillation for Mobile Robots
summary: Vision-based control on small mobile robots is framed around a practical tradeoff: policies need to transfer across scenes while staying cheap enough for limited onboard compute and sensors. The work points toward using omni-view perception and cross-modality knowledge distillation to give lightweight vision policies richer spatial and sensor-derived cues without requiring expensive hardware at deployment.

extra.full_text: Vision-based policies are widely applied in robotics for tasks such as manipulation and locomotion. On lightweight mobile robots, however, they face a trilemma of limited scene transferability, restricted onboard computation resources, and sensor hardware cost.

title: MM-Hand: A 21-DOF Multi-modal Modular Dexterous Robotic Hand with Remote Actuation
summary: MM-Hand is a 21-DOF dexterous robotic hand built around remote actuation, moving motors and heat sources out of the hand to preserve compactness, reduce end-effector mass, and improve thermal behavior. Its modular, multi-modal design targets the usual tradeoff in high-DOF hands: keeping rich sensing and dexterity while avoiding cramped in-hand packaging and heat buildup near the fingers.

extra.full_text: High-DOF dexterous hands require compact actuation, rich sensing, and reliable thermal behavior, but conventional designs often occupy valuable in-hand space, increase end-effector mass, and suffer from heat accumulation near the hand.

title: Evolving Embodied Intelligence: Graph Neural Network--Driven Co-Design of Morphology and Control in Soft Robotics
summary: Embodied intelligence is framed here as a co-design problem for soft robots, where morphology and control are optimized together rather than treated as separate modules. The paper centers on graph neural networks as the mechanism for representing and evolving the coupled body-brain system, aiming to capture how a robot’s physical structure shapes the behavior its controller can produce.

extra.full_text: The intelligent behavior of robots does not emerge solely from control systems, but from the tight coupling between body and brain, a principle known as embodied intelligence.

title: SOFTMAP: Sim2Real Soft Robot Forward Modeling via Topological Mesh Alignment and Physics Prior
summary: SOFTMAP targets forward modeling for soft robot manipulators, where mapping low-dimensional actuation commands to shape is difficult because real hardware departs from simulation through hysteresis, nonlinear materials, and fabrication variation. It combines topological mesh alignment with a physics prior to transfer simulated soft-body behavior into real-world prediction, aiming to preserve physically plausible structure while correcting the sim-to-real mismatch.

extra.full_text: While soft robot manipulators offer compelling advantages over rigid counterparts, including inherent compliance, safe human-robot interaction, and the ability to conform to complex geometries, accurate forward modeling from low-dimensional actuation commands remains an open challenge due to nonlinear material phenomena such as hysteresis and manufacturing variability.

title: Fire as a Service: Augmenting Robot Simulators with Thermally and Visually Accurate Fire Dynamics
summary: Fire as a Service augments robot simulators with fire behavior that is both thermally and visually realistic, targeting a gap in simulators that usually handle rigid-body physics and photorealistic scenes but not the heat transfer and optical effects of flames. It appears aimed at making fire-response robotics experiments more faithful to real environments, where perception, navigation, and hardware safety are shaped by temperature fields, smoke, light, and dynamic flame behavior.

extra.full_text: Most existing robot simulators prioritize rigid-body dynamics and photorealistic rendering, but largely neglect the thermally and optically complex phenomena that characterize real-world fire environments.

title: Whole-Body Safe Control of Robotic Systems with Koopman Neural Dynamics
summary: Whole-body safe control is tackled by learning Koopman-style neural dynamics that lift a robot’s nonlinear, high-dimensional behavior into a representation more amenable to real-time control. The setup is aimed at enforcing safety constraints without solving the full nonlinear constrained optimization problem online, making it relevant for robots whose coupled body dynamics are too complex for conventional safety-critical controllers to handle directly.

extra.full_text: Controlling robots with strongly nonlinear, high-dimensional dynamics remains challenging, as direct nonlinear optimization with safety constraints is often intractable in real time.

title: Rewind-IL: Online Failure Detection and State Respawning for Imitation Learning
summary: Rewind-IL tackles deployment failures in imitation-learned robot manipulation policies by detecting when execution has gone off track and respawning the robot into an earlier state instead of simply continuing a bad rollout. The idea is aimed at long-horizon, action-chunked visuomotor policies, where small errors can compound across many steps and demonstrations alone often do not provide a reliable recovery path.

extra.comment: 9 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Project page at https://sjay05.github.io/rewind-il
extra.full_text: Imitation learning has enabled robots to acquire complex visuomotor manipulation skills from demonstrations, but deployment failures remain a major obstacle, especially for long-horizon action-chunked policies.

title: DexViTac: Collecting Human Visuo-Tactile-Kinematic Demonstrations for Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation
summary: DexViTac focuses on collecting multimodal human demonstrations for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where visual and kinematic traces alone miss the forces and contacts that shape the task. It targets the data bottleneck in robot learning by adding tactile sensing to human-centric demonstration collection, aiming to produce richer training signals for policies that must reason through physical interaction rather than just object motion.

extra.full_text: Large-scale, high-quality multimodal demonstrations are essential for robot learning of contact-rich dexterous manipulation. While human-centric data collection systems lower the barrier to scaling, they struggle to capture the tactile information during physical interactions.

title: Uncovering Latent Phase Structures and Branching Logic in Locomotion Policies: A Case Study on HalfCheetah
summary: Deep reinforcement learning can produce strong HalfCheetah locomotion policies, but the resulting controller is hard to interpret. This study looks inside such a policy to expose latent phase structure and branching decision logic, aiming to make the gait-level organization and control choices visible rather than treating the policy as an opaque action mapper.

extra.comment: Accepted at XAI-2026: The 4th World Conference on eXplainable Artificial Intelligence
extra.full_text: In locomotion control tasks, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated high performance; however, the decision-making process of the learned policy remains a black box, making it difficult for humans to understand.

title: CABTO: Context-Aware Behavior Tree Grounding for Robot Manipulation
summary: CABTO focuses on grounding behavior trees for robot manipulation in context, aiming to connect modular, reactive BT controllers with automated BT planning methods that come with reliability guarantees. From the provided text, the concrete details stop at the framing: it situates the method in BT planning, where the appeal is generating controllers automatically while preserving the interpretability and robustness that make behavior trees useful in robotics.

extra.full_text: Behavior Trees (BTs) offer a powerful paradigm for designing modular and reactive robot controllers. BT planning, an emerging field, provides theoretical guarantees for the automated generation of reliable BTs.

title: A Pin-Array Structured Climbing Robot for Stable Locomotion on Steep Rocky Terrain
summary: A pin-array structured climbing robot is designed to improve attachment and stability on steep, irregular rocky terrain, where conventional contact mechanisms can struggle to maintain reliable grip. The available description only establishes the problem and the robot’s general mechanism, so the main takeaway is a terrain-adaptive climbing design focused on stable locomotion through many small pin contacts rather than a single smooth interface.

extra.comment: Author's version of a manuscript accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA). (c) IEEE
extra.full_text: Climbing robots face significant challenges when navigating unstructured environments, where reliable attachment to irregular surfaces is critical.

title: Conservative Offline Robot Policy Learning via Posterior-Transition Reweighting
summary: Offline post-training here means taking an already pretrained robot policy and adapting it to a target dataset by supervised regression on the recorded actions. The described idea, Conservative Offline Robot Policy Learning via Posterior-Transition Reweighting, appears to focus on making that regression-style adaptation more conservative by reweighting transitions according to posterior transition information, but the provided text does not include experiments, benchmarks, or results.

extra.full_text: Offline post-training adapts a pretrained robot policy to a target dataset by supervised regression on recorded actions.

title: An Intelligent Robotic and Bio-Digestor Framework for Smart Waste Management
summary: An intelligent waste-management concept combines robotic handling with a bio-digestor to automate parts of municipal solid waste processing. From the available abstract, the emphasis is on using automation to make urban waste collection or treatment smarter under pressure from rapid urbanization and population growth, but it does not provide enough detail to assess the robot design, digestion mechanism, or measured results.
