extra.full_text: Rapid urbanization and continuous population growth have made municipal solid waste management increasingly challenging. These challenges highlight the need for smarter and automated waste management solutions.

title: DigiForest: Digital Analytics and Robotics for Sustainable Forestry
summary: DigiForest is a robotics and digital analytics effort aimed at making forestry monitoring more scalable and sustainable. From the available text, it frames forests as critical infrastructure for biodiversity, climate regulation, and human well-being, and points toward robotic sensing and analytics as a way to gather richer operational data in forest environments.

extra.full_text: Covering one third of Earth's land surface, forests are vital to global biodiversity, climate regulation, and human well-being.

title: Formalisms for Robotic Mission Specification and Execution: A Comparative Analysis
summary: Robots are now being used in broader, multi-purpose settings, which makes mission specification and execution formalisms an important design question rather than just an implementation detail. The paper compares alternative ways to represent and carry out robotic missions, focusing on how different formalisms support specification, execution, and likely tradeoffs for increasingly diverse robot deployments.

extra.full_text: Robots are increasingly deployed across diverse domains and designed for multi-purpose operation.

title: Learning Bilevel Policies over Symbolic World Models for Long-Horizon Planning
summary: BISON learns a bilevel robot policy that pairs a low-level neural imitation policy for continuous manipulation with a high-level symbolic policy distilled from demonstrations and generalized inductively for long-horizon planning. On extended MetaWorld tasks, it handles longer horizons and more objects than VLA and end-to-end baselines while using less time and memory, and its symbolic planner alone can solve high-level problems with 10,000 relevant objects in under a minute.

extra.full_text: We tackle the challenge of building embodied AI agents that can reliably solve long-horizon planning problems. Imitation learning from demonstrations has shown itself to be effective in training robots to solve a diversity of complex tasks requiring fine motor control and manipulation over low-level (LL), continuous environments. Yet, it remains a difficult endeavour to generate long-horizon plans from imitation learning alone. In contrast, high-level (HL), symbolic abstractions facilitate efficient and interpretable long-horizon planning. We propose to combine the strengths of LL imitation learning for manipulation and control, and HL symbolic abstractions for long-horizon planning. We realise this idea via \emph{bilevel policies} of the form $(π^{\mathrm{hl}}, π^{\mathrm{ll}})$, consisting of a neural policy $π^{\mathrm{ll}}$ learned from LL demonstrations, and an HL symbolic policy $π^{\mathrm{hl}}$ that is constructed from symbolic abstractions of the LL demonstrations combined with inductive generalisation. We implement these ideas in the BISON system. Experiments on extended MetaWorld benchmarks demonstrate that BISON generalises to long horizons and problems with greater numbers of objects than those solved by VLA and end-to-end methods, and is more time and memory efficient in training and inference. Notably, when ignoring LL execution, BISON's HL policies can solve HL problems with 10,000 relevant objects in under a minute. Project page: https://dillonzchen.github.io/bison

title: MoE-ACT: Scaling Multi-Task Bimanual Manipulation with Sparse Language-Conditioned Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
summary: MoE-ACT targets multi-task bimanual robot manipulation with a unified policy, using a sparse language-conditioned mixture-of-experts Transformer to route different task instructions through specialized expert components. From the provided text, the concrete motivation is scaling a single embodied policy across household and industrial manipulation tasks, but no benchmark, dataset, or quantitative result is given.

extra.full_text: The ability of robots to handle multiple tasks under a unified policy is critical for deploying embodied intelligence in real-world household and industrial applications.

title: BodyGuards: Escorting by Multiple Robots in Unknown Environment under Limited Communication
summary: BodyGuards studies the problem of escorting a vulnerable or high-value agent through an unknown environment using multiple robots that can only communicate locally. The setup targets high-risk settings like reconnaissance, disaster response, and subterranean operations, where teams must coordinate protection and navigation despite incomplete maps and intermittent connectivity.

extra.full_text: Multi-robot systems are increasingly deployed in high-risk missions such as reconnaissance, disaster response, and subterranean operations.

title: Optimizing Line Segment Inspection with Limited-Range Drones
summary: The paper studies how to plan drone routes for inspecting line segments when each drone has limited flight range, a common constraint in battery-limited aerial surveillance. It frames the problem around covering linear infrastructure or terrain features efficiently despite range limits, linking drone inspection planning with operational-research questions about endurance and coverage.

extra.full_text: Optimization problems with drones are widely studied in a variety of civilian tasks, mainly due to their ability to traverse rough terrains and to carry cameras and other sensors for surveillance tasks. The limited battery life of these aerial robots poses challenges in operational research.

title: Self-adaptive Multi-Access Edge Architectures: A Robotics Case
summary: Self-adaptive multi-access edge architectures are applied to a robotics setting where compute-heavy AI workloads can be shifted or managed closer to the robot to reduce processing cost. The work is framed around improving performance and energy efficiency for robotic systems that cannot always afford to run demanding AI tasks entirely onboard.

extra.full_text: The growth of compute-intensive AI tasks highlights the need to mitigate the processing costs and improve performance and energy efficiency.

title: Policy Optimization in Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Action Spaces via Mixed Gradients
summary: Policy Optimization in Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Action Spaces via Mixed Gradients targets reinforcement learning problems where an agent must choose both a discrete mode or index and continuous parameters within that choice, a pattern that shows up in robotics, control, and operations. The method optimizes these hybrid policies with mixed gradients, aiming to handle the coupled discrete-continuous decision structure directly rather than flattening or separating the action space.

extra.full_text: We study reinforcement learning in hybrid discrete-continuous action spaces, such as settings where the discrete component selects a regime (or index) and the continuous component optimizes within it -- a structure common in robotics, control, and operations problems.

title: Distill: Uncovering the True Intent behind Human-Robot Communication
summary: Distill focuses on helping robots infer the underlying intent behind human instructions, especially when communication comes through natural language or end-user programming rather than low-level commands. The available description frames the problem as a practical one for everyday autonomy: as robots move into less controlled environments, they need communication interfaces that let non-experts specify behavior intuitively while still producing reliable robot actions.

extra.full_text: As robots become increasingly integrated into everyday environments, intuitive communication paradigms such as natural language and end-user programming have become indispensable for specifying autonomous robot behavior.

title: See, Learn, Assist: Safe and Self-Paced Robotic Rehabilitation via Video-Based Learning from Demonstration
summary: Therapists can teach robot-assisted rehabilitation exercises remotely by recording RGB-D demonstrations, which the system uses as the basis for guided patient assistance. The focus is on making rehabilitation robots learn from video while supporting safe, self-paced exercise, so therapy routines can be transferred without requiring the therapist and robot to be co-located.

extra.full_text: In this paper, we propose a novel framework that allows therapists to teach robot-assisted rehabilitation exercises remotely via RGB-D video.

title: Terminal Matters: Kinodynamic Planning with a Terminal Cost and Learned Uncertainty in Belief State-Cost Space
summary: Terminal Matters studies kinodynamic motion planning for robots that need to reach goals reliably while respecting dynamics and uncertainty. It centers on planning in a belief state-cost space with a terminal cost and learned uncertainty, aiming to make goal-reaching behavior more dependable in real-world settings where outcomes are not deterministic.

extra.full_text: In many real-world robotic tasks, robots must generate dynamically feasible motions that reliably reach desired goals even under uncertainty.

title: LARY: A Latent Action Representation Yielding Benchmark for Generalizable Vision-to-Action Alignment
summary: LARY targets the data bottleneck in vision-language-action models by turning large amounts of unlabeled human action video into a latent action representation for vision-to-action alignment. The benchmark is meant to test whether these learned action abstractions can generalize beyond explicitly labeled robot action data, which is interesting because it treats human video as scalable supervision rather than requiring costly robot demonstrations.

extra.full_text: While the shortage of explicit action data limits Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, human action videos offer a scalable yet unlabeled data source.

title: Data-Driven Autoregressive Power Prediction for GTernal Robots in the Robotarium
summary: Energy-aware multi-robot control on Robotarium GTernal robots is framed as a data-driven forecasting problem, using autoregressive power prediction instead of hand-built kinematic approximations. The appeal is that the model is meant to learn hardware-specific consumption patterns directly from robot data, capturing dynamics that simpler motion-based formulas miss.

extra.full_text: Energy-aware algorithms for multi-robot systems require accurate power consumption models, yet existing approaches rely on kinematic approximations that fail to capture the complex dynamics of real hardware.

title: Object Manipulation of the Variable Topology Truss system
summary: Object manipulation is framed for a Variable Topology Truss system, a robot made from actuated truss members joined by passive spherical joints. The interesting part is the morphology: by changing its truss topology rather than relying on a conventional arm or gripper, the robot can reposition and manipulate objects through coordinated member actuation.

extra.full_text: This paper presents an object manipulation strategy for the Variable Topology Truss (VTT) system, a truss robot that comprises actuated truss members connected by passive spherical joints.

title: When Absolute State Fails: Evaluating Proprioceptive Encodings for Robust Manipulation
summary: End-to-end robot manipulation policies often assume that proprioceptive state at deployment matches the distribution seen in training, but this paper examines what happens when that absolute state signal becomes unreliable. It evaluates alternative proprioceptive encodings for robustness under train-test mismatch, focusing on how the choice of state representation affects real-world manipulation performance.

extra.comment: Accepted to ICRA 2026 Workshop: From Data to Decisions
extra.full_text: As end-to-end robotic policies are progressively deployed in the real world to solve real tasks, they face a gap between the training and inference conditions.

title: Exploration-assisted Bottleneck Transition Toward Robust and Data-efficient Deformable Object Manipulation
summary: Exploration-assisted Bottleneck Transition targets the OOD failures of imitation learning in deformable object manipulation by using exploration to identify and traverse hard transition states in the object’s configuration space. The idea is especially relevant for DOM because exhaustive demonstrations are unrealistic: cloth, ropes, and other deformables can occupy too many states to cover with data alone, so robustness has to come from selectively learning around the bottlenecks where policies tend to break.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning has demonstrated impressive results in robotic manipulation but fails under out-of-distribution (OOD) states. This limitation is particularly critical in Deformable Object Manipulation (DOM), where the near-infinite possible configurations render comprehensive data collection infeasible.

title: Occlusion-Based Object Transportation Around Obstacles With a Swarm of Miniature Robots
summary: Swarm robotics uses many simple, limited robots that coordinate through decentralized, self-organizing rules rather than centralized control. In the context of occlusion-based object transportation, the idea is to move objects around obstacles with a miniature robot swarm by relying on collective behavior that emerges from local interactions, though the provided text does not include the specific mechanism, experiments, or results.

extra.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in the journal Swarm Intelligence
extra.full_text: Swarm robotics utilises decentralised self-organising systems to form complex collective behaviours built from the bottom-up using individuals that have limited capabilities.

title: BiPneu: Design and Control of a Bipolar-Pressure Pneumatic System for Soft Robots
summary: BiPneu focuses on a pneumatic architecture for soft robots that can regulate both positive and negative pressure, which matters because vacuum and pressurization together let soft actuators cover larger deformation ranges and switch between richer actuation modes. The system appears aimed at making bipolar-pressure control practical for soft robotic hardware, tying the actuator design to a control scheme rather than treating pressure generation as a separate utility.

extra.full_text: Positive-negative pressure regulation is critical to soft robotic actuators, enabling large motion ranges and versatile actuation modes.

title: Adaptive Smooth Tchebycheff Attention for Multi-Objective Policy Optimization
summary: Adaptive Smooth Tchebycheff Attention targets multi-objective policy optimization in robotics by replacing simple linear scalarization with a smooth Tchebycheff-style attention mechanism, so policies can pursue trade-offs that lie in non-convex parts of the Pareto front. The core appeal is that it is designed for settings where objectives genuinely conflict and averaging them with fixed weights would miss useful behaviors, while retaining enough structure for stable reinforcement learning.

extra.comment: To appear in the Proceedings of Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2026
extra.full_text: Multi-objective reinforcement learning in robotic domains requires balancing complex, non-convex trade-offs between conflicting objectives. While linear scalarization methods provide stability, they are theoretically incapable of recovering solutions within non-convex regions of the Pareto front.

title: WARPED: Wrist-Aligned Rendering for Robot Policy Learning from Egocentric Human Demonstrations
summary: WARPED targets the gap between egocentric human demonstrations and robot policy learning by rendering observations in a wrist-aligned view, making human-recorded behavior more directly usable for visuomotor control. The premise is that reframing human demonstrations around the robot wrist can reduce the cost of collecting robot-specific data while preserving task-relevant hand-object interactions for policy training.

extra.full_text: Recent advancements in learning from human demonstration have shown promising results in addressing the scalability and high cost of data collection required to train robust visuomotor policies.

title: Creating manufacturable blueprints for coarse-grained virtual robots
summary: Virtual robots have long been easy to evolve in simulation but hard to turn into buildable machines, and this paper targets that gap by creating manufacturable blueprints for coarse-grained robot designs. From the limited text available, the focus is on translating evolved embodied agents into physical robot specifications, making simulation-derived morphologies more usable beyond the screen.

extra.full_text: Over the past three decades, countless embodied yet virtual agents have freely evolved inside computer simulations, but vanishingly few were realized as physical robots.

title: Learning Actionable Manipulation Recovery via Counterfactual Failure Synthesis
summary: Learning Actionable Manipulation Recovery via Counterfactual Failure Synthesis tackles the problem of robots getting stuck after execution errors in manipulation tasks, where even strong foundation-model-based systems often lack reliable recovery behavior. From the provided abstract fragment, the work appears to focus on synthesizing counterfactual failures so a policy can learn recovery actions from situations where manipulation goes wrong, but no concrete mechanism, benchmark, or results are given here.

extra.full_text: While recent foundation models have significantly advanced robotic manipulation, these systems still struggle to autonomously recover from execution errors.

title: AffordGen: Generating Diverse Demonstrations for Generalizable Object Manipulation with Afford Correspondence
summary: AffordGen targets the data-diversity bottleneck in imitation learning for object manipulation by generating demonstrations that preserve affordance correspondences across geometric variations. The goal is to help policies generalize when object shapes or configurations differ from the limited demonstrations they were trained on.

extra.full_text: Despite the recent success of modern imitation learning methods in robot manipulation, their performance is often constrained by geometric variations due to limited data diversity.

title: F2F-AP: Flow-to-Future Asynchronous Policy for Real-time Dynamic Manipulation
summary: F2F-AP tackles the lag introduced by asynchronous inference in real-time robotic manipulation, where actions generated from delayed observations can arrive out of sync with a changing scene. It frames the policy around “flow-to-future” prediction, aiming to compensate for latency by producing actions aligned with where the environment is going rather than where it was when inference began.

extra.full_text: Asynchronous inference has emerged as a prevalent paradigm in robotic manipulation, achieving significant progress in ensuring trajectory smoothness and efficiency. However, a systemic challenge remains unresolved, as inherent latency causes generated actions to inevitably lag behind the real-time environment.

title: A Proprioceptive-Only Benchmark for Quadruped State Estimation: ATE, RPE, and Runtime Trade-offs Between Filters and Smoothers
summary: MUSE, the Invariant Extended Kalman Filter, and the Invariant Smoother are evaluated as proprioceptive-only state estimators for quadruped robots on the CYN-1 sequence of the GrandTour Dataset. The comparison frames the trade-off between filtering and smoothing in terms of absolute trajectory error, relative pose error, and runtime, giving a compact benchmark for choosing estimators when exteroceptive sensing is unavailable or deliberately excluded.

extra.comment: Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Practice
extra.full_text: We compare three state-of-the-art proprioceptive state estimators for quadruped robots: MUSE [1], the Invariant Extended Kalman Filter (IEKF) [2], and the Invariant Smoother (IS) [3], on the CYN-1 sequence of the GrandTour Dataset [4].

title: Offline Policy Evaluation for Manipulation Policies via Discounted Liveness Formulation
summary: Offline policy evaluation is framed as a discounted liveness problem for manipulation policies, turning the question of whether a policy will eventually achieve task-relevant progress into an evaluation objective that can be estimated from logged data. The aim is to make robotic policy development safer and cheaper by judging manipulation policies before deployment, without needing fresh online rollouts for every candidate.

extra.full_text: Policy evaluation is a fundamental component of the development and deployment pipeline for robotic policies.

title: Bridging the Awareness Gap: Socially Mediated State Externalization for Transparent Distributed Home Robots
summary: Home robots that work as a distributed team can disappear into other rooms, leaving users unsure what they are doing or why. Socially mediated state externalization addresses this by having robots communicate hidden task state through other visible robots, aiming to make off-screen activity more transparent and preserve a sense of control in domestic multi-robot settings.

extra.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Under review for IROS 2026
extra.full_text: Distributed multi-robot systems for the home often require robots to operate out of the user's sight, creating a state awareness gap that can diminish trust and perceived transparency and control.

title: Reconciling distributed compliance with high-performance control in continuum soft robotics
summary: High-performance closed-loop control for truly soft continuum manipulators is framed as a tension between the compliance that makes these robots useful and the precision demanded by fast feedback control. The work appears to focus on reconciling those distributed, deformable body dynamics with control strategies capable of producing more reliable, higher-performance motion.

extra.full_text: High-performance closed-loop control of truly soft continuum manipulators has remained elusive.

title: Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration for General-Purpose Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration targets the reward-design problem in dexterous manipulation by using contact coverage as an exploration signal, pushing a hand to discover useful object interactions rather than relying only on sparse task rewards. From the provided text, the concrete experiments and results are not available, so the safest reading is that it frames contact-rich exploration as the mechanism for making DRL more general across manipulation tasks.

extra.full_text: Deep Reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved remarkable success in domains with well-defined reward structures, such as Atari games and locomotion.

title: RL-Augmented MPC for Non-Gaited Legged and Hybrid Locomotion
summary: RL-Augmented MPC for Non-Gaited Legged and Hybrid Locomotion combines a high-level reinforcement learning policy with a low-level, contact-explicit model predictive controller. The RL agent chooses gait and navigation commands, while the MPC handles the detailed locomotion control, aiming to support legged and hybrid robots in settings where fixed gait patterns are not enough.

extra.full_text: We propose a contact-explicit hierarchical architecture coupling Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Model Predictive Control (MPC), where a high-level RL agent provides gait and navigation commands to a low-level locomotion MPC.

title: Visibility-Aware Mobile Grasping in Dynamic Environments
summary: Addresses mobile grasping when a robot has to navigate and pick objects in dynamic, unknown spaces while seeing only part of the scene at any moment. The emphasis is on making grasp planning visibility-aware, so the robot reasons not just about reaching and grasping but also about what it can observe as the environment changes.

extra.full_text: This paper addresses the problem of mobile grasping in dynamic, unknown environments where a robot must operate under a limited field-of-view.

title: A Cross-Layered Multi-Drone Coordination for Medical Supply Delivery during Disaster Response Management
summary: Autonomous drone fleets are framed as a way to deliver medical supplies during disaster response, where roads and conventional logistics may be disrupted. The paper focuses on cross-layer coordination across multiple drones, suggesting attention to both high-level mission management and lower-level fleet control, but the provided text does not give enough detail on the specific algorithm, evaluation setup, or results.

extra.full_text: Autonomous drone fleets have immense potential in medical supply delivery during disaster incident response.

title: TouchAnything: Diffusion-Guided 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Robot Touches
summary: TouchAnything tackles 3D object reconstruction for robots when vision is unreliable, using sparse tactile contacts as the input signal instead of relying on clean visual observations. The setup is motivated by manipulation settings with occlusions or difficult lighting, where accurate geometry still matters for planning and physical interaction.

extra.full_text: Accurate object geometry estimation is essential for many downstream tasks, including robotic manipulation and physical interaction. Although vision is the dominant modality for shape perception, it becomes unreliable under occlusions or challenging lighting conditions.

title: SPARC: Spatial-Aware Path Planning via Attentive Robot Communication
summary: SPARC tackles decentralized multi-robot path planning by making robot communication spatially aware instead of giving every neighbor equal weight. Its attentive communication mechanism prioritizes nearby robots, aiming to preserve coordination capacity in congested areas where path conflicts are most likely and uniform message aggregation can wash out the important interactions.

extra.comment: The manuscript is being withdrawn at the request of the first author for the purpose of revising content and re-uploading a revised version with updated data/figures/text . The revised manuscript will be resubmitted to arXiv promptly with the same author list and research theme
extra.full_text: Efficient communication is critical for decentralized Multi-Robot Path Planning (MRPP), yet existing learned communication methods treat all neighboring robots equally regardless of their spatial proximity, leading to diluted attention in congested regions where coordination matters most.

title: Trajectory-Consistent Flow Matching for Robust Visuomotor Policy Learning
summary: Trajectory-Consistent Flow Matching trains visuomotor policies as continuous velocity fields that map noise into robot actions, giving manipulation policies fast deterministic inference instead of iterative sampling. The approach focuses on making those generated action trajectories consistent over time, which is meant to improve robustness in closed-loop robot control.

extra.full_text: Flow matching policies learn continuous velocity fields that transport noise to actions, enabling fast deterministic inference for robot manipulation.

title: RoSHI: A Versatile Robot-oriented Suit for Human Data In-the-Wild
summary: RoSHI is a robot-oriented wearable suit for collecting long-horizon human interaction data outside controlled lab setups, aimed at the kind of rich demonstrations needed to scale robot learning. It is positioned around the practical data-capture problems that make in-the-wild collection hard: staying portable, handling occlusion, and keeping globally consistent motion and interaction signals over extended activities.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. *Equal contribution by first three authors. Project webpage: https://roshi-mocap.github.io/
extra.full_text: Scaling up robot learning will likely require human data containing rich and long-horizon interactions in the wild. Existing approaches for collecting such data trade off portability, robustness to occlusion, and global consistency.

title: Diff-Muscle: Efficient Learning for Musculoskeletal Robotic Table Tennis
summary: Diff-Muscle targets musculoskeletal robotic table tennis, where many muscle-like actuators must be coordinated fast enough for a dynamic striking task rather than the simpler motions usually used in this area. The interesting angle is its focus on efficient learning for multi-segment coordination, using table tennis as a demanding embodied-control setting to probe whether musculoskeletal robots can combine flexibility and dexterity in a genuinely agile task.

extra.full_text: Musculoskeletal robots provide superior advantages in flexibility and dexterity, positioning them as a promising frontier towards embodied intelligence. However, current research is largely confined to relative simple tasks, restricting the exploration of their full potential in multi-segment coordination.

title: TAVIS: A Benchmark for Egocentric Active Vision and Anticipatory Gaze in Imitation Learning
summary: TAVIS is an arXiv benchmark focused on egocentric active vision for imitation learning, where a robot policy must decide where to look while manipulating objects rather than passively consuming fixed camera views. It centers on anticipatory gaze: testing whether policies can shift attention toward task-relevant future interaction points, a capability that recent independent systems suggest can materially improve manipulation performance.

extra.full_text: Active vision -- where a policy controls its own gaze during manipulation -- has emerged as a key capability for imitation learning, with multiple independent systems demonstrating its benefits in the past year.

title: Interactive World Simulator for Robot Policy Training and Evaluation
summary: Interactive World Simulator targets the bottleneck in using action-conditioned video world models for robotics: making them fast enough and physically reliable enough for long-horizon policy training and evaluation. It focuses on simulating robot-environment interactions from action inputs, aiming to replace or augment slower real-world rollouts with predicted video trajectories that can support scalable testing and training of robot policies.

extra.full_text: Action-conditioned video prediction models (often referred to as world models) have shown strong potential for robotics applications, but existing approaches are often slow and struggle to capture physically consistent interactions over long horizons, limiting their usefulness for scalable robot policy training and evaluation.

title: 3PoinTr: 3D Point Tracks for Robot Manipulation Pretraining from Casual Videos
summary: 3PoinTr pretrains robot manipulation policies using 3D point tracks extracted from casual videos, aiming to reduce the need for large task-specific demonstration sets. The premise is that tracking object and scene motion in 3D gives a reusable representation for manipulation, potentially making policies more robust and data-efficient when demonstrations are scarce.

extra.full_text: Data-efficient training of robust robot policies is the key to unlocking automation in a wide array of novel tasks. Current systems require large volumes of demonstrations to achieve robustness, which is impractical in many applications.

title: PhaForce: Phase-Scheduled Visual-Force Policy Learning with Slow Planning and Fast Correction for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: PhaForce targets contact-rich manipulation by splitting control into slow, vision-driven planning and fast force/torque correction. The core idea is to let a generative visuomotor policy handle task-level semantics while a phase-scheduled mechanism reacts at higher frequency to contact transients, making better use of F/T feedback than action-chunked policies that update too slowly.

extra.full_text: Contact-rich manipulation requires not only vision-dominant task semantics but also closed-loop reactions to force/torque (F/T) transients. Yet, generative visuomotor policies are typically constrained to low-frequency updates due to inference latency and action chunking, underutilizing F/T for control-rate feedback.

title: Exploring the proprioceptive potential of joint receptors using a biomimetic robotic joint
summary: A biomimetic robotic joint is used to test whether joint receptors can provide richer proprioceptive signals than the usual “limit detector” view suggests. The study reframes these receptors as potential contributors to continuous joint-position sensing, complementing muscle spindles rather than only signaling extreme angles.

extra.comment: 26 pages including supplementary materials (17 pages main text), 6 main figures and 7 supplementary figures. Published in Scientific Reports
extra.full_text: In neuroscience, joint receptors have traditionally been viewed as limit detectors, providing positional information only at extreme joint angles, while muscle spindles are considered the primary sensors of joint angle position.

title: A Dynamic Toolkit for Transmission Characteristics of Precision Reducers with Explicit Contact Geometry
summary: Precision reducers shape the motion accuracy and dynamics of many robot platforms, from humanoids and quadrupeds to collaborative, industrial, and SCARA robots. The work presents a dynamic toolkit for analyzing their transmission characteristics with explicit contact geometry, aimed at capturing how reducer contact behavior affects precision robotic motion.

extra.full_text: Precision reducers are critical components in robotic systems, directly affecting the motion accuracy and dynamic performance of humanoid robots, quadruped robots, collaborative robots, industrial robots, and SCARA robots.

title: A Physical Agentic Loop for Language-Guided Grasping with Execution-State Monitoring
summary: Language-guided grasping is framed as a closed physical agent loop rather than a one-shot prediction problem: the robot executes a proposed grasp while monitoring execution state for failures like empty grasps, slips, stalls, timeouts, or picking the wrong object. The interesting part is the structured feedback path from low-level execution back to the decision layer, which lets the system reason about what actually happened during manipulation instead of treating grasp attempts as opaque successes or failures.

extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation systems that follow language instructions often execute grasp primitives in a largely single-shot manner: a model proposes an action, the robot executes it, and failures such as empty grasps, slips, stalls, timeouts, or semantically wrong grasps are not surfaced to the decision layer in a structured way.

title: See and Switch: Vision-Based Branching for Interactive Robot-Skill Programming
summary: See and Switch uses vision-based branching to let users build interactive robot-skill programs as conditional task graphs through programming by demonstration. The interesting part is that the graph can be expanded incrementally: a robot can follow demonstrated skills while using visual conditions to switch between branches, making PbD better suited to real-world task variability.

extra.full_text: Programming robots by demonstration (PbD) is an intuitive concept, but scaling it to real-world variability remains a challenge for most current teaching frameworks. Conditional task graphs are very expressive and can be defined incrementally, which fits very well with the PbD idea.

title: TAIL-Safe: Task-Agnostic Safety Monitoring for Imitation Learning Policies
summary: TAIL-Safe targets safety monitoring for imitation-learning manipulation policies, including newer flow-matching and diffusion-policy controllers, without assuming a specific downstream task. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available, so the safe summary is that it is a task-agnostic monitor meant to detect unsafe behavior around learned robot policies rather than another policy-learning algorithm.

extra.full_text: Recent imitation learning (IL) algorithms such as flow-matching and diffusion policies demonstrate remarkable performance in learning complex manipulation tasks.

title: Long-Short Term Agents for Pure-Vision Bronchoscopy Robotic Autonomy
summary: Long-Short Term Agents targets autonomous bronchoscopy navigation using only endoscopic vision, addressing the poor field of view and transient artifacts that make intraoperative localization hard in endoluminal robots. From the title and abstract snippet, the central idea appears to be an agent design that combines short-horizon visual control with longer-term navigation memory, but the provided text does not include experiments, datasets, or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Accurate intraoperative navigation is essential for robot-assisted endoluminal intervention, but remains difficult because of limited endoscopic field of view and dynamic artifacts.

title: HiPolicy: Hierarchical Multi-Frequency Action Chunking for Policy Learning
summary: HiPolicy tackles imitation learning by using hierarchical action chunking at multiple frequencies, aiming to combine long-horizon planning with fine-grained closed-loop control. Instead of forcing a policy to operate at one fixed temporal scale, it appears to structure actions so slower chunks can capture extended dependencies while faster chunks preserve responsive control.

extra.full_text: Robotic imitation learning faces a fundamental trade-off between modeling long-horizon dependencies and enabling fine-grained closed-loop control. Existing fixed-frequency action chunking approaches struggle to achieve both.

title: RoboPCA: Pose-centered Affordance Learning from Human Demonstrations for Robot Manipulation
summary: RoboPCA targets robot manipulation by learning spatial affordances from human demonstrations, focusing on both where an object should be contacted and the pose needed for that contact. The central idea is pose-centered affordance learning, tying interaction regions to corresponding contact poses so a robot can reason about manipulation opportunities in a more geometrically grounded way.

extra.full_text: Understanding spatial affordances -- comprising the contact regions of object interaction and the corresponding contact poses -- is essential for robots to effectively manipulate objects and accomplish diverse tasks.

title: AssistDLO: Assistive Teleoperation for Deformable Linear Object Manipulation
summary: AssistDLO targets teleoperated manipulation of deformable linear objects such as cables or ropes, where operators struggle because the object’s shape is high-dimensional and hard to perceive in depth. It focuses on assistive teleoperation: using AI support to improve state perception and reaction during DLO handling under nonlinear dynamics and depth uncertainty.

extra.comment: 20 pages, 14 figures. Submitted to a peer-reviewed journal
extra.full_text: Manipulating Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is challenging in robotics due to their infinite-dimensional configuration space and complex nonlinear dynamics. In teleoperation, depth uncertainty hinders state perception and reaction.

title: BiCoord: A Bimanual Manipulation Benchmark towards Long-Horizon Spatial-Temporal Coordination
summary: BiCoord is a benchmark for long-horizon bimanual manipulation, focusing on tasks where two robot arms must coordinate spatially and temporally rather than just execute parallel motions. It is positioned as a step beyond existing simulation benchmarks like RoboTwin and RLBench2, targeting the kind of sustained dual-arm coordination needed for more human-like robotic dexterity.

extra.full_text: Bimanual manipulation, i.e., the coordinated use of two robotic arms to complete tasks, is essential for achieving human-level dexterity in robotics. Recent simulation benchmarks, e.g., RoboTwin and RLBench2, have advanced data-driven learning for bimanual manipulation.

title: Monitoring autonomous persistent surveillance missions using invariance
summary: Runtime monitors are built for persistent-surveillance robots whose internal autonomy stack cannot be inspected, using invariance properties over a finite partition of the environment. Each region carries an uncertainty value that falls when observed and rises otherwise, so the monitor can check from observed behavior whether the mission is maintaining bounded uncertainty across the space.

extra.full_text: This paper studies runtime monitoring for persistent surveillance by autonomous robots when the autonomy stack is a black box. The environment is partitioned into finitely many parts, each carrying an uncertainty state that decreases when observed and increases otherwise.

title: Control Architecture and experimental validation of a Novel Surgical Robotic Instrument
summary: A surgical robotic instrument is presented as a way to overcome the restricted motion of conventional laparoscopic tools in minimally invasive surgery. The available text frames the contribution around its control architecture and experimental validation, but does not provide enough detail about the mechanism, degrees of freedom, experiments, or quantitative results to summarize the technical advance more specifically.

extra.full_text: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) reduces patient trauma and shortens recovery time; however, conventional laparoscopic instruments remain constrained by limited range of movements.

title: A Measure-Theoretic Finite-Sample Theory for Adaptive-Data Fitted Q-Iteration
summary: A measure-theoretic finite-sample analysis is developed for fitted Q-iteration when the training data are adaptive, matching the way off-policy robot-learning datasets are often collected rather than assuming fixed i.i.d. samples. The aim is to narrow the theory gap around model-free deep RL for nonlinear control by giving explicit performance guarantees beyond the tabular and linearizable regimes where most existing results live.

extra.full_text: While reinforcement learning (RL) promises to revolutionize the control of complex nonlinear robotic systems, a profound gap persists between the heuristic success of model-free off-policy deep RL and the underlying theory, which remains largely confined to tabular or linearizable settings.

title: LatentMimic: Terrain-Adaptive Locomotion via Latent Space Imitation
summary: LatentMimic targets quadruped locomotion that can handle complex terrain without losing the character and diversity of the imitated motion. It uses latent-space imitation to preserve motion style while adapting behavior to terrain, addressing the usual tradeoff between robust traversal and natural-looking movement.

extra.full_text: Developing natural and diverse locomotion controllers for quadruped robots that can adapt to complex terrains while preserving motion style remains a significant challenge.

title: Cable-driven Continuum Robotics: Proprioception via Proximal-integrated Force Sensing
summary: Cable-driven continuum robotics is being explored here through proprioception from force sensing integrated at the proximal end, aiming to infer three-dimensional contact forces without embedding sensors into the miniaturized distal structure. The interesting angle is that it targets a core bottleneck for micro-scale continuum robots: recovering contact force perception despite nonlinear mechanics, tight packaging constraints, and limited room for onboard sensing.

extra.full_text: Micro-scale continuum robots face significant limitations in achieving three-dimensional contact force perception, primarily due to structural miniaturization, nonlinear mechanical, and sensor integration.

title: DexKnot: Generalizable Visuomotor Policy Learning for Dexterous Bag-Knotting Manipulation
summary: DexKnot targets the surprisingly hard problem of tying knots in deformable plastic bags with dexterous robot hands, where each bag can present different shapes, wrinkles, and dynamics. It learns a generalizable visuomotor policy for bag-knotting manipulation, aiming to handle unseen bag instances and deformations rather than overfitting to a narrow setup.

extra.full_text: Knotting plastic bags is a common task in daily life, yet it is challenging for robots due to the bags' infinite degrees of freedom and complex physical dynamics. Existing methods often struggle in generalization to unseen bag instances or deformations.

title: Atomic-Probe Governance for Skill Updates in Compositional Robot Policies
summary: Atomic-Probe Governance addresses a gap in compositional robot policy systems where skill libraries keep changing after deployment, but composition methods assume each skill remains fixed. It frames skill replacement as something that must be locally probed and governed, so a robot can detect when an updated low-level skill may alter downstream composed behaviors rather than silently invalidating typed plans.

extra.comment: 8 pages main text + appendix; 3 figures, 12 tables;
extra.full_text: Skill libraries in deployed robotic systems are continually updated through fine-tuning, fresh demonstrations, or domain adaptation, yet existing typed-composition methods (BLADE, SymSkill, Generative Skill Chaining) treat the library as frozen at test time and do not analyze how composition outcomes change when a skill is replaced.

title: RODEO: RObotic DEcentralized Organization
summary: RODEO frames extended robot autonomy around decentralized organization, aiming to make robot actions auditable and decision processes transparent rather than simply more independent. From the provided abstract fragment, the emphasis appears to be on governance and human-robot interaction mechanisms needed for long-running autonomy with minimal supervision, though no concrete architecture, experiments, or results are given.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, Accepted at IEEE International Conference on Robotics & Automation (2026)
extra.full_text: Robots are improving their autonomy with minimal human supervision. However, auditable actions, transparent decision processes, and new human-robot interaction models are still missing requirements to achieve extended robot autonomy.

title: Task-Level Decisions to Gait Level Control: A Hierarchical Policy Approach for Quadruped Navigation
summary: A hierarchical policy links task-level navigation decisions to gait-level control for quadrupeds, aiming to bridge the gap between where the robot should go and how its legs should execute that plan. The approach is framed around improving stability when the robot encounters environmental shifts outside its training distribution, where low-level gait policies can otherwise become brittle.

extra.full_text: Real-world quadruped navigation is constrained by a scale mismatch between high-level navigation decisions and low-level gait execution, as well as by instabilities under out-of-distribution environmental changes.

title: RFM-HRI : A Multimodal Dataset of Medical Robot Failure, User Reaction and Recovery Preferences for Item Retrieval Tasks
summary: RFM-HRI is a multimodal dataset focused on medical item-retrieval scenarios where a robot fails, users react, and recovery preferences are recorded. It targets a practical gap in HRI by capturing both verbal and non-verbal user behavior around failures, giving researchers data for studying how people signal confusion, frustration, or desired recovery during healthcare robot interactions.

extra.full_text: While robots deployed in real-world environments inevitably experience interaction failures, understanding how users respond through verbal and non-verbal behaviors remains under-explored in human-robot interaction (HRI).

title: OpenRC: An Open-Source Robotic Colonoscopy Framework for Multimodal Data Acquisition and Autonomy Research
summary: OpenRC is an open-source robotic colonoscopy platform aimed at capturing synchronized multimodal data from the full procedure loop: operator inputs, scope motion, and visual feedback. It is built to make colonoscopy a more reproducible robotics research problem, giving researchers a shared framework for studying teleoperation dynamics, autonomy algorithms, and perception-control coupling in endoscopic navigation.

extra.full_text: Colorectal cancer screening critically depends on colonoscopy, yet existing platforms offer limited support for systematically studying the coupled dynamics of operator control, instrument motion, and visual feedback.

title: A Semantic Autonomy Framework for VLM-Integrated Indoor Mobile Robots: Hybrid Deterministic Reasoning and Cross-Robot Adaptive Memory
summary: Indoor mobile robots using ROS 2 Navigation 2 are extended with a semantic autonomy layer that lets them turn intent-level natural language commands into navigable goals rather than requiring explicit metric coordinates. The approach combines VLM-based interpretation with deterministic reasoning and an adaptive memory that can transfer across robots, aiming to make indoor navigation more robust when instructions refer to places, objects, or contextual intent.

extra.full_text: Autonomous indoor mobile robots can navigate reliably to metric coordinates using established frameworks such as ROS 2 Navigation 2, yet they lack the ability to interpret natural language instructions that express intent rather than positions.

title: BridgeACT: Bridging Human Demonstrations to Robot Actions via Unified Tool-Target Affordances
summary: BridgeACT tackles the problem of turning human manipulation videos into robot-executable actions by representing interactions through unified tool-target affordances. From the provided text, the core appeal is using the scale and diversity of human demonstrations while addressing the hard transfer step from human motion to robot behavior.

extra.full_text: Learning robot manipulation from human videos is appealing due to the scale and diversity of human demonstrations, but transferring such demonstrations to executable robot behavior remains challenging.

title: Designing and Validating a Self-Aligning Tool Changer for Modular Reconfigurable Manipulation Robots
summary: A misalignment-tolerant tool-changing system lets modular reconfigurable manipulation robots swap modules despite the position and orientation errors that commonly break rigid active couplings. The design centers on a self-aligning mechanism for automated module exchange, aiming to make reconfiguration more reliable without requiring perfectly precise docking.

extra.full_text: Modular reconfigurable robots require reliable mechanisms for automated module exchange, but conventional rigid active couplings often fail due to inevitable positioning and orientational errors. To address this, we propose a misalignment-tolerant tool-changing system.

title: Learning-Based Fault Detection for Legged Robots in Remote Dynamic Environments
summary: Learning-based fault detection is applied to quadruped robots operating in remote, dynamic, hazardous environments where a damaged limb may not be obvious from onboard execution alone. The idea is to give legged robots a way to recognize severe locomotion impairment and adapt before continued movement causes further failure, addressing a gap between animal-like recovery and current robot behavior.

extra.full_text: Operations in hazardous environments put humans, animals, and machines at high risk for physically damaging consequences. In contrast to humans and animals, quadruped robots cannot naturally identify and adjust their locomotion to a severely debilitated limb.

title: A Soft Robotic Demonstration in the Stratosphere
summary: A soft robot was designed and flown as a stratospheric demonstration, targeting the pressure and temperature extremes that normally make soft robotic systems fragile outside controlled environments. The work focuses on whether soft robotics can retain their adaptability while surviving near-space conditions, making it a small but concrete step toward deployable soft machines for space and other extreme missions.

extra.full_text: Machines designed for operation in Space, as well as other extreme environments, need to be both resilient and adaptable when mission parameters change. Soft robots offer advantages in adaptability, but most lack resilience to the pressure and temperature extremes found as close as the Stratosphere.

title: HALyPO: Heterogeneous-Agent Lyapunov Policy Optimization for Human-Robot Collaboration
summary: HALyPO applies heterogeneous-agent Lyapunov policy optimization to human-robot collaboration, treating varied human behaviors and task contexts as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. It is aimed at making robot policies generalize and remain resilient under the combinatorial diversity that appears when humans and robots share workspaces.

extra.full_text: To improve generalization and resilience in human-robot collaboration (HRC), robots must handle the combinatorial diversity of human behaviors and contexts, motivating multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL).

title: Passive Phase-Oriented Impedance Shaping for Rapid Acceleration in Soft Robotic Swimmers
summary: Rapid burst acceleration in soft robotic swimmers is framed around force-velocity phase alignment rather than precise resonance tracking. The approach uses passive phase-oriented impedance shaping so the swimmer’s mechanics time thrust production more effectively during rapid maneuvers, suggesting a route to faster underwater robots without relying on tightly controlled resonant operation.

extra.comment: Submitted to the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
extra.full_text: Rapid acceleration and burst maneuvers in underwater robots depend less on maintaining precise resonance and more on force--velocity phase alignment during thrust generation.

title: An Efficient Metric for Data Quality Measurement in Imitation Learning
summary: Fine-tuning imitation-learning robot policies with end-user demonstrations is framed as a way to reduce deployment failures under out-of-distribution conditions, but the excerpt only gives the motivation rather than the proposed metric itself. The work appears to focus on measuring demonstration data quality efficiently so robots can make better use of deployment-environment examples when adapting pretrained policies.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning (IL) has seen remarkable progress, yet field deployment of IL-powered robots remains hindered by the challenge of out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. Fine-tuning pre-trained policies with end-user demonstrations collected in deployment environments is a promising strategy to address this challenge.

title: Research on Vision-Language Question Answering Models for Industrial Robots
summary: A hierarchical cross-modal fusion model is introduced for vision-language question answering in industrial robot settings, where machines need to interpret visual scenes alongside operator questions that may contain ambiguous wording or manufacturing-specific terminology. The approach is aimed at structured but visually complex factory environments, with fusion across language and vision intended to improve how robots reason over layouts, objects, and task-relevant semantics.

extra.full_text: A hierarchical cross-modal fusion model is proposed for vision-language question answering (VLQA) in industrial robotics, targeting the challenges of semantic ambiguity, complex environmental layouts, and domain-specific terminology common in modern manufacturing.

title: Posterior Optimization with Clipped Objective for Bridging Efficiency and Stability in Generative Policy Learning
summary: Posterior Optimization with a clipped objective targets the RL fine-tuning problem for expressive generative robot policies, where rich multi-modal trajectory models can become unstable or waste samples during optimization. It frames policy improvement as posterior optimization while clipping the objective to keep updates controlled, aiming to preserve the flexibility of generative policies without the usual brittleness in reinforcement learning.

extra.full_text: Expressive generative models have advanced robotic manipulation by capturing complex, multi-modal action distributions over temporally extended trajectories. However, fine-tuning these policies via RL remains challenging due to instability and sample inefficiency.

title: VitaTouch: Property-Aware Vision-Tactile-Language Model for Robotic Quality Inspection in Manufacturing
summary: VitaTouch targets manufacturing quality inspection cases where visible appearance is not enough, using a vision-tactile-language model to reason about material and surface properties that can be hidden by occlusion, glare, or reflections. From the available description, the central idea is to fuse tactile sensing with visual and language understanding so a robot can inspect intrinsic properties rather than relying only on geometry or images.

extra.full_text: Quality inspection in smart manufacturing requires identifying intrinsic material and surface properties beyond visible geometry, yet vision-only methods remain vulnerable to occlusion and reflection.

title: Learning When to See and When to Feel: Adaptive Vision-Torque Fusion for Contact-Aware Manipulation
summary: Learning When to See and When to Feel targets contact-aware manipulation by adaptively fusing visual observations with torque feedback, so the policy can rely more on vision when geometry is informative and more on force-like signals during contact-rich phases. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified beyond the idea of vision-torque fusion for manipulation, but the interesting angle is the explicit decision of when sensing through sight is enough and when physical interaction cues should drive control.

extra.full_text: Vision-based policies have achieved a good performance in robotic manipulation due to the accessibility and richness of visual observations.

title: A Dual-Action Fabric-Based Soft Robotic Glove for Ergonomic Hand Rehabilitation
summary: A fabric-based soft robotic glove is presented for ergonomic hand rehabilitation after neurological impairment, targeting assistance with daily hand function. From the available text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, beyond the glove’s dual-action soft robotic design for rehabilitation use.

extra.full_text: Hand impairment following neurological disorders substantially limits independence in activities of daily living, motivating the development of effective assistive and rehabilitation strategies.

title: How to Train your Tactile Model: Tactile Perception with Multi-fingered Robot Hands
summary: Multi-fingered robot hands need tactile models that can be brought up quickly as new vision-based touch sensors are added, rather than requiring slow, sensor-specific engineering. The paper focuses on training tactile perception models for these hands so robots can make better use of distributed finger contact signals during manipulation.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication at the International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026, Vienna
extra.full_text: Rapid deployment of new tactile sensors is essential for scalable robotic manipulation, especially in multi-fingered hands equipped with vision-based tactile sensors.

title: ARIS: Agentic and Relationship Intelligence System for Social Robots
summary: ARIS targets the gap between fluent robot dialogue and sustained social interaction by adding agentic and relationship-aware reasoning for social robots. From the provided description, it is meant to help robots handle multi-turn engagement, reason about user relationships, and ground responses in interaction context at larger scale, rather than treating each exchange as an isolated conversational turn.

extra.full_text: Foundational models have advanced social robotics, enabling richer perception and communicative interaction with users. However, current systems still struggle with multi-turn engagement, social-relationship reasoning, and contextually grounded dialogue at scale.

title: Learning-Based Hierarchical Scene Graph Matching for Robot Localization Leveraging Prior Maps
summary: Learning-Based Hierarchical Scene Graph Matching targets indoor robot localization by matching a robot’s current scene representation against a prior map using hierarchical scene graphs. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not available beyond the basic problem setting: improving accurate localization for autonomous robots in indoor environments.

extra.full_text: Accurate localization is a fundamental requirement for autonomous robots operating in indoor environments.

title: Long-Reach Robotic Cleaning for Lunar Solar Arrays
summary: Long-reach robotic cleaning for lunar solar arrays targets routine maintenance of surface power infrastructure, especially dust removal and inspection needed to keep arrays productive over long missions. The described effort frames cleaning, dust mitigation, minor repair, and related upkeep as operational necessities for commercial lunar activity, with the robot’s value coming from extending reach over large array surfaces without requiring frequent repositioning or human intervention.

extra.comment: Extended abstract, 4 pages, 3 figures, accepted to and presented at the Sustainable Space Robotics Workshop at iSpaRo 2025
extra.full_text: Commercial lunar activity is accelerating the need for reliable surface infrastructure and routine operations to keep it functioning. Maintenance tasks such as inspection, cleaning, dust mitigation, and minor repair are essential to preserve performance and extend system life.

title: Dynamic-TD3: A Novel Algorithm for UAV Path Planning with Dynamic Obstacle Trajectory Prediction
summary: Dynamic-TD3 applies deep reinforcement learning to UAV path planning in environments with moving obstacles, combining TD3-style continuous control with trajectory prediction for dynamic obstacle avoidance. From the provided text, the concrete result details are not available, but the focus is on making autonomous drone navigation safer in complex, high-risk settings where obstacle motion must be anticipated rather than merely reacted to.

extra.full_text: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) finds extensive application in autonomous drone navigation within complex, high-risk environments.

title: Vision-Based Robotic Disassembly Combined with Real-Time MFA Data Acquisition
summary: Vision-based robotic disassembly is paired with real-time material flow analysis data capture to support recovery of rare-earth minerals and other critical raw materials from end-of-use products. The interesting angle is the closed loop between the physical recycling step and live MFA data acquisition, which could make automated disassembly more useful for tracking CRM recovery and strengthening supply resilience in regions dependent on imported materials.

extra.full_text: Stable and reliable supplies of rare-Earth minerals and critical raw materials (CRMs) are essential for the development of the European Union. Since a large share of these materials enters the Union from outside, a valid option for CRMs supply resilience and security is to recover them from end-of-use products.

title: Bi-Level Optimization for Contact and Motion Planning in Rope-Assisted Legged Robots
summary: Bi-Level Optimization for Contact and Motion Planning in Rope-Assisted Legged Robots presents a planning pipeline for legged robots that use a rope to climb vertical surfaces, separating contact decisions from motion generation through a bi-level optimization structure. The interesting part is the coupling of rope assistance with legged contact planning, aiming to make vertical locomotion feasible by jointly reasoning about where the robot should attach or step and how it should move under rope constraints.

extra.full_text: This paper presents a planning pipeline framework for locomotion in rope-assisted robots climbing vertical surfaces.

title: Probe-to-Grasp Manipulation Using Self-Sensing Pneumatic Variable-Stiffness Joints
summary: Probe-to-Grasp uses self-sensing pneumatic variable-stiffness joints to first probe a deformable object and estimate its local stiffness, then use that estimate to choose a safer, more stable grasp pose. The interesting part is the tight coupling between tactile-style stiffness sensing and grasp planning: instead of treating soft objects as unknown hazards, the robot actively measures how the object responds before committing to pickup.

extra.full_text: Grasping deformable objects with varying stiffness remains a significant challenge in robotics. Estimating the local stiffness of a target object is important for determining an optimal grasp pose that enables stable pickup without damaging the object.

title: Spectral Decomposition of Inverse Dynamics for Fast Exploration in Model-Based Manipulation
summary: Spectral decomposition is used to restructure inverse dynamics so a model-based planner can explore long-horizon manipulation trajectories more quickly despite nonlinear contact dynamics and many possible contact modes. The idea targets the main bottleneck in contact-rich planning: feasibility search becomes increasingly expensive as the manipulation sequence gets longer.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
extra.full_text: Planning long duration robotic manipulation sequences is challenging because of the complexity of exploring feasible trajectories through nonlinear contact dynamics and many contact modes. Moreover, this complexity grows with the problem's horizon length.

title: SlicerRoboTMS: An Open-Source 3D Slicer Extension for Robot-Assisted Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
summary: SlicerRoboTMS is an open-source 3D Slicer extension for planning and guiding robot-assisted transcranial magnetic stimulation from patient imaging. It is aimed at making Robo-TMS workflows more accurate and reproducible than manual coil positioning by integrating image guidance and robotic assistance into a familiar medical-imaging platform.

extra.comment: Accepted by the 48th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC) 2026
extra.full_text: Robot-assisted Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (Robo-TMS) is an image-guided robotic intervention that enhances the accuracy and reproducibility of conventional Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS), a widely used non-invasive brain stimulation procedure in clinical treatment and neuroscience research.

title: HANDFUL: Sequential Grasp-Conditioned Dexterous Manipulation with Resource Awareness
summary: HANDFUL targets dexterous robot hands that need to chain manipulation skills while keeping hold of objects already grasped, rather than treating each object or skill in isolation. It frames manipulation as sequential and grasp-conditioned, with resource awareness built in so the hand can manage limited fingers, contacts, and occupied grasp capacity across a multi-step task.

extra.full_text: Dexterous robot hands offer rich opportunities for multifunctional manipulation, where a robot must execute multiple skills in sequence while maintaining control over previously grasped objects. Most prior work in dexterous manipulation focuses on single-object, single-skill tasks.

title: UMI-Underwater: Learning Underwater Manipulation without Underwater Teleoperation
summary: UMI-Underwater tackles underwater robotic grasping by avoiding the need for costly underwater teleoperation data, instead learning manipulation policies from demonstrations collected in easier conditions. It targets the core deployment gap in underwater grasping: visual observations are degraded and variable, while diverse in-domain demonstrations are hard to obtain.

extra.full_text: Underwater robotic grasping is difficult due to degraded, highly variable imagery and the expense of collecting diverse underwater demonstrations.

title: Unleashing the Agility of Wheeled-Legged Robots for High-Dynamic Reflexive Obstacle Evasion
summary: Wheeled-legged robots are positioned here as a platform for fast reflexive obstacle evasion, combining wheel efficiency with legged adaptability for dynamic, cluttered settings. The work appears to focus on pushing these hybrid robots beyond basic mobility toward high-dynamic, agile responses to sudden obstacles, where rapid control reactions matter as much as terrain traversal.

extra.full_text: Wheeled-legged robots combine the energy efficiency of wheeled locomotion with the terrain adaptability of legged systems, making them promising platforms for agile mobility in complex and dynamic environments.

title: SpatialAnt: Autonomous Zero-Shot Robot Navigation via Active Scene Reconstruction and Visual Anticipation
summary: SpatialAnt targets zero-shot vision-and-language robot navigation by pairing MLLM-based instruction following with active scene reconstruction and visual anticipation, so the agent can reason about spaces it has not fully observed yet. The interesting piece is the shift from passively reacting to current camera views toward building and using an evolving spatial model of the scene during navigation.

extra.full_text: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) has recently benefited from Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), enabling zero-shot navigation.

title: Control Barrier Functions Solved with Hierarchical Quadratic Programming for Safe Physical Human-Robot Interaction
summary: Control Barrier Functions are formulated through hierarchical quadratic programming to enforce safety constraints during physical human-robot interaction. The setup targets settings like rehabilitation or collaborative assistance, where a robot must remain physically useful while respecting strict safety limits around a human partner.

extra.full_text: Physical human-robot interaction offers the potential to leverage human intelligence and robot physical capabilities to enable a range of exciting applications, e.g., collaborative robots for rehabilitation. Safety is critical for the successful deployment of this kind of robotic system.

title: FODMP: Fast One-Step Diffusion of Movement Primitives Generation for Time-Dependent Robot Actions
summary: FODMP targets the speed–horizon trade-off in diffusion-based robot policies by generating time-dependent movement primitives in a single diffusion step. From the provided excerpt, it is positioned as an alternative to fast action-chunking methods like ManiCM that can run quickly but only produce short motion segments.

extra.full_text: Diffusion models are increasingly used for robot learning, but current designs face a clear trade-off. Action-chunking diffusion policies like ManiCM are fast to run, yet they only predict short segments of motion.

title: HortiMulti: A Multi-Sensor Dataset for Localisation and Mapping in Horticultural Polytunnels
summary: HortiMulti is a real-world multi-sensor dataset aimed at localisation and mapping for agricultural robots operating inside horticultural polytunnels. It targets a setting where autonomy is difficult because the environment is structured but visually repetitive, GPS-limited, and operationally relevant, giving researchers representative data for developing and evaluating SLAM and navigation systems in protected-crop agriculture.

extra.full_text: Agricultural robotics is gaining increasing relevance in both research and real-world deployment. As these systems are expected to operate autonomously in more complex tasks, the availability of representative real-world datasets becomes essential.

title: Enhancing Drone Light Shows Performances: Optimal Allocation and Trajectories for Swarm Drone Formations
summary: Drone light shows are treated as a swarm-robotics planning problem, where large numbers of UAVs must be assigned to formation positions and given synchronized trajectories that preserve the visual pattern while avoiding inefficient motion. The work focuses on optimal allocation and path generation for these aerial formations, aiming to make large-scale reusable displays more reliable and practical than manually coordinated flight plans.

extra.full_text: Drone light shows (DLShows) represent a rapidly growing application of swarm robotics, creating captivating aerial displays through the synchronized flight of hundreds or thousands of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as environmentally friendly and reusable alternatives to traditional pyrotechnics.

title: LeHome: A Simulation Environment for Deformable Object Manipulation in Household Scenarios
summary: LeHome introduces a simulation environment for studying deformable object manipulation in everyday household settings, where robots must handle objects whose shape changes during interaction. From the provided text, the concrete detail is limited, but the focus is clear: making common home scenarios a testbed for one of robotics’ harder manipulation problems.

extra.full_text: Household environments present one of the most common, impactful yet challenging application domains for robotics.

title: AgentChemist: A Multi-Agent Experimental Robotic Platform Integrating Chemical Perception and Precise Control
summary: AgentChemist is a robotic chemistry platform that couples multi-agent AI planning with chemical perception and precise low-level control, aiming to move lab automation beyond fixed scripts toward more adaptable execution of experimental procedures. From the provided text, the central problem is the brittleness of current automated labs when faced with the long tail of real experimental tasks; no concrete benchmarks or results are given.

extra.full_text: Chemical laboratory automation has long been constrained by rigid workflows and poor adaptability to the long-tail distribution of experimental tasks.

title: A Case Study in Recovery of Drones using Discrete-Event Systems
summary: Discrete-event systems and supervisory control theory are applied here to drone recovery, using formal specifications to synthesize behavior that is correct by construction. The interesting angle is the attempt to bring a rigorous control framework, common in abstract event-driven systems, into the less explored setting of swarm robotics where failures and recovery behaviors need to be coordinated reliably.

extra.comment: Accepted for publication at WODES 2026; final version will appear in IEEE Xplore
extra.full_text: Discrete-event systems and supervisory control theory provide a rigorous framework for specifying correct-by-construction behavior. However, their practical application to swarm robotics remains largely underexplored.

title: Efficient Hybrid SE(3)-Equivariant Visuomotor Flow Policy via Spherical Harmonics for Robot Manipulation
summary: Efficient Hybrid SE(3)-Equivariant Visuomotor Flow Policy targets robot manipulation policies that need equivariance without the usual cost and brittleness. It uses spherical harmonics to build a hybrid SE(3)-equivariant visuomotor flow policy, aiming to handle multimodal inputs while staying stable with fast-sampling inference methods.

extra.full_text: While existing equivariant methods enhance data efficiency, they suffer from high computational intensity, reliance on single-modality inputs, and instability when combined with fast-sampling methods.

title: AirSimAG: A High-Fidelity Simulation Platform for Air-Ground Collaborative Robotics
summary: AirSimAG is a high-fidelity simulation platform for studying collaboration between UAVs and UGVs in complex environments. It targets spatial-intelligence scenarios such as search and rescue, urban surveillance, and environmental monitoring, where aerial agents can provide broad perception and ground agents can handle close-range navigation or interaction.

extra.full_text: As spatial intelligence continues to evolve, heterogeneous multi-agent systems-particularly the collaboration between Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs), have demonstrated strong potential in complex applications such as search and rescue, urban surveillance, and environmental monitoring.

title: PhotoAgent: A Robotic Photographer with Spatial and Aesthetic Understanding
summary: PhotoAgent is a robotic photography agent that turns high-level language requests into camera motions by combining large multimodal model reasoning with spatial, geometry-aware control. It targets the gap between aesthetic intent and embodied execution, letting a robot reason about scene content and composition while deciding how to position itself for the shot.

extra.comment: Accepted to the IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
extra.full_text: Embodied agents for creative tasks like photography must bridge the semantic gap between high-level language commands and geometric control. We introduce PhotoAgent, an agent that achieves this by integrating Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) reasoning with a novel control paradigm.

title: Full-Body Dynamic Safety for Robot Manipulators: 3D Poisson Safety Functions for CBF-Based Safety Filters
summary: 3D Poisson Safety Functions are used to encode full-body collision-avoidance constraints for robot manipulators, giving CBF-based safety filters a way to reason about the robot’s geometry in high-dimensional configuration spaces. The emphasis is on enforcing dynamic, whole-arm safety rather than relying on simplified point or link-level constraints.

extra.full_text: Collision avoidance for robotic manipulators requires enforcing full-body safety constraints in high-dimensional configuration spaces.

title: MapForest: A Modular Field Robotics System for Forest Mapping and Invasive Species Localization
summary: MapForest is a modular field robotics system for mapping forests and localizing invasive tree species in places where manual scouting is slow and under-canopy GNSS is unreliable. It targets large forests, parks, and trail networks by combining robotic survey capability with species localization, making invasive-species monitoring more scalable in difficult terrain.

extra.full_text: Monitoring and controlling invasive tree species across large forests, parks, and trail networks is challenging due to limited accessibility, reliance on manual scouting, and degraded under-canopy GNSS.

title: Parallel OctoMapping: A Scalable Framework for Enhanced Path Planning in Autonomous Navigation
summary: Parallel OctoMapping targets the mapping bottleneck in autonomous navigation by scaling octomap-style spatial representation so planners can update usable maps faster in complex environments. The emphasis is on making occupancy mapping practical for real-time path planning, where safer routes depend on quickly incorporating new spatial information rather than planning over stale or incomplete maps.

title: DexDrummer: In-Hand, Contact-Rich, and Long-Horizon Dexterous Robot Drumming
summary: DexDrummer tackles dexterous robot drumming as a combined test of in-hand manipulation, repeated contact, and long-horizon control, rather than treating those challenges separately.
