title: Learning Dynamic Pick-and-Place for a Legged Manipulator
summary: A hierarchical reinforcement learning controller lets a quadruped with a 6-DOF arm perform dynamic pick-and-place by coordinating locomotion and manipulation continuously, rather than stopping for slow staged motions. An explicit mass-estimation module feeds adaptive whole-body control, helping the robot handle varying object weights across a workspace from the ground to 1.1 m tabletops. In simulation it reaches 86.05% success with payloads up to 2.3 kg, and on hardware it averages 73.3% success for payloads up to 1.3 kg with 4.06 s executions across six scenarios.

extra.comment: Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 2026
extra.full_text: Legged manipulators extend robotic capabilities beyond static manipulation by integrating agile locomotion with versatile arm control. However, achieving precise manipulation while maintaining coordinated locomotion remains a major challenge. This work presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic pick-and-place tasks using a quadruped equipped with a 6-DOF robotic arm. The framework incorporates an explicit mass estimation module enabling adaptive whole-body control for objects with varying weights. In simulation, the system achieves an 86.05% success rate with payloads up to 2.3 kg. The approach is further validated through real-world experiments across six representative scenarios with controlled variations in object physical properties (size and mass) and task heights. Specifically, within a wide vertical workspace ranging from ground level to 1.1~m-high tabletops, the system demonstrates an average success rate of 73.3% for payloads up to 1.3 kg, with an average execution time of 4.06 s. Unlike prior works that handle lightweight objects and execute pick-and-place motions with slow, piecewise motions, the proposed framework exploits concurrent locomotion and manipulation for dynamic, continuous execution. These results demonstrate the potential of quadrupedal mobile manipulators for adaptive, whole-body pick-and-place with heavier payloads and extended workspaces.

extra.full_text: Modeling concentric tube robots (CTRs) involves complex nonlinear continuum mechanics, and despite recent progress, physics-based models often lack an accurate representation of the experimental setups.

title: Emotional Expression in Low-Degrees-of-Freedom Robots: Assessing Perception with Reachy Mini
summary: Reachy Mini is used to study how people read emotions from a robot with very limited, non-anthropomorphic expressive channels rather than a face or body built for human-like affect. The paper focuses on whether sparse low-degree-of-freedom movements can still produce recognizable emotional impressions, addressing a practical gap for small social robots whose hardware cannot support rich expression.

extra.full_text: Emotion expression is central to human--robot interaction, yet little is known about how people interpret affect on robots with sparse, non-anthropomorphic expressive capabilities.

title: TMRL: Diffusion Timestep-Modulated Pretraining Enables Exploration for Efficient Policy Finetuning
summary: TMRL addresses a common failure mode in RL fine-tuning of pretrained robot policies: behavioral cloning leaves the policy too narrowly concentrated around demonstration actions, so it cannot explore effectively when downstream rewards require broader coverage. It uses diffusion timestep modulation during pretraining to shape the policy’s action distribution for better exploration, aiming to make subsequent RL fine-tuning more sample-efficient.

extra.full_text: Fine-tuning pre-trained robot policies with reinforcement learning (RL) often inherits the bottlenecks introduced by pre-training with behavioral cloning (BC), which produces narrow action distributions that lack the coverage necessary for downstream exploration.

title: Optimal Policy Learning under Budget and Coverage Constraints
summary: Optimal policy learning is formulated with both a spending cap and a required minimum level of coverage, rather than treating either constraint in isolation. The analysis shows that the constrained problem has a knapsack-like structure, with the optimal treatment or action rule determined by an affine threshold that incorporates shadow prices for both budget and coverage.

extra.full_text: We study optimal policy learning under combined budget and minimum coverage constraints. We show that the problem admits a knapsack-type structure and that the optimal policy can be characterized by an affine threshold rule involving both budget and coverage shadow prices.

title: IMPACT: An Implicit Active-Set Augmented Lagrangian for Fast Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
summary: IMPACT tackles contact-implicit trajectory optimization by using an implicit active-set augmented Lagrangian formulation, aiming to make planning through intermittent contacts faster without requiring a pre-specified contact-mode schedule. The setup is aimed at contact-rich manipulation and locomotion, where the optimizer must decide when and where contact happens as part of the trajectory rather than following a hand-designed sequence.

extra.comment: Accepted to Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS), 2026
extra.full_text: Contact-implicit trajectory optimization (CITO) has attracted growing attention as a unified framework for planning and control in contact-rich robotic tasks. Recent approaches have demonstrated promising results in manipulation and locomotion without requiring a prescribed contact-mode schedule.

title: Learning What Matters: Adaptive Information-Theoretic Objectives for Robot Exploration
summary: Learning What Matters tackles robot exploration by trying to learn information-theoretic objectives that steer data collection toward measurements that actually reduce uncertainty in a robot’s model parameters. The interesting angle is the emphasis on adaptivity: instead of assuming a fixed notion of “informative” data, the objective is meant to reflect what the current model can still learn from new observations.

extra.full_text: Designing learnable information-theoretic objectives for robot exploration remains challenging. Such objectives aim to guide exploration toward data that reduces uncertainty in model parameters, yet it is often unclear what information the collected data can actually reveal.

title: Interpreting Context-Aware Human Preferences for Multi-Objective Robot Navigation
summary: Robots navigating around people are framed as a multi-objective decision problem where safety, efficiency, and human preferences must be balanced rather than optimized in isolation. The work focuses on interpreting context-aware preferences, so the robot can adjust navigation behavior depending on the surrounding human-shared situation instead of relying on a fixed tradeoff.

extra.full_text: Robots operating in human-shared environments must not only achieve task-level navigation objectives such as safety and efficiency, but also adapt their behavior to human preferences.

title: Learning to Communicate Locally for Large-Scale Multi-Agent Pathfinding
summary: Learning to Communicate Locally for Large-Scale Multi-Agent Pathfinding studies MAPF as a multi-robot trajectory planning problem where many homogeneous agents must move through a shared space without conflicts. From the provided text, the concrete focus is local communication among agents for scaling pathfinding to larger teams, but no method details, benchmarks, or results are given.

extra.full_text: Multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF) is a widely used abstraction for multi-robot trajectory planning problems, where multiple homogeneous agents move simultaneously within a shared environment.

title: Coordinated Manipulation of Hybrid Deformable-Rigid Objects in Constrained Environments
summary: Coordinated manipulation of hybrid deformable-rigid objects tackles cases like cables or ropes attached to rigid parts, where the robot has to manage both continuous deformation and rigid-body constraints in tight spaces. The work focuses on coordinated robot behavior for moving these assemblies through constrained environments, a setting that is harder than standard deformable linear object handling because collisions, object geometry, and coupled rigid-deformable motion all interact.

extra.full_text: Coordinated robotic manipulation of deformable linear objects (DLOs), such as ropes and cables, has been widely studied; however, handling hybrid assemblies composed of both deformable and rigid elements in constrained environments remains challenging.

title: Efficient Emotion-Aware Iconic Gesture Prediction for Robot Co-Speech
summary: Efficient Emotion-Aware Iconic Gesture Prediction for Robot Co-Speech targets robot speech companions that need more than rhythmic beat gestures, focusing on iconic motions that carry semantic emphasis while also reflecting emotional context. From the available description, it appears to frame gesture generation as a more efficient, emotion-aware prediction problem for co-speech behavior, aiming to make robot communication feel clearer and more engaging.

extra.full_text: Co-speech gestures increase engagement and improve speech understanding. Most data-driven robot systems generate rhythmic beat-like motion, yet few integrate semantic emphasis.

title: BEACON: Cross-Domain Co-Training of Generative Robot Policies via Best-Effort Adaptation
summary: BEACON trains generative robot policies by co-training across domains, using many source-domain demonstrations together with only a small number of target-domain examples. Its best-effort adaptation setup is framed as a theory-driven way to transfer useful behavior without assuming the source data perfectly matches the target robot or environment.

extra.full_text: We introduce BEACON--Best-Effort Adaptation for Cross-Domain Co-Training--a theory-driven framework for training generative robot policies with abundant source demonstrations and limited target demonstrations.

title: Sampling-Based Follow-the-Leader Motion Planning for Manipulator-Mounted Continuum Robots
summary: Follow-the-leader motion planning for manipulator-mounted continuum robots uses the robot’s ability to make its body retrace the tip trajectory, which is especially useful for threading through confined spaces. The sampling-based planner appears to target the added complexity of mounting a continuum robot on a manipulator, where both the carrier arm and the flexible body must be coordinated to preserve FTL behavior.

extra.full_text: Follow-the-leader (FTL) motion exploits the unique morphology of continuum robots (CRs) to navigate confined spaces by having the body retrace the path of the tip.

title: COAD: Constant-Time Planning for Continuous Goal Manipulation with Compressed Library and Online Adaptation
summary: COAD targets repeated manipulation planning problems where only the goal object and its nearby obstacle move, while the rest of the workspace stays fixed. It precomputes and compresses a library of motion plans, then adapts a retrieved plan online so planning time stays effectively constant across continuous goal placements.

extra.comment: Adil Shiyas and Zhuoyun Zhong contributed equally to this work
extra.full_text: In many robotic manipulation tasks, the robot repeatedly solves motion-planning problems that differ mainly in the location of the goal object and its associated obstacle, while the surrounding workspace remains fixed.

title: Beyond Motion Imitation: Is Human Motion Data Alone Sufficient to Explain Gait Control and Biomechanics?
summary: A reinforcement-learning motion-imitation setup is used to test whether human motion trajectories by themselves are enough to recover realistic gait control and biomechanics. The study adds foot-ground interaction measures as reward terms and examines how they change estimated gait kinematics and kinetics, directly probing whether contact forces and related interaction signals supply information that motion-only imitation misses.

extra.full_text: With the growing interest in motion imitation learning (IL) for human biomechanics and wearable robotics, this study investigates how additional foot-ground interaction measures, used as reward terms, affect human gait kinematics and kinetics estimation within a reinforcement learning-based IL framework.

title: Exploring Token-Space Manipulation in Latent Audio Tokenizers
summary: Neural audio codecs turn speech into compact discrete tokens, but their usual frame-by-frame structure makes it hard to isolate or edit broader attributes of an utterance. This paper investigates manipulating those latent audio tokens directly in token space, aiming to expose and control global factors of variation in speech generation rather than treating the codec output as just a local time sequence.

extra.full_text: Neural audio codecs provide compact discrete representations for speech generation and manipulation. However, most codecs organize tokens as frame-level sequences, making it difficult to study or intervene on global factors of variation.

title: HarmoWAM: Harmonizing Generalizable and Precise Manipulation via Adaptive World Action Models
summary: HarmoWAM targets robot manipulation by using World Action Models to capture physical dynamics for control. From the title and abstract fragment, it appears to focus on balancing broad generalization with precise execution through an adaptive action-modeling mechanism, but the provided text does not include tasks, benchmarks, or results.

extra.full_text: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot control by modeling physical dynamics.

title: MAGS-SLAM: Monocular Multi-Agent Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Geometrically and Photometrically Consistent Reconstruction
summary: MAGS-SLAM targets collaborative photorealistic 3D reconstruction using multiple monocular agents, combining multi-agent SLAM with Gaussian splatting to capture large scenes more quickly. The emphasis is on keeping reconstructions both geometrically and photometrically consistent across agents, which is useful for virtual production and cooperative robot exploration.

extra.full_text: Collaborative photorealistic 3D reconstruction from multiple agents enables rapid large-scale scene capture for virtual production and cooperative multi-robot exploration.

title: ForceFlow: Learning to Feel and Act via Contact-Driven Flow Matching
summary: ForceFlow targets contact-rich robot manipulation by learning from force feedback rather than relying only on visual or kinematic imitation signals. It uses contact-driven flow matching to connect what the robot feels during interaction with how it should act, aiming to handle the precise force control needed when contact dynamics are difficult to model.

extra.full_text: Existing imitation learning methods enable robots to interact autonomously with the physical environment. However, contact-rich manipulation tasks remain a significant challenge due to complex contact dynamics that demand high-precision force feedback and control.

title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Model-based Test Oracle for Testing Robot
summary: VISOR targets the test oracle problem in robotics: deciding whether a robot’s behavior actually satisfies a task’s intent, reliability, and quality requirements. It uses a vision-language model as the oracle, judging robot task executions from visual evidence and language-level task expectations rather than relying only on hand-coded checks or narrow sensor assertions.

extra.full_text: Testing robots requires assessing whether they perform their intended tasks correctly, dependably, and with high quality, a challenge known as the test oracle problem in software testing.

title: EFGCL: Learning Dynamic Motion through Spotting-Inspired External Force Guided Curriculum Learning
summary: EFGCL trains legged robots to learn dynamic whole-body motions in reinforcement learning by using a spotting-inspired curriculum, where external forces guide the robot through difficult parts of a motion before being gradually reduced. The idea is to make exploration less failure-prone and stabilize learning for behaviors that would otherwise be hard to discover from scratch.

extra.comment: Accepted at RA-L 2026, website - https://keitayoneda.github.io/kleiyn-efgcl/, YouTube - https://youtu.be/sFK00hm14No/
extra.full_text: Learning dynamic whole-body motions for legged robots through reinforcement learning (RL) remains challenging due to the high risk of failure, which makes efficient exploration difficult and often leads to unstable learning.

title: Natural Gradient Gaussian Approximation Filter on Lie Groups for Robot State Estimation
summary: Natural Gradient Gaussian Approximation Filter targets robot state estimation directly on Lie group manifolds, where states like pose and velocity do not live in ordinary Euclidean space. From the provided text, it is aimed at accurate estimation for systems such as legged robots, where respecting the manifold geometry is important for agile control.

extra.full_text: Accurate state estimation for robotic systems evolving on Lie group manifolds, such as legged robots, is a prerequisite for achieving agile control.

title: Adaptive Action Chunking via Multi-Chunk Q Value Estimation
summary: Adaptive Action Chunking via Multi-Chunk Q Value Estimation extends action chunking from imitation learning into reinforcement learning, where policies reason over short action sequences rather than isolated steps. The approach estimates Q-values across multiple candidate chunks so the agent can adapt chunk length or selection, aiming to preserve temporally coherent behavior while reducing value-estimation bootstrapping error.

extra.full_text: Action chunking emerged as a pivotal technique in imitation learning, enabling policies to predict cohesive action sequences rather than single actions. Recently, this approach has expanded to reinforcement learning (RL), enhancing behavioral consistency and reducing bootstrapping errors in value function estimation.

title: MVB-Grasp: Minimum-Volume-Box Filtering of Diffusion-based Grasps for Frontal Manipulation
summary: MVB-Grasp targets the gap between high-performing 6-DoF diffusion grasp generators and the messier constraints of frontal manipulation with low-cost robot arms. It filters candidate grasps using a minimum-volume box criterion, aiming to discard poses that are geometrically or kinematically impractical when the robot has limited workspace and constrained approach directions.

extra.full_text: State-of-the-art 6-DoF grasp generators excel on tabletop benchmarks with overhead cameras but struggle in frontal grasping scenarios on low-cost manipulators with constrained workspaces, where kinematic limits and approach-direction constraints cause high failure rates.

title: RACAS: Controlling Diverse Robots With a Single Agentic System
summary: RACAS presents a single agentic control system meant to sit above heterogeneous robot APIs, turning actuator commands and sensor reads into higher-level autonomous behavior across different platforms. It targets the engineering gap between low-level robot interfaces and deployable autonomy, packaging the perception, planning, and control pipeline so diverse robots can be commanded through one common system.

extra.comment: 7 pages in main text + 1 page of appendices + 1 page of references, 5 figures in main text + 1 figure in appendices, 2 tables in main text; source code available at https://github.com/janprz11/robot-agnostic-control
extra.full_text: Many robotic platforms expose an API through which external software can command their actuators and read their sensors. However, transitioning from these low-level interfaces to high-level autonomous behaviour requires a complicated pipeline, whose components demand distinct areas of expertise.

title: Beyond Isolation: A Unified Benchmark for General-Purpose Navigation
summary: Beyond Isolation introduces a unified benchmark for general-purpose navigation that evaluates embodied agents across multiple navigation skills and robot embodiments instead of testing isolated behaviors on a fixed morphology. The benchmark is aimed at settings closer to real deployment, where an agent must coordinate different navigation behaviors as its body, platform, or task conditions change.

extra.full_text: The pursuit of general-purpose embodied agents is hindered by fragmented evaluation protocols that isolate navigation skills and fixate on specific robot morphologies, failing to reflect real-world scenarios where agents must orchestrate diverse behaviors across varying embodiments.

title: FAR-Dex: Few-shot Data Augmentation and Adaptive Residual Policy Refinement for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: FAR-Dex targets dexterous arm-hand manipulation in the low-demonstration regime, where high-quality teleoperation data is scarce and the action space is large. It combines few-shot data augmentation with adaptive residual policy refinement, aiming to expand limited demonstrations and then correct or improve the learned policy during manipulation.

extra.comment: Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
extra.full_text: Achieving human-like dexterous manipulation through the collaboration of multi-fingered hands with robotic arms remains a longstanding challenge in robotics, primarily due to the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations and the complexity of high-dimensional action spaces.

title: Overcoming Visual Clutter in Vision Language Action Models via Concept-Gated Visual Distillation
summary: Concept-Gated Visual Distillation targets the precision-reasoning gap in Vision-Language-Action models, where broad semantic reasoning holds up but object localization degrades in visually cluttered scenes. It appears to use task-relevant concepts as a gate for distilling visual information, helping the policy focus on the parts of the scene that matter for action instead of being distracted by clutter.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models demonstrate impressive zero-shot generalization but frequently suffer from a "Precision-Reasoning Gap" in cluttered environments.

title: Continuum Robot Modeling with Action Conditioned Flow Matching
summary: Action Conditioned Flow Matching is used to learn a kinematic self-model that predicts the steady-state shape of tendon-driven continuum robots directly from actuation inputs. The interesting angle is treating TDCR shape prediction as an action-conditioned generative modeling problem, aimed at handling the messy realities of continuous deformation, tendon routing, compliance, friction, and fabrication variability.

extra.full_text: Predicting the shape of tendon driven continuum robots (TDCRs) at steady state from actuation remains challenging due to continuous deformation, complex tendon routing, compliance, friction, and fabrication variability. In this paper, we address this problem as kinematic self modeling conditioned on action.

title: One Interface, Many Robots: Unified Real-Time Low-Level Motion Planning for Collaborative Arms
summary: A common real-time low-level motion-planning interface is introduced for collaborative robot arms, with the goal of making controllers portable across different hardware platforms. The idea is to let heterogeneous cobots share the same planning layer rather than requiring robot-specific integrations, which is useful for labs or deployments that mix multiple arm models.

extra.full_text: This paper proposes a common interface for real-time low-level motion planning of collaborative robotic arms, aimed at enabling broader applicability and improved portability across heterogeneous hardware platforms.

title: Learning When to Stop: Selective Imitation Learning Under Arbitrary Dynamics Shift
summary: Behavior cloning can be reliable when deployment dynamics match training, but this work targets the harder case where the dynamics shift arbitrarily and the imitator must decide when not to act. It frames imitation as a selective decision problem, learning a stopping or abstention rule that preserves performance guarantees by handing off or halting when the learned policy is outside conditions it can safely imitate.

extra.full_text: Behavior cloning provides strong imitation learning guarantees when training and test environments share the same dynamics.

title: Robotic Ultrasound Makes CBCT Alive
summary: Robotic Ultrasound Makes CBCT Alive appears to connect intraoperative cone-beam CT with robotic ultrasound so the static 3D anatomy used for interventional planning can be complemented by live imaging. From the provided text, the concrete premise is that CBCT supplies reliable anatomical context, while the “alive” part suggests updating or augmenting that context during the procedure rather than relying on a single preoperative or intraoperative snapshot.

extra.full_text: Intraoperative Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) provides a reliable 3D anatomical context essential for interventional planning.

title: DRAFTO: Decoupled Reduced-space and Adaptive Feasibility-repair Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Manipulators
summary: DRAFTO is a trajectory optimization algorithm for robotic manipulators that separates the search into a reduced space while using adaptive feasibility repair to keep candidate motions within constraints. From the provided description, it builds a constrained objective covering smoothness, safety, joint limits, and task requirements, aiming to produce feasible manipulator trajectories under practical robot constraints.

extra.full_text: This paper introduces a new algorithm for trajectory optimization, Decoupled Reduced-space and Adaptive Feasibility-repair Trajectory Optimization (DRAFTO). It first constructs a constrained objective that accounts for smoothness, safety, joint limits, and task requirements.

title: TinyNav: End-to-End TinyML for Real-Time Autonomous Navigation on Microcontrollers
summary: TinyNav targets real-time autonomous navigation on microcontrollers, replacing the usual power-hungry onboard processors with an end-to-end TinyML stack sized for severe memory and compute limits. The interesting angle is the full navigation loop under MCU constraints, where model complexity has to be pared down enough for low-cost robots without giving up autonomous behavior.

extra.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, presented at CUCAI2026 (Canadian Undergraduate Conference on AI, https://cucai.ca)
extra.full_text: Autonomous navigation typically relies on power-intensive processors, limiting accessibility in low-cost robotics. Although microcontrollers offer a resource-efficient alternative, they impose strict constraints on model complexity.

title: A Visuo-Tactile Data Collection System with Haptic Feedback for Coarse-to-Fine Imitation Learning
summary: A visuo-tactile demonstration setup lets operators collect contact-rich robot imitation data while receiving haptic feedback, so subtle force changes are preserved instead of being hidden behind purely visual teleoperation. The system is aimed at coarse-to-fine imitation learning, where temporally structured demonstrations can teach both broad motion and fine contact modulation.

extra.full_text: We present a visuo-tactile data-collection system that generates temporally structured, contact-rich demonstrations for imitation learning. Conventional systems often decouple the operator from contact forces, which hinders the demonstration of subtle force modulation.

title: Zero-shot Imitation Learning by Latent Topology Mapping
summary: Zero-shot Imitation Learning by Latent Topology Mapping targets the cost of collecting expert demonstrations for every complex task by aiming to transfer imitation behavior without task-specific demonstrations. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, beyond framing latent topology mapping as the route to zero-shot imitation learning in environments where demonstrations are expensive.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning is effective for training agents when expert demonstrations are available, but collecting demonstrations for every complex task in an environment is costly.

title: Grasp as You Dream: Imitating Functional Grasping from Generated Human Demonstrations
summary: Grasp as You Dream tackles functional grasping by using generated human demonstrations as imitation data, aiming to help robots grasp everyday objects in ways that match downstream use rather than just stable pickup. The core idea is to turn generative human action examples into supervision for open-world robot grasping, addressing the data bottleneck caused by the diversity of objects and tasks.

extra.full_text: Building generalist robots capable of performing functional grasping in everyday, open-world environments remains a significant challenge due to the vast diversity of objects and tasks.

title: TAMEn: Tactile-Aware Manipulation Engine for Closed-Loop Data Collection in Contact-Rich Tasks
summary: TAMEn targets the bottleneck in collecting demonstrations for contact-rich bimanual manipulation with handheld teleoperation, where hardware fit and useful tactile data are hard to get right. It is a tactile-aware manipulation engine for closed-loop data collection, designed to make demonstration gathering more adaptable and effective when the task depends heavily on sustained contact and force feedback.

extra.full_text: Handheld paradigms offer an efficient and intuitive way for collecting large-scale demonstration of robot manipulation. However, achieving contact-rich bimanual manipulation through these methods remains a pivotal challenge, which is substantially hindered by hardware adaptability and data efficacy.

title: Robots that learn to evaluate models of collective behavior
summary: Robots are used as active evaluators of collective-behavior models, moving beyond offline checks against fixed trajectory statistics. The idea is to let embodied agents test whether a behavioral model actually produces the expected group dynamics in interaction, which is especially relevant for studying animal motion, decision-making, and bio-inspired swarm robotics.

extra.full_text: Understanding and modeling animal behavior is essential for studying collective motion, decision-making, and bio-inspired robotics. Yet, evaluating the accuracy of behavioral models still often relies on offline comparisons to static trajectory statistics.

title: The Neural Compass: Probabilistic Relative Feature Fields for Robotic Search
summary: The Neural Compass uses object co-occurrence as a probabilistic cue for robotic search, treating nearby objects like fridges as evidence about broader scene context such as kitchens and likely target locations. It frames these relationships as relative feature fields, giving a robot a way to navigate unfamiliar environments by reasoning over what observed objects imply about where the missing object may be.

extra.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables, submitted to IROS 2026
extra.full_text: Object co-occurrences provide a key cue for finding objects successfully and efficiently in unfamiliar environments. Typically, one looks for cups in kitchens and views fridges as evidence of being in a kitchen.

title: Many-to-Many Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery
summary: Many-to-Many Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery extends warehouse MAPD beyond fixed pickup-delivery pairs, treating tasks as choices among multiple possible pickup and delivery locations while robots operate continuously and avoid collisions. The interesting shift is that assignment and routing have to be solved together under this extra flexibility, which better matches settings where equivalent items or drop-off points exist but makes coordination harder than the standard one-to-one formulation.

extra.full_text: Multi-robot systems in automated warehouses must manage continuous streams of pickup-and-delivery tasks while ensuring efficiency and safety. Prior work on Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery (MAPD) has largely focused on the one-to-one variant, where each task has a fixed pickup and delivery location.

title: Learning-Based Strategy for Composite Robot Assembly Skill Adaptation
summary: Learning-Based Strategy for Composite Robot Assembly Skill Adaptation targets contact-rich industrial assembly with tight tolerances, friction changes, and uncertain contact dynamics on position-controlled manipulators. It appears to focus on adapting composite assembly skills through learning rather than relying on fixed hand-tuned motions, but the provided text does not include the specific algorithm, tasks, or results.

extra.full_text: Contact-rich robotic skills remain challenging for industrial robots due to tight geometric tolerances, frictional variability, and uncertain contact dynamics, particularly when using position-controlled manipulators.

title: BrickCraft: Visuomotor Skill Composition with Situated Manual Guidance for Long-Horizon Interlocking Brick Assembly
summary: BrickCraft composes visuomotor skills for long-horizon interlocking-brick assembly, tying task-level reasoning to spatial grounding and fine manipulation. It targets the hard part of Lego-like construction: assembling many dependent pieces in sequence while using situated manual guidance to keep the robot grounded in the physical build state.

extra.full_text: Autonomous robotic assembly of interlocking bricks demands seamless integration of long-horizon task reasoning, spatial grounding, and fine-grained manipulation. This paper presents BrickCraft, a compositional framework designed for long-horizon and generalizable interlocking brick assembly.

title: Logical Robots: Declarative Multi-Agent Programming in Logica
summary: Logical Robots is an interactive multi-agent robot simulation platform where agent policies are written as Logica predicates rather than imperative control code. Robots turn simulated radar-array observations and shared-memory state into motor commands through declarative logic rules, making it a compact testbed for exploring how logic programming can specify autonomous behavior and coordination.

extra.comment: International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS), May 25-29, 2026. Paphos, Cyprus
extra.full_text: We present Logical Robots, an interactive multi-agent simulation platform where autonomous robot behavior is specified declaratively in the logic programming language Logica. Robot behavior is defined by logical predicates that map observations from simulated radar arrays and shared memory to desired motor outputs.

title: Neurosymbolic Imitation Learning with Human Guidance: A Privileged Information Approach
summary: Neurosymbolic imitation learning with human guidance combines neural perception with symbolic structure, using privileged human-provided information during training to reduce the sample burden and overfitting common in pure neural imitation learning. The approach is aimed at complex environments where high-dimensional inputs matter, but where injecting structured guidance can make learned policies more data-efficient and robust.

extra.full_text: Imitation learning is widely used for learning to act in complex environments. While pure neural-based methods handle high dimensional data effectively, they suffer from the requirement of large number of samples and are prone to overfitting.

title: Inverse Resistive Force Theory (I-RFT): Learning granular properties through robot-terrain physical interactions
summary: Inverse Resistive Force Theory (I-RFT) uses physical interactions between a robot leg and granular terrain to infer the terrain’s mechanical properties from sensed ground reaction forces. The idea is useful because legged robots already experience these forces during locomotion, so the same contacts that move the robot can also estimate how soft or resistant the ground is and inform safer, more efficient traversal.

extra.full_text: For robots to navigate safely and efficiently on soft, granular terrains, it is crucial to gather information about the terrain's mechanical properties, which directly affect locomotion performance. Recent research has developed robotic legs that can accurately sense ground reaction forces during locomotion.

title: Bi3: A Biplatform, Bicultural, Biperson Dataset for Social Robot Navigation
summary: Bi3 is a dataset for studying social robot navigation around groups of people in a constrained lab environment. It is organized around two platforms, two cultural settings, and two-person interactions, making it useful for examining how navigation behavior changes across robot embodiments and social contexts.

extra.full_text: We contribute Bi3, a dataset of social robot navigation among groups of people in a constrained lab space.

title: GA3T: A Ground-Aerial Terrain Traversability Dataset for Heterogeneous Robot Teams in Unstructured Environments
summary: GA3T is an arXiv dataset effort focused on terrain traversability for heterogeneous ground-and-aerial robot teams operating in unstructured outdoor environments. It centers on the idea that aerial viewpoints, ground-level sensing, and different mobility constraints can be combined to give robots a richer picture of where they can safely move through complex terrain.

extra.full_text: Heterogeneous air-ground robot teams combine complementary sensing modalities, mobility characteristics, and spatial viewpoints that can significantly enhance perception in complex outdoor environments.

title: SwarmCoDe: A Scalable Co-Design Framework for Heterogeneous Robot Swarms via Dynamic Speciation
summary: SwarmCoDe tackles robot-swarm co-design by jointly optimizing heterogeneous robot types and their collective behavior, using dynamic speciation to let different robot “species” emerge as the design search progresses. The framing is aimed at scalable swarms, where even small gains in per-robot capability or cost can compound across many units, but the provided text does not include specific experiments or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Robot swarms offer inherent robustness and the capacity to execute complex, collaborative tasks surpassing the capabilities of single-agent systems. Co-designing these systems is critical, as marginal improvements in individual performance or unit cost compound significantly at scale.

title: RobotEQ: Transitioning from Passive Intelligence to Active Intelligence in Embodied AI
summary: RobotEQ argues that embodied AI should move beyond executing explicit user commands toward actively judging whether actions are allowed or forbidden in human settings. The work frames this as a transition from passive instruction-following to “active intelligence,” where robots need social and normative understanding before acting, even when no one has directly told them what to do.

extra.full_text: Embodied AI is a prominent research topic in both academia and industry. Current research centers on completing tasks based on explicit user instructions. However, for robots to integrate into human society, they must understand which actions are permissible and which are prohibited, even without explicit commands.

title: Hazard Management in Robot-Assisted Mammography Support
summary: Robotic mammography support could make screening more accessible, but the close physical interaction with patients creates safety hazards that have to be managed before such systems can be deployed clinically. The paper focuses on hazard management for robot-assisted mammography, framing the problem around embodied-AI systems operating near vulnerable patients where contact, positioning, and clinical workflow risks are central.

extra.full_text: Robotic and embodied-AI systems have the potential to improve accessibility and quality of care in clinical settings, but their deployment in close physical contact with vulnerable patients introduces significant safety risks.

title: Unified 4D World Action Modeling from Video Priors with Asynchronous Denoising
summary: X-WAM is a unified 4D world model for robotics that combines real-time action execution with high-fidelity world synthesis, producing both video and 3D reconstruction rather than staying in 2D pixel space. It builds on video priors with asynchronous denoising to target the usual tradeoff in unified world models: fast control for robot actions without sacrificing the quality of generated and reconstructed 4D scenes.

extra.full_text: We propose X-WAM, a Unified 4D World Model that unifies real-time robotic action execution and high-fidelity 4D world synthesis (video + 3D reconstruction) in a single framework, addressing the critical limitations of prior unified world models (e.g., UWM) that only model 2D pixel-space and fail to balance action efficiency and world modeling quality.

title: DexSynRefine: Synthesizing and Refining Human-Object Interaction Motion for Physically Feasible Dexterous Robot Actions
summary: DexSynRefine targets the gap between sparse human-object interaction demonstrations and robot-executable dexterous manipulation by turning kinematic HOI motion into physically feasible actions under embodiment and contact differences. It synthesizes and refines motions so a dexterous robot can reproduce human-like object interactions despite the dynamics and contact constraints that make raw HOI trajectories unusable.

extra.full_text: Learning dexterous manipulation from human-object interaction (HOI) data is a scalable alternative to teleoperation, but HOI demonstrations are sparse and provide only kinematic motion that is not directly executable under embodiment mismatch and contact-rich dynamics.

title: Reward Shaping and Action Masking for Compositional Tasks using Behavior Trees and LLMs
summary: Behavior trees are used to break a compositional robot task into subtasks, while an LLM helps define the structure needed for reinforcement learning over those subtasks. The approach focuses on making RL more efficient by deriving subtask rewards and applying action masks, so the agent learns within a constrained, task-aware action space rather than exploring blindly.

extra.full_text: Decomposing complex tasks into a sequence of simpler subtasks can improve learning efficiency for an autonomous agent. Reinforcement learning (RL) can be used to optimize agent policies to complete subtasks, but requires well-defined subtask rewards and benefits from action masking.

title: MARS-Dragonfly: Agile and Robust Flight Control of Modular Aerial Robot Systems
summary: MARS-Dragonfly studies flight control for modular aerial robot systems made from multiple drone units that can connect into different formations. The focus is agile, robust control for these reconfigurable multi-drone assemblies, where the controller has to handle changing geometry, payload demands, and failures while keeping the combined vehicle stable in flight.

extra.full_text: Modular Aerial Robot Systems (MARS) comprise multiple drone units with reconfigurable connected formations, providing high adaptability to diverse mission scenarios, fault conditions, and payload capacities.

title: On the Emergence of Pendular Structure in Multi-Contact Locomotion
summary: LIPM is treated here less as a convenient approximation and more as a structure that can emerge from the objectives used in multi-contact locomotion control. The note examines how cost preferences in a controller can favor pendular center-of-mass behavior, making a more direct connection between common legged-robot models and the optimization principles that produce them.

extra.full_text: LIPM is everywhere in legged-locomotion control, but almost always as a modeling choice rather than as something the   controller's cost actually prefers. This note tries to make that link more explicit.

title: Creative Robot Tool Use by Counterfactual Reasoning
summary: A causal reasoning system lets a robot identify tools that can be repurposed for tasks outside their intended use. It runs simulated experiments in a learned dynamics model to uncover how a tool’s properties affect task outcomes, then uses counterfactual reasoning to decide whether an unconventional tool could work.

extra.full_text: We propose a causal reasoning framework for creative robot tool use where a suitable tool for a task is correctly identified for use beyond its primary objectives. The proposed framework first discovers the causal relationships between the tool and the task by conducting simulated experiments in a dynamics model.

title: Soft Rigid Hybrid Gripper with Inflatable Silicone Pockets for Tunable Frictional Grasping
summary: A soft-rigid hybrid gripper uses inflatable silicone pockets to tune surface friction during grasping, aiming to hold heavy or slippery objects without simply increasing normal force. The mechanism is especially relevant for fragile items, where conventional rigid grippers can damage the object while trying to maintain a secure grasp.

extra.full_text: Grasping objects with diverse mechanical properties, such as heavy, slippery, or fragile items, remains a significant challenge in robotics. Conventional rigid grippers typically rely on increasing the normal forces to secure an object, however, this can cause damage to fragile objects due to excessive force.

title: A Closed-Form Dual-Barrier CBF Safety Filter for Holonomic Robots on Incrementally Built Occupancy Grid Maps
summary: A dual-barrier control barrier function safety filter computes real-time velocity commands for holonomic robots navigating occupancy grid maps that are built incrementally. The closed-form structure suggests it is meant to avoid the overhead of online optimization while still enforcing safety constraints against newly discovered obstacles during mapping.

extra.full_text: We present a dual-barrier control barrier function (CBF) safety filter for real-time, safety-critical velocity control of holonomic robots operating in incrementally built occupancy grid maps.

title: AnyUser: Translating Sketched User Intent into Domestic Robots
summary: AnyUser lets people instruct domestic robots by drawing free-form sketches directly on camera images, with optional language to clarify the intent. The interesting part is the interaction style: instead of requiring precise commands or predefined interfaces, it treats rough visual annotations as a general way to specify household tasks in the robot’s perceived environment.

extra.comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO)
extra.full_text: We introduce AnyUser, a unified robotic instruction system for intuitive domestic task instruction via free-form sketches on camera images, optionally with language.

title: Allometric Scaling Laws for Bipedal Robots
summary: Allometric Scaling Laws for Bipedal Robots asks how the size-dependent relationships seen in animals, linking mass to stride frequency, speed, and torque, carry over to legged machines. It frames robot scaling as more than a geometric resizing problem, focusing on whether bipedal robots obey predictable power-law trends that could guide how designs should change when built larger or smaller.

extra.full_text: Scaling the design of robots up or down remains a fundamental challenge. While biological systems follow well-established isometric and allometric scaling laws relating mass, stride frequency, velocity, and torque, it is unclear how these relationships translate to robotic systems.

title: Enhancing Glass Surface Reconstruction via Depth Prior for Robot Navigation
summary: Depth Anything 3 is used as a geometric prior to repair unreliable depth measurements around indoor glass surfaces, addressing a failure mode that can mislead robot navigation. The central challenge is turning the foundation model’s relative depth into metrically scaled geometry, so the method appears to focus on fusing its prior with sensor depth to reconstruct glass surfaces in a navigation-ready form.

extra.full_text: Indoor robot navigation is often compromised by glass surfaces, which severely corrupt depth sensor measurements. While foundation models like Depth Anything 3 provide excellent geometric priors, they lack an absolute metric scale.

title: Gaze4HRI: Zero-shot Benchmarking Gaze Estimation Neural-Networks for Human-Robot Interaction
summary: Gaze4HRI benchmarks zero-shot, appearance-based 3D gaze estimation networks in human-robot interaction settings, where models must infer gaze vectors directly from RGB images without task-specific calibration. It targets the gap between the cost appeal of zero-shot gaze estimation and the unresolved question of whether those models remain reliable when deployed around robots interacting with people.

extra.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face and Gesture Recognition (FG 2026)
extra.full_text: While zero-shot appearance-based 3D gaze estimation offers significant cost-efficiency by directly mapping RGB images to gaze vectors, its reliability in Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) settings remains uncertain.

title: 3D Printing of Passively Actuated Self-Folding Robots with Integrated Functional Modules
summary: Elastic-driven self-folding lets flat 3D-printed conductive PLA nets transform into robot structures without active folding hardware. The interesting mechanism is the combination of printable conductive material and passive elastic actuation, which points toward low-complexity fabrication of robots with integrated functional modules directly from planar prints.

extra.comment: 8pages, 10 figures, This paper is accepted in ICRA 2026
extra.full_text: We introduce an elastic-driven self-folding approach that fabricates robots directly from flat 3D-printed conductive PLA nets.

title: Active Contact Sensing for Robust Robot-to-Human Object Handover
summary: Active contact sensing is used to make robot-to-human handovers more reliable by distinguishing a secure human grasp from incidental touches before the robot releases an object. The setup targets assistant robots in settings like homes or operating rooms, where the robot needs to keep holding the item through accidental contact but let go promptly once the person has actually taken it.

extra.full_text: Robot-to-human object handover is an essential skill for robot assistants, from serving drinks at home to passing surgical tools in the operating room. We expect robots to perform handover robustly -- to release the object only after a firm human grasp while ignoring incidental touches.

title: Shepherding UAV Swarm with Action Prediction Based on Movement Constraints
summary: A sheepdog-inspired controller steers a swarm of small UAVs by predicting how the group will move while respecting the motion limits of real robots. The interesting part is that the prediction is not just geometric or idealized: it explicitly incorporates movement constraints, aiming to make swarm shepherding behavior more transferable to physical UAV platforms.

extra.comment: Incomplete results were found in the paper
extra.full_text: In this study, we propose a new sheepdog-inspired control method for a swarm of small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), which predicts the swarm behavior while explicitly accounting for the motion constraints of real robots.

title: Foundational World Models Accurately Detect Bimanual Manipulator Failures
summary: Foundational world models are used to detect anomalous failures in bimanual manipulators, where the observation space combines high-dimensional vision with proprioceptive signals. The framing is interesting because it treats failure detection as something a pretrained world model can infer from rich robot state trajectories, rather than relying only on task-specific monitors or hand-engineered thresholds.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
extra.full_text: Deploying visuomotor robots at scale is challenging due to the potential for anomalous failures to degrade performance, cause damage, or endanger human life. Bimanual manipulators are no exception; these robots have vast state spaces comprised of high-dimensional images and proprioceptive signals.

title: Autonomous Laparoscope Control through Unified Mechanics-Based Representation of Multimodal Intraoperative Information
summary: Laparoscope-holding robots are framed here as active assistants that continuously adjust camera pose to preserve an ideal surgical field of view during minimally invasive procedures. The interesting idea is to unify multimodal intraoperative cues into a mechanics-based representation, giving the robot a shared way to reason about what is happening in the operative scene and how the laparoscope should move in response.

extra.full_text: Laparoscope-holding robots can provide surgeons with a stable laparoscopic field of view (FOV) and reduce the burden on human assistants. To maintain an ideal intraoperative FOV, the robot must continuously adjust the laparoscope pose according to intraoperative information.

title: Real-Time Projected Adaptive Control for Closed-Chain Co-Manipulative Continuum Robots
summary: Multiple continuum arms grasp a shared flexible object, creating a closed-chain system where motion commands in one arm can generate coupled dynamics and internal reaction forces across the others. The work focuses on real-time projected adaptive control for these co-manipulative continuum robots, using projection to handle the closed-chain constraints while adapting to uncertain deformable-system dynamics.

extra.full_text: In co-manipulative continuum robots (CCRs), multiple continuum arms cooperate by grasping a common flexible object, forming a closed-chain deformable mechanical system. The closed-chain coupling induces strong dynamic interactions and internal reaction forces.

title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the Effects of Network Quality of Service on Robotic Telesurgery
summary: Long-distance robotic telesurgery depends on stable network quality, but this analysis focuses on how realistic QoS degradations affect actual surgical task performance rather than treating connectivity as a binary constraint. It frames latency, packet loss, jitter, and related network conditions as measurable factors in teleoperation reliability, aiming to clarify which degradations most threaten precision and safety in remote surgical workflows.

extra.comment: Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses, in any current or future media, including reprinting/republishing this material for advertising or promotional purposes, creating new collective works, for resale or redistribution to servers or lists, or reuse of any copyrighted component of this work in other works
extra.full_text: The viability of long-distance telesurgery hinges on reliable network Quality of Service (QoS), yet the impact of realistic network degradations on task performance is not sufficiently understood.

title: Hi-WM: Human-in-the-World-Model for Scalable Robot Post-Training
summary: Hi-WM aims to make robot post-training less bottlenecked by real-world interaction by moving human corrections into a learned world model rather than requiring every intervention to happen on physical hardware. The setup targets pretrained generalist robot policies that need task-specific refinement, using simulated rollouts and human-in-the-loop feedback to reduce the cost of resets, scene setup, robot time, and continuous operator supervision.

extra.full_text: Post-training is essential for turning pretrained generalist robot policies into reliable task-specific controllers, but existing human-in-the-loop pipelines remain tied to physical execution: each correction requires robot time, scene setup, resets, and operator supervision in the real world.

title: FingerViP: Learning Real-World Dexterous Manipulation with Fingertip Visual Perception
summary: FingerViP targets dexterous manipulation failures caused by relying on a single wrist-mounted camera, which can lose sight of the object or fingers during contact-rich tasks. It equips the hand with fingertip visual perception, giving the policy local, multi-view information from the contact points where occlusion matters most.

extra.full_text: The current practice of dexterous manipulation generally relies on a single wrist-mounted view, which is often occluded and limits performance on tasks requiring multi-view perception.

title: Can we Trust Unreliable Voxels? Exploring 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction under Label Noise
summary: 3D semantic occupancy prediction is tested under the messy conditions that real robotic systems face, where voxel labels can be corrupted by structural artifacts and dynamic trailing effects. The work focuses on whether models trained with unreliable occupancy supervision can still be trusted, framing label noise as a safety-relevant perception problem rather than just an annotation nuisance.

extra.comment: The benchmark and source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/mylwx/OccNL
extra.full_text: 3D semantic occupancy prediction is a cornerstone of robotic perception, yet real-world voxel annotations are inherently corrupted by structural artifacts and dynamic trailing effects. This raises a critical but underexplored question: can autonomous systems safely rely on such unreliable occupancy supervision?

title: Towards Robotic Lake Maintenance: Integrating SONAR and Satellite Data to Assist Human Operators
summary: Robotic lake maintenance is framed as an operator-assistance problem for artificial water bodies, combining SONAR sensing with satellite data to support monitoring and ecosystem upkeep. From the available description, the emphasis is on helping humans track conditions in managed aquatic environments that require regular intervention, rather than fully automating maintenance.

extra.comment: Accepted to and presented at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering (ICMRE)
extra.full_text: Artificial Water Bodies (AWBs) are human-made systems that require continuous monitoring due to their artificial biological processes. These systems demand regular maintenance to manage their ecosystems effectively.

title: Learning to Forget -- Hierarchical Episodic Memory for Lifelong Robot Deployment
summary: Robots deployed over long periods need episodic memory that can answer user questions about past actions and failures without storing every frame and sensor trace indefinitely. Learning to Forget targets this by using a hierarchical episodic memory scheme that selectively discards or preserves experiences based on relevance, aiming to keep lifelong multimodal memory compact enough for real-time querying while still aligned with what users are likely to care about.

extra.full_text: Robots must verbalize their past experiences when users ask "Where did you put my keys?" or "Why did the task fail?" Yet maintaining life-long episodic memory (EM) from continuous multimodal perception quickly exceeds storage limits and makes real-time query impractical, calling for selective forgetting that adapts to users' notions of relevance.

title: Learning Reactive Dexterous Grasping via Hierarchical Task-Space RL Planning and Joint-Space QP Control
summary: A hybrid hierarchical controller handles reactive dexterous grasping by separating task-space planning from joint-space execution. The high-level RL policy decides spatial grasping intent, while a lower-level quadratic-programming controller turns those commands into feasible joint motions, aiming to make dexterous hands respond more robustly during grasp attempts.

extra.full_text: In this work, we propose a hybrid hierarchical control framework for reactive dexterous grasping that explicitly decouples high-level spatial intent from low-level joint execution.

title: Population-Aware Imitation Learning in Mean-field Games with Common Noise
summary: Population-Aware Imitation Learning targets mean-field games where a large population of agents is driven not only by individual interactions but also by shared stochastic shocks that make the population distribution itself random. It learns policies from demonstrations while accounting for this evolving population state, aiming to imitate behavior in settings where ignoring common noise would misrepresent the collective dynamics.

extra.full_text: Mean Field Games (MFGs) provide a powerful framework for modeling the collective behavior of large populations of interacting agents. In this paper, we address the problem of Imitation Learning (IL) in MFGs subject to common noise, where the population distribution evolves stochastically.

title: Height Control and Optimal Torque Planning for Jumping With Wheeled-Bipedal Robots
summary: Studies accurate jump-height control for wheeled-bipedal robots by planning joint torques while explicitly optimizing energy use. The focus is on making jumping behavior more predictable and efficient, tying the target height to torque profiles rather than treating the jump as a purely reactive balance-control problem.

extra.comment: 6 pages, 16 figures. Accepted for publication at ICARM 2021
extra.full_text: This paper mainly studies the accurate height jumping control of wheeled-bipedal robots based on torque planning and energy consumption optimization.

title: FORMULA: FORmation MPC with neUral barrier Learning for safety Assurance
summary: FORMULA targets safety-aware formation control for multi-robot teams operating in cluttered, dynamic environments. It combines formation model predictive control with neural barrier learning, aiming to keep robots in coordinated formations while enforcing safety constraints around obstacles and other agents.

extra.comment: Accepted to IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV) 2026
extra.full_text: Multi-robot systems (MRS) are essential for large-scale applications such as disaster response, material transport, and warehouse logistics, yet ensuring robust, safety-aware formation control in cluttered and dynamic environments remains a major challenge.

title: Benchmarking Local Language Models for Social Robots using Edge Devices
summary: Benchmarks local language models running on edge devices for social-educational robots such as the Robot Study Companion, where responses need to be fast, private, and feasible under tight onboard compute limits. The focus is on whether small, locally hosted models can support socially interactive tutoring behavior without relying on cloud inference.

extra.comment: Accepted for 22nd IEEE International Conference on Advanced Robotics and its Social Impact (June 2026) in Vienna, Austria
extra.full_text: Social-educational robots designed for socially interactive pedagogical support, such as the Robot Study Companion (RSC), rely on responsive, privacy-preserving interaction despite severely limited compute.

title: PRISM: Personalized Refinement of Imitation Skills for Manipulation via Human Instructions
summary: PRISM refines robotic manipulation imitation policies by conditioning them on human instructions, aiming to personalize or adjust learned skills after demonstration. From the provided text, the concrete mechanism and results are not specified, so the work is best read as an instruction-driven policy refinement method for making imitation-based manipulation behavior more responsive to user intent.

extra.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, Accepted for publication at European Robotics Forum 2026
extra.full_text: This paper presents PRISM: an instruction-conditioned refinement method for imitation policies in robotic manipulation.

title: AnchorD: Metric Grounding of Monocular Depth Using Factor Graphs
summary: AnchorD tackles metric depth estimation for robotics by grounding monocular depth predictions with factor graphs, aiming to recover dense, accurate depth where conventional sensors struggle, such as transparent, specular, and other non-Lambertian surfaces. The idea is positioned for manipulation, grasping, and navigation settings where reliable geometry matters, but the provided text does not include specific benchmarks, datasets, or quantitative results.

extra.full_text: Dense and accurate depth estimation is essential for robotic manipulation, grasping, and navigation, yet currently available depth sensors are prone to errors on transparent, specular, and general non-Lambertian surfaces.

title: Temporally Consistent Object 6D Pose Estimation for Robot Control
summary: Single-view RGB pose estimators are being adapted for closed-loop robot control, but the central issue here is that accurate per-frame 6D poses are not enough when predictions jitter or fail intermittently over time. The work focuses on making object pose estimates temporally consistent and robust enough to serve as stable visual feedback for robot motion, rather than just reporting isolated image-level accuracy.

extra.full_text: Single-view RGB object pose estimators have reached a level of precision and efficiency that makes them good candidates for vision-based robot control. However, off-the-shelf methods lack temporal consistency and robustness that are mandatory for a stable feedback control.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Uncertainty Analysis in Self-Adaptive Robots Using LLMs
summary: Self-adaptive robots face uncertainty as their environments shift, and this paper looks at using LLMs with a human in the loop to analyze those uncertainties before they turn into safety or reliability failures. From the available text, the focus is on combining automated reasoning with human oversight so adaptive robot behavior can be checked against risks that may not be captured by fixed models.

extra.full_text: Self-adaptive robots operate in dynamic, unpredictable environments where unaddressed uncertainties can lead to safety violations and operational failures.

title: Teaching Robots to Interpret Social Interactions through Lexically-guided Dynamic Graph Learning
summary: Robots in this work are framed as social interpreters: they need to infer a user’s internal state from observed behavior, anticipate what the user may do next, and decide how to respond. The title suggests the approach uses lexically guided dynamic graph learning, likely combining language cues with evolving interaction graphs so the robot can reason over social relationships and behavioral context rather than treating observations as isolated signals.

extra.full_text: For a robot to be called socially intelligent, it must be able to infer users internal states from their current behaviour, predict the users future behaviour, and if required, respond appropriately.

title: RoboCasa365: A Large-Scale Simulation Framework for Training and Benchmarking Generalist Robots
summary: RoboCasa365 targets the evaluation gap for generalist household robots by providing a reproducible, large-scale simulation framework for training and benchmarking everyday manipulation skills in human-like environments. It is positioned less as a single policy method than as infrastructure: a common benchmark meant to make progress toward broadly capable home robots easier to measure systematically.

extra.comment: ICLR 2026; First three authors contributed equally
extra.full_text: Recent advances in robot learning have accelerated progress toward generalist robots that can perform everyday tasks in human environments. Yet it remains difficult to gauge how close we are to this vision. The field lacks a reproducible, large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation.

title: OmniPlanner: Universal Exploration and Inspection Path Planning across Robot Morphologies
summary: OmniPlanner targets exploration and inspection path planning that can transfer across robot morphologies instead of being tied to aerial, ground, or marine platforms. It frames the problem around a universal planner for complex, unstructured environments, aiming to make mapping, monitoring, and inspection systems more scalable across heterogeneous robotic deployments.

extra.comment: The code for this paper is open-sourced and released at: https://github.com/ntnu-arl/gbplanner_ros/tree/gbplanner3
extra.full_text: Autonomous robotic systems are increasingly deployed for mapping, monitoring, and inspection in complex and unstructured environments. However, most existing path planning approaches remain domain-specific (i.e., either on air, land, or sea), limiting their scalability and cross-platform applicability.

title: AMP2026: A Multi-Platform Marine Robotics Dataset for Tracking and Mapping
summary: AMP2026 is a marine robotics dataset aimed at tracking and mapping across aerial, surface, and underwater platforms, where perception has to handle moving water, poor visibility, and cross-medium sensing. It is positioned as a resource for studying autonomy in realistic marine settings where robots must combine heterogeneous views rather than rely on a single clean sensing modality.

extra.full_text: Marine environments present significant challenges for perception and autonomy due to dynamic surfaces, limited visibility, and complex interactions between aerial, surface, and submerged sensing modalities.

title: GarmentPile++: Affordance-Driven Cluttered Garments Retrieval with Vision-Language Reasoning
summary: GarmentPile++ tackles garment manipulation in the messier setting of piled clothing, where a robot has to retrieve a target garment from clutter rather than handle a single isolated item. It frames retrieval around affordances and vision-language reasoning, aiming to identify how garments in a pile can be perceived and manipulated in a more realistic home-assistant robotics scenario.

extra.full_text: Garment manipulation has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in home-assistant robotics. However, the majority of existing garment manipulation works assume an initial state consisting of only one garment, while piled garments are far more common in real-world settings.

title: Structural Action Transformer for 3D Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Structural Action Transformer targets 3D dexterous manipulation with high-DoF robot hands, focusing on imitation learning across heterogeneous datasets where actions and embodiments do not line up cleanly. It frames cross-embodiment skill transfer as the central obstacle, suggesting a transformer-based structure for mapping manipulation behavior in a way that can generalize beyond a single hand or dataset.

extra.full_text: Achieving human-level dexterity in robots via imitation learning from heterogeneous datasets is hindered by the challenge of cross-embodiment skill transfer, particularly for high-DoF robotic hands.

title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use
summary: Reward Hacking Benchmark targets a failure mode in RL-trained tool-using LLM agents: agents that learn to exploit loopholes in their environment or tools rather than completing the intended task. It provides a way to measure these exploit behaviors in settings relevant to coding assistants, research agents, and autonomous systems, making reward hacking more concrete and testable instead of an anecdotal safety concern.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) trained language model agents with tool access are increasingly deployed in coding assistants, research tools, and autonomous systems.

title: Act-Observe-Rewrite: Multimodal Coding Agents as In-Context Policy Learners for Robot Manipulation
summary: Act-Observe-Rewrite treats a multimodal coding agent as an in-context policy learner for robot manipulation: it acts in the environment, observes failures, and rewrites its own control code without gradient updates, demonstrations, or hand-shaped rewards. The interesting claim is that a language model can improve physical manipulation through iterative self-debugging, with the paper focusing on the conditions under which that loop reliably works.

extra.full_text: Can a multimodal language model learn to manipulate physical objects by reasoning about its own failures-without gradient updates, demonstrations, or reward engineering? We argue the answer is yes, under conditions we characterise precisely.

title: How to Peel with a Knife: Aligning Fine-Grained Manipulation with Human Preference
summary: Aligning Fine-Grained Manipulation with Human Preference targets knife-based peeling, a dexterous contact-rich task where small differences in angle, force, and trajectory determine whether the robot removes peel cleanly or damages the object. The work frames fine manipulation around human preference, suggesting a training or alignment signal that captures the qualitative judgments people use for tasks like food preparation, surgery, and craftsmanship.

extra.comment: Project page can be found at https://toruowo.github.io/peel
extra.full_text: Many essential manipulation tasks - such as food preparation, surgery, and craftsmanship - remain intractable for autonomous robots.

title: Integrated Identification of Collaborative Robots for Robot Assisted 3D Printing Processes
summary: Integrated identification is applied to collaborative robots used in robot-assisted 3D printing, where accurate robot behavior matters for producing complex additive-manufactured parts. From the available text, the focus is on connecting industrial robotics with additive manufacturing for applications such as automotive component production, but the excerpt does not provide the specific identification method, experiments, or results.

extra.full_text: In recent years, the integration of additive manufacturing (AM) and industrial robotics has opened new perspectives for the production of complex components, particularly in the automotive sector.

title: Emerging trends in Cislunar Space for Lunar Science Exploration and Space Robotics aiding Human Spaceflight Safety
summary: An arXiv article frames cislunar space and the Moon as a testbed for lunar science, space robotics, and technologies needed for sustained human presence beyond Earth. From the available abstract text, it appears to survey emerging directions rather than present a specific robot-AI method or benchmark, with emphasis on how robotic systems can support exploration and improve human spaceflight safety.

extra.comment: Conference Proceedings of 2nd IAA Conference on AI in and for Space (2nd IAA SPAICE), Suzhou, China, 1-3 November, 2025
extra.full_text: In recent years, the Moon has emerged as an unparalleled extraterrestrial testbed for advancing cuttingedge technological and scientific research critical to enabling sustained human presence on its surface and supporting future interplanetary exploration.

title: Assistance Without Interruption: A Benchmark and LLM-based Framework for Non-Intrusive Human-Robot Assistance
summary: Assistance Without Interruption studies how robots can help people without disrupting their ongoing activity, introducing a benchmark and an LLM-based framework for deciding when and how to assist. From the provided text, the concrete technical details and results are not available, but the focus is clearly on non-intrusive coordination in human-robot interaction rather than simply maximizing task completion.

extra.full_text: Human-robot interaction (HRI) has long studied how agents and people coordinate to achieve shared goals.

title: What Does a Meow Mean? In Search of Intuitively Understandable Communication by a Nonverbal Companion Robot
summary: Explores how a nonverbal companion robot for older adults living alone might communicate through intuitively understandable cat-like vocalizations, centered on the question of what a meow can convey without speech. The motivating use case is practical eldercare support: reminders, activity prompts, and comfort delivered by a robot whose signals need to be quickly interpretable without adding cognitive burden.

extra.comment: To appear in the Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on Social Robotics (ICSR 2026)
extra.full_text: Older adults living alone have a number of challenges, and robots can help with some of them--by providing reminders, initiating activity, or offering comfort.

title: Learning Object-Centric Spatial Reasoning for Sequential Manipulation in Cluttered Environments
summary: Learning Object-Centric Spatial Reasoning targets sequential object retrieval in dense clutter by emphasizing modular, data-efficient reasoning over object-centered spatial relationships rather than relying solely on large end-to-end manipulation models. From the provided abstract fragment, the work is positioned around helping robots decide how to manipulate or remove obstructing objects in cluttered scenes, where the interesting part is the explicit spatial reasoning structure for long-horizon retrieval.

extra.full_text: Robotic manipulation in cluttered environments presents a critical challenge for automation. Recent large-scale, end-to-end models demonstrate impressive capabilities but often lack the data efficiency and modularity required for retrieving objects in dense clutter.

title: Instant and Reversible Adhesive-free Bonding Between Silicones and Glossy Papers for Soft Robotics
summary: Silicone soft actuators are bonded to glossy paper without adhesives by exploiting a reversible interface, replacing the usual permanent glues or embedded layers used to pair elastic silicone with stiff strain-limiting materials. The result is a fabrication route for fluidic soft robots that can be assembled instantly, adjusted, and taken apart, making actuator design less labor-intensive and easier to iterate.

extra.full_text: Integrating silicone with non-extensible materials is a common strategy used in the fabrication of fluidically-driven soft actuators, yet conventional approaches often rely on irreversible adhesives or embedding processes that are labor-intensive and difficult to modify.

title: Safe Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via Combined Model and Learning-based Control
summary: Safe Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via Combined Model and Learning-based Control tackles the coupled problem of making a legged robot walk and use its arm at the same time while staying safe and compliant during contact. The setup combines model-based control with learning-based components, aiming to coordinate whole-body motion rather than treating locomotion and manipulation as separate behaviors.

extra.comment: Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), June 2026, in Vienna, Austria
extra.full_text: Simultaneous locomotion and manipulation enables robots to interact with their environment beyond the constraints of a fixed base. However, coordinating legged locomotion with arm manipulation, while considering safety and compliance during contact interaction remains challenging.

title: Learning to Race in Minutes: Infoprop Dyna on the Mini Wheelbot
summary: Infoprop Dyna is applied to the Mini Wheelbot, a small racing robot with fast, nonlinear, unstable dynamics, to learn high-performance control quickly. The work focuses on using reinforcement learning to push the robot toward its performance limits in minutes rather than requiring long training runs, making it relevant for real robotic systems where data collection time and hardware wear matter.

extra.comment: Originally submitted to the German Robotics Conference, 2026
extra.full_text: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has the potential to enable robots with fast, nonlinear, and unstable dynamics to reach the limits of their performance.

title: Functional Force-Aware Retargeting from Virtual Human Demos to Soft Robot Policies
