summary: SoftAct teaches soft robot hands human-like manipulation skills by transferring virtual human demonstrations into robot policies while explicitly modeling contact forces. The interesting part is the force-aware retargeting step: instead of only matching kinematics, it reasons about how the hand should press, grasp, and interact with objects so the resulting soft-hand behaviors are more physically functional.

extra.full_text: We introduce SoftAct, a framework for teaching soft robot hands to perform human-like manipulation skills by explicitly reasoning about contact forces.

title: Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication for ISAC-Enabled Robotic Obstacle Avoidance
summary: Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication (GOSC) uses an ISAC-enabled base station to support UAV obstacle avoidance by transmitting only task-relevant sensing and command-and-control information. The setup frames communication around the robot’s navigation goal rather than raw data delivery, aiming to make wireless sensing and control more efficient for real-time avoidance decisions.

extra.full_text: We investigate an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC)-enabled BS for the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) obstacle avoidance task, and propose a goal-oriented semantic communication (GOSC) framework for the BS to transmit sensing and command and control (C&C) signals efficiently and effectively.

title: An Edge-Host-Cloud Architecture for Robot-Agnostic, Caregiver-in-the-Loop Personalized Cognitive Exercise: Multi-Site Deployment in Dementia Care
summary: Speaking Memories is a distributed robotic interaction platform for dementia care that supports personalized cognitive exercises while keeping caregivers involved in the loop. Its edge-host-cloud architecture is designed to be robot-agnostic and deployable across multiple care sites, so the same personalization and caregiver oversight layer can run over different robot embodiments.

extra.comment: 21 pages, 6 figures, 10 tables, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO)
extra.full_text: We present Speaking Memories, a distributed, stakeholder-in-the-loop robotic interaction platform for personalized cognitive exercise support.

title: Go Big or Go Home: Simulating Mobbing Behavior with Braitenbergian Robots
summary: Using Webots, the study simulates groups of Braitenbergian robots that switch between predator avoidance and cooperative mobbing behavior. The interesting part is the minimal-agent framing: simple sensor-driven robots collectively reproduce an antipredator strategy where individuals harass or attack a predator to reduce risk, offering a compact simulation model for studying emergent defensive coordination.

extra.comment: This work was completed in 2019 as a final project for a graduate course at the University of Waterloo, titled: ECE 750 - Artificial Life: Embodied Intelligence
extra.full_text: We used the Webots robotics simulation platform to simulate a dyadic avoiding and mobbing predator behavior in a group of Braitenbergian robots. Mobbing is an antipredator adaptation used by some animals in which the individuals cooperatively attack or harass a predator to protect themselves.

title: Task-Conditioned Uncertainty Costmaps for Legged Locomotion
summary: Task-Conditioned Uncertainty Costmaps for Legged Locomotion appears to focus on helping legged robots reason about terrain in a way that depends on the locomotion task, rather than treating traversability as a fixed property of the ground. From the provided text, the core setting is dynamic, multicontact locomotion, where feasibility depends on how the robot can make and sustain contacts with terrain while moving.

extra.full_text: Legged robots maintain dynamic feasibility through multicontact interactions with terrain.

title: OmniRobotHome: A Multi-Camera Platform for Real-Time Multiadic Human-Robot Interaction
summary: OmniRobotHome is a multi-camera platform aimed at studying real-time human-robot collaboration in home-like settings where several people and robots act at once rather than taking turns. It targets tightly coupled, interleaved subtasks in shared spaces, making it useful for probing the perception, coordination, and timing problems that dyadic or sequential human-robot interaction setups tend to miss.

extra.full_text: Human-robot collaboration has been studied primarily in dyadic or sequential settings. However, real homes require multiadic collaboration, where multiple humans and robots share a workspace, acting concurrently on interleaved subtasks with tight spatial and temporal coupling.

title: Being-H0.7: A Latent World-Action Model from Egocentric Videos
summary: Being-H0.7 targets the shortcut-learning problem in visual-language-action robot policies by learning a latent world-action model from egocentric video, so the representation is shaped around dynamics, contact, and task progress rather than only sparse action labels. From the provided text, the concrete result details are not given, but the interesting part is the attempt to use first-person video as a source of structured action-relevant world modeling for generalist robot control.

extra.full_text: Visual-Language-Action models (VLAs) have advanced generalist robot control by mapping multimodal observations and language instructions directly to actions, but sparse action supervision often encourages shortcut mappings rather than representations of dynamics, contact, and task progress.

title: Learning Semantic Priorities for Autonomous Target Search
summary: Learning Semantic Priorities for Autonomous Target Search addresses robotic search in unfamiliar environments by using semantic cues to guide where a target is likely to be, rather than depending on large training sets from similar domains. The interesting angle is adaptability: it aims to make search-and-rescue robots reason over object or scene semantics in new spaces, improving search efficiency when prior domain-specific data is limited.

extra.full_text: The use of semantic features can improve the efficiency of target search in unknown environments for robotic search and rescue missions. Current target search methods rely on training with large datasets of similar domains, which limits the adaptability to diverse environments.

title: A Novel Camera-to-Robot Calibration Method for Vision-Based Floor Measurements
summary: A hand-eye calibration method is introduced for mobile robots whose cameras look down at the floor, targeting vision-based floor measurement rather than general scene perception. It uses laser-tracker-style precise localization as part of the calibration setup, aiming to make the camera-to-robot transform accurate enough for ground-observing measurement tasks that are uncommon in typical mobile robot camera pipelines.

extra.comment: 8 pages; accepted for publication in the ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
extra.full_text: A novel hand-eye calibration method for ground-observing mobile robots is proposed. While cameras on mobile robots are common, they are rarely used for ground-observing measurement tasks. Laser trackers are increasingly used in robotics for precise localization.

title: SASI: Leveraging Sub-Action Semantics for Robust Early Action Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
summary: SASI targets early action recognition for human-robot interaction by using sub-action semantics, aiming to infer what a person is doing before the full action has unfolded. The available text only states the motivation and title-level mechanism, so the concrete benchmarks, architecture details, and results are not specified here.

extra.full_text: Understanding human actions is critical for advancing behavior analysis in human-robot interaction.

title: MRReP: Mixed Reality-based Hand-drawn Reference Path Editing Interface for Mobile Robot Navigation
summary: MRReP lets a user edit a mobile robot’s navigation path in mixed reality by hand-drawing reference paths that encode human spatial preferences, such as leaving comfortable clearance or avoiding pedestrian flow. It targets the gap between autonomous planning and the kinds of context-sensitive indoor routes people often want robots to follow in shared spaces.

extra.full_text: Autonomous mobile robots operating in human-shared indoor environments often require paths that reflect human spatial intentions, such as avoiding interference with pedestrian flow or maintaining comfortable clearance.

title: Global Sampling-Based Trajectory Optimization for Contact-Rich Manipulation via KernelSOS
summary: KernelSOS tackles contact-rich manipulation by casting long-horizon hybrid contact planning as a global sampling-based trajectory optimization problem. The setup targets cases where many contact mode changes and high-dimensional robot dynamics make local optimization brittle, using kernel sum-of-squares structure to search more broadly over feasible manipulation trajectories.

extra.full_text: Contact-rich manipulation is challenging due to its high dimensionality, the requirement for long time horizons, and the presence of hybrid contact dynamics.

title: See Something, Say Something: Context-Criticality-Aware Mobile Robot Communication for Hazard Mitigations
summary: Autonomous mobile robots need to decide not just whether they have seen a hazard, but how urgently and explicitly to communicate it, especially when nearby humans may need to react quickly. The paper frames robot communication around context criticality, aiming to make hazard reports sensitive to the severity and immediacy of the situation rather than treating every detection as the same kind of message.

extra.full_text: The proverb ``see something, say something'' captures a core responsibility of autonomous mobile robots in safety-critical situations: when they detect a hazard, they must communicate--and do so quickly.

title: Persona-Based Process Design for Assistive Human-Robot Workplaces for Persons with Disabilities
summary: Human-robot workplace systems for people with disabilities are often built around one person’s needs, which makes them hard to reuse or scale. This paper argues for persona-based process design: abstracting from individual accommodations into representative user profiles so assistive robot workflows can be designed for broader groups while still reflecting concrete disability-related needs.

extra.comment: Accepted at IEEE International Conference on Human-Machine Systems (ICHMS), Singapore, 2026
extra.full_text: Human-robot interaction is emerging as an important paradigm for integrating persons with disabilities into the workplace. While these systems can enable individuals to work, their design is mostly personalized, hindering widespread use beyond the individual user.

title: Reference-Augmented Learning for Precise Tracking Policy of Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
summary: Reference-Augmented Learning targets precise tracking control for tendon-driven continuum robots, whose hysteresis, path dependence, and non-Markovian dynamics make standard policy learning difficult. From the available text, the core idea is to augment the learned tracking policy with reference information so the controller can better account for the robot’s nonlinear motion history, but no benchmark setup or quantitative result is provided here.

extra.full_text: Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots (TDCRs) pose significant control challenges due to their highly nonlinear, path-dependent dynamics and non-Markovian characteristics.

title: Learning-Based Dynamics Modeling and Robust Control for Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
summary: Tendon-driven continuum robots are hard to model and control because effects like frictional hysteresis and compliant transmission make their dynamics strongly nonlinear. The work builds a differentiable learning framework that pairs high-fidelity learned dynamics with a robust neural controller, aiming to make these flexible tendon-actuated systems more predictable and controllable under real mechanical uncertainty.

extra.full_text: Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots (TDCRs) pose significant modeling and control challenges due to complex nonlinearities, such as frictional hysteresis and transmission compliance. This paper proposes a differentiable learning framework that integrates high-fidelity dynamics modeling with robust neural control.

title: Bridging the Indoor-Outdoor Gap: Cross-Technology Ranging for Seamless Robot Navigation
summary: Mobile robots moving across indoor and outdoor spaces need positioning that does not break when GPS fades or infrastructure changes, and this paper targets that handoff through cross-technology ranging. From the provided text, the work appears to focus on maintaining seamless navigation by bridging otherwise separate indoor and outdoor localization signals, though no specific mechanism, experiment, or result is given here.

extra.full_text: Mobile robots that move between outdoor and indoor environments still struggle with consistent positioning.

title: Multi-Periodogram Velocity Estimation with Irregular Reference Signals for Robot-Aided ISAC
summary: Multi-Periodogram Velocity Estimation estimates robot or target velocity in robot-aided ISAC settings where sensing nodes cannot rely on regularly spaced pilots and must instead reuse irregular 5G/6G reference signals. It adapts periodogram-based velocity estimation to those uneven reference-signal timings, aiming to make opportunistic communication waveforms usable for sensing without dedicated radar transmissions.

extra.full_text: This paper addresses velocity estimation within robot-aided integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), where mobile robots act as sensing nodes but can only opportunistically reuse irregular 5G/6G reference signals (RSs).

title: Tendon-Actuated Robots with a Tapered, Flexible Polymer Backbone: Design, Fabrication, and Modeling
summary: A 3D-printed continuum robot uses tendon actuation around a tapered thermoplastic polyurethane backbone, giving the structure both flexibility and a built-in change in stiffness along its length. The paper ties together the mechanical design, fabrication process, and modeling needed to predict how this soft, tapered backbone bends under tendon loads.

extra.full_text: This paper presents the design, modeling, and fabrication of 3D-printed, tendon-actuated continuum robots featuring a flexible, tapered backbone constructed from thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU).

title: Complementarity by Construction: A Lie-Group Approach to Solving Quadratic Programs with Linear Complementarity Constraints
summary: Complementarity by Construction tackles robotics problems where smooth dynamics meet discrete contact switches by formulating quadratic programs with linear complementarity constraints through a Lie-group lens. The idea is to encode complementarity directly in the optimization geometry, so contact-style constraints are satisfied by construction rather than handled as awkward external conditions.

extra.full_text: Many problems in robotics require reasoning over a mix of continuous dynamics and discrete events, such as making and breaking contact in manipulation and locomotion.

title: Sliding Mode Control for Safe Trajectory Tracking with Moving Obstacles Avoidance: Experimental Validation on Planar Robots
summary: Sliding mode control is used as a single robust controller for mobile robots that need to track planned trajectories while avoiding moving obstacles. The paper frames trajectory following and obstacle avoidance within one control setup and reports experimental validation on planar robots, emphasizing practical safe tracking rather than only simulation.

extra.full_text: This paper presents a unified control framework for robust trajectory tracking and moving obstacle avoidance applicable to a broad class of mobile robots.

title: SCRAMPPI: Efficient Contingency Planning for Mobile Robot Navigation via Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
summary: SCRAMPPI uses Hamilton-Jacobi reachability to give a mobile robot an efficient contingency plan: while it pursues a nominal navigation objective, it can compute when and how to fall back to a safe set if the nominal plan becomes risky. The interesting angle is the explicit coupling of cost-driven navigation with backup planning, targeting the common failure mode where optimizing the main task leaves the robot without a viable escape route.

extra.full_text: Autonomous robots commonly aim to complete a nominal behavior while minimizing a cost; this leaves them vulnerable to failure or unplanned scenarios, where a backup or contingency plan to a safe set is needed to avoid a total mission failure.

title: Addressing Ambiguity in Imitation Learning through Product of Experts based Negative Feedback
summary: Imitation learning is framed here as a way to make robot programming less dependent on hand-engineered controllers by learning from human demonstrations, with the paper focusing on ambiguity that arises when demonstrations alone do not specify the intended behavior cleanly. The approach uses Product of Experts based negative feedback, suggesting a mechanism for ruling out undesired interpretations of a task rather than only reinforcing demonstrated behavior.

extra.full_text: Programming robots to perform complex tasks is often difficult and time consuming, requiring expert knowledge and skills in robot software and sometimes hardware. Imitation learning is a method for training robots to perform tasks by leveraging human expertise through demonstrations.

title: Generalizable task-oriented object grasping through LLM-guided ontology and similarity-based planning
summary: Task-oriented object grasping is framed as a planning problem where an LLM helps build an ontology of object parts and task-relevant grasp regions, then uses similarity-based reasoning to transfer grasp choices to new objects. The interesting part is the emphasis on generalization: instead of only detecting an object and grasping it anywhere stable, the system tries to identify which part should be held for a manipulation task and choose a robust contact area accordingly.

extra.comment: Accepted by Robotics and Autonomous Systems
extra.full_text: Task-oriented grasping (TOG) is more challenging than simple object grasping because it requires precise identification of object parts and careful selection of grasping areas to ensure effective and robust manipulation.

title: DRUM: Diffusion-based Raydrop-aware Unpaired Mapping for Sim2Real LiDAR Segmentation
summary: DRUM targets sim-to-real LiDAR semantic segmentation by using diffusion-based unpaired mapping with explicit awareness of raydrop, the missing-return patterns that make simulated point clouds differ from real scans. The aim is to reduce reliance on costly real-world point-cloud annotations by making synthetic LiDAR data better match real sensor behavior for downstream segmentation.

extra.full_text: LiDAR-based semantic segmentation is a key component for autonomous mobile robots, yet large-scale annotation of LiDAR point clouds is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming.

title: DART: Learning-Enhanced Model Predictive Control for Dual-Arm Non-Prehensile Manipulation
summary: DART tackles dual-arm tray manipulation where the robot must move objects without grasping them, combining model predictive control with learned components to handle the unstable, contact-rich dynamics. The setup targets waiter-like behavior: coordinating two arms to control a tray so objects can be repositioned or transported despite the difficulty of non-prehensile interaction.

extra.full_text: What appears effortless to a human waiter remains a major challenge for robots. Manipulating objects nonprehensilely on a tray is inherently difficult, and the complexity is amplified in dual-arm settings.

title: Learning from Demonstration with Failure Awareness for Safe Robot Navigation
summary: Learning from Demonstration with Failure Awareness targets a common blind spot in robot navigation: demonstrations mostly show what succeeds, leaving the policy poorly informed about unsafe or unrecoverable states. It frames navigation learning around explicit awareness of failure cases, so the robot can use demonstrations while also reasoning about where imitation alone may lead it into danger.

extra.full_text: Learning from demonstration is widely used for robot navigation, yet it suffers from a fundamental limitation: demonstrations consist predominantly of successful behaviors and provide limited coverage of unsafe states.

title: Adaptive vs. Static Robot-to-Human Handover: A Study on Orientation and Approach Direction
summary: Robot-to-human handover policies are compared across static strategies and adaptive approaches that account for how the recipient is likely to grasp the object, especially its orientation and the robot’s approach direction. The study targets the common mismatch where robots deliver objects in a convenient pose for themselves, forcing humans to compensate, and examines whether adapting handover geometry can make the exchange more natural for the person.

extra.full_text: Robot-to-human handovers often rely on static, open-loop strategies (or, at best, approaches that adapt only the position), which generally do not consider how the object will be grasped by the human, thus requiring the user to adapt.

title: Characterizing pitch and roll torque coupling in insect-sized flapping-wing robots using a microfabricated gimbal
summary: Sub-gram flapping-wing insect robots are hard to model because their wing mechanics and unsteady aerodynamics interact in ways that are difficult to measure at this scale. The paper uses a microfabricated gimbal to characterize how pitch and roll torques couple during flapping, giving a more direct experimental handle on rotational dynamics that are usually inferred indirectly or simplified away.

extra.comment: Submitted for journal publication in Mechatronics and conference presentation at IFAC World Congress 2026. 9 pages, 11 figures
extra.full_text: Sub-gram flapping-wing flying insect robots (FIRs) are challenging to model because of mechanical complexity in their wings, unsteady aerodynamic flow, and the difficulty of making precise measurements at a small scale.

title: Dynamic Coupling and Indirect Control of Jointed Robots Rolling Atop A Moving Platform
summary: An asymmetric two-link robot on freely pivoting, laterally constrained wheels can move forward across a flat platform using only internal actuation at its joint. The mechanism is a dynamic coupling between the robot’s shape change, rolling constraints, and the moving support surface, showing how indirect control can generate net momentum without wheel torques or lateral slip.

extra.full_text: An asymmetric two-link robot supported atop a flat platform by wheels that roll and pivot freely, but do not slip laterally, will develop forward momentum if the joint between the links is actuated internally.

title: Effects of Swarm Size Variability on Operator Workload
summary: Human-swarm operators can be pushed into abrupt workload shifts when robots fail, join, or get redeployed mid-mission, so this study focuses on swarm size variability rather than assuming a fixed team size. It frames dynamic swarm membership as a workload-management problem for human-swarm teaming, asking how changes in the number of robots affect an operator’s ability to stay effective without becoming overloaded.

extra.full_text: Real-world deployments of human--swarm teams depend on balancing operator workload to leverage human strengths without inducing overload. A key challenge is that swarm size is often dynamic: robots may join or leave the mission due to failures or redeployment, causing abrupt workload fluctuations.

title: MOMO: A framework for seamless physical, verbal, and graphical robot skill learning and adaptation
summary: MOMO lets non-expert users teach and adapt industrial robot skills through a mix of physical demonstration, verbal instruction, and graphical interaction, matching the modality to the kind of change the task needs. The framing is interesting because it treats robot skill learning as an interactive, multimodal adaptation problem rather than forcing every correction through a single interface.

extra.full_text: Industrial robot applications require increasingly flexible systems that non-expert users can easily adapt for varying tasks and environments. However, different adaptations benefit from different interaction modalities.

title: ZipFold: Modular Actuators for Scaleable Adaptive Robots
summary: ZipFold introduces modular actuators intended to let robots reconfigure their shape, size, and mechanical properties as tasks or environments change. From the provided text, the emphasis is on scalable adaptive robot hardware: building robot bodies from actuator modules rather than treating morphology as fixed.

extra.full_text: There is a growing need for robots that can change their shape, size and mechanical properties to adapt to evolving tasks and environments.

title: Wake Up to the Past: Using Memory to Model Fluid Wake Effects on Robots
summary: Autonomous aerial and aquatic robots can disturb each other through the wakes they leave in the surrounding fluid, making nearby agents harder to model and control. The paper frames these wake interactions as a memory problem, using past robot motion or disturbance history to predict fluid wake effects on neighboring robots rather than treating them as instantaneous forces.

extra.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to IROS 2026. Project website: https://sites.google.com/view/wake-up-to-the-past
extra.full_text: Autonomous aerial and aquatic robots that attain mobility by perturbing their medium, such as multicopters and torpedoes, produce wake effects that act as disturbances for adjacent robots.

title: UniDex: A Robot Foundation Suite for Universal Dexterous Hand Control from Egocentric Human Videos
summary: UniDex targets universal dexterous hand control by trying to learn from egocentric human videos instead of expensive robot teleoperation data. It is positioned as a foundation suite for transferring human hand manipulation behavior across heterogeneous robotic hand embodiments, addressing the embodiment mismatch and high-dimensional control problems that make dexterous manipulation hard to scale.

extra.full_text: Dexterous manipulation remains challenging due to the cost of collecting real-robot teleoperation data, the heterogeneity of hand embodiments, and the high dimensionality of control.

title: VTouch++: A Multimodal Dataset with Vision-Based Tactile Enhancement for Bimanual Manipulation
summary: VTouch++ is an arXiv paper introducing a multimodal dataset for bimanual manipulation, aimed at contact-rich tasks where vision alone misses important physical interaction cues. It focuses on enriching manipulation data with vision-based tactile signals and systematic task organization, addressing a gap in scale and interaction detail for embodied AI research.

extra.full_text: Embodied intelligence has advanced rapidly in recent years; however, bimanual manipulation-especially in contact-rich tasks remains challenging. This is largely due to the lack of datasets with rich physical interaction signals, systematic task organization, and sufficient scale.

title: Multi-Cycle Spatio-Temporal Adaptation in Human-Robot Teaming
summary: Multi-Cycle Spatio-Temporal Adaptation targets human-robot teaming by repeatedly updating joint plans as it learns an individual human partner’s capabilities and preferences over time. The work is interesting because it treats collaboration as an adaptive planning problem rather than relying on a fixed human model, aiming to make robot behavior better aligned with the specific person and workspace dynamics.

extra.full_text: Effective human-robot teaming is crucial for the practical deployment of robots in human workspaces. However, optimizing joint human-robot plans remains a challenge due to the difficulty of modeling individualized human capabilities and preferences.

title: Warmth and Competence in the Swarm: Designing Effective Human-Robot Teams
summary: Investigates how people perceive robot swarms through the social dimensions of warmth and competence, framing these perceptions as a design factor for human-robot teaming. The work is aimed at helping designers tune group robot behavior so multi-robot systems are not just effective, but also legible and acceptable to human collaborators.

extra.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures, camera-ready version for ANTS 2026
extra.full_text: As groups of robots increasingly collaborate with humans, understanding how humans perceive them is critical for designing effective human-robot teams.

title: HALO: Hybrid Auto-encoded Locomotion with Learned Latent Dynamics, Poincaré Maps, and Regions of Attraction
summary: HALO targets reduced-order modeling for legged robots by learning a latent representation of hybrid locomotion dynamics with autoencoding, then using learned latent dynamics, Poincaré maps, and regions of attraction for analysis and control. The interesting part is that it treats the discontinuities and mode switches of walking robots directly, aiming to make high-dimensional locomotion systems amenable to the kinds of stability and control tools that are usually easier to apply to simpler dynamical models.

extra.full_text: Reduced-order models are powerful for analyzing and controlling high-dimensional dynamical systems. Yet constructing these models for complex hybrid systems such as legged robots remains challenging.

title: Diffusion Sequence Models for Generative In-Context Meta-Learning of Robot Dynamics
summary: Diffusion Sequence Models target robot dynamics modeling under distribution shifts and tight real-time control loops, using diffusion-style sequence generation for in-context meta-learning. From the provided text, the work appears focused on quickly adapting dynamics predictions from context rather than retraining, but no benchmark, mechanism details, or results are given beyond the problem framing.

extra.comment: Angelo Moroncelli, Matteo Rufolo and Gunes Cagin Aydin contributed equally to this work
extra.full_text: Accurate modeling of robot dynamics is essential for model-based control, yet remains challenging under distributional shifts and real-time constraints.

title: Optimal control of differentially flat underactuated planar robots in the perspective of oscillation mitigation
summary: Differential flatness is used as a control lens for underactuated planar robots whose mass distribution makes their otherwise underactuated dynamics tractable. The paper frames optimal control around mitigating oscillations, aiming to generate motions that respect the flatness structure while reducing residual vibration in these lightly actuated systems.

extra.full_text: Underactuated robots are characterized by a larger number of degrees of freedom than actuators and if they are designed with a specific mass distribution, they can be controlled by means of differential flatness theory.

title: SpaceDex: Generalizable Dexterous Grasping in Tiered Workspaces
summary: SpaceDex tackles dexterous grasping in tiered workspaces, where shelves and stacked levels introduce occlusion, tight clearances, and height-specific constraints that make high-DoF hand control harder than open-tabletop grasping. From the provided text, the emphasis is on generalizing grasp policies to these constrained 3D layouts rather than assuming objects are fully visible and easy to approach.

extra.full_text: Generalizable grasping with high-degree-of-freedom (DoF) dexterous hands remains challenging in tiered workspaces, where occlusion, narrow clearances, and height-dependent constraints are substantially stronger than in open tabletop scenes.

title: A Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability-Guided Search Framework for Efficient and Safe Indoor Planar Robot Navigation
summary: Hamilton-Jacobi reachability is used to guide graph search for indoor planar robot navigation, aiming to preserve the safety guarantees of reachability analysis while making planning more efficient in complex or changing environments. The idea is to fold reachability-derived safety information into an admissible-heuristic search process, so the planner can reach goals without exhaustively exploring unsafe or dynamically infeasible regions.

extra.full_text: Autonomous navigation requires planning to reach a goal safely and efficiently in complex and potentially dynamic environments. Graph search-based algorithms are widely adopted due to their generality and theoretical guarantees when equipped with admissible heuristics.

title: Planning Smooth and Safe Control Laws for a Unicycle Robot Among Obstacles
summary: Plans smooth, input-limited feedback control laws for a unicycle point robot navigating to a goal among obstacles. The setup emphasizes safety from almost any admissible initial state, combining goal-reaching behavior with obstacle avoidance under realistic control constraints.

extra.comment: This work has been accepted for publication in the 2026 European Control Conference (ECC)
extra.full_text: This paper presents a framework for safe navigation of a unicycle point robot to a goal position in an environment populated with obstacles from almost any admissible state, considering input limits.

title: Learning Sim-Grounded Policies for Bimanual Rope Manipulation from Human Teleoperation Data
summary: Human teleoperation data is used to train bimanual rope-untangling policies, with the central comparison being whether wrist-camera RGB observations are enough or whether a physics-grounded rope state is a better learning signal. Using Action Chunking with Transformers on the same demonstrations, the state policy reconstructs a 3D particle representation from multi-view fusion and rolls it forward in an XPBD simulator, then predicts actions from that simulated DLO state. On an unseen rope configuration, this sim-grounded state policy reduces L1 error by 30.8% for the initial grasp-and-pull action, suggesting that much of the visual policy’s failure comes from poor observability rather than architecture or dataset size.

extra.comment: Accepted to the Beyond Teleoperation Workshop at ICRA 2026, 5 pages, 2 figures
extra.full_text: Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) such as ropes and cables are widely encountered in both household and industrial applications, yet remain challenging to manipulate due to their infinite-dimensional configuration space and frequent self-occlusion. Imitation learning from teleoperation offers a practical path to bimanual DLO manipulation, but its scalability is limited by human effort, making the choice of observation space critical for generalization from small datasets. In this study, we investigate whether the lack of generalization in egocentric visual policies for the knot-untangling task stems from the observation space itself, rather than from the policy architecture or data scale. We compare two Action Chunking with Transformers policies trained on the same bimanual teleoperation data: a vision-based policy conditioned on two egocentric RGB streams from wrist-mounted cameras, and a state-based policy conditioned on the DLO's 3D particle state, extracted from an initial observation via multi-view fusion and evolved in a particle-based eXtended Position-Based Dynamics simulation. Evaluated open-loop on an unseen rope configuration, the state-based policy outperforms its visual counterpart with a 30.8% reduction in L1 error when predicting the initial grasp-and-pull action, quantifying the observability gap between pixels and physics-consistent state, and pointing toward more data-efficient robot learning for the DLO manipulation task from limited human demonstrations.

title: Mind Dreamer: Untethering Imagination via Active Latent Intervention on Latent Manifolds
summary: Mind Dreamer extends model-based RL by letting the agent “dream” from generated latent states instead of only from states it has actually visited, using an adversarial generator to jump to plausible but underexplored regions of the world model’s manifold. Its Relay Value and Relay Uncertainty functions propagate reward and epistemic value across these discontinuous imagined anchors, with a formal quadratic uncertainty discount. On DeepMind Control Suite it reports a 1.67x average speedup over DreamerV3, rising to 8.8x on sparse-reward tasks.

extra.full_text: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) leverages latent imagination for sample efficiency, yet remains constrained by Historical Tethering: imagination is typically initialized from observed states. This creates a learning asymmetry, where the world model's manifold discovery outpaces the policy's sparse-reward optimization. We propose Mind Dreamer (MD), a framework that operationalizes Active Latent Intervention (ALI) to transcend Markovian continuity. MD reformulates discovery as the minimization of a global Relay Manifold Expected Free Energy (R-EFE); by sampling initial states from a learned generator $s_0 \sim p_{gen}(\cdot)$ rather than the historical buffer, MD utilizes an adversarial generator to synthesize non-continuous latent jumps to epistemic blind spots that are physically plausible yet cognitively challenging. To resolve the credit assignment paradox across these spatial ruptures, we derive the Relay Value Function (RVF) and Relay Uncertainty Function (RUF). These potentials treat synthesized anchors as counterfactual intermediary states, propagating pragmatic and epistemic value through a principled Bellman-style formulation. Notably, we prove that uncertainty propagation across discontinuities necessitates a quadratic discount $γ^2$, establishing a formal epistemic horizon. Theoretically, MD approximates a variance-minimizing importance sampler that expands the manifold's spectral gap, reducing the hitting time to critical bottleneck states. Empirically, MD achieves a 1.67$\times$ average speedup over DreamerV3 on DeepMind Control Suite, reaching 8.8$\times$ in sparse-reward tasks.

title: WorldVLN: Autoregressive World Action Model for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
summary: WorldVLN treats aerial vision-language navigation as short-horizon world-state prediction coupled directly to waypoint selection, using a latent autoregressive video backbone that updates its context after each executed action from the drone’s new observations. It is trained first to align the video prior with instruction-conditioned navigation dynamics, then with Action-aware GRPO to optimize decisions by rollout consequences. On indoor and outdoor VLN benchmarks it reports 12%+ success-rate gains over Vision-Language-Action baselines, with zero-shot transfer to real drone deployment.

extra.full_text: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow natural-language instructions through closed-loop perception and action in 3D environments. We argue that aerial VLN can be formulated as a prediction-driven world-action problem: the agent should anticipate latent world evolution and act according to the predicted consequences. To this end, we propose WorldVLN, the first autoregressive world action model for aerial VLN. Unlike full-sequence video-generation world models that generate an entire visual clip, WorldVLN adapts a latent autoregressive video backbone to predict short-horizon world-state transitions and directly decodes them into executable waypoint actions. After each action segment is executed, newly received observations are encoded back into the autoregressive context, enabling closed-loop world-action prediction. We further introduce a two-stage training framework that first grounds the video prior in instruction-conditioned navigation dynamics and then develops Action-aware GRPO, the first reinforcement learning method tailored to autoregressive WAMs, to optimize waypoint decisions through their downstream rollout consequences. On public outdoor and indoor benchmarks, WorldVLN consistently outperforms existing Vision-Language-Action baselines with 12\%+ success-rate gains and larger advantages on challenging cases. It further transfers zero-shot to real drone deployment, suggesting that the proposed WorldVLN offers a promising route for spatial action tasks. Demos and code are available at https://embodiedcity.github.io/WorldVLN/.

title: RLWRLD unveils ‘dexterity-first’ foundation model for humanoid robots
summary: RLWRLD unveiled RLDX-1, a dexterity-first robotics foundation model for humanoid manipulation. It targets contact-rich tasks like grasping, pouring, and tool use; no code, benchmark, or release details are mentioned.

extra.full_text: RLWRLD, a physical AI company developing robotics foundation models for dexterous manipulation, unveiled RLDX-1 at “Dexterity Night in SF”, introducing a model designed to help humanoid robots perform contact-rich tasks such as grasping, pouring and tool use.

title: Arrive AI using Nvidia Isaac Sim and Blackwell GPUs to develop autonomous drone delivery network
summary: Arrive AI is using Nvidia Isaac Sim and Blackwell-powered GPU workstations to speed development of its autonomous drone delivery network. The update matters mainly as an infrastructure and simulation play: the company is leaning on high-fidelity robotics simulation and newer GPU hardware to train, test, and iterate delivery autonomy before deploying it in the field.

extra.full_text: Arrive AI, an autonomous delivery infrastructure company, says it is accelerating its artificial intelligence and robotics development using Nvidia Isaac Sim and high-performance GPU workstations powered by Nvidia Blackwell architecture.

title: Richtech Robotics now available in Microsoft Marketplace
summary: Richtech Robotics has listed its AI-driven service robot fleet and associated data services on Microsoft Marketplace, making them easier for Azure customers to discover, procure, and deploy through Microsoft’s cloud ecosystem. The move matters less as a technical robotics advance than as a distribution and integration step: it positions Richtech’s robots as cloud-connected enterprise services alongside other Azure-compatible applications.

extra.full_text: Richtech Robotics, a Nevada-based provider of AI-driven service robots, has announced the availability of its fleet of robotic solutions and data services in the Microsoft Marketplace, an online store providing applications and services for use on Azure.

title: Deep Robotics launches new wheeled-legged robot for industrial inspection and emergency response
summary: Deep Robotics unveiled the Lynx M20S, a new industry-grade wheeled-legged robot aimed at industrial inspection and emergency response. The launch matters because it points to continued movement toward hybrid mobility platforms that can combine wheeled efficiency with legged traversal for difficult, unstructured work sites.

extra.full_text: Deep Robotics has unveiled its next-generation industry-grade wheeled-legged robot, the Lynx M20S.

title: Tungsten Carbide Manufacturing and the Future of Next-Generation Robotics
summary: The article argues that next-generation robotics depends not only on AI, sensors, and automation software, but also on advances in the physical materials used to build robots. It points to tungsten carbide manufacturing as a foundational enabler for more durable, precise robotic components, shifting attention from intelligence alone to the hardware that lets robots operate reliably in demanding environments.

extra.full_text: Robotics is often discussed through software, sensors, artificial intelligence, and automation platforms. Those areas deserve attention, but they are not the whole story.

title: ShengShu unveils world action model to offer ‘infinite possibilities’ for robotic intelligence
summary: ShengShu Technology introduced Motubrain, a unified world action model meant to serve as a general robotic brain for operating in the physical world. The company frames it as a replacement for stacks of task-specific robotics systems, with the promise that one model could support many forms of embodied intelligence rather than being retrained or rebuilt around each individual task.

extra.full_text: ShengShu Technology has unveiled Motubrain, a world action model that replaces multiple task-specific systems with a single, unified model that functions as a robotic brain for the physical world. ShenShu describes Motubrain as one brain that offers infinite possibilities for robotic intelligence.

title: Achieving Dataset Parity to Close the Robotics Training Gap
summary: A news item frames “dataset parity” as the next bottleneck in robotics training, contrasting early fixed-task industrial robots like Unimate with 2026 systems such as Unitree GD01 that need data for adaptive mobility, AI decision-making, and terrain navigation. The emphasis is that closing the robotics training gap depends less on hardware alone and more on giving embodied models training datasets rich enough to support robust behavior outside repetitive factory settings.

extra.full_text: It was in 1954 when the world witnessed its first real industrial robot, Unimate, a machine built to perform repetitive factory operations. Fast forward to 2026: today robots like Unitree GD01 are being trained to learn adaptive mobility, AI decision-making, and terrain navigation.

title: Rivian spinoff Mind Robotics raises another $400M
summary: Mind Robotics, the Rivian spinoff first disclosed in late 2025, has raised another $400 million, bringing its total funding to more than $1 billion. The news signals unusually large investor backing for a young robotics-AI company, though the provided text does not give details on its technical approach, products, or deployment plans.

extra.full_text: Mind Robotics, which was first revealed in late 2025, has now raised more than $1 billion to date.

title: NVIDIA, Ineffable Intelligence Team Up to Build the Future of Reinforcement Learning Infrastructure
summary: NVIDIA is partnering with Ineffable Intelligence to build infrastructure for reinforcement-learning agents, aiming to make trial-and-error learning a more practical way to turn large-scale compute into new capabilities. The announcement is thin on implementation details or results, but it signals investment in the tooling layer needed to train and run agents that learn from interaction rather than static datasets.

extra.full_text: Reinforcement-learning agents — AI systems that learn by trial and error — can convert computation into new knowledge.

title: Khosla-backed robotics startup Genesis AI has gone full stack, demo shows
summary: Genesis AI has unveiled GENE-26.5, its first robotics foundation model, after raising a $105 million seed round backed by Khosla. The accompanying demo shows robotic hands carrying out complex manipulation tasks, signaling that the company is pursuing a full-stack path from model development to embodied robotic control rather than releasing only software abstractions.

extra.full_text: Genesis AI, a startup that raised a $105 million seed round to build foundational AI for robotics, has unveiled its first model, GENE-26.5, but also a demo showcasing a set of robotic hands performing complex tasks.

title: Rocsys raises $13 million and unveils multi-bay hands-free charging solution for robotaxis
summary: Rocsys raised $13 million and introduced the Rocsys M1, a hands-free charging system designed to serve multiple robotaxi bays in depot operations. The system targets a practical bottleneck for autonomous EV fleets: keeping vehicles charged without human plug-in labor, which becomes increasingly important as robotaxi depots scale beyond single-bay automation.

extra.full_text: Rocsys, a developer of hands-free depot solutions for autonomous electric vehicles, has launched the Rocsys M1 – which the company says is “the world’s first hands-free charging solution capable of serving multiple bays in robotaxi operations”.

title: Fanuc strengthens Nvidia partnership for AI robot simulation and digital twins
summary: Fanuc is deepening its integration between Nvidia Isaac Sim and its RoboGuide robot simulation software, so users can operate Fanuc robot cells inside a virtual factory while keeping the simulation tied to a high-fidelity digital twin. The partnership matters because it brings Nvidia’s AI-focused robotics simulation stack closer to Fanuc’s industrial programming environment, making robot testing, validation, and deployment workflows more seamless before anything is run on physical hardware.

extra.full_text: Fanuc has further strengthened the integration between Nvidia’s open robot simulation reference framework Nvidia Isaac Sim and Fanuc’s robot simulation software RoboGuide, enabling intuitive operation within a virtual factory and realizing highly accurate, seamlessly integrated digital twins.

title: Epson Robots expands SCARA lineup with high-payload LS50C
summary: Epson Robots added the LS50C to its SCARA robot lineup, positioning it as the company’s largest-payload SCARA model. The point is a higher-payload arm that still targets compact, cost-conscious automation setups, giving manufacturers more headroom for heavier pick-and-place, assembly, or handling tasks without moving to a larger robot class.

extra.full_text: Epson Robots has expanded its SCARA lineup with the new LS50C. As Epson’s largest payload SCARA, the LS50C is designed to deliver powerful performance and flexibility in a compact, cost-effective form factor.

title: Korea’s biggest manufacturers back Config, the TSMC of robot data
summary: Config is positioning itself as a robot-data infrastructure company rather than a robot maker, aiming to supply the training and operational data that manufacturers need to build more capable robots. Backing from Korea’s major manufacturers suggests industry demand for a shared data layer, with the bet that higher-quality robot data will become as central to robotics as semiconductor foundries are to chip design.

extra.full_text: Instead of building robots themselves, the team is focused on a simpler goal — providing data that robots need to learn and operate. They believe that better data will be key to making robots more useful.

title: GFT takes AI from visual inspection to physical action for auto manufacturers
summary: GFT Technologies has launched AI-powered robotic arms for automotive manufacturing, extending AI from visual inspection into systems that can physically act on the production line. The announcement points to a shift from detecting defects or process issues toward automating responses in the same workflow, though the provided text does not give technical details, deployment sites, or performance results.

extra.full_text: Global digital transformation company GFT Technologies has launched its new AI-powered robotic arms designed for automotive manufacturing.

title: New research enables a robot to chart a better course
summary: MIGHTY is an open-source robot path-planning system that quickly generates smooth routes that avoid obstacles while reducing travel time. The work is positioned for time-sensitive navigation settings such as disaster recovery and parcel delivery, where faster, cleaner trajectory planning could make mobile robots more useful in cluttered real-world environments.

extra.full_text: By rapidly generating a smooth path plan that cuts travel time and avoids obstacles, the open-source “MIGHTY” system could streamline disaster recovery and parcel delivery.

title: starVLA/starVLA
summary: StarVLA is a modular open-source platform for building and evaluating vision-language-action models, with separated components for models, data, training, configs, and evaluation so researchers can swap backbones, benchmarks, and robot setups without rewriting the whole stack. It already covers practical VLA workflows such as LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin, VLA-Arena, RoboCasa, CALVIN, Behavior-1K, Franka real-robot examples, RL post-training via RLinf, and world-model-based action prediction using Cosmos-Predict2 or Wan2. Its appeal is as much engineering substrate as model code: it is designed for rapid prototyping, benchmark co-training, custom robot or dataset integration, and even coding-agent-assisted extensions.

extra.readme: StarVLA: A Lego-like Codebase for Vision-Language-Action Model Developing An open-source research platform for integrating and exploring cutting-edge technologies for generalist robots. 📢 Citation Update: Our technical report is now on arXiv (2604.05014). We kindly invite you to use the updated BibTeX for any ongoing or future citations. If you have already cited StarVLA in a previous version of your work, we would greatly appreciate it if you could update the citation entry in your camera-ready or future revisions. Thank you for your understanding and support! 🙏 --- In StarVLA (also a pun on "start VLA" ), each functional component (model, data, trainer, config, evaluation, etc.) follows a top-down, intuitive separation and high-cohesion, low-coupling principle, enabling plug-and-play design, rapid prototyping, and independent debugging. News ⚠️ Branch notice: The starVLA dev branch is where we actively merge new features and may be temporarily unstable. For verified results, use the stable starVLA branch. Thanks to StarVLA's low-coupling design, switching between branches is painless. We encourage trying starVLA dev and welcome PRs if you spot any issues! 💡 Tip: Files under any /bar/ directory are git-ignored, so you can place your custom scripts there (e.g., examples/LIBERO/train files/bar/my train.sh ) without polluting the repo. [2026/04/09] 🚀 unified multi-benchmark co-training example (combining LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin, VLA-Arena, etc.) is coming soon. Stay tuned! [2026/05/01] 🔥 We now provide a step-by-step guide for integrating your own robot / dataset into StarVLA. [2026/05/01] 🔥 We are building agent skills to make StarVLA a powerful substrate for AI coding agents — we have verified that GitHub Copilot (Claude Opus 4.7) can autonomously integrate examples/Robocasa 365 and examples/RoboChallenge table30v2 from scratch. Going forward, StarVLA will be continuously optimised to be equally easy to use for humans and code agents. [2026/05/01] 🙏 Special thanks to the AllenAI team for providing optimised Docker environments and evaluation-acceleration support via vla-evaluation-harness! If you need to speed up large-scale VLA benchmark evaluation, we recommend checking it out. [2026/04/18] 🔥 StarVLA now supports DOMINO, a dynamic manipulation benchmark for moving objects and time-varying scenes. Original DOMINO repository is here. [2026/04/09] 🎯 Thanks to the RLinf team, StarVLA now supports RL post-training ! Check out the StarVLA × RLinf tutorial to get started. [2026/04/09] 🔥 WM4A (World Model for Action) is now integrated! Use pretrained video-generation DiT models (Cosmos-Predict2, Wan2.2) as backbones for action prediction. See docs/WM4A.md for architecture details and training instructions. Pretrained checkpoints are available at the StarVLA/world-model-to-vla HuggingFace collection. [2026/03/29] 🔥 Thanks to the ABot-M0 team for providing the pre-trained weights. For Qwen3-VL 4B , you can reload the qwen vl interface module in various frameworks! [2026/03/19] 🔥 StarVLA now provides a complete real-robot development case with Franka robot examples! [2026/03/03] 🔥 We now support Qwen3.5 as a backbone for VLA — the fastest integration in the community ⚡ With more model size options: 0.8B, 2B, 4B, and 9B ! Build your VLA flexibly on top of native multimodal models! [2026/01/29] 🔥 StarVLA Training Efficiency Report & Training Curves released! Training configs and efficiency benchmarks for community reference. [2026/01/29] Calvin benchmark experiments were conducted by the UNT team. For inquiries, please contact Zhijie Song (1600013008@pku.edu.cn) or Feng Yan (bphengyan@163.com). [2025/12/25] We've simultaneously established pipelines for Behavior-1K, RoboTwin 2.0, and CALVIN. We'd love to collaborate and share baseline results for more benchmarks with the community! title: huggingface/lerobot
summary: Collect datasets, train policies, and deploy/evaluate robots in one PyTorch stack: the unified Robot interface spans SO-100, Reachy2 and Unitree G1, while LeRobotDataset stores synchronized MP4/images plus Parquet state/action logs on HF Hub. It bundles ACT, Diffusion, VQ-BeT, Pi0Fast, GR00T N1.5 and SmolVLA.

extra.readme: LeRobot aims to provide models, datasets, and tools for real-world robotics in PyTorch. The goal is to lower the barrier to entry so that everyone can contribute to and benefit from shared datasets and pretrained models. 🤗 A hardware-agnostic, Python-native interface that standardizes control across diverse platforms, from low-cost arms (SO-100) to humanoids. 🤗 A standardized, scalable LeRobotDataset format (Parquet + MP4 or images) hosted on the Hugging Face Hub, enabling efficient storage, streaming and visualization of massive robotic datasets. 🤗 State-of-the-art policies that have been shown to transfer to the real-world ready for training and deployment. 🤗 Comprehensive support for the open-source ecosystem to democratize physical AI. Quick Start LeRobot can be installed directly from PyPI. [!IMPORTANT] For detailed installation guide, please see the Installation Documentation. Robots & Control LeRobot provides a unified Robot class interface that decouples control logic from hardware specifics. It supports a wide range of robots and teleoperation devices. Supported Hardware: SO100, LeKiwi, Koch, HopeJR, OMX, EarthRover, Reachy2, Gamepads, Keyboards, Phones, OpenARM, Unitree G1. While these devices are natively integrated into the LeRobot codebase, the library is designed to be extensible. You can easily implement the Robot interface to utilize LeRobot's data collection, training, and visualization tools for your own custom robot. For detailed hardware setup guides, see the Hardware Documentation. LeRobot Dataset To solve the data fragmentation problem in robotics, we utilize the LeRobotDataset format. - Structure: Synchronized MP4 videos (or images) for vision and Parquet files for state/action data. - HF Hub Integration: Explore thousands of robotics datasets on the Hugging Face Hub. - Tools: Seamlessly delete episodes, split by indices/fractions, add/remove features, and merge multiple datasets. Learn more about it in the LeRobotDataset Documentation SoTA Models LeRobot implements state-of-the-art policies in pure PyTorch, covering Imitation Learning, Reinforcement Learning, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, with more coming soon. It also provides you with the tools to instrument and inspect your training process. Training a policy is as simple as running a script configuration: Category Models -------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Imitation Learning ACT, Diffusion, VQ-BeT, Multitask DiT Policy Reinforcement Learning HIL-SERL, TDMPC & QC-FQL (coming soon) VLAs Models Pi0Fast, Pi0.5, GR00T N1.5, SmolVLA, XVLA Similarly to the hardware, you can easily implement your own policy & leverage LeRobot's data collection, training, and visualization tools, and share your model to the HF Hub For detailed policy setup guides, see the Policy Documentation. For GPU/RAM requirements and expected training time per policy, see the Compute Hardware Guide. Inference & Evaluation Evaluate your policies in simulation or on real hardware using the unified evaluation script. LeRobot supports standard benchmarks like LIBERO , MetaWorld and more to come. Learn how to implement your own simulation environment or benchmark and distribute it from the HF Hub by following the EnvHub Documentation Resources - Documentation: The complete guide to tutorials & API. - Chinese Tutorials: LeRobot+SO-ARM101中文教程-同济子豪兄 Detailed doc for assembling, teleoperate, dataset, train, deploy. Verified by Seed Studio and 5 global hackathon players. - Discord: Join the LeRobot server to discuss with the community. - X: Follow us on X to stay up-to-date with the latest developments. - Robot Learning Tutorial: A free, hands-on course to learn robot learning using LeRobot. Citation If you use LeRobot in your project, please cite the GitHub repository to acknowledg

The goal is to lower the barrier to entry so that everyone can contribute to and benefit from shared datasets and pretrained models. 🤗 A hardware-agnostic, Python-native interface that standardizes control across diverse platforms, from low-cost arms (SO-100) to humanoids. 🤗 A standardized, scalable LeRobotDataset format (Parquet + MP4 or images) hosted on the Hugging Face Hub, enabling efficient storage, streaming and visualization of massive robotic datasets. 🤗 State-of-the-art policies that have been shown to transfer to the real-world ready for training and deployment. 🤗 Comprehensive support for the open-source ecosystem to democratize physical AI. Quick Start LeRobot can be installed directly from PyPI. [!IMPORTANT] For detailed installation guide, please see the Installation Documentation. Robots & Control LeRobot provides a unified Robot class interface that decouples control logic from hardware specifics. It supports a wide range of robots and teleoperation devices. Supported Hardware: SO100, LeKiwi, Koch, HopeJR, OMX, EarthRover, Reachy2, Gamepads, Keyboards, Phones, OpenARM, Unitree G1. While these devices are natively integrated into the LeRobot codebase, the library is designed to be extensible. You can easily implement the Robot interface to utilize LeRobot's data collection, training, and visualization tools for your own custom robot. For detailed hardware setup guides, see the Hardware Documentation. LeRobot Dataset To solve the data fragmentation problem in robotics, we utilize the LeRobotDataset format. - Structure: Synchronized MP4 videos (or images) for vision and Parquet files for state/action data. - HF Hub Integration: Explore thousands of robotics datasets on the Hugging Face Hub. - Tools: Seamlessly delete episodes, split by indices/fractions, add/remove features, and merge multiple datasets. Learn more about it in the LeRobotDataset Documentation SoTA Models LeRobot implements state-of-the-art policies in pure PyTorch, covering Imitation Learning, Reinforcement Learning, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, with more coming soon. It also provides you with the tools to instrument and inspect your training process. Training a policy is as simple as running a script configuration: Category Models -------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Imitation Learning ACT, Diffusion, VQ-BeT, Multitask DiT Policy Reinforcement Learning HIL-SERL, TDMPC & QC-FQL (coming soon) VLAs Models Pi0Fast, Pi0.5, GR00T N1.5, SmolVLA, XVLA Similarly to the hardware, you can easily implement your own policy & leverage LeRobot's data collection, training, and visualization tools, and share your model to the HF Hub For detailed policy setup guides, see the Policy Documentation. For GPU/RAM requirements and expected training time per policy, see the Compute Hardware Guide. Inference & Evaluation Evaluate your policies in simulation or on real hardware using the unified evaluation script. LeRobot supports standard benchmarks like LIBERO , MetaWorld and more to come. Learn how to implement your own simulation environment or benchmark and distribute it from the HF Hub by following the EnvHub Documentation Resources - Documentation: The complete guide to tutorials & API. - Chinese Tutorials: LeRobot+SO-ARM101中文教程-同济子豪兄 Detailed doc for assembling, teleoperate, dataset, train, deploy. Verified by Seed Studio and 5 global hackathon players. - Discord: Join the LeRobot server to discuss with the community. - X: Follow us on X to stay up-to-date with the latest developments. - Robot Learning Tutorial: A free, hands-on course to learn robot learning using LeRobot. title: Denghaoyuan123/Awesome-RL-VLA
summary: Curated RL-VLA reading list for robotic manipulation, organizing papers by offline, online, offline+online, and test-time RL regimes. It adds comparison tables for action type, reward sparsity, MF/MB status, sim/real validation, base VLA, and policy class, but no new algorithm.

extra.full_text: Awesome RL-VLA for Robotic Manipulation 🤖 [Paper] A curated list of papers and resources on Reinforcement Learning of Vision-Language-Action (RL-VLA) models for Robotic Manipulation. This repository provides a comprehensive overview of training paradigms, methodologies, and state-of-the-art approaches in RL-VLA research. 📢 Latest News 🔥 [November 2025] Our comprehensive survey paper "A Survey on Reinforcement Learning of Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation" is now available on TechRxiv! Stay tuned for future updates. 📖 Table of Contents - Awesome RL-VLA for Robotic Manipulation 🤖 - 📢 Latest News - 📖 Table of Contents - 🔍 Overview - 🚀 Training Paradigms - Offline RL-VLA - Online RL-VLA - Test-time RL-VLA - 📚 Paper Collection - Legend - Offline RL-VLA - Online RL-VLA - Offline + Online RL-VLA - Test-time RL-VLA - 🔗 Useful Resources - 🎯 RL-VLA Action Optimization - Base VLA Models - Datasets \& Benchmarks - Frameworks \& Tools - 🤝 Contributing - Contribution Guidelines - 📄 Citation - ⭐ Star History 🔍 Overview RL training is crucial for enabling VLAs to generalize out-of-distribution (OOD) from large-scale pre-trained data. Existing RL-VLA training paradigms can be categorized into three types based on how agents obtain and utilize feedback from the environment: - Online RL-VLA : Direct interaction with the environment during training - Offline RL-VLA : Learning from static datasets without further environmental interaction - Test-time RL-VLA : Models adapt their behavior during deployment without altering parameters 🚀 Training Paradigms Offline RL-VLA Offline RL trains VLA models on pre-collected static datasets, enabling learning independently from environment interactions. This paradigm is suitable for high-risk or resource-constrained deployment scenarios. Key Research Directions: - Data Utilization : Effective utilization of static datasets for policy improvement - Objective Modification : Customizing RL objectives for novel architectures and data augmentation Online RL-VLA Online RL-VLA enables interactive policy learning through continuous environment interaction, empowering pre-trained VLAs with adaptive closed-loop control capability for real-world OOD environments. Key Research Directions: - Policy Optimization : Direct policy improvement based on environmental rewards - Sample Efficiency : Learning effective policies with limited interaction budget - Active Exploration : Efficient exploration strategies for higher performance gains - Training Stability : Ensuring consistent policy updates and convergence - Infrastructure : Scalable frameworks for online RL-VLA training Test-time RL-VLA Test-time RL-VLA adapts behavior during deployment through lightweight updates, addressing the expensive cost of full model fine-tuning in real-world scenarios. Key Adaptation Mechanisms: - Value Guidance : Using pre-trained value functions to influence action selection - Memory Buffer Guidance : Retrieving relevant historical experiences during inference - Planning-guided Adaptation : Explicit reasoning over future action sequences 📚 Paper Collection Legend - Action : AR (Autoregressive), Diffusion, Flow (Flow-matching) - Reward : D (Dense Reward), S (Sparse Reward) - Model Type : MB (Model-based), MF (Model-free) - Environment : Sim. (Simulation), Real (Real-world) - Task : MT (Multi-task), ST (Single-task) - Policy : On-Policy, Off-Policy, Hybrid (mixed on/off-policy), Test-time (inference-time adaptation) Offline RL-VLA Method Date Publication Sim. title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab
summary: GPU-accelerated robot-learning workflows on NVIDIA Isaac Sim let researchers train RL, imitation learning, and motion-planning agents with RTX sensor simulation and sim-to-real-focused physics. It packages 16+ robots, 30+ environments, multi-agent RL, and integrations with RSL-RL, SKRL, RL Games, and Stable Baselines.

extra.readme: --- Isaac Lab Isaac Lab is a GPU-accelerated, open-source framework designed to unify and simplify robotics research workflows, such as reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and motion planning. Built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim, it combines fast and accurate physics and sensor simulation, making it an ideal choice for sim-to-real transfer in robotics. Isaac Lab provides developers with a range of essential features for accurate sensor simulation, such as RTX-based cameras, LIDAR, or contact sensors. The framework's GPU acceleration enables users to run complex simulations and computations faster, which is key for iterative processes like reinforcement learning and data-intensive tasks. Moreover, Isaac Lab can run locally or be distributed across the cloud, offering flexibility for large-scale deployments. A detailed description of Isaac Lab can be found in our arXiv paper. Key Features Isaac Lab offers a comprehensive set of tools and environments designed to facilitate robot learning: - Robots : A diverse collection of robots, from manipulators, quadrupeds, to humanoids, with more than 16 commonly available models. - Environments : Ready-to-train implementations of more than 30 environments, which can be trained with popular reinforcement learning frameworks such as RSL RL, SKRL, RL Games, or Stable Baselines. We also support multi-agent reinforcement learning. - Physics : Rigid bodies, articulated systems, deformable objects - Sensors : RGB/depth/segmentation cameras, camera annotations, IMU, contact sensors, ray casters. Getting Started Documentation Our documentation page provides everything you need to get started, including detailed tutorials and step-by-step guides. Follow these links to learn more about: - Installation steps - Reinforcement learning - Tutorials - Available environments Isaac Sim Version Dependency Isaac Lab is built on top of Isaac Sim and requires specific versions of Isaac Sim that are compatible with each release of Isaac Lab. Below, we outline the recent Isaac Lab releases and GitHub branches and their corresponding dependency versions for Isaac Sim. Isaac Lab Version Isaac Sim Version ----------------------------- ------------------------- main branch Isaac Sim 4.5 / 5.0 / 5.1 v2.3.X Isaac Sim 4.5 / 5.0 / 5.1 v2.2.X Isaac Sim 4.5 / 5.0 v2.1.X Isaac Sim 4.5 v2.0.X Isaac Sim 4.5 Contributing to Isaac Lab We wholeheartedly welcome contributions from the community to make this framework mature and useful for everyone. These may happen as bug reports, feature requests, or code contributions. For details, please check our contribution guidelines. Show & Tell: Share Your Inspiration We encourage you to utilize our Show & Tell area in the Discussions section of this repository. This space is designed for you to: Share the tutorials you've created Showcase your learning content Present exciting projects you've developed By sharing your work, you'll inspire others and contribute to the collective knowledge of our community. Your contributions can spark new ideas and collaborations, fostering innovation in robotics and simulation. Troubleshooting Please see the troubleshooting section for common fixes or submit an issue. For issues related to Isaac Sim, we recommend checking its documentation or opening a question on its forums. title: NVlabs/ProtoMotions
summary: GPU-accelerated ProtoMotions3 trains physically simulated humanoids on motion corpora, claiming AMASS-scale skill learning in 12 hours on 4 A100s. Distinctive pieces are PyRoki one-command retargeting, IsaacGym/Newton/MuJoCo sim-to-sim testing, and ONNX sim-to-real deployment for Unitree G1.

extra.full_text: ProtoMotions 3 A GPU-Accelerated Framework for Simulated Humanoids (unverified AI generation) --- Overview ProtoMotions3 is a GPU-accelerated simulation and learning framework for training physically simulated digital humans and humanoid robots. Our mission is to provide a fast prototyping platform for various simulated humanoid learning tasks and environments—for researchers and practitioners in animation , robotics , and reinforcement learning —bridging efforts across communities. Modularity , extensibility , and scalability are at the core of ProtoMotions3. It is community-driven and permissively licensed under the Apache-2.0 license. Also check out MimicKit , our sibling repository for a lightweight framework for motion imitation learning. --- What You Can Do with ProtoMotions3 🏃 Large-Scale Motion Learning Train your fully physically simulated character to learn motion skills from the entire public AMASS human animation dataset ( 40+ hours ) within 12 hours on 4 A100s. 📈 Scalable Multi-GPU Training Scale training to even larger datasets with each GPU handling a subset of motions. For example, we have trained with 24 A100s with 13K motions on each GPU with the BONES dataset in SOMA skeleton format. Check out Quick Start and SEED BVH Data Preparation to play around with the dataset and pre-trained models today. 🔄 One-Command Retargeting Transfer (retarget) the entire AMASS dataset to your favorite robot with the built-in PyRoki -based optimizer—in one command. Note: As of v3, we use PyRoki for retargeting. Earlier versions used Mink. 🤖 Train Any Robot Train your robot to perform AMASS motor skills in 12 hours , by just changing one command argument: --robot-name=smpl → --robot-name=h1 2 and preparing retargeted motions (see here) 🔬 Sim2Sim Testing One-click test ( --simulator=isaacgym → --simulator=newton → --simulator=mujoco ) of robot control policies on H1 2 or G1 in different physics engines (NVIDIA Newton, MuJoCo CPU). Policies shown below only use observations you could actually get from real hardware. 🤖 From Sim to Real Train in simulation, deploy on real hardware. ProtoMotions trains one General Tracking Policy on entire BONES-SEED dataset ( 142K motions) and transfers directly to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot zero-shot. Our deployment pipeline exports a single ONNX model (with observation computation baked in), so deployment frameworks only need to provide raw sensor signals — no need to rewrite obs functions or match training internals. We tested on the Unitree G1 via the brilliant RoboJuDo framework, adding just one policy file with no mandatory changes to RoboJuDo core. 📖 Full Deployment Tutorial — from data preparation to real robot, fully reproducible. 🎨 High-Fidelity Rendering Test your policy in IsaacSim 5.0+ , which allows you to load beautifully rendered Gaussian splatting backgrounds (with Omniverse NuRec — this rendered scene is not physically interact-able yet). 🎬 Motion Authoring with Kimodo With Kimodo (NVIDIA's text-to-motion generation model), generate any motion from a text prompt and use ProtoMotions to train a physics-based policy that performs the motion — for both the SOMA animation character and the Unitree G1 robot. Policies trained this way can be deployed directly on real hardware. See Kimodo Data Preparation for how to convert Kimodo outputs to ProtoMotions format. Image Credit: NVIDIA Human Motion Modeling Research 🏗️ Procedural Scene Generation Procedurally generate many scenes for scalable Synthetic Data Generation (SDG) : start from a seed motion set, use RL to adapt motions to augmented scenes. 🎭 Generative Policies Train a generative policy (e.g., MaskedMimic ) that can autonomously choose its "move" to finish the task. ⛰️ Terrain Navigation Train your robot to hike challenging terrains! 🎯 Custom Environments Have a new task? Build it from modular components — no monolithic env class needed. Here's how the steering task is composed: Layer File What it does ------- ------ ------------

title: Genesis-Embodied-AI/genesis-world
summary: Simulates robotics and embodied-AI worlds with a Python physics platform unifying rigid body, MPM, SPH, FEM, PBD, and fluid solvers plus ray-traced rendering. Its differentiator is speed and breadth: reports >43M FPS for a Franka arm on one RTX 4090, with URDF/MJCF loading and partial differentiability.

What is Genesis? 2. Key Features 3. Quick Installation 4. Docker 5. Documentation 6. Contributing to Genesis 7. Support 8. License and Acknowledgments 9. Associated Papers 10. Citation What is Genesis? Genesis is a physics platform designed for general-purpose Robotics/Embodied AI/Physical AI applications. It is simultaneously multiple things: 1. A universal physics engine re-built from the ground up, capable of simulating a wide range of materials and physical phenomena. 2. A lightweight , ultra-fast , pythonic , and user-friendly robotics simulation platform. 3. A powerful and fast photo-realistic rendering system . 4. A generative data engine that transforms user-prompted natural language description into various modalities of data. Powered by a universal physics engine re-designed and re-built from the ground up, Genesis integrates various physics solvers and their coupling into a unified framework. This core physics engine is further enhanced by a generative agent framework that operates at an upper level, aiming towards fully automated data generation for robotics and beyond. Note : Currently, we are open-sourcing the underlying physics engine and the simulation platform . Our generative framework is a modular system that incorporates many different generative modules, each handling a certain range of data modalities, routed by a high level agent. Some of the modules integrated existing papers and some are still under submission. Access to our generative feature will be gradually rolled out in the near future. If you are interested, feel free to explore more in the paper list below. Genesis aims to: - Lower the barrier to using physics simulations, making robotics research accessible to everyone. See our mission statement. - Unify diverse physics solvers into a single framework to recreate the physical world with the highest fidelity. - Automate data generation , reducing human effort and letting the data flywheel spin on its own. Project Page: Key Features - Speed : Over 43 million FPS when simulating a Franka robotic arm with a single RTX 4090 (430,000 times faster than real-time). - Cross-platform : Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and supports multiple compute backends (CPU, Nvidia/AMD GPUs, Apple Metal). - Integration of diverse physics solvers : Rigid body, MPM, SPH, FEM, PBD, Stable Fluid. - Wide range of material models : Simulation and coupling of rigid bodies, liquids, gases, deformable objects, thin-shell objects, and granular materials. - Compatibility with various robots : Robotic arms, legged robots, drones, soft robots , and support for loading MJCF (.xml) , URDF , .obj , .glb , .ply , .stl , and more. - Photo-realistic rendering : Native ray-tracing-based rendering. - Differentiability : Genesis is designed to be fully differentiable. Currently, our MPM solver and Tool Solver support differentiability, with other solvers planned for future versions (starting with rigid & articulated body solver). - User-friendliness : Designed for simplicity, with intuitive installation and APIs.
